# LAMMPS Python frontend reference

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/lammps_fix_external.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/lammps_fix_external.html

### Constructor

```python
FixExternal(
    lmp,
    potential,
    elements,
    *,
    fix_id="rgpot",
    create=True,
    comm=None,
    virial="auto",
    allow_periodic_on_free_box=False,
)
```

`lmp` is an initialized object from LAMMPS' Python module.
`potential` is a Python rgpot potential object: an
`evaluate(positions, numbers, cell)` method returns a dictionary with `energy`,
`forces` and optional `stress`, or a callable returns
`(energy, forces, variance)`.
A callable `stress()` method, when present, supplies the stress after a call.

`elements` is one symbol or atomic number per LAMMPS atom type, in type order;
it may be a whitespace-separated string or a sequence. rgpot's element table
resolves symbols.

### Units

Python rgpot potentials use Angstrom, eV, eV/Angstrom and eV/Angstrom cubed.
The frontend uses rgpot's unit-expression converter for these LAMMPS styles:

| LAMMPS `units` | Length | Energy | Force |
|-----------------|--------|--------|-------|
| `metal` | Angstrom | eV | eV/Angstrom |
| `real` | Angstrom | kcal/mol | kcal/(mol Angstrom) |
| `electron` | Bohr | Hartree | Hartree/Bohr |

Any other style raises `ValueError` before the fix is created.

### Cell, positions and atom order

The cell has one vector per row.
For LAMMPS' restricted triclinic box it is

```
((xhi-xlo, 0,       0),
 (xy,       yhi-ylo, 0),
 (xz,       yz,      zhi-zlo))
```

The origin is not subtracted.
With periodic boundaries, image flags unwrap each Cartesian position as
`x + ix*a + iy*b + iz*c`.
All three boundaries must be periodic or all three non-periodic; mixed
boundaries raise `ValueError`.
The potential protocol always receives the 3 by 3 cell.
A free-boundary potential may ignore it; a periodic potential such as `LJPot`
folds pairs across the cell vectors, so it is refused with `boundary f f f` (see
below).

### Free boundaries and periodic potentials

With `boundary f f f` the cell is the box extent, which is not a periodic cell
of the system.
A potential that applies periodic boundary conditions to the cell it is given
would pair atoms through the box faces and return a wrong energy.
The constructor therefore raises `ValueError` when all three LAMMPS boundaries
are non-periodic and the potential is periodic.
The message names the potential and points to `rgpot.LJClusterPot`.
The check runs before any fix is created, so nothing is left registered in
LAMMPS.

A potential counts as periodic when its `caps()` method returns a mapping whose
`periodic` entry is true. rgpot potentials report this as `caps()["periodic"]`;
`LJPot` reports true and `LJClusterPot` reports false.
A potential with no `caps()` method, or whose mapping has no `periodic` entry,
is not classified and is never refused.
Boxes that are periodic in all three directions are not checked.

`allow_periodic_on_free_box=True` turns the check off.
The periodic potential is then evaluated on the box extents exactly as before,
which is only meaningful when that cell is the intended periodic cell.

The evaluation is in increasing atom-ID order.
Returned forces are mapped back to each rank's local order.
IDs must be the integers `1..N` without duplicates.

### Virial and pressure

An rgpot stress is the Cauchy tensor `sigma = V^-1 dE/depsilon`.
LAMMPS' external-fix virial is `W = -dE/depsilon`, so the frontend returns
`-V sigma`, symmetrized, in LAMMPS order `xx yy zz xy xz yz` and in the LAMMPS
energy unit.

With `virial`"auto"`, a missing stress on a periodic box raises =RuntimeError`
naming the potential and saying it lacks analytic stress.
A non-periodic box with no stress returns a zero virial.
`virial`"none"= returns zeros.

### MPI and errors

For one LAMMPS rank, mpi4py is not imported.
For several ranks, `comm` or `MPI.COMM_WORLD` must have the same size as LAMMPS.
Rank zero gathers `(IDs, positions, atomic numbers)`, evaluates once, broadcasts
energy and virial, and scatters forces in each rank's local atom order.
Collective status checks before the gather and after the rank-zero evaluation
turn a failure on any one rank into the same error on every rank.

A Python exception cannot cross LAMMPS' C callback.
The callback stores the first exception in `driver.error`, writes zero forces,
and sets an internal variable watched by `fix halt`.
`driver.run(steps, *keywords)` clears the flag and re-raises that exception
after LAMMPS stops.
A collective failure raises `RuntimeError` with the same rank, phase, exception
type, and message on every rank.
Calling `lmp.command("run ...")` directly instead exposes LAMMPS' halt error;
the stored Python exception remains in `driver.error`.

`close()` removes the halt fix and external fix, deregisters the callback, and
releases the LAMMPS object.
This also applies with `create=False`: the caller supplies the fix but transfers
its teardown to `FixExternal`.
Closing twice is harmless; an `unfix` failure is raised and teardown can be
retried.
`close()` does not close the potential object supplied by the caller.

---

# C++ API

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/cpp_api.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/cpp_api.html

The C++ API in `include/rgpot/` wraps the C ABI of `rgpot-core` in move-only
handles.
`rgpot/rgpot.hpp` includes `errors.hpp`, `potential.hpp` and `types.hpp`, and
`rpc_client.hpp` only when `RGPOT_HAS_RPC` is defined.
It does not include `CppCore/rgpot/Potential.hpp`; each potential header (for
example `rgpot/LennardJones/LJPot.hpp`) brings in `rgpot::PotentialBase` and
`rgpot::Potential`.
Most wrapper methods pass the C status code to an internal check that throws
`rgpot::Error` for any status other than `RGPOT_SUCCESS`.
The exceptions are stated in each entry: `invalidate_hvp` and `reset_hvp_counts`
call C functions that return nothing, and the factories and the `InputSpec` and
`CalcResult` constructors check nothing.
The wrappers call the C functions of `rgpot-core`, which a Meson build links
only with `-Dwith_rust_core=true`.
Meson defines `RGPOT_HAS_RPC` only when `with_rust_core` is on together with
`with_rpc` or `with_rpc_client_only`.

The handles do not convert units.
Positions, cell, energy and forces are in the units of the wrapped potential.
The built-in potentials use Angstrom, eV and
eV/Angstrom (`CppCore/rgpot/units.hpp`).

### include/rgpot/errors.hpp

#### `rgpot::Error`

```cpp
explicit Error(const std::string &msg,
               rgpot_status_t status = RGPOT_INTERNAL_ERROR);
```

- Inputs :: `msg`, the text that `what()` returns, and `status`, the code the C
  API returned (default `RGPOT_INTERNAL_ERROR`).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: an exception derived from `std::runtime_error`.
- Errors :: none; the constructor has no failure path.

#### `rgpot::Error::status`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] rgpot_status_t status() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the status the C API returned, so a caller tells
  `RGPOT_SCC_NOT_CONVERGED` from other failures.
  An `Error` built without a status holds `RGPOT_INTERNAL_ERROR`.
- Errors :: none.

The wrappers build `msg` from a category prefix and the `rgpot_last_error()`
text, or "unknown error" when that pointer is NULL.
The prefixes are "invalid parameter: " for `RGPOT_INVALID_PARAMETER`, "RPC
error: " for `RGPOT_RPC_ERROR`, "buffer size error: " for
`RGPOT_BUFFER_SIZE_ERROR`, "SCC not converged: " for `RGPOT_SCC_NOT_CONVERGED`,
"no Taylor jet: " for `RGPOT_NO_JET`, "Taylor jet branch: " for
`RGPOT_JET_BRANCH`, "Taylor jet domain: " for `RGPOT_JET_DOMAIN`, and "internal
error: " for `RGPOT_INTERNAL_ERROR` and any other code.
Every category throws the same type, `rgpot::Error`.

### include/rgpot/types.hpp

#### `rgpot::InputSpec`

```cpp
InputSpec(size_t n_atoms, double *pos, int *atmnrs, double *box);
InputSpec(std::vector<double> &positions, std::vector<int> &atmnrs, double *box);
```

- Inputs :: `n_atoms`; `pos` or `positions`, 3*n doubles, row-major xyz per
  atom; `atmnrs`, n atomic numbers; `box`, 9 doubles, the cell vectors as rows.
  The vector overload takes n as `positions.size() / 3`.
- Units :: positions and cell in the length unit of the potential (Angstrom for
  the built-in potentials); atomic numbers and counts have none.
- Outputs :: a move-only object holding an `rgpot_force_input_t` with non-owning
  DLPack tensors over the caller's arrays.
  The arrays are borrowed, not copied, and must outlive the object.
  The destructor frees the tensor metadata, not the arrays.
- Errors :: none; nothing is checked.
  The vector overload does not compare `atmnrs.size()` with n.
  NULL pointers are stored as given and surface as errors from the call that
  reads them.

#### `rgpot::InputSpec::c_struct`

```cpp
const rgpot_force_input_t &c_struct() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a const reference to the wrapped `rgpot_force_input_t`, valid while
  the `InputSpec` lives.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::InputSpec::n_atoms`

```cpp
size_t n_atoms() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the atom count given at construction.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CalcResult`

```cpp
CalcResult();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a move-only result buffer from `rgpot_force_out_create()`: NULL
  forces, energy and variance 0.0.
  The destructor frees the forces tensor with `rgpot_tensor_free` when one was
  set.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CalcResult::c_struct`

```cpp
rgpot_force_out_t &c_struct();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a mutable reference to the wrapped `rgpot_force_out_t`.
  The `CalcResult` keeps ownership of any forces tensor stored in it.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CalcResult::energy`

```cpp
double energy() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: the energy unit of the potential (eV for the built-in potentials).
- Outputs :: the potential energy; 0.0 before a calculation.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CalcResult::variance`

```cpp
double variance() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: as the potential reports it; most potentials leave it at 0.0.
- Outputs :: the variance or uncertainty estimate; 0.0 when unused.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CalcResult::forces_data`

```cpp
const double *forces_data(size_t &n_elements) const;
```

- Inputs :: `n_elements`, an out-parameter.
- Units :: forces in the energy-per-length unit of the potential (eV/Angstrom
  for the built-in potentials).
- Outputs :: a pointer to the forces tensor data, 3*n doubles in row-major
  `[n, 3]` order, valid while the `CalcResult` lives; `n_elements` is set to the
  product of the tensor shape.
  With no forces tensor it returns `nullptr` and sets `n_elements` to 0.
- Errors :: none.
  The pointer is read as CPU memory; the device of the tensor is not checked.

#### `rgpot::CalcResult::forces_vec`

```cpp
std::vector<double> forces_vec() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: as `forces_data`.
- Outputs :: a copy of the forces, 3*n doubles row-major; empty when there is no
  forces tensor.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CalcResult::has_forces`

```cpp
bool has_forces() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `true` when a forces tensor is set.
- Errors :: none.

### include/rgpot/potential.hpp

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle`

```cpp
explicit PotentialHandle(rgpot_potential_t *handle);
```

- Inputs :: `handle`, a pointer from `rgpot_potential_new` or
  `rgpot_potential_new_eindir`, or NULL.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a move-only handle that owns `handle` and passes it to
  `rgpot_potential_free` on destruction.
  A moved-from handle holds NULL.
- Errors :: none; a NULL `handle` is stored as given.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::from_impl`

```cpp
template <typename Impl> static PotentialHandle from_impl(Impl &impl);
template <typename Impl>
static PotentialHandle from_impl(Impl &impl, size_t n_atoms,
                                 const int32_t *atomic_numbers,
                                 const double *box_matrix,
                                 const double *bounds_low = nullptr,
                                 const double *bounds_high = nullptr);
```

- Inputs :: `impl`, an object with
  `forceImpl(const rgpot::ForceInput &, rgpot::ForceOut *)`; the caller keeps
  ownership and must keep it alive while the handle lives.
  The second overload also takes `n_atoms`, `atomic_numbers` (n values),
  `box_matrix` (9 doubles) and optional bounds (3*n doubles each, default -50 and 50 per coordinate when NULL); `rgpot_potential_new_eindir`
  copies them.
- Units :: positions, cell and bounds in the length unit of `impl`.
- Outputs :: a handle whose callback calls `impl.forceImpl` and returns the
  forces as a new owning `[n, 3]` tensor.
  Each derivative hook of `impl` is registered when this instance sets its
  `caps()` bit: `hessianVectorImpl` as the analytic Hessian-vector product
  (`analyticHvp`), `hessianVectorAdImpl` as the dual-number one (`adHvp`),
  `hessianImpl` as the analytic Hessian (`analyticHessian`) and `hessianAdImpl`
  as the dual-number one (`adHessian`).
- Errors :: throws `std::invalid_argument` when a `caps()` bit is set and `Impl`
  lacks the matching hook; nothing else is thrown by the factory.
  When `n_atoms * 3` overflows, the second overload returns a handle holding
  NULL, and later calls on it throw `rgpot::Error` ("invalid parameter").
  At calculation time an exception from `impl.forceImpl` becomes
  `RGPOT_INTERNAL_ERROR`, or
  `RGPOT_SCC_NOT_CONVERGED` for `rgpot::SccNotConverged`, and missing positions become `RGPOT_INVALID_PARAMETER`;
  the calling method throws `rgpot::Error`.
  The exception's `what()` text is stored with `rgpot_set_last_error`.

The trampoline copies energy, variance and forces from `ForceOut`; it does not
pass stress through.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::from_callback`

```cpp
static PotentialHandle from_callback(rgpot_status_t (*callback)(void *, const rgpot_force_input_t *, rgpot_force_out_t *),
                                     void *user_data, void (*free_fn)(void *) = nullptr);
```

- Inputs :: `callback`, a C potential callback;
  `user_data`, passed to every call; `free_fn`, called with `user_data` when the
  handle is freed, or `nullptr`.
- Units :: those of `callback`.
- Outputs :: a handle from `rgpot_potential_new`.
- Errors :: none; the result of `rgpot_potential_new` is not checked for NULL.
  A non-success status from `callback` is thrown as `rgpot::Error` by the method
  that called it.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::eam_table`

```cpp
static PotentialHandle eam_table(const std::string &path, int format = RGPOT_EAM_TABLE_AUTO,
                                 bool periodic = true);
```

- Inputs :: `path`, a funcfl, setfl or Finnis-Sinclair table; `format`, one of
  `RGPOT_EAM_TABLE_AUTO`, `RGPOT_EAM_TABLE_FUNCFL`,
  `RGPOT_EAM_TABLE_SETFL` and `RGPOT_EAM_TABLE_FINNIS_SINCLAIR`; `periodic`,
  nearest image on the cell or a free cluster.
- Units :: positions and cell in Angstrom, energy in eV, forces in eV per
  Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a handle from `rgpot_potential_new_eam_table`: the tabulated EAM
  potential of the Rust core, evaluated in process with no C++ kernel and no
  engine plugin.
  The handle needs a build with `with_rust_core`.
  See [C ABI of rgpot-core](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/c_abi.html) for what it evaluates.
- Errors :: throws `rgpot::Error` with status `RGPOT_INVALID_PARAMETER` and a
  message starting `invalid parameter: EAM table:` when the core returns NULL:
  an empty `path`, an unknown `format`, a file that cannot be opened or is not a
  table of that format.
  A calculation on a cell whose face spacing is not above twice the cutoff
  throws the same status from `calculate`.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::calculate`

```cpp
CalcResult calculate(const InputSpec &input);
```

- Inputs :: `input`, the configuration.
- Units :: those of the wrapped potential.
- Outputs :: a `CalcResult` with energy, variance and the `[n, 3]` forces tensor
  set by the callback.
- Errors :: throws `rgpot::Error` when `rgpot_potential_calculate` returns a
  non-success status: a NULL handle gives "invalid parameter", and a failing
  callback gives the category of its status.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::hvp`

```cpp
rgpot_hvp_scheme_t hvp(const InputSpec &input, const double *direction,
                       double *hv_out, double step = 0.0,
                       rgpot_hvp_scheme_t scheme = RGPOT_HVP_AUTO) const;
std::vector<double> hvp(const InputSpec &input,
                        const std::vector<double> &direction,
                        double step = 0.0,
                        rgpot_hvp_scheme_t scheme = RGPOT_HVP_AUTO,
                        rgpot_hvp_scheme_t *scheme_used = nullptr) const;
```

- Inputs :: `input`, the geometry; `direction`,
  3*n doubles laid out like the positions; `hv_out`, room for 3*n doubles that
  must not overlap `direction`; `step`, the displacement length, where 0 selects
  `RGPOT_HVP_DEFAULT_STEP`; `scheme`, one of `RGPOT_HVP_AUTO`, `RGPOT_HVP_FORWARD`, `RGPOT_HVP_CENTRAL`, `RGPOT_HVP_ANALYTIC`, `RGPOT_HVP_AD`, `RGPOT_HVP_EXACT`; `scheme_used`,
  `nullptr` or writable.
- Units :: `step` in the length unit of the positions; the product is the
  Hessian (energy per length squared, eV/Angstrom^2 for the built-in potentials)
  times `direction`.
- Outputs :: the Hessian-vector product, 3*n doubles: written to `hv_out`, or
  returned as a new vector by the second overload.
  The scheme that computed it, from
  `rgpot_potential_hvp_resolved`, is returned by the first overload and written to a non-null `scheme_used`
  by the second: `RGPOT_HVP_AUTO` reports `RGPOT_HVP_ANALYTIC` or
  `RGPOT_HVP_FORWARD`, and `RGPOT_HVP_EXACT` reports `RGPOT_HVP_ANALYTIC` or
  `RGPOT_HVP_AD`.
- Errors :: throws `rgpot::Error` when
  `rgpot_potential_hvp_resolved` returns a non-success status: NULL pointers, an unknown scheme, a negative or non-finite step, a non-finite direction value, overlapping buffers, `RGPOT_HVP_ANALYTIC` with no analytic callback, `RGPOT_HVP_AD` with no dual-number callback, or `RGPOT_HVP_EXACT`
  with neither give "invalid parameter"; a failing force callback gives the
  category of its status.
  The vector overload throws `rgpot::Error` ("invalid parameter: direction must
  hold 3 * n_atoms values") when `direction.size()` is not 3*n.

With `RGPOT_HVP_FORWARD`, k products at one geometry make k+1 force calls.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::hessian`

```cpp
rgpot_hessian_scheme_t hessian(const InputSpec &input, double *hessian_out,
                               rgpot_hessian_scheme_t scheme,
                               double step = 0.0) const;
std::vector<double> hessian(const InputSpec &input,
                            rgpot_hessian_scheme_t scheme, double step = 0.0,
                            rgpot_hessian_scheme_t *scheme_used = nullptr) const;
```

- Inputs :: `input`, the geometry;
  `hessian_out`, room for (3*n)^2 doubles; `scheme`, one of `RGPOT_HESSIAN_ANALYTIC`, `RGPOT_HESSIAN_AD`, `RGPOT_HESSIAN_EXACT` and `RGPOT_HESSIAN_CENTRAL`, with no default; `step`, the central displacement, where 0 selects `RGPOT_HVP_DEFAULT_STEP`;
  `scheme_used`, `nullptr` or writable.
- Units :: `step` in the length unit of the positions; the Hessian in energy per
  length squared, eV/Angstrom^2 for the built-in potentials.
- Outputs :: the dense Hessian, row-major with coordinate 3i+k for axis k of
  atom i: written to `hessian_out`, or returned as a new vector by the second
  overload.
  The scheme that computed it is returned by the first overload and written to a
  non-null
  `scheme_used` by the second; `RGPOT_HESSIAN_EXACT` reports `RGPOT_HESSIAN_ANALYTIC` or `RGPOT_HESSIAN_AD`.
  `RGPOT_HESSIAN_CENTRAL` makes 6n force calls and writes a symmetric matrix.
- Errors :: throws `rgpot::Error` when `rgpot_potential_hessian` returns a
  non-success status: an unknown scheme, a negative or non-finite step,
  `RGPOT_HESSIAN_ANALYTIC` with no Hessian callback, `RGPOT_HESSIAN_AD` with no
  dual-number Hessian callback, or `RGPOT_HESSIAN_EXACT` with neither give
  "invalid parameter" before any call; a failing force or Hessian callback gives
  the category of its status.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::hvp_centre`

```cpp
CalcResult hvp_centre(const InputSpec &input) const;
```

- Inputs :: `input`, the geometry.
- Units :: those of the wrapped potential.
- Outputs :: a `CalcResult` with energy and an owning `[n, 3]` forces tensor,
  taken from the cached centre when the geometry matches, otherwise from one
  force call that becomes the cached centre.
- Errors :: throws `rgpot::Error` when `rgpot_potential_hvp_centre` returns a
  non-success status (NULL handle, failing callback).

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::set_hvp_callback`

```cpp
void set_hvp_callback(HessianVectorCallback callback) const;
```

- Inputs :: `callback`, an analytic Hessian-vector product called with the
  handle's `user_data`, or `nullptr` to clear it.
- Units :: those of the wrapped potential.
- Outputs :: none.
- Errors :: throws `rgpot::Error` ("invalid parameter") when the handle is NULL.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::set_ad_hvp_callback`

```cpp
void set_ad_hvp_callback(HessianVectorCallback callback) const;
```

- Inputs :: `callback`, a dual-number Hessian-vector product called with the
  handle's `user_data`, or `nullptr` to clear it.
- Units :: those of the wrapped potential.
- Outputs :: none; `RGPOT_HVP_AD` calls it, and `RGPOT_HVP_EXACT` when no

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::set_hessian_callback`

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::set_ad_hessian_callback`

- Inputs :: `callback`, a dual-number dense Hessian called with the handle's

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::invalidate_hvp`


- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; drops the cached centre.
- Errors :: none; a NULL handle is a no-op.

Call it after changing the state behind the potential at a fixed geometry,
because the centre is keyed on positions, atomic numbers and cell only.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::hvp_counts`

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::reset_hvp_counts`

```cpp

```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; zeroes the counters, those of `derivative_counts` included,
  and keeps the cached centre.
- Errors :: none; a NULL handle is a no-op.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::set_fused_settings`

```cpp
void set_fused_settings(const FusedSettingsSpec &spec) const;
```

- Inputs :: `spec`, the settings of the engine that change its answer at a fixed
  geometry.
- Units :: `charge` in elementary charges, `electronicTemperature` in kelvin.
- Outputs :: none; the settings key the fused cache of the handle (see the C ABI
  reference).
  A request under other settings runs the engine even at positions whose
  outcome, a failure included, is stored.
  A failed energy is not retried at the same bits, so a warm-start retry after a
  failure needs a changed setting.
- Errors :: throws `rgpot::Error` when the core refuses the settings.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::sync_fused_settings`

```cpp
template <ProvidesFusedSettings Impl>
void sync_fused_settings(const Impl &impl) const;
```

- Inputs :: `impl`, an object whose `fusedSettings()` returns a
  `FusedSettingsSpec`.
- Units :: as `set_fused_settings`.
- Outputs :: none; installs `impl.fusedSettings()`.
  `from_impl` does this once for an `Impl` that has `fusedSettings()` (`XTBPot`
  and `XTBDlopen` do).
  After a setter of the potential, such as `XTBPot::setMaxIterations`, call it:
  the changed setting is a new key.
  Without the call the handle keeps returning the stored failure.
- Errors :: throws `rgpot::Error` when the core refuses the settings.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::fused_error_kind`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] rgpot_fused_error_kind_t fused_error_kind() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the kind of the failure the fused cache stores,
  `RGPOT_FUSED_SCC_NOT_CONVERGED`,
  `RGPOT_FUSED_ENGINE_FAILED` or `RGPOT_FUSED_INVALID_RESULT`, or
  `RGPOT_FUSED_OK` when it stores none.
- Errors :: none.

An `Impl` whose `forceImpl` throws `rgpot::SccNotConverged` has the failure
typed: the trampoline stores the message with
`rgpot_set_last_error` and returns `RGPOT_SCC_NOT_CONVERGED`.
Another `std::exception` returns `RGPOT_INTERNAL_ERROR` with its `what()`.
`rgpot::HessianVectorCache` is the same cache for potentials used without the
Rust core: it stores the exception a force call threw and throws it again, the
same type and message, for the same bits and settings.

#### `rgpot::PotentialHandle::raw`

```cpp
rgpot_potential_t *raw() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the owned `rgpot_potential_t` pointer, NULL after a move; the
  handle keeps ownership.
- Errors :: none.

### CppCore/rgpot/Potential.hpp: rgpot::PotentialBase

#### `rgpot::PotentialBase`

```cpp
explicit PotentialBase(PotType inp_type);
```

- Inputs :: `inp_type`, the `PotType` of the potential.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the abstract base of every potential.
  Its pure virtual `operator()` takes positions (n x 3 `AtomMatrix`), atomic
  numbers and a 3 x 3 cell, and returns energy, forces (n x 3) and variance.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::PotentialBase::caps`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] virtual PotCaps caps() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a `PotCaps` with the reentrancy, per-image, batched, periodic,
  group-collective, stress, analytic-HVP, analytic-Hessian, dual-number Hessian
  and dual-number HVP flags; the default is a value-initialised `PotCaps`
  (`SharedInstance`, periodic, nothing else set).
- Errors :: none; the method is `noexcept`.

#### `rgpot::PotentialBase::hessianVectorImpl`

```cpp
virtual void hessianVectorImpl(const ForceInput &, const double *,
                               double *) const;
```

- Inputs :: `in` and `direction`, with `3 * in.nAtoms` Cartesian entries.
- Units :: the energy Hessian times a direction, so eV/Angstrom when the
  coordinates and direction are in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: `product` receives `H direction`.
- Errors :: the base throws `std::runtime_error`.
  Potentials whose `caps().analyticHvp` is true override this method.

#### `rgpot::PotentialBase::hessianImpl`

```cpp
virtual void hessianImpl(const ForceInput &, double *) const;
```

- Inputs :: `in`, a geometry of `in.nAtoms` atoms.
- Units :: the energy Hessian, eV/Angstrom^2 when the coordinates are in
  Angstrom.
- Outputs :: `hessian` receives the dense `3 * in.nAtoms` by `3 * in.nAtoms`
  matrix, row-major, with coordinate `3 * i + k` for axis `k= of atom =i`.
  It is written symmetric.
- Errors :: the base throws `std::runtime_error`.
  Potentials whose `caps().analyticHessian` is true override this method.

#### `rgpot::PotentialBase::hessianAdImpl`

```cpp
virtual void hessianAdImpl(const ForceInput &, double *) const;
```

- Inputs :: as for `hessianImpl`.
- Units :: as for `hessianImpl`.
- Outputs :: the dense Hessian of `hessianImpl`, computed by evaluating the
  energy kernel on dual numbers instead of from closed-form derivatives.
- Errors :: the base throws `std::runtime_error`.
  Potentials whose `caps().adHessian` is true override this method.

#### `rgpot::PotentialBase::hessianVectorAdImpl`

```cpp
virtual void hessianVectorAdImpl(const ForceInput &, const double *,
                                 double *) const;
```

- Inputs :: as for `hessianVectorImpl`.
- Units :: as for `hessianVectorImpl`.
- Outputs :: `product` receives `H direction`, computed by evaluating the energy
  kernel on dual numbers.
- Errors :: the base throws `std::runtime_error`.
  Potentials whose `caps().adHvp` is true override this method.

#### `rgpot::PotentialBase::forceBatch`

```cpp
virtual void forceBatch(const ForceBatch & /*batch*/);
```

- Inputs :: a `ForceBatch` of independent systems.
- Units :: none in the base.
- Outputs :: none in the base; `rgpot::Potential::forceBatch` overrides it.
- Errors :: the base implementation throws `std::runtime_error`
  ("PotentialBase::forceBatch called directly").

#### `rgpot::PotentialBase::paramsKey`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] virtual uint64_t paramsKey() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a 64-bit fingerprint of the parameter set, mixed into the
  result-cache key; the default is 0.
- Errors :: none; the method is `noexcept`.

#### `rgpot::PotentialBase::setCache`

```cpp
virtual void setCache(rgpot::cache::PotentialCache * /*c*/);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::cache::PotentialCache` pointer.

- Outputs :: none in the base; `rgpot::Potential::setCache` overrides it.
