### CppCore/rgpot/Potential.hpp: rgpot::Potential

#### `rgpot::Potential`

- Inputs :: the template argument `Derived`, the concrete potential; the
  constructor is inherited from `PotentialBase` and takes a `PotType`.
- Units :: those of `Derived`; the built-in potentials use Angstrom, eV and
  eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a CRTP base whose `operator()` flattens the positions and cell,
  calls `forceImpl` with zeroed outputs, counts the force call, and returns
  energy, forces (n x 3) and variance.
  With `RGPOT_HAS_CACHE` and a cache set, `operator()` returns a cached result
  when the key matches.
- Errors :: `operator()` propagates any exception from `forceImpl`.

#### `rgpot::Potential::forceImpl`

```cpp
virtual void forceImpl(const ForceInput &in, ForceOut *out) const = 0;
```

- Inputs :: `in.nAtoms`; `in.pos`, 3*n doubles row-major; `in.atmnrs`, n atomic
  numbers; `in.box`, 9 doubles, cell vectors as rows.
- Units :: those of `Derived`; built-in potentials take Angstrom and write eV,
  eV/Angstrom and, for stress, eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: `out->F`, 3*n force doubles row-major; `out->energy`;
  `out->variance`; `out->stress`, 9 doubles row-major xx..zz; `out->has_stress`,
  0 when no stress was computed.
  `operator()` and `forceBatch` pass `out` zeroed.
- Errors :: defined by each potential; an override may throw with `out` partly
  written.

#### `rgpot::Potential::forceBatchImpl`

```cpp
virtual void forceBatchImpl(const ForceBatch &batch) const;
```

- Inputs :: `batch`, `batch.nSystems` systems with parallel arrays `batch.in`
  and `batch.out`.
- Units :: as `forceImpl`.
- Outputs :: fills `batch.out[i]` from `batch.in[i]` for every i.
  The default calls `forceImpl` once per system.
  A potential whose `caps().reentrancy` is `Reentrancy::SharedInstance`, and
  whose caps do not set `perImageInstances` or `groupCollective`, spreads those
  systems across the threads `OMP_NUM_THREADS` requests when `teamSize` would
  leave every system on one thread.
  The counts are the potential's `kTeamMinAtoms` and `kTeamFrom`, or
  `rgpot::kTeamMinAtoms` when it publishes neither, and a call already inside a
  team does not spread.
  One requested thread, one system, or any system that would open a team keeps
  the serial loop, so that system can take the team itself.
  Each system is evaluated whole, and the bits match that loop.
  Any other potential keeps the serial loop, so per-instance scratch is not
  shared.
- Errors :: the default propagates an exception from `forceImpl`.
  When several slices run, the exception from the lowest numbered slice is the
  one rethrown, after the team joins.

An override must treat the systems as independent and set `caps().batched`.

#### `rgpot::Potential::forceBatch`

```cpp
void forceBatch(const ForceBatch &batch) override;
```

- Inputs :: `batch`; each `batch.out[i].F` must have room for 3 *
  `batch.in[i].nAtoms` doubles.
- Units :: as `forceImpl`.
- Outputs :: `batch.out[i]` for every system.
  Every slot is zeroed first.
  With `RGPOT_HAS_CACHE` and a cache set, hits are served from the cache and
  only the misses reach `forceBatchImpl`.
  The lookup and the miss batch are built on the calling thread.
- Errors :: propagates any exception from `forceBatchImpl`; the slots stay
  zeroed or partly written.

#### `rgpot::Potential::setCache`

```cpp
void setCache(rgpot::cache::PotentialCache *c) override;
```

- Inputs :: `c=, a =rgpot::cache::PotentialCache` pointer, or `nullptr` to stop
  caching.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; stores `c= for =operator()` and `forceBatch`.
  The caller keeps ownership.
- Errors :: none.

Declared only when `RGPOT_HAS_CACHE` is defined.

### CppCore/rgpot/ForceStructs.hpp

#### `rgpot::ForceInput`

- Inputs :: four fields, all `const`, so the struct is filled by aggregate
  initialisation: `nAtoms` (`size_t`), the atom count n; `pos`
  (`const double *`), 3*n positions, row-major xyz per atom; `atmnrs`
  (`const int *`), n atomic numbers; `box` (`const double *`), 9 doubles, the
  three cell vectors as rows (ax ay az bx by bz cx cy cz).
- Units :: `pos` and `box` in the length unit of the potential (Angstrom for the
  built-in potentials); `nAtoms` and `atmnrs` have none.
- Outputs :: none; the struct borrows the caller's arrays and owns nothing.
- Errors :: none; the struct is plain data and nothing is checked.

#### `rgpot::ForceOut`

- Inputs :: `F= (=double *`), a caller-owned buffer with room for 3*n doubles.
- Units :: `F` in the force unit of the potential
  (eV/Angstrom for the built-in potentials); `energy` in its energy unit (eV); `stress` in energy per length cubed (eV/Angstrom^3);
  `variance` as the potential reports it.
- Outputs :: `F=, 3*n forces row-major like the positions; =energy` (`double`);
  `variance` (`double`), 0 when unused; `stress` (`double[9]`), the Cauchy
  stress row-major xx xy xz yx yy yz zx zy zz; `has_stress` (`int`), 0 when the
  potential did not compute stress.
- Errors :: none; the struct is plain data.

Potentials that write stress set `caps().stress`.

#### `rgpot::ForceBatch`

- Inputs :: `nSystems` (`size_t`), the number of systems; `in`
  (`const ForceInput *`), `nSystems` inputs; `out` (`ForceOut *`), `nSystems`
  result slots, where `out[i]` belongs to `in[i]` and `out[i].F` has room for 3 *
  `in[i].nAtoms` doubles.
- Units :: as `ForceInput` and `ForceOut`.
- Outputs :: none; the caller owns both arrays and every buffer they point at.
- Errors :: none; the struct is plain data.

The systems are independent: each has its own atom count, cell and species.

### CppCore/rgpot/pot_caps.hpp

#### `rgpot::Reentrancy`

- Inputs :: none; an `enum class` with `uint8_t` storage.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: one of three values: `SharedInstance`, one instance may be called
  from many threads at once; `PerInstance`, concurrent evaluation needs one
  instance per thread; `ProcessSerial`, all evaluations in the process must be
  serialised, whatever the instance count.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::PotCaps`

- Inputs :: none; a struct of fields with default member initialisers.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `reentrancy` (`Reentrancy`, default `SharedInstance`);
  `perImageInstances` (`bool`, default false), callers should clone one instance
  per NEB image; `batched` (`bool`, default false), the potential overrides
  `forceBatchImpl`; `periodic` (`bool`, default true), the kernel supports
  periodic boundaries; `groupCollective` (`bool`, default false), every rank of
  a calculator group enters each force call together, so the result cache
  decides hit or miss jointly over the group; `stress` (`bool`, default false),
  `forceImpl` writes the Cauchy stress for a positive cell volume.
- Errors :: none.

`rgpot::PotentialBase::caps` returns this struct.

### CppCore/rgpot/pot_types.hpp

#### `rgpot::PotType`

- Inputs :: none; an `enum class` with one enumerator per potential kind.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `UNKNOWN` (0), `CuH2`, `LJ`, `XTB`, `TBLite`, `Metatomic`,
  `NWChem`, `CPMD`, `Morse`, `LJCluster`, `ZBL`, `SWSi`, `EDIP`, `LenoskySi`,
  `TersoffSi`, `EAMAl`, `FeHe`, `WaterH`, `D3`, `D4`, `Expr`, `Uma`, `Skala`,
  `MOPAC`, `EMT`, `EAMCell`, `TIP4P`, `SPCE`, `TIP4PPt`, `IPI`, `SuttonChen`,
  `SWSi1985`, `EAMTable`, `Lammps`, `Gromacs`, `OpenMM`, `CP2K`, `LrCoulomb`,
  `LrDispersion`, `LrNlh`, `LrSum`, `Eckart`, `MullerBrown`,
  `ModifiedMullerBrown`, `LepsHH2`, `LepsHCl2`, `LepsFH2`, `DoubleWell`,
  `CoupledProtonWell`, `CBE`, `D2`, `D2Cpmd`, numbered in that order.
- Errors :: none.

Every enumerator is declared in every build; whether the potential behind it is
compiled depends on the Meson options.
The value is part of the result-cache key, and `rgpot::PotentialBase::getType`
returns it.

### CppCore/rgpot/CalculatorGroup.hpp

A calculator is one independent evaluation, such as a NEB image or a dimer end;
the ranks of one calculator share a subcommunicator.
`librgpot` never links MPI.
The MPI side is
`librgpot_mpi`, which `bindCalculators` and `calculatorsUseMpi` load with `dlopen` on first use (Meson option `-Dwith_mpi=enabled`).
Until that library is loaded, every function below behaves as a process of one
calculator with one rank.
Running under MPI is described in [MPI](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/mpi.html).

#### `rgpot::CalculatorGroup`

- Inputs :: none; a struct of four `int` fields.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `index` (default 0), the calculator this rank belongs to, or -1
  when the bind was refused; `ranks` (default 1), ranks per calculator;
  `rank_in_group` (default 0), this rank within its calculator;
  `world_size` (default 1), the size of `MPI_COMM_WORLD`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::addCalculatorHook`

```cpp
void addCalculatorHook(CalculatorHook hook);
```

- Inputs :: `hook`, a function `int (*)(int ranks_per_calculator)` that returns
  the group index or -1 to refuse the bind.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; `hook` is called on every rank from each later
  `bindCalculators` that performs a bind.
  A hook already registered is not added twice.
- Errors :: none; a null `hook` is ignored.

#### `rgpot::bindCalculators`

```cpp
CalculatorGroup bindCalculators(int ranks_per_calculator);
```

- Inputs :: `ranks_per_calculator`; 0 or less means one calculator for the whole
  world.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the `CalculatorGroup` of this rank, also kept for `thisCalculator`.
  With
  `librgpot_mpi` loaded it is collective on `MPI_COMM_WORLD`, calls `MPI_Init`
  when MPI is not up yet, and splits the world.
  Without it, 1 or 0 or less gives index 0 with one rank, and any other value
  gives index -1.
  Registered hooks and communicator adopters are then called; a negative result
  from any of them sets index to -1.
- Errors :: no exception; failure is reported as index -1.
  Index is -1 when the world size is not a multiple of `ranks_per_calculator` or
  is smaller than it, and when a hook or adopter refuses.
  After a bind, a call whose argument equals the stored ranks per calculator
  returns the stored group.
  Any other argument returns a group with index -1 and leaves the stored group
  unchanged.
  An argument of 0 or less is compared as its resolved value (the world size, or
  1 without MPI), so repeating `bindCalculators(0)` returns the stored group.

#### `rgpot::thisCalculator`

```cpp
const CalculatorGroup &thisCalculator();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the group stored by the last bind; a default `CalculatorGroup`
  (index 0, one rank, world size 1) before any bind.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::calculatorComm`

```cpp
int calculatorComm(void *comm_out, std::size_t comm_bytes);
```

- Inputs :: `comm_out`, storage for an `MPI_Comm`;
  `comm_bytes`, `sizeof(MPI_Comm)` on the caller.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 1 after copying the calculator's communicator into `*comm_out`; 0
  otherwise.
- Errors :: none; returns 0 without
  `librgpot_mpi`, without a split, for a null `comm_out`, or when
  `comm_bytes` differs from the library's `sizeof(MPI_Comm)`.

#### `rgpot::adoptCalculatorComm`

```cpp
int adoptCalculatorComm(CalculatorCommAdopter callback);
```

- Inputs :: `callback`, a function
  `int (*)(const void *, std::size_t, int)` that receives the address and byte size of the calculator's `MPI_Comm`,
  then the ranks per calculator; it must borrow the handle and not free it.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the result of `callback`.
- Errors :: none; returns -1 without `librgpot_mpi`, for a null `callback`,
  before a bind, after a refused bind, or without a communicator.

#### `rgpot::addCalculatorCommAdopter`

```cpp
bool addCalculatorCommAdopter(CalculatorCommAdopter callback);
```

- Inputs :: `callback`, as for `adoptCalculatorComm`; its code must stay loaded
  for the life of the process.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `true` when registered.
  Before a bind the callback is queued for `bindCalculators`; after a bind it is
  called at once with the existing communicator.
  A callback already registered is not added twice.
- Errors :: no exception; returns `false` for a null `callback` or after a
  refused bind.
  When the immediate call after a bind returns a value other than the group
  index, the stored index becomes -1 and the result is `false`.

Every rank must register the same callbacks in the same order.
Registration does not load MPI.

#### `rgpot::calculatorsUseMpi`

```cpp
int calculatorsUseMpi();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 1 when
  `librgpot_mpi` is loaded (it loads it if needed) and `MPI_Initialized` reports
  MPI up; else 0.
- Errors :: none; a failed load returns 0, with the reason in
  `calculatorMpiLoadError`.

#### `rgpot::loadCalculatorMpi`

```cpp
int loadCalculatorMpi(const char *path = nullptr);
```

- Inputs :: `path`, the library file to open, or `nullptr` (or an empty string)
  to try in order: the `RGPOT_MPI_LIBRARY` environment variable,
  `librgpot_mpi.so.3` (`librgpot_mpi.3.dylib` on macOS) in the directory of
  `librgpot`, then that name through the dynamic linker's search path.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 1 when the MPI side is available, also when it was loaded already;
  else 0.
  The library stays loaded for the life of the process.
- Errors :: none thrown; returns 0 when no candidate opens, lacks the
  `rgpot_mpi_api_v1` symbol, or has an incompatible ABI version, and on Windows.
  The reason is kept for `calculatorMpiLoadError`.

#### `rgpot::calculatorMpiLoaded`

```cpp
int calculatorMpiLoaded();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 1 once `librgpot_mpi` is loaded in this process, else 0.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::calculatorMpiLoadError`

```cpp
std::string calculatorMpiLoadError();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the reason the last `loadCalculatorMpi` failed; empty after a
  success or before any attempt.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::calculatorWorldSize`

```cpp
int calculatorWorldSize();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the `MPI_COMM_WORLD` size recorded by `bindCalculators`, also after
  a refused split; 1 before a bind.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::calculatorCount`

```cpp
int calculatorCount();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the number of calculators, world size divided by ranks per
  calculator; 1 before a bind and after a refused one.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::shareFromCalculator`

```cpp
int shareFromCalculator(int owner, void *data, std::size_t bytes);
```

- Inputs :: `owner`, a calculator index from 0 to `calculatorCount()` - 1;
  `data`, `bytes` bytes, read on the first rank of `owner` and written on every
  other rank.
- Units :: none; the data is copied as raw bytes.
- Outputs :: 1 once every rank of `MPI_COMM_WORLD` holds the bytes of `owner`; 0
  otherwise.
  With more than one rank it is collective on `MPI_COMM_WORLD`.
- Errors :: returns 0 without `librgpot_mpi`, before a bind, after a refused
  bind, for a null `data` with nonzero `bytes`, or for an out-of-range `owner`
  in a single process.
  With more than one rank, when any rank has one of those problems or the ranks
  disagree on `owner` or `bytes`, every rank prints the reason to stderr and
  `MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1)` runs.

#### `rgpot::finalizeMpiAtExit`

```cpp
void finalizeMpiAtExit();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; registers, once per process, an exit handler.
  The handler calls
  `MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1)` when `abortMpiAtExit` was called, otherwise `MPI_Finalize`
  when `bindCalculators` called `MPI_Init` and MPI is not yet finalized.
- Errors :: none; a no-op without `librgpot_mpi`.

#### `rgpot::abortMpiAtExit`

```cpp
void abortMpiAtExit();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; sets a process-wide flag that the `finalizeMpiAtExit` handler
  reads.
- Errors :: none; harmless without MPI.

A backend calls it before throwing out of a failed engine call, so the other
ranks are not left waiting in a collective.

#### `rgpot::mpiAbortRequested`

```cpp
bool mpiAbortRequested();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `true` once `abortMpiAtExit` was called in this process.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::calculatorAgree`

```cpp
int calculatorAgree(unsigned char *flags, std::size_t n);
```

- Inputs :: `flags`, `n` bytes, each read as a boolean; every rank of the
  calculator must pass the same `n`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 1 after replacing `flags` in place with their logical AND over the
  ranks of this calculator; 0 with `flags` untouched.
  It is collective on the calculator's communicator; other calculators take no
  part.
- Errors :: none; returns 0 without `librgpot_mpi`, when MPI is not initialized
  or already finalized, before a split, after a refused bind, or for a
  calculator of one rank.

#### `rgpot::publishCalculatorError`

```cpp
void publishCalculatorError(const std::string &message);
```

- Inputs :: `message`, empty for success; every rank of the calculator calls it
  at the end of a `groupCollective` force call.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none when no rank has a message.
- Errors :: when any rank has a message, every message (at most 512 bytes each)
  is printed to stderr on every rank of the calculator and
  `MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1)` runs.
  Without a split, or for a calculator of one rank, a non-empty message prints
  and aborts.
  A rank with a message that waits more than 10 seconds for the exchange aborts
  on its own.
  Without `librgpot_mpi`, or when MPI is not initialized, it returns and the
  caller's exception carries the message.

### Example

The build in this tree is configured with `with_rust_core` off, so the
`rgpot-core` symbols that the handles call are not linked; the example is only
compiled.

```cpp
#include <cstdio>

#include "rgpot/LennardJones/LJPot.hpp"
#include "rgpot/rgpot.hpp"

int main() {
  rgpot::LJPot lj;
  auto pot = rgpot::PotentialHandle::from_impl(lj);

  double pos[] = {0, 0, 0, 1.1, 0, 0};
  int atm[] = {1, 1};
  double box[] = {10, 0, 0, 0, 10, 0, 0, 0, 10};
  rgpot::InputSpec input(2, pos, atm, box);

  try {
    rgpot::CalcResult result = pot.calculate(input);
    std::vector<double> forces = result.forces_vec();
    std::printf("E = %.6f, Fx0 = %.6f\n", result.energy(), forces[0]);
  } catch (const rgpot::Error &e) {
    std::printf("%s\n", e.what());
    return 1;
  }
  return 0;
}
```

---

# C++ potentials

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/cpp_potentials.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/cpp_potentials.html

Every potential derives from `rgpot::Potential<Derived>`, which derives from
`rgpot::PotentialBase`.
Energies are eV, lengths are Angstrom and forces are eV/Angstrom unless an entry
says otherwise.
This page lists the constructors, their configuration structs and the members
each class adds.
The members every potential inherits (`forceImpl`, `forceBatch`, `caps`,
`setCache`, ...) are on [C++ API](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/cpp_api.html).
How the classes fit together is on [Architecture](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/architecture.html).

### CppCore/rgpot/Models/ModelPots.hpp: analytic models

#### `rgpot::AnalyticModelPot`

The common `rgpot::Potential` implementation for Eckart, Muller-Brown, modified
Muller-Brown, LEPS H + H2 / H + Cl2 / F + H2, the generic quartic double well
and the coupled proton well.
Forces are minus the energy gradient; all models advertise and implement an
exact Hessian-vector product.

- Inputs :: constructed through one of its concrete model classes.
- Units :: the non-LEPS constructors use eV and Angstrom.
  LEPS evaluates the published hartree/bohr formulas and converts at the rgpot
  boundary.
- Outputs :: a built-in potential with energy, force and analytic HVP calls.
- Errors :: model-specific invalid parameters and nondifferentiable LEPS
  geometries throw.

#### `rgpot::MullerBrownConfig`

- Inputs :: six four-entry arrays: `amplitude`, `a=, =b`, `c=, =x0` and `y0`.
  They default to the published parameters.
- Units :: reduced energy and coordinate units.
  The rgpot boundary carries them as eV and Angstrom.
- Outputs :: constructor settings for `MullerBrownPot`.
  It is the standard Muller-Brown surface on the first atom's x and y.
  The first atom's z force and all coordinates of later atoms have zero force.
  The product hook is the analytic Hessian-vector product.
- Errors :: a non-finite parameter throws `std::invalid_argument`.

Parameter source: Müller and Brown, Theoretica Chimica Acta 53, 75-93 (1979),
doi:10.1007/BF00547608.

#### `rgpot::AnalyticModelPot::dimensions`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] std::size_t dimensions() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the natural coordinate count, including counts not divisible by
  three.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::AnalyticModelPot::evaluateCoordinates`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] ModelEvaluation
evaluateCoordinates(std::span<const double> coordinates,
                    std::span<const double> direction) const;
```

- Inputs :: natural coordinates and a same-sized direction.
- Units :: Angstrom for coordinates and direction; eV for energy.
- Outputs :: energy, the energy gradient, and the analytic product
  `H direction`.
- Errors :: throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for a wrong coordinate count or an invalid model parameter, and `std::domain_error`
  at a nondifferentiable LEPS geometry.

#### `rgpot::ModelEvaluation`

- Inputs :: none; a struct returned by `evaluateCoordinates`.
- Units :: as the model: eV for `energy`, eV/Angstrom for `gradient` and eV
  Angstrom^-2 times the direction for `product`.
- Outputs :: `energy`, `gradient` (the energy gradient, one entry per natural
  coordinate) and `product` (the Hessian-vector product for the direction that
  was passed).
- Errors :: none.

The concrete model classes share the force convention of `AnalyticModelPot`.
The natural coordinates are the first `dimensions()` doubles of
`ForceInput.pos`.
`F` is the negative gradient in those entries and zero in the rest of the 3 *
`nAtoms` carrier, so the carrier must hold at least `dimensions()` doubles or
the call throws `std::invalid_argument`.
`caps()` reports a non-periodic potential with an analytic Hessian-vector
product.

#### `rgpot::EckartPot`

```cpp
explicit EckartPot(double v0 = 1.0, double width = 1.0);
```

- Inputs :: `v0`, the barrier height in eV, and `width`, the length scale in
  Angstrom.
- Units :: eV and Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the one-dimensional barrier V(x) = v0 sech^2(x / width).
  The potential type is `PotType::Eckart`.
- Errors :: a zero `width` throws `std::invalid_argument` when the model is
  evaluated.

#### `rgpot::MullerBrownPot`

```cpp
MullerBrownPot();
explicit MullerBrownPot(MullerBrownConfig config);
```

- Inputs :: none for the default constructor, or a `MullerBrownConfig` for the
  explicit constructor.
- Units :: eV and Angstrom, as the constants are written in the source.
- Outputs :: the two-dimensional surface V(x, y) = sum_i A_i
  exp(a_i (x - x0_i)^2 + b_i (x - x0_i)(y - y0_i) + c_i (y - y0_i)^2) over four
  terms with A = (-200, -100, -170, 15), a = (-1, -1, -6.5, 0.7), b = (0, 0, 11,
  0.6), c = (-10, -10, -6.5, 0.7), x0 = (1, 0, -0.5, -1) and y0 = (0, 0.5, 1.5,
  1).
  The potential type is `PotType::MullerBrown`.
- Errors :: a coordinate count other than 2 throws `std::invalid_argument`.

#### `rgpot::ModifiedMullerBrownPot`

```cpp
explicit ModifiedMullerBrownPot(double amplitude = 9.0, double waveNumber = 5.0);
```

- Inputs :: `amplitude`, the height of a ripple, and `waveNumber`, its spatial
  frequency in cycles per Angstrom.
- Units :: eV and Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the Muller-Brown surface plus the ripple amplitude * sin(2 pi
  waveNumber x) sin(2 pi waveNumber y).
  The potential type is `PotType::ModifiedMullerBrown`.
- Errors :: a coordinate count other than 2 throws `std::invalid_argument`.

#### `rgpot::LepsSystem`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `HH2`, `HCl2` and `FH2`, which select the three Morse curves of
  `LepsPot`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::LepsPot`

```cpp
explicit LepsPot(LepsSystem system);
```

- Inputs :: `system`.
- Units :: the potential evaluates the published formulas in Hartree and Bohr
  and converts coordinates, energy, gradient and product at the rgpot boundary,
  so the caller uses Angstrom and eV.
- Outputs :: the London-Eyring-Polanyi-Sato surface of three atoms, nine
  coordinates ordered atom by atom, with E = sum_p Q_p - sqrt(sum_p J_p^2 -
  J_1 J_2 - J_2 J_3 - J_3 J_1) over the pairs (0, 1), (1, 2) and (0, 2).
  Each pair has a Morse curve (De, re, exponent, Sato parameter S): Q = (De / 2)
  [(t^2 - 2t) / (1 + S) + (t^2 + 2t) / (1 - S)] and J the half difference of the
  same two terms, with t = exp(-exponent (r - re)).
  The potential types are `PotType::LepsHH2`, `LepsHCl2` and `LepsFH2`.
  Atom 0 is the single atom of H + H2, H + Cl2 and F + H2 for `HH2`, `HCl2` and
  `FH2`: atom 0 is the first H, a hydrogen and a fluorine respectively, and the
  pair (1, 2) is the diatom.
- Errors :: a coordinate count other than 9 throws
  `std::invalid_argument`; a zero bond length or a vanishing exchange root throws `std::domain_error`.

#### `rgpot::DoubleWellPot`

```cpp
DoubleWellPot(std::size_t dimensions, double v0, double x0, double omega, double coupling);
```

- Inputs :: `dimensions`, the natural coordinate count; `v0`, the barrier height
  in eV; `x0`, the well position in Angstrom; `omega`, whose square is the
  transverse force constant in eV/Angstrom^2; `coupling`, which bends the
  transverse minimum along the first coordinate.
- Units :: eV and Angstrom.
- Outputs :: V = v0 ((x_0 / x0)^2 - 1)^2 + sum_{i >= 1} (omega^2 / 2)
  (x_i - coupling x_0)^2. The potential type is `PotType::DoubleWell`.
- Errors :: zero `dimensions`, a zero `x0`, or a mismatched coordinate count
  throws `std::invalid_argument`.

#### `rgpot::CoupledProtonWellPot`

```cpp
CoupledProtonWellPot(double v0, double x0, double spring);
```

- Inputs :: `v0`, the barrier in eV; `x0`, the well position in Angstrom;
  `spring`, the transverse force constant in eV/Angstrom^2.
- Units :: eV and Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the two-dimensional surface V = v0 ((x / x0)^2 - 1)^2 + (spring /
  2) (y - x^2 / x0)^2.
The potential type is `PotType::CoupledProtonWell`.
- Errors :: a zero `x0` or a coordinate count other than 2 throws
  `std::invalid_argument`.

#### `rgpot::CBEPot`

The optional linked frontend to the CH5 2008 (H + CH4) surface, `ch52008`, of
the external `potlibc` library.

- Inputs :: exactly six Cartesian atoms ordered as required by `ch52008`.
- Units :: positions in Angstrom, energy in eV, force and HVP result in
  eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: energy, force and potlibc's analytic Hessian-vector product.
- Errors :: throws for the wrong atom count or a non-success `potlibc` status.
  It is built only with `with_cbe` / `RGPOT_WITH_CBE` and does not compile a
  local PES library: the surface is the one potlibc generates from the PotLib
  2023 deposit, loaded as a private plugin image per handle.
  It evaluates a batch of systems in one `potlibc_evaluate` call and reports
  `PotCaps::batched`; the bits equal the per-system answers. potlibc permits
  concurrent use of distinct handles and forbids overlapping calls on one
  handle.
  Each handle serializes its own potlibc calls, and `caps().reentrancy` is
  `Reentrancy::PerInstance`.

#### `rgpot::CBEPot::maxJetOrder`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] int maxJetOrder() const noexcept override;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `POTLIBC_JET_MAX_ORDER` of `potlibc`, 3.
- Errors :: none; the method is `noexcept`.

#### `rgpot::CBEPot::gradientJet`

```cpp
DerivativeReport gradientJet(std::size_t systems, std::size_t nAtoms,
                             const double *positions, const int *atomicNrs,
                             const double *boxes, const double *directions,
                             int order, double *jet) const override;
```

- Inputs :: `systems` systems of six atoms, `directions` of 18 entries per
  system and an `order` in 1 to 3.
- Units :: positions and directions in Angstrom; every block of `jet` is
  eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: `jet` receives `order * systems * 18` values laid out
  `[order][system][18]`, the exact derivatives with respect to the line
  parameter of the gradient at `positions + t * directions` (block 0 is the
  Hessian-vector product), from one `potlibc_gradient_jet` call for the whole
  batch; the returned `DerivativeReport` holds the summed operation count of
  `potlibc` and its largest magnitude in eV/Angstrom.
- Errors :: throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for the wrong atom count or an order outside 1 to 3, and `std::runtime_error`
  for a non-success `potlibc` status.

A force call takes a `rgpot::ForceInput`: `nAtoms`, `pos` (3 * nAtoms doubles, x
y z per atom, Angstrom), `atmnrs` (one atomic number per atom) and `box` (nine
doubles, one cell vector per row, Angstrom).
It writes a `rgpot::ForceOut`: `F= (3 * nAtoms doubles, same layout as =pos`,
eV/Angstrom), `energy` (eV), `variance`, and `stress` with `has_stress`. `stress` is the Cauchy stress in eV/Angstrom^3,
nine entries row-major. A potential that writes it sets `has_stress` to 1, and
to 0 when the cell volume is not positive.

The program below evaluates a Lennard-Jones dimer with the default parameters.
It links against `librgpot`.

```cpp
#include <cstdio>

#include "rgpot/LennardJones/LJPot.hpp"

int main() {
  rgpot::LJPot pot({.u0 = 1.0, .cutoff = 15.0, .psi = 1.0});
  const double pos[6] = {0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.5, 0.0, 0.0};
  const int z[2] = {18, 18};
  const double box[9] = {40.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 40.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 40.0};
  double forces[6] = {};
  rgpot::ForceInput in{2, pos, z, box};
  rgpot::ForceOut out{};
  out.F = forces;
  pot.forceImpl(in, &out);
  std::printf("energy %.6f eV\n", out.energy);
  std::printf("force on atom 1, x: %.6f eV/Angstrom\n", forces[3]);
  return 0;
}
```

### Configuration structs

Each struct is a plain aggregate with inline defaults.
Construct it with designated initializers and pass it to the constructor of its
class.

#### `rgpot::LJConfig`

- Inputs :: `u0` (well depth, default 1.0), `cutoff` (truncation distance,
  default 15.0), `psi` (zero-crossing distance, default 1.0), `switch_width`
  (width of the quintic switch that ends at `cutoff`, default 0.0, which keeps
  the shifted truncation).
- Units :: `u0` in eV; `cutoff`, `psi` and `switch_width` in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::LJPot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` when `switch_width`
  is non-zero and not in (0, cutoff]. No other field is checked.

#### `rgpot::LJClusterConfig`

- Inputs :: the fields of `rgpot::LJConfig` with the same defaults: `u0` 1.0,
  `cutoff` 15.0, `psi` 1.0, `switch_width` 0.0.
- Units :: `u0` in eV; `cutoff`, `psi` and `switch_width` in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::LJClusterPot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` when `switch_width`
  is non-zero and not in (0, cutoff]. A `cutoff` of 0 or less is accepted, and
  the pair kernel then keeps every pair, but the energy shift is computed from
  the configured value, so a `cutoff` of 0 gives an infinite energy. Give a
  positive `cutoff`.

#### `rgpot::MorseConfig`

- Inputs :: `De` (well depth, default 0.7102), `a= (range, default 1.6047), =re`
  (equilibrium distance, default 2.8970), `cutoff` (default 9.5), `switch_width`
  (default 0.0).
  The defaults are the platinum set of the header.
- Units :: `De` in eV, `a= in 1/Angstrom, =re`, `cutoff` and `switch_width` in
  Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::MorsePot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` when `switch_width`
  is non-zero and not in (0, cutoff]. No other field is checked.

#### `rgpot::ZBLConfig`

- Inputs :: `cut_inner` (where the switch starts, default 2.0), `cut_global`
  (truncation distance, default 2.5).
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::ZBLPot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws
  `std::invalid_argument` unless 0 < `cut_inner` < `cut_global`.

#### `rgpot::SuttonChenConfig`

- Inputs :: `epsilon` (default 1.0), `c= (default 34.408), =a` (default 1.0),
  `n= (repulsive exponent, default 10), =m` (density exponent, default 8),
  `cutoff` (default 40.0; 0 or less keeps every pair), `periodic` (minimum
  image, default false), `stress` (write the stress, default false).
  The defaults are the reduced platinum and gold 10-8 potential.
- Units :: `epsilon` sets the energy unit and `a= the length unit; =cutoff` is
  in the coordinate unit; `c=, =n` and `m` are dimensionless.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::SuttonChenPot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` when `n= or =m` is
  below 1, when `a= is not positive, when =epsilon`, `c= or =cutoff` is not
  finite, and when `periodic` is set with a `cutoff` that is not positive.

#### `rgpot::EAMCellConfig`

- Inputs :: none; the struct has no fields.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the argument of `rgpot::EAMPot`, whose element table is built into
  the kernel.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::EAMTableConfig`

- Inputs :: `path` (the table file, no default), `format`
  (`EAMTableFormat::Funcfl`, `Setfl` or `FinnisSinclair`, default `Setfl`),
  `periodic` (sum over periodic images, default true), `stress` (write the
  stress, default false), `skin` (Verlet skin of the potential's own pair list,
  default 1.0).
- Units :: none; the table carries its own units, eV and Angstrom for the LAMMPS
  metal files.
  `skin` is in the length unit of the table.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::EAMTablePot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` when `path` cannot be
  opened, when the file does not parse as `format`, and when `skin` is negative
  or not finite.

#### `rgpot::MEAMConfig`

- Inputs :: `library` (the LAMMPS meam library file, no default), `parameters`
  (the parameter file, empty for none), `elements` (the library entries to use,
  in the order the parameter file indexes them; empty takes the whole library),
  `atomic_numbers` (one per entry; empty reads each from the leading symbol of
  the entry name), `periodic` (count every image within reach, default true),
  `stress` (write the stress, default false).
- Units :: eV and Angstrom, as the files.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::MEAMPot`.
  See [Modified embedded-atom method](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/meam.html).
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` for a file that
  cannot be opened or does not parse.
  It throws the same for a library that lacks a requested element, for
  `atomic_numbers` without one entry per element, and for a parameter set the
  model cannot build (`ibar` 2, or `nn2` on a C11 pair).
  `forceImpl` throws it for an atom whose number no element has and for a
  singular cell.

#### `rgpot::EMTConfig`

- Inputs :: `rasmussen` (default false): true selects the Rasmussen parameter
  provider of Asap, false the Asap default provider.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::EMTPot`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::WaterConfig`

- Inputs :: `cutoff` (default 8.5), `switching_width` (default 1.0).
  The defaults are the values the eOn wrappers pass.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::TIP4PPot`, `rgpot::SPCEPot` and
  `rgpot::TIP4PPtPot`.
- Errors :: none; the constructors do not check the fields.

#### `rgpot::D3Config`

- Inputs :: `damping` (`D3Damping::BJ`, the rational damping, or
  `D3Damping::Zero`; default `BJ`), `functional` (the s-dftd3 method key,
  default `"pbe"`), `atm` (the Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body term, default
  true).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::D3Pot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for an empty `functional`, and `std::runtime_error`
  when s-dftd3 cannot load damping parameters for it.

#### `rgpot::D2Config`

- Inputs :: `s6` (global scaling, default 1.2), `d` (steepness of the damping,
  default 20.0), `sr` (scale on the tabulated R0, default 1.1), `cutoff` (pair
  cutoff over all periodic images, default 150.0).
  The defaults are BLYP; `rgpot::d2_config_for` gives the set of another
  functional.
- Units :: `cutoff` in Angstrom; the others are dimensionless.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::D2Pot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` unless `cutoff` is
  positive and finite, `sr` is positive and finite and `s6` and `d` are finite.

#### `rgpot::D2CpmdConfig`

- Inputs :: `s6` (CPMD's `S6GRIMME`, default 1.2), `alpha` (the damping
  exponent, default 20.0), `vdweps` (default 0.01; a pair with
  \(\lvert\alpha(r/R_r-1)\rvert\ge\frac{1}{\mathrm{vdweps}}\) is dropped).
  The defaults are CPMD's for BLYP; `rgpot::d2_cpmd_config_for` gives the `s6`
  of another functional.
  `symmetry` is the `SYMMETRY` code of the CPMD run, which picks the branch of
  `pbc3`: 1 and 8 fold per axis, 2 is face centred cubic, 4 and 14 with alpha
  and beta at 90 degrees take the shear branch, 12 the monoclinic branch, and 3,
  5, 6 and 7 the nearest integer image.
  The default, `kCpmdInferSymmetry` (-1), reads the branch from the box, which
  has the shape of 14 for a cell of 12 and cannot name it.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::D2CpmdPot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` unless `s6` and
  `alpha` are finite, `vdweps` is positive and finite and `symmetry` is -1, 1 to
  8, 12 or 14 (9, 10, 11 and 13 are codes `latgen` does not build).
  A call throws `std::invalid_argument` when the box of a periodic system does
  not have the shape of the code (a cube for 1, orthogonal vectors for 8,
  `latgen`'s face centred vectors for 2, the hexagonal vectors for 4, a1 along x
  and a2 in the xy plane for 12).

#### `rgpot::D4Config`

- Inputs :: `functional` (the dftd4 method key, default `"pbe"`, `"blyp"` for
  BLYP), `charge` (total charge, default 0.0), `atm` (the many-body term,
  default true), `periodic` (pass the box as a lattice periodic along all three
  vectors, default false).
- Units :: `charge` in elementary charges.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::D4Pot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for an empty `functional`, and `std::runtime_error`
  when dftd4 cannot load damping parameters for it.
  `charge` is not checked.

#### `rgpot::lr::CoulombConfig`

- Inputs :: `method` (`CoulombMethod::Ewald`, `SPME` or `DSF`, default `Ewald`),
  `cutoff` (real-space or DSF cutoff, default 9.0), `alpha` (splitting
  parameter, default 0.30), `kmax` (Ewald reciprocal shell, default 8), `grid`
  (SPME mesh, default 32 32 32),
  `spline_order` (SPME B-spline order, default 6), `short_cutoff` (short list,
  default 4.0), `skin` (default 1.0), `periodic` (default true), `stress`
  (default true).
- Units :: `cutoff`, `short_cutoff` and `skin` in Angstrom; `alpha` in
  1/Angstrom; the others are counts or flags.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::lr::CoulombPot`.
  `stress` false skips the strain and lets the SPME mesh run in single
  precision.
- Errors :: the constructor checks no field.
  The force call throws
  `std::invalid_argument` when `cutoff` or `alpha` is not positive, when `kmax` is below 1 with `Ewald`, and when `spline_order`
  is outside 3 to 16 with `SPME`.
  SPME raises a `grid` entry below 4 to 4.

#### `rgpot::lr::DispersionConfig`

- Inputs :: `kind` (`DispersionKind::D3BJ`, `D4`, `MBD` or `QDO`, default
  `QDO`), `functional` (D3 and D4 method key, default `"pbe"`), `atm`
  (three-body term, default true), `charge` (D4 total charge, default 0.0),
  `mbd_beta` (default 0.83), `mbd_a` (default 6.0),
  `mbd_k` (Monkhorst-Pack mesh for periodic MBD, default 4 4 4), `mbd_gamma`
  (one k-point at Gamma instead of the shifted mesh, default false),
  `qdo_scale` (default 1.0), `qdo_legacy` (legacy QDO tables, default false),
  `qdo_damped` (default true), `cutoff` (pair list cutoff, default 15.0), `lib_disp2`,
  `lib_disp3` and `lib_cn` (library real-space cutoffs, default 0.0, which keeps
  the library default),
  `switch_width` (default 0.0, a hard cutoff), `short_cutoff` (default 4.0),
  `skin` (default 1.0), `periodic` (default false).
- Units :: `cutoff`, `switch_width`, `short_cutoff` and `skin` in Angstrom;
  `lib_disp2`, `lib_disp3` and `lib_cn` in bohr; `charge` in elementary charges;
  the others are dimensionless, counts or flags.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::lr::DispersionPot`.
- Errors :: the constructor checks no field.
  Invalid values surface as the errors of the force call listed under
  `rgpot::lr::DispersionPot`.

#### `rgpot::lr::NlhConfig`

- Inputs :: `cutoff` (default 2.0), `skin` (default 0.5), `switch_off` (distance
  by which the repulsion is switched off, default 1.5).
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the parameters of `rgpot::lr::NlhPot`.
- Errors :: the constructor throws
  `std::invalid_argument` unless `cutoff` > `switch_off` > 0.
  `skin` is not checked.

### Shared members

These members have the same declaration and behaviour on every class listed.
A sentence after the fields names a class whose behaviour differs in detail.

#### `.paramsKey`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] uint64_t paramsKey() const noexcept override;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::D2CpmdPot, rgpot::D2Pot, rgpot::EAMPot,
  rgpot::EAMTablePot, rgpot::EMTPot, rgpot::ExprPot, rgpot::LJClusterPot,
  rgpot::LJPot, rgpot::MEAMPot, rgpot::MorsePot, rgpot::SPCEPot,
  rgpot::StillingerWeberSi, rgpot::SuttonChenPot, rgpot::TIP4PPot,
  rgpot::TIP4PPtPot, rgpot::TersoffSiC, rgpot::ZBLPot, rgpot::lr::CoulombPot,
  rgpot::lr::DispersionPot, rgpot::lr::NlhPot
- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a 64-bit FNV-1a hash of the parameters and a kernel version,
  computed in the constructor.
  The result cache mixes it into its key.
- Errors :: none.

`rgpot::ExprPot` hashes the expression, each term name and each child's
`paramsKey`.
`rgpot::lr::CoulombPot` does not hash `stress` or `short_cutoff`.
`rgpot::lr::DispersionPot` does not hash `functional`, `periodic`,
`switch_width`, `lib_disp2`, `lib_disp3`, `lib_cn`, `mbd_gamma`, `qdo_damped`,
`short_cutoff` or `skin`.

#### `.setNeighbourMode`

```cpp
void setNeighbourMode(nlist::Mode mode) noexcept;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::EAMPot, rgpot::EAMTablePot, rgpot::LJClusterPot,
  rgpot::LJPot, rgpot::MorsePot, rgpot::StillingerWeberSi, rgpot::SuttonChenPot,
  rgpot::TersoffSiC, rgpot::ZBLPot
- Inputs :: `mode`: `nlist::Mode::Stored` keeps a Verlet list of candidate
  pairs, `nlist::Mode::Stream` walks the cells and stores no pairs,
  `nlist::Mode::Auto` (the default) stores when the index fits in the memory the
  OS reports.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: sets the mode used by later force calls.
- Errors :: none.

In `Auto`, `rgpot::MorsePot` stores from 20000 atoms up and `rgpot::ZBLPot`
stores below two million atoms.

#### `.forcePerAtom`

```cpp
void forcePerAtom(const ForceInput &in, ForceOut *out, const PerAtomOut &atoms) const;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::EAMTablePot, rgpot::LJClusterPot, rgpot::LJPot,
  rgpot::MorsePot, rgpot::SuttonChenPot, rgpot::ZBLPot
- Inputs :: `in` and `out` as for `forceImpl`; `atoms.energy` (nAtoms doubles or
  null) and `atoms.virial` (6 * nAtoms doubles or null).
- Units :: per-atom energy and per-atom virial in eV.
- Outputs :: fills `out` as `forceImpl` does, then writes the per-atom arrays.
  Each pair term goes half to each atom, and an embedding term goes to its own
  atom.
  Per-atom energies sum to `out->energy`.
  The virial order per atom is xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy.
  A null array is skipped.
- Errors :: the exceptions of the class's `forceImpl`.

`rgpot::LJClusterPot` always walks the cells here, so its energy can differ from
`forceImpl` in the last bits.

#### `.locality`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] Locality locality() const noexcept;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::EAMTablePot, rgpot::LJPot, rgpot::MorsePot,
  rgpot::StillingerWeberSi, rgpot::SuttonChenPot, rgpot::TersoffSiC
- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: `cutoff` in the length unit of the potential: Angstrom for
  `rgpot::LJPot`, `rgpot::MorsePot`, `rgpot::StillingerWeberSi` and
  `rgpot::TersoffSiC`, the unit of `a= for =rgpot::SuttonChenPot` and the unit
  of the table for `rgpot::EAMTablePot`.
- Outputs :: a `rgpot::Locality` from `CppCore/rgpot/Locality.hpp`.
  `cutoff` is the range of each site energy, `pairwise` is true when every
  energy term is a function of one pair distance, and `densities` is the number
  of values per atom that `densityStage` sums and `forceStage` reads.
  `full` asks for the full neighbour list, and `reach` is how many cutoffs of
  copies the host holds.
  `ghostReach()` is `reach` times `cutoff`, or 0 when there is no finite range.
  `forceRange()` is `cutoff` for a pairwise potential and twice `cutoff`
  otherwise; the atoms within it of an atom set the force on that atom.
  A host that evaluates its own atoms with every atom within `forceRange()` of
  them, free of periodic images, gets the forces, site energies and per-atom
  virials those atoms have in the whole system.
  With `densityStage` and `forceStage` the copies reach `ghostReach()`.
  A pair potential and a density potential set `reach` to 1 and leave `full`
  unset: the exchange of `densities` values per atom carries the second shell,
  so the copies stop at one cutoff.
  A three-body kernel sets `full` and `reach` 2, so the copies reach twice the
  cutoff and each neighbour's list can be filled.
  A `cutoff` of 0 declares no finite range.
- Errors :: none.

`rgpot::LJPot` and `rgpot::MorsePot` return their cutoff with `pairwise` set,
and 0 when the cutoff is 0 or less.
`rgpot::SuttonChenPot` and `rgpot::EAMTablePot` return their cutoff as a
many-body range with `densities` 1.
`rgpot::SuttonChenPot` returns 0 when its cutoff is 0 or less, since it then
keeps every pair.
`rgpot::StillingerWeberSi` returns `kCut * kSigma` with `full` set and `reach` 2.
`rgpot::TersoffSiC` returns the silicon outer cutoff, 3 Angstrom, with `full`
set and `reach` 2.
Both have `densities` 0, and `ghostReach()` is twice the cutoff.

#### `.densityStage`

```cpp
void densityStage(const HalfList &list, double *densities) const;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::EAMTablePot, rgpot::SuttonChenPot
- Inputs :: `list`, a `rgpot::HalfList` from `CppCore/rgpot/Staged.hpp`.
  It holds the positions and atomic numbers of the host's `nOwned` atoms
  followed by their copies, `nAtoms` in all, and a half neighbour list over the
  owned atoms in the layout of a LAMMPS `NeighList`.
  `densities` holds `locality().densities` values per atom for all `nAtoms`
  atoms, zeroed by the caller.
- Units :: positions in the length unit of the potential.
  The densities are those of the table for `rgpot::EAMTablePot` and sums of
  \((a/r)^m\) for `rgpot::SuttonChenPot`.
- Outputs :: adds the density of each listed pair to its row atom, and to the
  other atom when that one is owned or `list.newton` is set.
  Pairs beyond the cutoff are skipped, so a list built with a skin works.
  The host completes the sums before `forceStage`: with `newton` it adds the
  values of each copy into its owner, and it copies the values of each owner to
  its copies.
- Errors :: `rgpot::EAMTablePot` throws `std::invalid_argument` when a pair
  within the cutoff has an atomic number in no element line.
  `rgpot::SuttonChenPot` throws nothing.

`rgpot::LJPot` and `rgpot::MorsePot` have no densities; their `densityStage` is
listed with each class.

#### `.forceStage`

```cpp
void forceStage(const HalfList &list, const double *densities, double *forces,
                StageTally *tally) const;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::EAMTablePot, rgpot::LJPot, rgpot::MorsePot,
  rgpot::SuttonChenPot
- Inputs :: `list` as for `.densityStage`, and `densities` after the host
  completed them; the pair potentials do not read `densities`.
  `forces` holds 3 * nAtoms doubles, and `tally` is a `rgpot::StageTally` or
  null.
- Units :: the units of `forceImpl`.
- Outputs :: adds the force of each listed pair to its row atom, and the
  opposite force to the other atom when that one is owned or `list.newton` is
  set.
  The many-body potentials take the embedding derivative of both atoms of a pair
  from their densities, so a copy needs the densities of its owner.
  With a tally it adds the host's share of the energy and of the virial W = -V
  sigma, in the order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy.
  That share is all of a pair that only this host lists, half of a pair that
  both hosts list, and the embedding energy of each owned atom.
  `tally->atoms` takes the per-atom split of `.forcePerAtom`; the entries of a
  copy are written only with `newton`, for the host to add to its owner.
- Errors :: `rgpot::EAMTablePot` throws `std::invalid_argument` when a pair
  within the cutoff, or with a tally an owned atom, has an atomic number in no
  element line.
  The other classes throw nothing.

`rgpot::LJPot` sets `tally->energy` to NaN when two listed atoms coincide.

#### `.listReused`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] bool listReused() const noexcept;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::EAMPot, rgpot::EAMTablePot, rgpot::LJClusterPot,
  rgpot::LJPot, rgpot::MorsePot, rgpot::SuttonChenPot, rgpot::TersoffSiC,
  rgpot::ZBLPot
- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true when the last force call kept the Verlet list, because no atom
  had moved by more than half the skin.
- Errors :: none.

#### `.retainedPairs`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] std::size_t retainedPairs() const noexcept;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::LJClusterPot, rgpot::LJPot, rgpot::MorsePot,
  rgpot::ZBLPot
- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the number of pair indices the last force call kept.
  It is 0 after a streaming call.
- Errors :: none.

`rgpot::LJClusterPot` also reports 0 after a call that took the direct all-pairs
kernel.

#### `.neighbourSkin`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] static double neighbourSkin(double cutoff) noexcept;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::MorsePot, rgpot::ZBLPot
- Inputs :: `cutoff`.
- Units :: `cutoff` and the result in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the skin added to the cutoff for a stored list, `cutoff / 5`.
  A streaming call uses no skin.
- Errors :: none.

#### `.setHeldSkin`

```cpp
void setHeldSkin(double skin);
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::TersoffSiC, rgpot::fortranpots::TersoffPot
- Inputs :: `skin`, the extra search distance of a Verlet list kept across force
  calls.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a positive skin keeps one list until an atom has moved by more than
  skin/2, or the cell or the atom count changes. 0, the default, rebuilds the
  pairs on every call.
  Each call drops the list held before.
- Errors :: throws `std::invalid_argument` when `skin` is negative or not
  finite.

`rgpot::fortranpots::TersoffPot` passes the skin to its `rgpot::TersoffSiC`, so
it applies only to calls that reach the 1989 kernel.

#### `.setNeighbours`

```cpp
void setNeighbours(std::shared_ptr<DualList> lists);
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::lr::CoulombPot, rgpot::lr::DispersionPot,
  rgpot::lr::NlhPot
- Inputs :: `lists`, a pair list with a short and a long cutoff.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: replaces the list the instance built in its constructor.
  Later force calls update and read `lists`, so several summands can share one
  list.
  The cutoffs of `lists` then decide which pairs the summand sees.
- Errors :: none; a null pointer is stored and the next force call dereferences
  it.

`rgpot::lr::NlhPot` reads the short pairs and updates the list without
periodicity.

#### `.energyAndGradient`

```cpp
void energyAndGradient(const double *positions, const int *atomic_numbers,
                       const double *box, std::size_t n_atoms, double *energy,
                       double *gradient,
                       nlist::NeighborList *neighbors = nullptr) const;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::StillingerWeberSi, rgpot::TersoffSiC
- Inputs :: `positions` (3 * n_atoms doubles, row-major), `atomic_numbers`
  (n_atoms entries), `box` (nine doubles, periodic in every direction), `n_atoms`,
  and an optional Verlet list `neighbors`.
- Units :: positions and box in Angstrom; energy in eV; gradient in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: `*energy` and `gradient` (3 * n_atoms doubles), the derivative
  dE/dx.
  The force is the negative of the gradient.
  A null `neighbors` rebuilds the pairs on every call; a list is reused while
  each atom has moved by at most half its skin and the cell is unchanged.
  That list is an `nlist::NeighborList`, which rebuilds on any cell change,
  unlike the variable-cell rule of `nlist::Builder`.
- Errors :: throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for a null `energy`, or for a null `positions`, `box` or `gradient` when `n_atoms`
  > 0.

`rgpot::StillingerWeberSi` does not read
`atomic_numbers` and also throws `std::invalid_argument` for a non-finite
position.
`rgpot::TersoffSiC` also throws
`std::invalid_argument` for a null `atomic_numbers` and for an atomic number
other than 14 or 6.

#### `.energyAndGradientBatch`

```cpp
void energyAndGradientBatch(std::size_t n_config, const double *positions,
                            const int *atomic_numbers, const double *box,
                            std::size_t n_atoms, double *energies,
                            double *gradients) const;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::StillingerWeberSi, rgpot::TersoffSiC
- Inputs :: `n_config` configurations of `n_atoms` atoms each, `positions` as
  `n_config` blocks of 3 * n_atoms doubles, one `atomic_numbers` array and one
  `box` shared by every configuration.
- Units :: positions and box in Angstrom; energies in eV; gradients in
  eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: `energies` (n_config doubles) and `gradients` (n_config * n_atoms *
  3 doubles, dE/dx per configuration).
  `n_config` of 0 returns without writing.
  When `teamSize` would leave every configuration on one thread, more than one
  thread is requested through `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, and the call is not already
  inside a team, the configurations are spread across that many threads.
  The counts are `kTeamMinAtoms` and `kTeamFrom` of the potential.
  Each configuration is evaluated whole, on its own neighbour list, and the bits
  match the one-thread loop and a fresh `energyAndGradient` of that
  configuration.
  A configuration that would open a team, or a batch that contains one, stays on
  the calling thread.
- Errors :: throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for a null `energies`, or for a null `positions`, `box` or `gradients` when `n_atoms`
  > 0, and the errors of `energyAndGradient` for each configuration.
  When several slices run, the exception from the lowest numbered slice is the
  one rethrown, after the team joins.

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const WaterConfig &config() const noexcept;
```

- Applies to :: rgpot::TIP4PPot, rgpot::SPCEPot, rgpot::TIP4PPtPot

- Outputs :: the `rgpot::WaterConfig` the instance was built with.

### Pair potentials

Each class here has a `config()` member that returns its configuration struct;
the return type differs, so each has its own entry.

#### `rgpot::LJPot`

```cpp
LJPot();
explicit LJPot(const LJConfig &c);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::LJConfig`; the default constructor uses `LJConfig{}`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: a shifted 12-6 Lennard-Jones potential.
  With `switch_width` 0 each pair energy is shifted to zero at `cutoff` and the
  force jumps there.
  A non-zero
  `switch_width` drops the shift and multiplies each pair term by a C^2 quintic switch over [cutoff - switch_width,
  cutoff].
  Pairs use the minimum image in every direction, so the call needs a cell.
  Atomic numbers are not read.
  A cutoff of 0 or less gives zero energy and forces.
  The force call writes the stress.
- Errors :: the errors of `rgpot::LJConfig`.
  The force call does not check its pointers.

Parameter source: Lennard-Jones, Proc.
R. Soc.
A 106, 463 (1924), doi:10.1098/rspa.1924.0082.
The defaults `u0` 1 and `psi` 1 are reduced units, not a fitted material.
Reference value: the unshifted pair at `r = 2^(1/6) psi` is `-u0`.
With the default cutoff of 15 the shifted dimer is -0.999999648834 eV.
`rgpot_cluster_lj` checks the unshifted minimum to 1e-12.

#### `rgpot::LJPot::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const LJConfig &config() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: as in `rgpot::LJConfig`.
- Outputs :: the `rgpot::LJConfig` the instance was built with.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::LJPot::densityStage`

```cpp
void densityStage(const HalfList &, double *) const;
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::HalfList` and a density array, as for `.densityStage`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none.
  A pair potential has no densities: `locality().densities` is 0, and the call
  writes nothing.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::LJClusterPot`

```cpp
LJClusterPot();
explicit LJClusterPot(const LJClusterConfig &c);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::LJClusterConfig`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the pair kernel of `rgpot::LJPot` with free boundaries.
  The cell is never used to fold pair vectors, and `caps().periodic` is false.
  A cutoff of 0 or less keeps every pair in the kernel, and a cutoff of 0 makes
  the energy shift infinite.
  Atomic numbers are not read.
  The force call does not write a stress.
- Errors :: the errors of `rgpot::LJClusterConfig`.
  The direct all-pairs kernel throws `std::bad_alloc` when its scratch
  allocation fails.

#### `rgpot::LJClusterPot::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const LJClusterConfig &config() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: as in `rgpot::LJClusterConfig`.
- Outputs :: the `rgpot::LJClusterConfig` the instance was built with.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::MorsePot`

```cpp
MorsePot();
explicit MorsePot(const MorseConfig &c);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::MorseConfig`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: the pair energy De [1 - exp(-a (r - re))]^2 - De, shifted to zero
  at `cutoff`.
  A non-zero `switch_width` replaces the shift by the quintic switch, as in
  `rgpot::LJPot`.
  Pairs use the minimum image in every direction on an orthogonal or sheared
  cell: a diagonal cell wraps each axis whose diagonal entry (`box[0]`,
  `box[4]`, `box[8]`) is positive and leaves non-positive axes free, while any
  non-zero off-diagonal entry uses `nlist::MinimumImage` across the 3x3 cell.
  Each distinct atom pair contributes at most one minimum image.
  That is every image inside the cutoff only while the smallest perpendicular
  face height is at least twice the cutoff.
  A narrower cell lists every image through `nlist::build`.
  A cutoff of 0 or less gives zero energy and forces.
  Atomic numbers are not read.
  The force call writes the stress.
- Errors :: the errors of `rgpot::MorseConfig`.
  On a sheared cell `nlist::MinimumImage` throws
  `std::invalid_argument` when the cell is singular or not finite and `std::overflow_error`
  when its inverse is not finite or the periodic image search bound overflows.
  The force call does not check its pointers.

Parameter source: the form is Morse, Phys.
Rev. 34, 57 (1929),
doi:10.1103/PhysRev.34.57. The defaults and the 9.5 Angstrom cutoff are the platinum set of Sheppard, Terrell and Henkelman, J. Chem. Phys. 128, 134106 (2008), doi:10.1063/1.2841941:
`De` 0.7102 eV, `a= 1.6047 per Angstrom, =re` 2.8970 Angstrom.
Reference value: the unshifted well is -0.7102 eV.
The shifted kernel at `re` is -0.710164462003 eV.

#### `rgpot::ZBLPot`

```cpp
ZBLPot();
explicit ZBLPot(const ZBLConfig &c);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::ZBLConfig`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: the universal screened nuclear repulsion.
  A polynomial between `cut_inner` and `cut_global` takes energy and force to
  zero at `cut_global`.
  Coefficients come from the atomic numbers of the call, so any atomic number is
  accepted.
  Boundaries are free: `caps().periodic` is false and the cell is not used to
  fold pairs.
  The force call writes the stress when the cell volume is positive.
- Errors :: the errors of `rgpot::ZBLConfig`.

Parameter source: Ziegler, Biersack and Littmark, The Stopping and Range of Ions
in Matter, Pergamon (1985).
`ZBLPot.cc` uses the LAMMPS metal transcription of the screening weights,
0.02817, 0.28022, 0.50986 and 0.18175.
Reference value: those four weights sum to 1, the universal function at zero
argument.
The cutoffs are eOn's defaults, 2.0 and 2.5 Angstrom.

#### `rgpot::EAMTablePot`

```cpp
explicit EAMTablePot(const EAMTableConfig &c);
EAMTablePot(const EAMTable &table, bool periodic, bool stress,
            double skin = 1.0);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::EAMTableConfig`, or a parsed `EAMTable` with the
  `periodic` and `stress` flags and the `skin` of the pair list.
- Units :: the units of the table; eV and Angstrom for the LAMMPS metal files.
  Stress in energy per length cubed of the table.
- Outputs :: the tabulated EAM or Finnis-Sinclair energy and forces.
  Each atom picks its element by its atomic number, matched against the first
  field of each element line.
  A pair counts when r is below the cutoff on the grid line of the table.
  With `stress` set the force call writes the stress.
  The force calls keep a list of the pairs within the cutoff plus `skin` while
  every atom stays within half of it, so `caps().reentrancy` is
  `Reentrancy::PerInstance`.
  See [Tabulated EAM and Finnis-Sinclair potentials](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/eam_table.html).
- Errors :: `std::invalid_argument` with a message starting `EAM table:`.
  The constructors throw it in the cases of `rgpot::EAMTableConfig`, when an
  array count or length does not match, when `skin` is negative or not finite,
  and for a negative atomic number in an element line.
  The force call throws it for an atomic number in no element line, for a
  periodic call without a cell, when the image extent on one axis would pass
  1024, when one pair would visit more than 262144 lattice shifts, when a
  fractional separation is not finite, and when the nearest integer to that
  separation plus the image extent does not fit in an `int` lattice index.

This class is built with `-Dwith_eam_table=true`.

#### `rgpot::SuttonChenPot::setPairTermLimit`

```cpp
void setPairTermLimit(std::size_t pairs) noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: `pairs`, the pair-count limit: the maximum candidate upper pairs
  (`total_up <` pairs=) for the three-phase stored OpenMP path, and the maximum
  pairs, summed over the threads of a call, whose density-pass terms the
  two-pass force pass reads back.
- Units :: none (a pair count, not a byte count).
- Outputs :: none.
  On the three-phase stored path, the candidate upper-pair count must satisfy
  `total_up <` pairs= and `pairScratchFits(total_up, atoms, scratch_avail)`, or that path is skipped before building the half-pair index when `est_half_pairs > pairs`
  and otherwise falls back to the threaded two-pass row walk.
  `pairScratchFits` checks that the per-slot vectors fit within half of
  `nlist::availableBytes()` (or allows the path when `availableBytes()` returns
  0): 69 bytes per candidate upper pair (`active` 1 byte +
  `pair_phi` 8 + `pair_force` 48 + `up_j` 4 + `lo_refs` 8), or 77 bytes with
  per-atom energies (`forcePerAtom` with `atoms.energy` non-null, where
  `pair_he` adds 8).
  Per-atom vectors (`up_off`, `lo_off`, `rho`, `weight`, `row_e`, `row_emb`, and
  `row_s` with stress) are `O(nAtoms)`, already bounded by `Neighbours::buildCells` and present as `rho_`
  and `weight_` on the two-pass path, so they are not counted against the
  pair-slot budget; the per-call scratch vectors are released when the
  three-phase call returns.
  On the two-pass path, a force call keeps `epsilon n (a/r)^n`, `m (a/r)^m` and
  `1/r^2` in `PairTerms<3>` for each accepted pair up to `pairs / lanes` per
  lane (24 bytes per pair), and the force pass computes the terms of any pairs
  past the kept room from the coordinates, with the same bits.
  The room for a two-pass call follows the pairs the previous call saw, so a
  walk whose pair count is not known in advance keeps its terms from the second
  call on.
  The default is `PairTerms<3>::kDefaultLimit` (1398101 pairs, which is 32 MiB
  of two-pass `PairTerms<3>` storage at 24 bytes per pair), and 0 skips the
  three-phase path and keeps no two-pass terms.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::EMTPot`

```cpp
EMTPot();
explicit EMTPot(const EMTConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::EMTConfig`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the effective-medium theory energy and forces of the vendored Asap
  kernel.
  The default provider covers H (1), Mg (12), Al (13), Ni (28), Cu (29), Pd
  (46), Ag (47), Pt (78) and Au (79).
  The Rasmussen provider covers Al (13), Cu (29), Ag (47) and Au (79).
  The cell is periodic in every direction.
  The kernel keeps its neighbour list for one cell and one list of atomic
  numbers, and is rebuilt when either changes.
  Below `rgpot::kTeamMinAtoms` the force path runs on one thread.
  From `rgpot::kTeamMinAtoms` up it uses OpenMP with per-atom row ownership and
  a second incoming-partner reduction pass, so energies and forces match the
  one-thread bits at 1, 2, 4 and 8 threads.
  The force call does not write a stress.
- Errors :: an element the provider does not cover, and a cell too thin for the
  kernel, throw `std::invalid_argument` with a message that starts `EMTPot:` and
  drop the cached kernel.
  The Asap `Exception` class does not derive from `std::exception` and never
  escapes; that `std::invalid_argument` is how it is reported.
  A singular or non-finite cell, and positions that are not finite, throw
  `std::invalid_argument` with a message that starts `EMTPot:` before the kernel
  runs, and keep a kernel cached by an earlier successful call.
  Zero atoms throw `std::invalid_argument`
  (`invalid parameter: nAtoms must be positive`) and keep that kernel too.
  An energy or a force that is not finite, which two atoms at one point cause,
  throws `std::domain_error` and keeps the cached kernel.
  Any other exception from the kernel drops the cached kernel and propagates.

Parameter source: Jacobsen, Stoltze and Norskov, Surf.
Sci. 366, 394 (1996), doi:10.1016/0039-6028(96)00816-3.
The numbers are the Asap tables vendored from eOn.
Reference value: the four-atom copper cluster in `EMTPotTest` is 5.129167 eV
within 5e-4, the pin from eOn `EMTCuTest`.

#### `rgpot::EMTPot::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const EMTConfig &config() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the `rgpot::EMTConfig` the instance was built with.
- Errors :: none.

### Covalent potentials

#### `rgpot::StillingerWeberSi`

```cpp
StillingerWeberSi();
```

- Inputs :: none; the parameters are the static members `kEpsilon`, `kSigma`,
  `kA`, `kB`, `kP`, `kCut`, `kLambda` and `kGamma`.
- Units :: `kEpsilon` in eV (2.16723920), `kSigma` in Angstrom (2.0951); the
  others are dimensionless.
  Energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.

  The cutoff is `kCut * kSigma`.
  Atomic numbers are not read.
  The cell is periodic in every direction.
  The force call writes the stress.
  `locality`, `densityStage` and `forceStage` evaluate one host's owned atoms on
  a full neighbour list; see those entries.
  This is not the kernel behind `PotType::SWSi`; see `rgpot::fortranpots::SWPot`
  and [Stillinger-Weber silicon (1985)](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/sw_si.html).
- Errors :: the force call throws `std::invalid_argument` for a null `ForceOut`,
  for a null position, cell or force buffer when `nAtoms` > 0, and for a
  non-finite position.

#### `rgpot::StillingerWeberSi::densityStage`


- Inputs :: `list` and `densities`, as for `.densityStage`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none.

#### `rgpot::StillingerWeberSi::forceStage`

```cpp
void forceStage(const HalfList &list, const double *densities, double *forces,
                StageTally *tally) const;
```

- Inputs :: `list` with `full` and `newton` set, `densities` (not read),
  `forces` of length 3 * nAtoms, and `tally` or null.
  The rows are the owned centres.
  A copy's row, when the host fills it, is that neighbour's full list and is not
  a centre.
- Units :: the units of `forceImpl`.
- Outputs :: adds the forces of each owned centre.
  A two-body term on the full list is counted from the atom whose partner sits
  strictly above it in z, then y, then x, the tie break `pair_sw` uses when two
  tags match, so exactly one host counts the pair.
  A three-body term is counted at each owned centre.
  Pairs at or beyond `kCut * kSigma` are skipped, so a list built out to
  `ghostReach()` works.
  With a tally the host's energy is added, and the virial W = -dE/dε is added in
  the order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy.
  Forces written on copies are for the host to add back to their owners.
  `Staged3BodyTest` splits a periodic silicon cell into 2, 4 and 8 slabs, and
  repeats the check on a triclinic cell and on a slab thinner than two cutoffs.
  The owned energies, the forces after that reverse sum, and the virial match
  `forceImpl` to a relative tolerance of 1e-10.
- Errors :: throws `std::invalid_argument` when the list is not full, when
  `newton` is off, when a buffer or a neighbour row is null and the host has
  atoms, and when a position is not finite.
  An empty host returns without reading the buffers.

  1990 erratum.

  carbide.
  The taper runs from 2.7 to 3.0 Angstrom for silicon and from 1.8 to 2.1
  Angstrom for carbon; a mixed pair takes the geometric mean of each.
  The cell is periodic in every direction.
  The force call writes the stress.
  `locality`, `densityStage` and `forceStage` evaluate one host's owned atoms on
  a full neighbour list; see those entries.
  See [Tersoff Si-C](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/tersoff_sic.html).
- Errors :: the force call throws `std::invalid_argument` for a null `ForceOut`,
  for a null position, atomic number, cell or force buffer when `nAtoms` > 0,
  and for an atomic number other than 14 or 6.

#### `rgpot::TersoffSiC::forceStage`

```cpp
void forceStage(const HalfList &list, const double *densities, double *forces,
                StageTally *tally) const;
```

- Inputs :: `list` with `full` and `newton` set, `densities` (not read),
  `forces` of length 3 * nAtoms, and `tally` or null.
  The rows are the owned centres.
  A copy's row, when the host fills it, is that neighbour's full list and is not
  a centre.
  Atomic numbers are read for every atom, copies included.
- Units :: the units of `forceImpl`.
- Outputs :: adds the forces of each owned centre.
  Every directed bond is kept: the 1989 sum already carries the one half, and
  the partner's owner counts the bond that leaves the partner.
  Pairs at or beyond the silicon outer cutoff, and pairs beyond a pair's own
  outer cutoff, are skipped, so a list built out to `ghostReach()` works.
  With a tally the host's energy is added, and the virial W = -dE/dε is added in
  the order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy.
  Forces written on copies are for the host to add back to their owners.
  `Staged3BodyTest` splits a periodic silicon carbide cell into 2, 4 and 8
  slabs, and repeats the check on a triclinic cell and on a slab thinner than
  two cutoffs.
  The owned energies, the forces after that reverse sum, and the virial match
  `forceImpl` to a relative tolerance of 1e-10.
- Errors :: throws `std::invalid_argument` when the list is not full, when
  `newton` is off, when a buffer or a neighbour row is null and the host has
  atoms, and when an atomic number is other than 14 or 6.
  An empty host returns without reading the buffers.

### Water

Parameter source: TIP4P is Jorgensen et al., J. Chem.
Phys. 79, 926 (1983), doi:10.1063/1.445869. SPC/E is Berendsen, Grigera and
Straatsma, J. Phys.
Chem. 91, 6269 (1987),
doi:10.1021/j100308a038, made flexible by Amira, Spangberg and Hermansson, Chem. Phys. 303, 327 (2004), doi:10.1016/j.chemphys.2004.04.024.
The platinum-water terms are Zhu and Philpott, J. Chem.
Phys. 100, 6961 (1994), doi:10.1063/1.467012; the water is the flexible SPC/E
model with the CCL intramolecular terms.
The cutoff 8.5 Angstrom and the switching width 1.0 Angstrom are what the eOn
wrappers pass.
Reference value: `WaterPotTest` pins one distorted TIP4P molecule at
0.141344038570 eV.

The three water classes take a `rgpot::WaterConfig`.
The cell is periodic and only its diagonal is used.
Energy is eV and forces are eV/Angstrom; no class writes a stress.

#### `rgpot::TIP4PPot`

```cpp
TIP4PPot();
explicit TIP4PPot(const WaterConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::WaterConfig`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: flexible TIP4P water.
  For N molecules the first 2N atoms are the hydrogens, two per molecule in
  molecule order, and the last N atoms are the oxygens.
  Atomic numbers are not read.
  Zero atoms give zero energy.
- Errors :: the force call throws `std::invalid_argument` when the atom count is
  not a multiple of 3.

#### `rgpot::SPCEPot`

```cpp

explicit SPCEPot(const WaterConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::WaterConfig`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: flexible SPC/E water with the CCL intramolecular term, in the atom
  order of `rgpot::TIP4PPot`.
  Atomic numbers are not read.
- Errors :: the force call throws `std::invalid_argument` when the atom count is
  not a multiple of 3.

#### `rgpot::TIP4PPtPot`

```cpp
TIP4PPtPot();
explicit TIP4PPtPot(const WaterConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::WaterConfig`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: flexible SPC/E water on platinum (Zhu-Philpott).
  The hydrogens come first in pairs, then one oxygen per pair, then the platinum
  atoms.
  The leading run of atomic number 1, read two atoms at a time, sets the number

- Errors :: the force call throws `std::invalid_argument` for null atomic
