### Grimme D2

`rgpot::D2Pot` is Grimme's DFT-D2 (J. Comput. Chem. 27, 1787 (2006),
doi:10.1002/jcc.20495) written in rgpot, with no library to link:

\[
E = -s_6 \sum_{i<j} \sum_{\mathbf T} \frac{C_6^{ij}}{r_{ij,\mathbf T}^6}
\frac{1}{1 + e^{-d (r_{ij,\mathbf T} / (s_R R_0^{ij}) - 1)}},
\quad C_6^{ij} = \sqrt{C_6^i C_6^j},\ R_0^{ij} = R_0^i + R_0^j .
\]

The C6 and R0 tables, the unit conversions and the per-functional s6 and d are
those of the reference dftd3 program (V3.1, `loadoldpar` and `setfuncpar`),
which reproduces the paper for H to Xe and extends it to Rn.
In a cell, \(\mathbf T\) runs over every lattice vector that brings a pair
within `cutoff`, including the images of an atom with itself at weight one half,
so the sum is the periodic energy of any cell, sheared or not.
An all-zero box sums the pairs of the molecule.
The force call writes the stress, \(\sigma = V^{-1}\,\partial
E/\partial \varepsilon\) in eV/Angstrom^3.

The pair energy falls as \(r^{-6}\), so the lattice sum beyond \(r_c\) falls as
\(r_c^{-3}\).
The default cutoff of 150 Angstrom is where doubling it moves the energy of
liquid water (the 24-atom cubic and sheared boxes of `D2PotTest`) by less than
\(\sqrt{\epsilon}\) Hartree per atom, the gradient threshold of the s-dftd3 and
dftd4 tests:

The images come from the neighbour walk (`nlist::Walk`), which streams every
image within the cutoff, so no image list is held.
A cutoff that reaches more than `d2::detail::kMaxImagesPerAxis` (256) lattice
images along a cell vector throws `std::invalid_argument`: that many images
along each of three vectors is already of the order of 10^8 per atom pair, and a
count past the range of an `int` would otherwise wrap.
| cutoff (Angstrom) | \(\lvert\Delta E\rvert\) per atom (Ha) | max \(\lvert\Delta F\rvert\) (Ha/bohr) |
|-------------------|---------------------------------|-------------------------------|
|              37.5 | 5.1e-7                          | 2.7e-10                       |
|                75 | 6.3e-8                          | 2.0e-12                       |
|               150 | 7.0e-9                          | 4.3e-14                       |

The differences are against a 300 Angstrom sum.
The forces converge far sooner than the energy, so a relaxation or dynamics that
only needs forces can pass a smaller `cutoff`. dftd3's own `-pbc` default
(\(\sqrt{9000}\) bohr, about 50 Angstrom) leaves an energy error near 2e-7 Ha
per atom.

#### `rgpot::D2Pot`

```cpp
explicit D2Pot(D2Config cfg = {});
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::D2Config`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: the D2 energy, forces and stress, periodic or molecular.
- Errors :: the errors of `rgpot::D2Config`.
  The force call throws `std::invalid_argument` when the atomic numbers are
  missing or one is outside 1 to 86, and when a non-zero cell is singular.

#### `rgpot::D2Pot::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const D2Config &config() const noexcept { return cfg_; }
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: as in `rgpot::D2Config`.
- Outputs :: the `rgpot::D2Config` the instance was built with.
- Errors :: none.

Two free functions in `rgpot/D2Pot/D2Pot.hpp` expose the parameters.
`rgpot::d2_config_for(functional)` returns a `rgpot::D2Config` with the `s6` and
`d= dftd3 uses for a =-func` name (`b-lyp`, `b-p`, `b97-d`, `revpbe`, `pbe`,
`tpss`, `b3-lyp`, `pbe0`, `pw6b95`, `tpss0`, `b2-plyp`, `b2gp-plyp`, `dsd-blyp`,
or the aliases `blyp`, `bp86` and `b3lyp`, in any case) and the default `sr` and
`cutoff`; any other name throws `std::invalid_argument`.
`rgpot::d2_c6(z)` and `rgpot::d2_r0(z)` return the tabulated C6 (J nm^6 mol^-1)
and R0 (Angstrom) of atomic number `z= and throw =std::invalid_argument` outside
1 to 86.

### CPMD's empirical D2

`rgpot::D2CpmdPot` is the D2 term OpenCPMD adds with `VDW CORRECTION ON` and
`EMPIRICAL CORRECTION` / `ALL DFT-D2`, reproduced from the source cpmdc builds
against (OpenCPMD 062582b, `vdw` in
`src/vdw_utils.mod.F90`, the tables of `empvdwin` in `src/vdwin_utils.mod.F90` and `pbc3` in `src/pbc_utils.mod.F90`).
It exists to subtract that term from a CPMD BLYP-D2 run, for example to put
`rgpot::D2Pot` or `rgpot::D4Pot` in its place, so it keeps every CPMD detail:

- CPMD's own C6 and R0 tables (Grimme 2006, Table 1, as CPMD types them, boron's
  C6 of 3.31 included), `convfac` 17.33979 for the C6 and CPMD's bohr,
  0.529177210859, for R0, positions and cell, as cpmdc converts them.
- \(R_r = R_0^i + R_0^j\) with the paper's radii, the damping
  \(1/(1 + e^{-\alpha (r/R_r - 1)})\) with \(\alpha = 20\), and the `S6GRIMME` of CPMD's `set_s6`
  (BLYP 1.2, B3LYP 1.05, BP86 1.05, TPSS 1.0, PBE 0.75, REVPBE 1.25, PBE0 0.6).
- One image per pair, the one `pbc3` picks: per axis in an orthorhombic cell
  (off-diagonal box entries exactly zero), the nearest integer fractional shift
  otherwise, none for an all-zero box.
  This is CPMD's default single cell
  (`VAN DER WAALS SUM IN REAL SPACE OVER 1* 1* 1 CELLS`).
- A pair is dropped when
  \(\lvert\alpha(r/R_r-1)\rvert\ge\frac{1}{\mathrm{vdweps}}\), so at \(r \ge 6 R_r\)
  by default, and below 0.01 bohr; elements 87 to 99 give nothing.

The results go back to eV with rgpot's units, as cpmdc and `rgpot::CPMDPot`
convert CPMD's, so the term cancels a CPMD run's to the last bits;
`D2CpmdPotTest` matches OpenCPMD's own D2 energy and forces to 100 eps Ha and
sqrt(eps) Ha/bohr on water and methane in cubic, orthorhombic and triclinic
cells.

The minimum image has a cusp.
When a pair crosses half a cell the image on the other side takes over: the
energy is continuous, but the force on the pair changes sign, and the 6 \(R_r\)
truncation adds a step in the energy wherever a pair crosses it.
A geometry optimisation or dynamics in a cell under twice the truncation radius
sees both.
`rgpot::D2Pot` sums every image within its cutoff and has neither, so for
anything but undoing CPMD's term use it instead.

#### `rgpot::D2CpmdPot`

```cpp
explicit D2CpmdPot(D2CpmdConfig cfg = {});
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::D2CpmdConfig`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: CPMD's empirical D2 energy, forces and stress.
- Errors :: the errors of `rgpot::D2CpmdConfig`.
  The force call throws `std::invalid_argument` when the atomic numbers are
  missing or one is outside 1 to 99, and when a non-zero cell is singular.

#### `rgpot::D2CpmdPot::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const D2CpmdConfig &config() const noexcept { return cfg_; }
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the `rgpot::D2CpmdConfig` the instance was built with.
- Errors :: none.

`rgpot::d2_cpmd_config_for(functional)` returns a `rgpot::D2CpmdConfig` with the `s6` CPMD's `set_s6`
gives one of the seven names above, in any case, and throws
`std::invalid_argument` for any other.

### Dispersion libraries

`rgpot::D3Pot` needs
`-Dwith_dftd3=true` and `rgpot::D4Pot` needs `-Dwith_dftd4=true`.
Both convert positions to bohr for the library and convert the result back to eV
and eV/Angstrom.
`D3Pot` needs a non-null cell and evaluates the molecule without periodicity and
writes no stress.
`D4Pot` reads the box only when `D4Config::periodic` is set, so a molecule may
come with a null box; then dftd4 gets the box as a 3D lattice and returns its
virial, which `D4Pot` divides by the cell volume for the stress, and a null box
throws `std::invalid_argument`. dftd4 cuts the pair, three-body and coordination
sums off at 60, 40 and 30 bohr without smoothing, so a periodic energy steps
when a strain carries an image pair across one of them.
The structure is built on the first call and rebuilt when the atom count or any
atomic number changes; other calls only update the positions and the cell.

#### `rgpot::D3Pot`

```cpp
D3Pot();
explicit D3Pot(const D3Config &config);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::D3Config`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: Grimme DFT-D3 dispersion through the s-dftd3 C API.
  Parameter source: Grimme, Antony, Ehrlich and Krieg, J. Chem.
  Phys. 132, 154104 (2010), doi:10.1063/1.3382344.
  The default is rational damping, the `pbe` parameters and the three-body term.
  `D3PotTest` checks the energy against the s-dftd3 C API.
- Errors :: the errors of `rgpot::D3Config`.
  The force call throws `std::runtime_error` with the s-dftd3 message when
  building the structure or model, updating it, or computing the dispersion
  fails.

#### `rgpot::D3Pot::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const D3Config &config() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the `rgpot::D3Config` the instance was built with.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::D4Pot`

```cpp
D4Pot();
explicit D4Pot(const D4Config &config);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::D4Config`; the damping is always rational, with the
  parameters dftd4 tabulates for the functional.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: Grimme DFT-D4 dispersion through the dftd4 C API, and the stress
  when `periodic` is set; `caps()` then reports `periodic` and `stress`.
  Parameter source: Caldeweyher et al., J. Chem.
  Phys. 150, 154122 (2019), doi:10.1063/1.5090222.
  The default is rational damping, the `pbe` parameters, charge 0, the many-body
  term and a molecule without periodicity.
  `D4PotTest` checks a fresh call against a reused structure.
- Errors :: the errors of `rgpot::D4Config`.
  A periodic force call throws `std::invalid_argument` for a null box or a box
  of zero volume.
  The force call throws `std::runtime_error` with the dftd4 message when
  building the structure or model, updating it, or computing the dispersion
  fails.
- Tests :: `CppCore/tests/D4BlypTest.cc` compares BLYP against the dftd4 program
  (4.2.0, `dftd4 coord --func blyp --grad`) on a water dimer, benzene and an
  eight-water box in a cubic and a sheared cell: energies within 100 eps Ha,
  gradients within sqrt(eps) Ha/bohr and virials within sqrt(eps) Ha/bohr times
  the cube root of the cell volume.
  `scripts/regen_d4_references.py` writes the references.

#### `rgpot::D4Pot::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const D4Config &config() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: `charge` in elementary charges.
- Outputs :: the `rgpot::D4Config` the instance was built with.
- Errors :: none.

```cpp

```

- Inputs :: none.

- Errors :: none.

### Expression of potentials

#### `rgpot::ExprPot`

```cpp
ExprPot(std::string expression, std::vector<Term> terms);
```

- Inputs :: `expression`, a Lepton expression over the term names; `terms`,
  pairs of a name and a `std::unique_ptr<PotentialBase>` child.
- Units :: each name stands for its child's energy in eV.
  The energy is the value of the expression, and the forces are the sum of each
  child's forces times the derivative of the expression with respect to that
  child's energy.
- Outputs :: a potential whose energy is f(E_0, E_1, ...) over the children.
  The expression and each derivative are compiled once in the constructor.
  The variance is the sum of each child's variance times the square of its
  derivative, or 0 when any child variance is not finite.
  `caps()` is the least reentrant of the children, periodic only when every
  child is.
  The force call does not write a stress.
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` for an empty
  expression, zero terms, a name that is not a Lepton identifier, a duplicate
  name, a null child, a parse, compile or differentiation failure, a term name
  the expression does not use, and an identifier in the expression that is not a
  term name.

This class is built with `-Dwith_expr=true`.

#### `rgpot::ExprPot::expression`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const std::string &expression() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the expression string given to the constructor.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::ExprPot::dEnergyDTerm`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] double dEnergyDTerm(const std::string &name) const;
```

- Inputs :: `name`, a term name.
- Units :: none; the derivative of eV by eV.
- Outputs :: the derivative of the expression with respect to that term,
  evaluated at the child energies of the last force call.
  Before any force call the child energies are 0.
- Errors :: throws `std::invalid_argument` when `name` is not a term.

#### Term names and constructor failures

How to compose terms is in
[Compose potentials with ExprPot](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/howto/exprpot.html).

A term name must be a Lepton identifier: an ASCII letter or underscore first,
then ASCII letters, digits, or underscores.
`lj`, `morse`, and `d3` are valid.
`1lj`, `lj-x`, and `lj.x` are not.

The constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` before any force call when:

- the expression is empty or blank
- there are zero terms
- a name is not a Lepton identifier
- a name is duplicated
- a child pointer is null
- Lepton cannot parse or compile the expression
- a supplied name is missing from the expression
- an identifier in the expression has no child
- `ParsedExpression::differentiate(name)` fails

Python raises `ValueError` with the same message.

### Weighted sums

#### `rgpot::SumPot`

```cpp
SumPot();
```

- Inputs :: none; terms are added with `add`.
  Each term is a `rgpot::SumTerm`: `name` (the label in the record and the log),
  `weight` (any finite value, the sign allowed, default 1) and `enabled`
  (default true).
- Units :: the sum keeps the units of its terms: eV,
  eV/Angstrom and eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: E = sum of weight times energy over the enabled terms, and the same
  weights on the forces and the stress; the variance takes the square of each
  weight.
  A disabled term is not evaluated.
  The stress is the weighted sum when every evaluated term reports one, and
  `has_stress` is 0 otherwise or when no term ran.
  An empty sum, or one whose terms are all disabled, gives zero energy and
  forces.
  `caps()` intersects the enabled terms: periodic only when every one has it,
  stress only when at least one term is enabled and every one has it, per-image
  instances and group collectives when any one needs them, never batched, and a
  reentrancy that is the weakest of the terms and `PerInstance`, because the
  component record belongs to the instance.
  Setting `RGPOT_SUM_LOG` to anything but empty or `0` writes one line per term
  and call, and a total, to standard error.
- Errors :: a term that throws stops the call; the exception reaches the caller
  unchanged after a line naming the term is logged, so a failing child's status
  (a NumericalError, a refused geometry) is the sum's status.

#### `rgpot::SumPot::add`

```cpp
void add(std::unique_ptr<PotentialBase> term);
void add(SumTerm spec, std::unique_ptr<PotentialBase> term);
```

- Inputs :: `term`, a potential the sum takes ownership of; `spec`, its name,
  weight and switch.
  The first form names the term `term<i>` with weight 1, enabled.
- Units :: `weight` has no unit.
- Outputs :: appends the term.
  A disabled `spec` may come with a null `term`: the term is recorded, shows in
  the component record, and is never built, so switching off a DFT engine term
  does not load the engine.
- Errors :: throws `std::invalid_argument` for a null `term` on an enabled term
  and for a weight that is not finite.

#### `rgpot::SumPot::setEnabled`

```cpp
void setEnabled(std::size_t index, bool enabled);
```

- Inputs :: `index`, a term index; `enabled`, its new switch.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: switches the term on or off for the following calls.
- Errors :: throws `std::out_of_range` for an index past the last term and
  `std::logic_error` when enabling a term that was added without a potential.

#### `rgpot::SumPot::setWeight`

```cpp
void setWeight(std::size_t index, double weight);
```

- Inputs :: `index`, a term index; `weight`, its new weight.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the weight of the following calls.
- Errors :: throws `std::out_of_range` for an index past the last term and
  `std::invalid_argument` for a weight that is not finite.

#### `rgpot::SumPot::size`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] std::size_t size() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the number of terms, enabled or not.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::SumPot::term`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const SumTerm &term(std::size_t index) const;
```

- Inputs :: `index`, a term index.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the name, weight and switch of that term.
- Errors :: throws `std::out_of_range` for an index past the last term.

#### `rgpot::SumPot::child`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] PotentialBase *child(std::size_t index) const;
```

- Inputs :: `index`, a term index.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the potential of that term, owned by the sum, or null for a term
  added disabled without one.
- Errors :: throws `std::out_of_range` for an index past the last term.

#### `rgpot::SumPot::lastComponents`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const std::vector<SumComponent> &lastComponents() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: `energy` in eV, `forces` in
  eV/Angstrom (3 per atom), `stress` in eV/Angstrom^3 row-major, each the term's
  own value before its weight.
- Outputs :: one `rgpot::SumComponent` per term in the order they were added,
  from the last force call on this instance: `name`, `weight`, `enabled`,
  `evaluated` (false for a disabled term and before the first call), `energy`,
  `forces` (empty when not evaluated), `variance`, `has_stress` and `stress`.
  A call that throws keeps the record of the last successful call.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::SumPot::setLogSink`

```cpp
void setLogSink(LogSink sink);
```

- Inputs :: `sink`, a `std::function<void(std::string_view)>`.
- Units :: the lines give energies in eV and the largest force component in
  eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the per-term lines go to `sink` instead of standard error, whether
  or not `RGPOT_SUM_LOG` is set:
  `rgpot sum: NAME weight=W energy=E eV fmax=F eV/A stress=0|1`,
  `rgpot sum: NAME disabled`, `rgpot sum: NAME failed: WHAT` and
  `rgpot sum: total energy=E eV`.
  An empty sink restores the default.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::SumPot::paramsKey`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] uint64_t paramsKey() const noexcept override;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a hash of every term's name, weight, switch, and its potential's
  type and `paramsKey`, so a cache entry is not reused across a change of any of
  them.
- Errors :: none.

### Long-range summands

These classes are in namespace `rgpot::lr` and are built with
`-Dwith_long_range=true`.
Each one owns a `DualList`, a pair list with a short and a long cutoff, until
`setNeighbours` replaces it.
Periodic lists include every image inside the cutoff, including one canonical
half of an atom's interactions with its own images.
The cutoff may exceed the shortest lattice vector, including for a triclinic
cell.

#### `rgpot::lr::CoulombPot`

```cpp
CoulombPot(CoulombConfig cfg, std::shared_ptr<ChargeSource> charges,
           std::shared_ptr<ChargeResponse> response = nullptr);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::lr::CoulombConfig`; `charges` gives the per-atom charges
  and the net charge each call; `response`, when not null, adds the chain rule
  for charges that depend on positions.
- Units :: charges in elementary charges; energy in eV, forces in
  eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: electrostatics: Ewald with a conducting boundary, smooth
  particle-mesh Ewald, or the damped shifted force in the gas phase.
  `DSF` always runs without a cell and writes no stress.
  With `Ewald` or `SPME` the force call writes the stress when the cell volume
  is positive.
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` for a null `charges`.
  The force call throws `std::invalid_argument` in the cases of
  `rgpot::lr::CoulombConfig`, when a charge, the net charge or a position is not
  finite, and when the charges do not sum to the net charge within 1e-6 (1 +
  `|net charge|`).
  `FixedCharges` throws `std::invalid_argument` when its length does not match
  the atom count.

#### `rgpot::lr::CoulombPot::neighbours`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const DualList &neighbours() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the pair list the instance uses.
- Errors :: none; after `setNeighbours(nullptr)` the call dereferences a null
  pointer.

#### `rgpot::lr::DispersionPot`

```cpp
explicit DispersionPot(DispersionConfig cfg, std::shared_ptr<RatioSource> ratios = nullptr,
                       std::shared_ptr<RatioResponse> response = nullptr);
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::lr::DispersionConfig`; `ratios` gives the Hirshfeld volume
  ratio and the C6 ratio per atom, and null uses ratio 1 for every atom;
  `response`, when not null, adds the chain rule for ratios that depend on
  positions, by central differences of the energy.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: one dispersion model as an additive potential.
  `D3BJ` and `D4` need s-dftd3 and dftd4 linked into the build.
  `MBD` accepts atomic numbers 1 to 102.
  `QDO` accepts 1 to 86, or 1 to 102 with `qdo_legacy`.
  The force call writes the stress when the model reports one and the cell
  volume is positive.
- Errors :: the force call throws `std::invalid_argument` for null atomic
  numbers, for an atomic number outside the model's table, and for MBD
  parameters that are not positive.
  It throws `std::runtime_error` when the D3 or D4 library was not linked, when
  the library reports an error, when the MBD screening matrix is singular and
  when an MBD eigenvalue is negative.
  `FixedRatios` throws `std::invalid_argument` when a ratio vector does not
  match the atom count.

#### `rgpot::lr::NlhPot`

```cpp
explicit NlhPot(NlhConfig cfg = {});
```

- Inputs :: a `rgpot::lr::NlhConfig`.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: the short-range repulsion of SO3LR, a sum of exponentials times a
  screened Coulomb term, switched off by `switch_off`.
  It accepts atomic numbers 1 (H) to 92 (U).
  The list is always built without periodicity.
  Fewer than two atoms give zero energy.
- Errors :: the errors of `rgpot::lr::NlhConfig`.
  The force call throws `std::invalid_argument` for null atomic numbers and for
  an atomic number outside 1 to 92.

#### `rgpot::lr::SumPot`

- Inputs :: none to construct.
  `shareNeighbours` takes one `DualList` shared across long-range terms.
- Units :: those of `rgpot::SumPot` (eV, eV/Angstrom, eV^2).
- Outputs :: the weighted sum `rgpot::SumPot` with long-range convenience:
  `shareNeighbours` calls `setNeighbours(lists)` on every current `CoulombPot`,
  `DispersionPot` and `NlhPot` term so they reuse one pair list.
  Non-long-range terms and terms added later keep their own lists unless set.
- Errors :: the same as `rgpot::SumPot` and each child term.

### Fortran kernels

These classes are in namespace `rgpot::fortranpots` and are built with
`-Dwith_fortran_pots=enabled`.
Each has only a default constructor.
Each instance owns a Fortran workspace with its own neighbour table, kept
between calls.
A kernel failure throws `std::runtime_error` with the label of the kernel, the
status and the kernel's message.
A workspace that cannot be allocated throws `std::bad_alloc` from the
constructor.
Zero atoms give zero energy and forces.
Energy is eV and forces are eV/Angstrom.
The porting rules are on
[Fortran potentials: porting rules](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/fortran_potentials.html).

#### `rgpot::fortranpots::CuH2Pot`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the EAM potential for copper (29) and hydrogen (1) from eOn, with a
  cutoff of 6.1 Angstrom.
  The force call does not write a stress.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` for an atomic number other than 29 or 1, and
  when two atoms occupy the same position.

The form is the embedded-atom method of Daw and Baskes, Physical Review B 29,
6443 (1984), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.29.6443.
The parameters are the eOn set; this tree has no separate paper for that fit.
CuH2PotTest requires -2.7114096242662238 eV within 1e-6 for its four-atom cell.

#### `rgpot::fortranpots::EAMAlPot`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the double-exponential EAM for aluminium from eOn, with a cutoff of
  7.1 Angstrom stored as a single-precision literal.
  Atomic numbers are not read.
  The force call does not write a stress.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when the kernel or the neighbour table reports
  a failure.

The form is Daw and Baskes, Physical Review B 29, 6443 (1984),
doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.29.6443.
The parameters are the eOn set.
The four-atom `al_fcc` cluster in a 20 Angstrom cube is pinned to the EON r2549
energy -5.217864006173226 eV within 1e-12.

#### `rgpot::fortranpots::EDIPPot`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the environment-dependent interatomic potential for silicon, with a
  cutoff of 3.1213820 Angstrom.
  Atomic numbers are not read.
  The force call does not write a stress.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when the cell is thinner than the cutoff, and
  when the neighbour table reports a failure.

The potential is Bazant, Kaxiras and Justo, Physical Review B 56, 8542-8552
(1997),
doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.56.8542, with the parameters from Table I of Justo, Bazant, Kaxiras, Bulatov and Yip, Physical Review B 58, 2539-2550 (1998), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.58.2539.
Eight silicon atoms in a 20 Angstrom cube give -18.838135 eV within a relative
1e-4.

#### `rgpot::fortranpots::FeHePot`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the iron (26) and helium (2) potential from eOn, with Fe-Fe, Fe-He
  and He-He pair terms.
  The neighbour table uses the largest of its cutoffs, 5.4 Angstrom for the
  He-He pair.
  The force call does not write a stress.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` for an atomic number other than 26 or 2.

The iron part is Ackland and coauthors, Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter 16,
S2629-S2642 (2004), doi:10.1088/0953-8984/16/27/003.
A pure helium configuration reduces to an HFD-B dimer: the form is Aziz, McCourt
and Wong, Molecular Physics 61, 1487-1511 (1987),
doi:10.1080/00268978700101941, and the constants are those of Aziz, Janzen and Moldover, Physical Review Letters 74, 1586-1589 (1995), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.1586.
Sixteen iron atoms in a 20 Angstrom cube give -43.959774 eV within a relative
1e-4.

#### `rgpot::fortranpots::LenoskyPot`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the Lenosky silicon potential from eOn, with a cutoff of 4.5
  Angstrom.
  Atomic numbers are not read.
  The force call does not write a stress.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when the neighbour table reports a failure.

The potential is Lenosky and coauthors, Modelling and Simulation in Materials
Science and Engineering 8, 825-841 (2000), doi:10.1088/0965-0393/8/6/305.
Eight silicon atoms in a 20 Angstrom cube give -17.284558 eV within a relative
1e-4.

#### `rgpot::fortranpots::SWPot`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: Stillinger-Weber silicon with eOn's epsilon, 2.16826 * 1.06767385
  eV, and sigma 2.0951 Angstrom; the cutoff is 1.8 sigma.
  This is `PotType::SWSi`; `rgpot::StillingerWeberSi` carries the published
  epsilon.
  Atomic numbers are not read.
  `forceImpl` writes the stress; the batch call does not.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when the kernel or the neighbour table reports
  a failure.

The published potential is Stillinger and Weber, Physical Review B 31, 5262
(1985), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.31.5262.
This class uses eOn's rescaled epsilon.
Eight silicon atoms in a 20 Angstrom cube give -16.204955 eV within a relative
1e-4.

#### `rgpot::fortranpots::TersoffPot`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: Tersoff silicon (`PotType::TersoffSi`).
  A call where every atomic number is 14, or the atomic numbers are null, uses
  the Fortran gather with a cutoff of 3.0 Angstrom.
  Any other atomic number sends the call to `rgpot::TersoffSiC`.
  Calls with a positive cell volume write the Cauchy stress.
  A zero-atom call with a null box succeeds without stress.
  `has_stress` stays 0 and the nine entries are zero.
  A call with no atoms does the same for any box.
- Errors :: An all-silicon call with atoms and a null box throws
  `std::runtime_error` `Tersoff potential failed (status 2): rgpot_neighbors: a required neighbour pointer is null`.
  An all-silicon call with atoms and a zero-volume or non-finite box throws
  `std::runtime_error` `Tersoff potential failed (status 4): rgpot_neighbors: box must be finite, and a periodic box must have positive volume`.
  A mixed-species call with atoms and a null box throws `std::invalid_argument`
  `TersoffSiC: null cell`.
  A mixed-species call with atoms and a zero-volume orthorhombic cell leaves
  `has_stress` at 0 and the nine entries at zero.
  A mixed-species call with atoms and a singular skewed cell throws
  `std::invalid_argument` `periodic cell must be nonsingular`.
  A mixed-species call with a non-finite cell throws `std::invalid_argument`
  `periodic cell must be finite`.
  Other Fortran failures throw
  `std::runtime_error`, and the remaining `std::invalid_argument` cases of
  `rgpot::TersoffSiC` apply on that path.

The potential is Tersoff, Physical Review B 39, 5566 (1989),
doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.39.5566.
Eight silicon atoms in a 20 Angstrom cube give -17.440266 eV within a relative
1e-4.

#### `rgpot::fortranpots::WaterHPot`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: one hydrogen atom in the field of water molecules, Andersson's
  potH-H2O surface.
  Atoms are hydrogen (1) and oxygen (8): whole water molecules followed by the
  lone H as the last atom.
  Every site interacts with the lone H at its nearest periodic image; there is
  no cutoff.
  The force call does not write a stress.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` for fewer than 4 atoms, for an atomic number
  other than 1 or 8, when the last atom is not hydrogen, for no oxygen, when the
  hydrogens are not two per oxygen plus one, and when an atom coincides with the
  lone H.

The surface is Andersson, Al-Halabi, Kroes and van Dishoeck, Journal of Chemical
Physics 124, 064715 (2006), doi:10.1063/1.2162901.
No test in this tree pins an absolute energy for this class.

---

# C++ engine-backed potentials

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/cpp_backends.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/cpp_backends.html

These potentials call an external program or library: a quantum-chemistry
engine, a tight-binding library, a machine-learned model or a socket peer.
Every class derives from `rgpot::Potential<Derived>`, except the dlopen
frontends `XTBDlopen` and `MetatomicDlopen`, which have no base class and
declare `forceImpl` themselves.
The members they inherit (`forceImpl`, `forceBatch`, `caps`, the call operator)
are described with the base class; this page lists only the members each class
declares itself.
The in-process kernels are in [C++ potentials](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/cpp_potentials.html).

Unless an entry says otherwise, a class takes positions and the cell in Angstrom
(cell vectors as rows) and returns the energy in eV and the forces in
eV/Angstrom. Engines that work in atomic units get positions converted with `units::ANGSTROM_TO_BOHR`, the energy with `units::HARTREE_TO_EV` and gradients with `units::NEG_GRAD_TO_FORCE` (minus Hartree/bohr
to eV/Angstrom), all from `CppCore/rgpot/units.hpp`.

### How each class finds its engine

The dlopen frontends try a list of library names in order.
A bare name is resolved by the dynamic linker search path.
`CP2KPot`, `CPMDPot`, `MOPACPot`, `NWChemPot`, `XTBDlopen` and `MetatomicDlopen`
stop at the first library that opens and then check its symbols, so a library
with missing symbols ends the search.
`LammpsPot`, `GromacsPot` and `OpenMMPot` skip a library that lacks the symbols
and try the next name.

| Class        | Library                 | Search order                                                                                  |
|--------------|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `CP2KPot`    | `libcp2kc_rgpot`        | `enginePath`, `CP2KC_LIBRARY`, `RGPOT_CP2K_ENGINE`, `libcp2kc_rgpot.so`, `./libcp2kc_rgpot.so` |
| `CPMDPot`    | `libcpmdc`              | `enginePath`, `CPMDC_LIBRARY`, `RGPOT_CPMDC_ENGINE`, `RGPOT_CPMD_ENGINE`, `libcpmdc.so`, `./libcpmdc.so` |
| `MOPACPot`   | `libmopacc`             | `Config::engine_path`, `MOPACC_LIBRARY`, `RGPOT_MOPACC_ENGINE`, `libmopacc.so`, `./libmopacc.so` |
| `NWChemPot`  | `libnwchemc`            | `enginePath` alone when set; else the variables that are set among `NWCHEMC_LIBRARY`, `RGPOT_NWCHEMC_ENGINE` and `RGPOT_NWCHEM_ENGINE`, in that order, with no default names after them; else `libnwchemc.so`, `./libnwchemc.so` |
| `SkalaPot`   | `libnwchemc`            | as `NWChemPot`                                                                                |
| `LammpsPot`  | engine plugin           | `engine_path` alone when set; else `RGPOT_LAMMPS_ENGINE`, `LAMMPS_ENGINE`, `liblammps_engine.so`, `liblj_engine.so` |
| `GromacsPot` | `rgpot_md_native_force` | `engine_path` alone; empty means the in-process Lennard-Jones                                 |
| `OpenMMPot`  | `rgpot_md_native_force` | as `GromacsPot`                                                                               |
| `XTBDlopen`  | `libxtb_engine`         | `engine_path` alone when set; else `RGPOT_XTB_ENGINE`, `XTB_ENGINE`, `libxtb_engine.so`, then each directory of `EON_POTENTIALS_PATH` and `RGPOT_ENGINE_PATH` |
| `MetatomicDlopen` | `libmetatomic_engine` | `engine_path`, `RGPOT_METATOMIC_ENGINE`, `METATOMIC_ENGINE`, `libmetatomic_engine.so`, then each directory of `EON_POTENTIALS_PATH` and `RGPOT_ENGINE_PATH` |

After the `.so` names the CP2K, CPMD, MOPAC and NWChem lists also try the
`.dylib` names (bare and with `./`), and CPMD, MOPAC and NWChem try `cpmdc.dll`,
`mopacc.dll` and `nwchemc.dll`.
`LammpsPot` uses `.dylib` names on macOS and `.dll` names on Windows instead of
`.so`.
`XTBDlopen` and `MetatomicDlopen` try the `.dylib` name before the `.so` name on
macOS, and on Windows try `xtb_engine.dll` and `libxtb_engine.dll`
(`metatomic_engine.dll` and `libmetatomic_engine.dll`) in place of the `.so`
name.
`TBLitePot` and `XTBPot` link `libtblite` and `libxtb` at build time.
`MetatomicPot` and `UmaPot` link libtorch.
`XTBDlopen` and `MetatomicDlopen` are in every `librgpot` and need neither;
their engine libraries carry the C ABIs in
[Engine C ABI](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/engine_abi.html).
`IPIPot` opens a socket and waits for a driver.
`ORCAPot` starts the `orca` program for every force and needs no library.

None of the dlopen constructors throw when the library is missing.
They record the reason, `available()` returns false, and the first force throws
`std::runtime_error` with that reason.
The exceptions are `LammpsPot`, `GromacsPot` and `OpenMMPot` with an
`engine_path`: their constructors throw `std::runtime_error` when no library
opens.
`XTBDlopen` and `MetatomicDlopen` also throw from the constructor, so
`available()` is true for every object they construct.

### CP2K

The Quickstep method is VandeVondele and coauthors, Computer Physics
Communications 167, 103-128 (2005), doi:10.1016/j.cpc.2004.12.014.
CP2KPotFakeEngineTest does not run Quickstep.
Its surface is a spring, half k times the sum of squared displacements, in
Hartree and Bohr with k = 0.5.
On the water geometry in that test the spring is 1.8600113677425840 Hartree, so
the host energy is 50.613487749571874 eV, and the test requires a relative
agreement of 1e-12.

#### `rgpot::CP2KPot`

```cpp
CP2KPot();
explicit CP2KPot(const ::CP2KParams::Reader &params);
```

- Inputs :: optional `CP2KParams` (Cap'n Proto); the default constructor uses
  the schema defaults.
- Units :: positions and cell in Angstrom, energy in eV, forces in
  eV/Angstrom. The class converts positions and cell to bohr, and the shim's Hartree energy and Hartree/bohr
  forces back.
  The shim returns forces, so there is no sign change.
- Outputs :: a potential that runs CP2K Quickstep through the `libcp2kc_rgpot`
  shim.
- Errors :: the constructors do not throw when the shim is missing; see
  `loadError`.
  A force throws `rgpot::CP2KScfError` (a `std::runtime_error`) when the SCF
  does not converge, on every rank of the calculator.
  Any other failure throws `std::runtime_error`: shim not loaded, a bad
  `inputTemplate`, `nAtoms` of zero, a null buffer, a refused calculator
  binding, the shim refusing the deck or the orbital key, or a nonzero shim
  status.

The shim must report `cp2kc_abi_version()` equal to `CP2KC_ABI_VERSION` and
export the session functions, and `cp2kc_available()`, when exported, must be
nonzero.
The deck is rendered from the params (or from `inputTemplate`, which must
contain both `@RGPOT_COORD@` and `@RGPOT_CELL@`) on the first force and again
whenever the sequence of atomic numbers changes.
A non-empty `dataDir` sets `CP2K_DATA_DIR` before the session starts.
The build option is `-Dwith_cp2k=enabled` and it needs `-Dwith_rpc=true`.

#### `rgpot::CP2KPot::setParams`

```cpp
bool setParams(const ::CP2KParams::Reader &params);
```

- Inputs :: `params`, the next `CP2KParams`.
- Units :: as the message fields (`cutoffRy` in Rydberg); the call converts
  nothing.
- Outputs :: true when the shim is loaded and the params are usable.
  False when the shim cannot be loaded, or `inputTemplate` lacks
  `@RGPOT_COORD@` or `@RGPOT_CELL@`.
  The params are stored either way.
- Errors :: no exception of its own; failures are reported by the return value
  and `loadError`.

The live session is destroyed when the serialized params differ or `enginePath`
changes; otherwise it keeps its wavefunctions.
The shim is loaded again when it was not loaded or `enginePath` changed.

#### `rgpot::CP2KPot::getParams`

```cpp
void getParams(::CP2KParams::Builder out) const;
```

- Inputs :: `out`, a builder to fill.
- Units :: as the message fields.
- Outputs :: `out` holds every field of the stored params, including
  `enginePath`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CP2KPot::available`

```cpp
bool available() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true when the shim is loaded and the params are usable.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CP2KPot::loadError`

```cpp
std::string loadError() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: why `available()` is false: the shim load error when the shim is
  not loaded, else the template error; empty when available.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CP2KPot::runDirectory`

```cpp
std::string runDirectory() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the directory that holds the live session's input and CP2K output;
  empty before the first force.
- Errors :: none.

The directory is `rgpot-cp2k-<pid>-g<group>-r<rank>-i<serial>` under `workDir`,
else under `TMPDIR`, else under the system temporary directory.
It is removed when the session ends unless `keepWorkDir` is set.

### CPMD

The method is Car and Parrinello, Phys.
Rev. Lett. 55, 2471 (1985), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.2471.
`CPMDPot` loads `libcpmdc` and does not carry a plane-wave energy of its own.
Positions are Angstrom and the energy is eV.
The parameters are the `CPMDParams` arm.
The tutorial's 0.77 eV is the stand-in engine on a 20 Angstrom cell (0.75 plus
0.001 times the cell's z length), not a published water energy.

#### `rgpot::CPMDPot`

```cpp
CPMDPot();
explicit CPMDPot(const ::CPMDParams::Reader &params);
```

- Inputs :: optional `CPMDParams` (Cap'n Proto); the default constructor uses
  the schema defaults.
- Units :: positions in Angstrom, energy in eV, forces in
  eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
  With the session ABI, rgpot sends a `ForceInput` tagged `angstrom` and `eV`
  and the engine returns those units.
  With the one-shot ABI, positions go in Angstrom and the class converts the
  Hartree energy and the
  Hartree/bohr gradient. It also converts a Hartree/bohr^3 stress when the
  engine exports `cpmdc_last_stress` and reports a valid tensor.
- Outputs :: a potential that runs CPMD through `libcpmdc`.
- Errors :: the constructors do not throw when the engine is missing.
  A force throws `std::runtime_error` when the engine is not available, `nAtoms`
  is zero, a buffer is null, the calculator binding was refused, the orbital key
  is refused, the engine reports failure, or the returned `PotentialResult` is
  malformed or has the wrong force count.

The engine must export the feature discovery functions (`cpmdc_feature_count`,
`cpmdc_feature_table`, `cpmdc_feature_find`) and either the session result ABI
or `cpmdc_energy_gradient` with `cpmdc_set_params`.
A non-empty `cpmdRoot` sets `CPMD_ROOT`.
The one-shot ABI does not receive the cell.
The class is built when `-Dwith_rpc=true`.

#### `rgpot::CPMDPot::setParams`

```cpp
bool setParams(const ::CPMDParams::Reader &params);
```

- Inputs :: `params`, the next `CPMDParams`.
- Units :: as the message fields (`cutOffRy` in Rydberg); the call converts
  nothing.
- Outputs :: true when the engine is loaded and accepts the params (a session is
  created, or `cpmdc_set_params` returns 0).
- Errors :: no exception of its own; a false return covers a missing engine and
  a refusal.

The engine is loaded again when it was not loaded or `enginePath` changed.
A live session is kept when the engine path and the serialized params are
unchanged.
A refused orbital key drops the session just created, so the same params are
applied again on the next call.

#### `rgpot::CPMDPot::getParams`

```cpp
void getParams(::CPMDParams::Builder out) const;
```

- Inputs :: `out`, a builder to fill.
- Units :: as the message fields.
- Outputs :: `out` holds the stored params, including `enginePath` and
  `cpmdRoot`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CPMDPot::available`

```cpp
bool available() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true when the engine is loaded and, for the session ABI, a session
  exists; for the one-shot ABI, when both one-shot functions are present.
- Errors :: none.

### MOPAC

The default model is AM1: Dewar, Zoebisch, Healy and Stewart, Journal of the
American Chemical Society 107, 3902-3909 (1985),
doi:10.1021/ja00299a024. PM6 is Stewart, Journal of Molecular Modeling 13, 1173-1213 (2007), doi:10.1007/s00894-007-0233-4.
MOPACPotTest does not pin an AM1 energy.
The fake engine returns 0.25 Hartree, and the test requires the host energy to
equal that times `HARTREE_TO_EV` (27.211386245988), which is 6.802846561497 eV.

#### `rgpot::MOPACPot`

```cpp
MOPACPot();
explicit MOPACPot(const Config &cfg);
```

- Inputs :: `Config` with `charge`, `spin`, `model` (0 PM7, 1 PM6-D3H4, 2
  PM6-ORG, 3 PM6, 4 AM1, 5 RM1; default 4), `tolerance`,
  `max_time` and `engine_path`.
- Units :: positions in Angstrom, energy in eV, forces in
  eV/Angstrom. `libmopacc` returns Hartree and a Hartree/bohr gradient, which
  the class converts.
  The cell is not sent; the class reports `periodic = false`.
- Outputs :: a potential that runs OpenMOPAC through `libmopacc`.
- Errors :: the constructors do not throw when the engine is missing.
  A force throws `std::runtime_error` when the engine is not loaded, `nAtoms` is
  zero, a buffer is null, or the engine reports failure.

The library must export `mopacc_energy_gradient`.
When it exports
`mopacc_c_abi_version`, the version must equal `RGPOT_MOPACC_C_ABI_VERSION`, and when it exports `mopacc_available`,
that must be nonzero.
The constructor passes the params once through `mopacc_set_params` when present
and ignores its status.

#### `rgpot::MOPACPot::available`

```cpp
bool available() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true when `libmopacc` is loaded and exports
  `mopacc_energy_gradient`.
- Errors :: none.

### NWChem

The engine is NWChem: Valiev and coauthors, Computer Physics Communications 181,
1477-1489 (2010),
doi:10.1016/j.cpc.2010.04.018, and Aprà and coauthors, Journal of Chemical Physics 152, 184102 (2020), doi:10.1063/5.0004997.
NWChemPotTest requires a water B3LYP/6-31G* energy below -2070.0 eV and a second
SCF within 1e-3 eV of the first.

#### `rgpot::NWChemPot`

```cpp
NWChemPot();
explicit NWChemPot(const ::NWChemParams::Reader &params);
```

- Inputs :: optional `NWChemParams` (Cap'n Proto); the default constructor uses
  the schema defaults.
- Units :: positions in Angstrom, energy in eV, forces in
  eV/Angstrom. `libnwchemc` returns Hartree and a Hartree/bohr gradient, which
  the class converts.
  The cell is not sent; the class reports `periodic = false`.
- Outputs :: a potential that runs NWChem through `libnwchemc`.
- Errors :: the constructors do not throw when the engine is missing.
  A force throws
  `std::runtime_error` when the engine is not loaded, `nAtoms` is zero, a buffer is null, or `nwchemc_energy_gradient`
  reports failure.

The library must export `nwchemc_energy_gradient` and `nwchemc_set_params`.
A loaded library stays mapped for the life of the process.
`enginePath` and `nwchemRoot` are cleared from the message the engine receives.
A non-empty `nwchemRoot` sets `NWCHEM_TOP`, and sets `NWCHEM_BASIS_LIBRARY` to
`<nwchemRoot>/src/basis/libraries/` when that variable is unset or empty.
The class is built when `-Dwith_rpc=true`.

#### `rgpot::NWChemPot::setParams`

```cpp
bool setParams(const ::NWChemParams::Reader &params);
```

- Inputs :: `params`, the next `NWChemParams`.
- Units :: as the message fields; the call converts nothing.
- Outputs :: true when the engine is loaded and `nwchemc_set_params` returns 0.
  The params are stored either way and are sent again with every force.
- Errors :: no exception of its own; a false return covers a missing engine and
  a refusal.

A library that is already loaded is kept while `enginePath` is empty or names
that same library.
A non-empty `enginePath` that differs from the loaded library is loaded in its
place, and a failed load leaves no engine loaded, so the call returns false.

#### `rgpot::NWChemPot::getParams`

```cpp
void getParams(::NWChemParams::Builder out) const;
```

- Inputs :: `out`, a builder to fill.
- Units :: as the message fields.
- Outputs :: `out` holds the stored params, including `enginePath` and
  `nwchemRoot`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::NWChemPot::available`

```cpp
bool available() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true when `libnwchemc` is loaded with both required functions.
- Errors :: none.

This example compiles here; running it needs `libnwchemc`.

```cpp
#include "rgpot/NWChemPot/NWChemPot.hpp"

#include <capnp/message.h>

#include <cstdio>
#include <string>

int main() {
  ::capnp::MallocMessageBuilder msg;
  auto params = msg.initRoot<::NWChemParams>();
  params.setTheory("scf");
  params.setBasis("6-31g*");
  params.setCharge(0);
  params.setMultiplicity(1);

  rgpot::NWChemPot pot(params.asReader());
  std::string message;
  ::capnp::MallocMessageBuilder cfg_msg;
  auto cfg = cfg_msg.initRoot<::PotentialConfig>();
  cfg.setNwchem(params.asReader());
  if (!pot.setPotentialConfig(cfg.asReader(), &message)) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", message.c_str());
    return 1;
  }
  return 0;
}
```

### ORCA

`ORCAPot` runs the `orca` executable as a child process and reads the energy and
gradient from the `.engrad` file it writes.
ORCA is not linked or loaded.
It is described in Neese, WIREs Computational Molecular Science 2, 73-78 (2012),
doi:10.1002/wcms.81, and in Neese, Wennmohs, Becker and Riplinger, J. Chem. Phys. 152, 224108 (2020), doi:10.1063/5.0004608.
Version 5 is Neese, WIREs Computational Molecular Science 12, e1606 (2022),
doi:10.1002/wcms.1606, and version 6 is Neese, WIREs Computational Molecular Science 15, e70019 (2025), doi:10.1002/wcms.70019.
The how-to is [ORCA single points](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/howto/orca.html).
The tests use a fake `orca` script that returns a Hartree energy of -1.25 and a
gradient of 0.01 Hartree/bohr times the component number, and require the host
energy and forces to equal those times the `units.hpp` factors.
They do not pin an ORCA energy.

#### `rgpot::ORCAConfig`

- Inputs :: `executable` (a path, or a bare name looked up on PATH; empty looks
  up `orca`), `method` (an ORCA method keyword, required), `basis` (a basis set
  keyword, empty for a composite method), `keywords` (further simple-input
  keywords, empty for none), `charge` (default 0), `multiplicity` (default 1),
  `nprocs` (default 1),
  `maxcore_mb` (default 1024), `restart` (default true), `scratch_dir` (empty
  for the system temporary directory),
  `keep_files` (default false) and `timeout_s` (default
  `ORCAConfig::kDefaultTimeout`, 3600 seconds; 0 waits with no limit).
- Units ::
  `maxcore_mb` in MB per process; `charge` in elementary charges; `timeout_s` in
  seconds; the other fields have no unit.
- Outputs :: a plain struct read by `rgpot::ORCAPot`.
  `method`, `basis` and `keywords` become the `!= line, =nprocs` above 1 becomes
  `%pal nprocs`, `maxcore_mb` becomes `%maxcore`, and `charge` and
  `multiplicity` go on the `* xyz` line.
  `restart` turns the `%moinp` and `MORead` reuse of the previous `.gbw` on and
  off.
  `timeout_s` is the time to wait for the `orca` process.
  The process is the leader of a new process group.
  Past the limit that group is sent SIGTERM and, if any process in the group is
  still alive two seconds later, SIGKILL even if the leader has exited, and the
  child is reaped.
- Errors :: `rgpot::ORCAPot` throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for an empty `method`, for `multiplicity`, `nprocs` or `maxcore_mb`
  below 1, for a `timeout_s` that is negative or not finite, and for a `method`,
  `basis` or `keywords` that holds a line break.

#### `rgpot::ORCAPot`

```cpp
explicit ORCAPot(const ORCAConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `rgpot::ORCAConfig`.
- Units :: positions in Angstrom, energy in eV, forces in
  eV/Angstrom. ORCA takes Angstrom in a `* xyz` block, so the positions are written as they are. The `.engrad` energy in Hartree is multiplied by `units::HARTREE_TO_EV` and its Hartree/bohr
  gradient by `units::NEG_GRAD_TO_FORCE`.
  The box must be absent or all zero, in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a potential that runs one ORCA energy and gradient per force call.
  `caps()` reports `Reentrancy::PerInstance`, `periodic = false` and no stress.
  The constructor resolves the executable and makes a directory of its own under
  `scratch_dir`; the destructor removes it unless `keep_files` is set.
  Each call writes
  `rgpot_orca.inp` there, closes extra file descriptors above 2 before `exec`, runs `orca rgpot_orca.inp`
  with the standard output in
  `rgpot_orca.out` and the standard error in `rgpot_orca.err`, and reads
  `rgpot_orca.engrad` in the C locale (as when writing coordinates).
  An `.engrad` and a `.gbw` left by an earlier call are removed first, and any
  removal failure other than a missing file throws `rgpot::ORCAError`.
  The orbitals of a successful call are copied to `rgpot_orca_guess.gbw`, and
  the next call with the same atomic numbers reads them through `%moinp` and
  `! MORead`.
  A call without a `.gbw`, after a failure, after `reset()`, or with other
  atomic numbers starts from ORCA's own guess.
- Errors :: the constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` in the cases of
  `rgpot::ORCAConfig`, and `rgpot::ORCAError` when no executable is found or the
  directory cannot be made.
  A force call throws `std::invalid_argument` for a box with a non-zero entry
  (ORCA has no periodic boundary conditions), for an atomic number outside 1 to
  118, and for a charge and multiplicity that the electron count cannot hold.
  It throws `rgpot::ORCAError`, a
  `std::runtime_error`, when a stale `.engrad` or `.gbw` cannot be removed, the input cannot be written, ORCA cannot be started or is ended by a signal, the run passes `timeout_s`
  (the process group is then stopped and the child reaped), ORCA exits with a
  non-zero status, no `.engrad` appears, the `.engrad` is malformed or lists
  other atoms, or the energy or a gradient component is not finite.
  The message holds the last 2048 bytes of the standard error and of the output
  file.

#### `rgpot::ORCAPot::reset`

```cpp
void reset();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the stored `.gbw` copy is removed, so the next force starts
  from ORCA's own guess.
- Errors :: none.

[[nodiscard]] const ORCAConfig &config() const noexcept;
```

- Units :: as `rgpot::ORCAConfig`.
- Outputs :: the config the instance was built with.
- Errors :: none.

[[nodiscard]] const std::string &executablePath() const noexcept;
```

- Outputs :: the absolute path of the executable the instance runs.
  A name with a directory part is made absolute; a bare name is the first
  executable of that name in the directories of `PATH`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::ORCAPot::runDirectory`

[[nodiscard]] const std::string &runDirectory() const noexcept;
```

  files of the instance.
  Two instances never share one.

#### `rgpot::ORCAPot::reusedWavefunction`

```

  before it.

#### `rgpot::ORCAPot::probeAvailable`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] static bool probeAvailable(const std::string &executable = {});
```

- Inputs :: `executable`, as in `rgpot::ORCAConfig` (empty looks up `orca` on
  PATH).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true when that name resolves to an executable regular file
  (including through a symlink).
  A test that needs ORCA calls this and skips when it is false.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::ORCAError`

- Inputs :: a message; the class inherits the constructors of
  `std::runtime_error`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the exception `rgpot::ORCAPot` throws when a run fails: no
  executable, a working directory that cannot be made, a stale `.engrad` or
  `.gbw` that cannot be removed, an input that cannot be written, a process that
  cannot start, is ended by a signal, passes `timeout_s` or exits with a
  non-zero status, and a missing, malformed or non-finite `.engrad`.
  The message names the input file and ends with the last 2048 bytes of the
  standard error and of the ORCA output file.
  Input the caller got wrong throws `std::invalid_argument` instead.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::orca::Engrad`

- Inputs :: none; a struct that `rgpot::orca::parseEngrad` fills from the text
  of a `.engrad` file (`CppCore/rgpot/ORCAPot/ORCAFiles.hpp`).
- Units :: ORCA's own:
  `energy_hartree` in Hartree and `gradient_hartree_per_bohr` in Hartree/bohr.
- Outputs :: `energy_hartree`, `gradient_hartree_per_bohr` (3 * `nAtoms` entries
  of dE/dR, atom-major) and `atomic_numbers` (one per atom).
  The Bohr coordinates of the file are read past and not kept.
  The parser does not check that the numbers are finite; `rgpot::ORCAPot` does.
- Errors :: none on the struct.
  `parseEngrad` throws `std::runtime_error` naming the first value that does not
  fit, including an atom count other than the one asked for.

#### `rgpot::orca::InputSpec`

- Inputs :: none; a struct that `rgpot::ORCAPot` fills from its
  `rgpot::ORCAConfig` for `rgpot::orca::renderInput`.
- Units :: `maxcore_mb` in MB per process; `charge` in elementary charges; the
  other fields have no unit.
- Outputs :: everything the input of one single point depends on: `method`,
  `basis` and `keywords` (joined on the `!= line, followed by =EnGrad`),
  `charge` and `multiplicity` (the `* xyz` line), `nprocs` (`%pal nprocs` above
  1), `maxcore_mb` (`%maxcore`) and `moinp`, the `.gbw` the orbitals are read
  from relative to the run directory.
  A non-empty `moinp` adds `%moinp` and `MORead`; an empty one starts from
  ORCA's own guess.
- Errors :: none on the struct.
  `renderInput` throws `std::invalid_argument` when `method`, `basis`,
  `keywords` or `moinp` holds a line break, or an atomic number is outside 1 to 118.

### Skala

skala-1.1 is the exchange-correlation keyword this class writes into NWChem, not
a separate energy surface.
The functional is Luise and coauthors, arXiv:2506.14665,
doi:10.48550/arXiv.2506.14665. The abstract reports an error of 2.8 kcal/mol on
GMTKN55.
SkalaPotTest checks that the keyword is written; it does not pin an energy.

#### `rgpot::SkalaConfig`

- Inputs :: `xc` (exchange-correlation keyword, default `skala-1.1`), `basis`
  (default `def2-tzvp`), `charge` (default 0), `multiplicity` (2S+1, default 1),
  `engine_path` (default empty), `nwchem_root` (default empty).
- Units :: `charge` in elementary charges; the other fields have no unit.
- Outputs :: a plain struct read by `SkalaPot`, which copies the fields into an
  `NWChemParams` message.
- Errors :: `SkalaPot` throws `std::runtime_error` when `basis` or `xc` is empty
  or `multiplicity` is below 1.
  Other values reach NWChem unchecked; a rejection makes `NWChemPot::setParams`
  return false, and `SkalaPot` ignores that result.

#### `rgpot::SkalaPot`

```cpp
SkalaPot();
explicit SkalaPot(const SkalaConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `rgpot::SkalaConfig`; the default constructor, where
  there is one, uses its defaults.
- Units :: as `rgpot::NWChemPot`: Angstrom in, eV and eV/Angstrom out.
- Outputs :: a potential that runs NWChem Kohn-Sham DFT with the Skala
  functional through an owned `NWChemPot`.
  The message it builds sets `theory` to `dft`, `task` to `gradient` and one DFT
  stanza with `xc`.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` from the constructor when `basis` or `xc` is
  empty or `multiplicity` is below 1.
  A missing engine does not throw here; forces then throw `std::runtime_error`
  from `NWChemPot`.

The owned `NWChemPot` is default-constructed first, so a library found by the
environment search is kept while `engine_path` is empty.
A non-empty `engine_path` is passed on as `enginePath`, and that library is
loaded in place of the one the search found.
The build option is `-Dwith_skala=true` and it needs `-Dwith_rpc=true`.

#### `rgpot::SkalaPot::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const SkalaConfig &config() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the stored `SkalaConfig`, including charge and multiplicity set
  later.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::SkalaPot::setChargeMultiplicity`

```cpp
void setChargeMultiplicity(int charge, int multiplicity);
```

- Inputs :: `charge` in elementary charges and `multiplicity` as 2S+1.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the new params are passed to the engine and `paramsKey` is
  recomputed.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when `multiplicity` is below 1.
  The config already holds the new values when that throws.

#### `rgpot::SkalaPot::available`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] bool available() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `NWChemPot::available()` of the owned engine.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::SkalaPot::getParams`

```cpp
void getParams(::NWChemParams::Builder out) const;
```

- Inputs :: `out`, a builder to fill.
- Units :: as the message fields.
- Outputs :: the `NWChemParams` the class built and passed to the engine.
- Errors :: none.

### tblite

The library is the extended tight-binding implementation of Bannwarth and
coauthors, WIREs Computational Molecular Science 11, e1493,
doi:10.1002/wcms.1493. GFN1-xTB is the 2017 GFN-xTB method of Grimme, Bannwarth and Shushkov, Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation 13, 1989-2009 (2017), doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.7b00118.
IPEA1-xTB is the IPEA parametrization of Ásgeirsson, Bauer and Grimme, Chemical
Science 8, 4879-4895 (2017), doi:10.1039/c7sc00601b.
GFN2-xTB, the default, is cited under xtb.
TBLitePotTest requires the GFN2 energy of its three-atom water geometry to lie
within 1 eV of -137.9 eV.

#### `rgpot::TBLiteConfig`

- Inputs :: `method` (`TBLiteMethod::GFN1`, `GFN2` or `IPEA1`; default `GFN2`),
  `accuracy` (default 1.0),
  `electronic_temperature` (default 300.0), `max_iterations` (default 250),
  `charge` (default 0.0), `uhf` (unpaired electrons, default 0).
- Units :: `electronic_temperature` in K; `charge` in elementary charges; the
  other fields have no unit.
- Outputs :: a plain struct read by `TBLitePot`.
- Errors :: `TBLitePot` does not check the values. tblite rejects them on the
  first force, and `TBLitePot` throws `std::runtime_error` with the tblite
  message.

#### `rgpot::TBLitePot`

```cpp
TBLitePot();
explicit TBLitePot(const TBLiteConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `rgpot::TBLiteConfig`; the default constructor, where
  there is one, uses its defaults.
- Units :: positions in Angstrom, energy in eV, forces in
  eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
  The class sends positions and cell in bohr and the electronic temperature in
  Hartree (times `KB_HARTREE`), and converts the Hartree energy, the
  Hartree/bohr gradient and the Hartree virial divided by the cell volume.
  Stress is set only when the cell volume is positive.
- Outputs :: a potential that calls the linked tblite C API.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` from the constructor when the tblite context or
  result cannot be created.
  A force throws `std::runtime_error` on a tblite structure, calculator,
  geometry update or SCF error.

The first force builds the structure and the calculator from that call's atoms.
Later forces only update the geometry.
The build option is `-Dwith_tblite=true`.

### xtb

The default method is GFN2-xTB: Bannwarth, Ehlert and Grimme, J. Chem.
Theory Comput. 15, 1652 (2019),
doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.8b01176. Host positions are Angstrom and the host energy is eV. `XTBConfig` holds the parameters: the method, accuracy 1, an electronic temperature of 300 K, 250 iterations, charge 0 and no unpaired electrons. A numerical GFN2 energy needs libxtb, which the default build does not link, so this tree does not pin one. GFN1-xTB is the 2017 GFN-xTB method of Grimme, Bannwarth and Shushkov, Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation 13, 1989-2009 (2017), doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.7b00118.
GFN0-xTB is Pracht, Caldeweyher, Ehlert and Grimme, ChemRxiv (2019),
doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.8326202.v1. GFN-FF is Spicher and Grimme, Angewandte Chemie International Edition 59, 15665-15673 (2020), doi:10.1002/anie.202004239.

#### `rgpot::XTBConfig`

- Inputs :: `method` (`GFNMethod::GFNFF`, `GFN0xTB`, `GFN1xTB` or `GFN2xTB`;
  default `GFN2xTB`), `accuracy` (default 1.0),
  `electronic_temperature` (default 300.0), `max_iterations` (default 250),
  `charge` (default 0.0), `uhf` (unpaired electrons, default 0),
  `warm_move` (default 1.0), `warm_min_gap` (default 1.0).
- Units ::
  `electronic_temperature` in K; `charge` in elementary charges; `warm_move` in
  Angstrom; `warm_min_gap` in eV; the other fields have no unit.
- Outputs :: a plain struct read by `XTBPot` and, inside `XTBDlopenConfig`, by
  `XTBDlopen`.
- Errors :: neither class checks the values.
  A value xtb rejects fails the force with `std::runtime_error`.
  Zero or a negative `warm_move` disables wavefunction reuse.
  Zero or a negative `warm_min_gap` reuses the wavefunction at any gap.

#### `rgpot::XTBDlopenConfig`

- Inputs :: `xtb` (an `XTBConfig`, default-constructed), `engine_path` (default
  empty).
- Units :: as `XTBConfig`; `engine_path` none.
- Outputs :: a plain struct read by `XTBDlopen`, the frontend that loads
  `libxtb_engine` instead of linking libxtb.
- Errors :: `XTBDlopen` throws
  `std::runtime_error` when a non-empty `engine_path` has no directory
  separator, when no candidate library opens, or when the library lacks the C
  ABI or reports another ABI version.

A non-empty `engine_path` is the only candidate.
An empty one searches `RGPOT_XTB_ENGINE`,
`XTB_ENGINE`, the platform name (`libxtb_engine.so` on Linux), then
`libxtb_engine.so` in each directory of `EON_POTENTIALS_PATH` and `RGPOT_ENGINE_PATH`.

#### `rgpot::XTBPot`

```cpp
XTBPot();
explicit XTBPot(const XTBConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `rgpot::XTBConfig`; the default constructor, where
  there is one, uses its defaults.
- Units :: positions in Angstrom, energy in eV, forces in
  eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
  The class sends positions and cell in bohr and converts the Hartree energy,
  the Hartree/bohr gradient and the Hartree virial divided by the cell volume.
  The molecule is created non-periodic in all three directions; stress is set
  when the cell volume is positive.
- Outputs :: a potential that calls the linked libxtb C API.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` from the constructor when the xtb environment,
  calculator or results cannot be created.
  A force throws `rgpot::SccNotConverged`, a
  `std::runtime_error`, when the SCC does not converge and the rescue below does not help, and `std::runtime_error`
  when the handles are missing, `xtb_newMolecule` fails, another single point
  failure occurs, or the energy or gradient is not finite.
  After such a failure the handles are replaced.

A new composition rebuilds the molecule.
A force starts the SCC from the previous wavefunction when the composition is
unchanged, no atom moved further than `warmMove()`, and the HOMO-LUMO gap of
that wavefunction is at least `warmMinGap()`.
A single point started that way that does not converge, or whose gap falls below
`warmMinGap()`, is run again from xtb's own guess.
GFN-FF has no orbitals, so its gap never blocks reuse.
The first single point of a force runs at most 48 SCC iterations, or
`max_iterations` when that is smaller.
An SCC that does not converge is retried at 1000, 3000 and 5000 K (those above
the configured temperature) and then evaluated again at the configured
temperature.
The build option is `-Dwith_xtb=true`.

#### `rgpot::XTBPot::reset`

```cpp
void reset();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the stored SCC wavefunction and the previous geometry are
  dropped, so the next force starts from xtb's own guess.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when a new xtb results object cannot be
  created.

- Inputs :: `angstrom`, the largest atom displacement that still reuses the

  Zero or a negative value disables reuse.

#### `rgpot::XTBPot::reusedWavefunction`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] bool reusedWavefunction() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true when the last successful force kept the previous wavefunction
  as its guess: same composition, a stored wavefunction, a positive displacement

  after the single point.
  False when that force fell back to xtb's own guess.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::XTBDlopen`

```cpp
explicit XTBDlopen(const XTBDlopenConfig &config);
explicit XTBDlopen(const XTBConfig &xtb = XTBConfig{});
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `rgpot::XTBDlopenConfig`; the second form takes only
  the `XTBConfig` and searches for the engine with an empty `engine_path`.
- Units :: as `XTBPot`; `libxtb_engine` wraps an `XTBPot`.
- Outputs :: a frontend that loads
  `libxtb_engine` and drives it through the XTB C ABI in [[file:engine_abi.org][Engine
  C ABI]].
  `warm_move` and `warm_min_gap` are passed to the engine after it is created.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when a non-empty `engine_path` has no directory
  separator, when no candidate library opens, when the library lacks any
  `rgpot_xtb_*` symbol, when
  `rgpot_xtb_abi_version` is not `RGPOT_XTB_ABI_VERSION`, and with the engine's
  message when `rgpot_xtb_create` fails.

A library that opens but lacks a symbol ends the search; the next candidate is
not tried.
The destructor destroys the engine object and closes the library.
