### Metatomic

The model container is metatomic: Bigi et al., J. Chem.
Phys. 164, 064113 (2026), doi:10.1063/5.0304911.
Positions are Angstrom and the energy is eV.
The parameters are the exported model plus `MetatomicConfig`.
Reference value: the 13-atom geometry in `MetatomicPotTest`, on
`CppCore/tests/data/lj38/lennard-jones.pt`, is 98374.87753058573 eV within 1e-2,
the pin from eOn `MetatomicTest`.

#### `rgpot::MetatomicConfig`

- Inputs :: the fields and their defaults:
  `model_path` (empty; the exported model file), `device` (empty; let metatomic pick from the model's devices), `length_unit`
  (`angstrom`), `extensions_directory` (empty), `check_consistency` (false),
  `uncertainty_threshold` (-1.0; a positive value requests the model's per-atom `energy_uncertainty`
  output), `dtype_override` (empty; `float32` or `float64`), `random_rotation`
  (false), `n_symmetry_rotations` (0; 12 or more averages over a rotation group,
  12 elements below 24 and 24 from 24 up), `so3_probe_scatter` (false; with
  rotations, the unrotated pass gives the energy and forces and the rotated
  passes only the variance),
  `torch_determinism` (`TorchDeterminismPolicy::Fast`), `engine_path` (empty),
  `task_name` (empty), `charge` (0), `spin` (multiplicity, 1), `attach_system_extras`
  (false; true attaches the charge and spin names to every system).
- Units :: `length_unit` names the unit of the positions given to the model;
  `charge` in elementary charges; the other fields have no unit.
- Outputs :: a plain struct read by `MetatomicPot` and by the dlopen frontend
  `MetatomicDlopen`.
- Errors :: `MetatomicPot` throws what metatomic raises for a model that does
  not load, and `std::runtime_error` for a model without an energy output or
  with a dtype other than `float32` or `float64`.
  A `dtype_override` other than `float32` or `float64` is ignored, and a model
  that cannot move to the override keeps its own dtype.
  An `energy_uncertainty` output that is missing or not per-atom turns the
  uncertainty request off.
  `MetatomicDlopen` throws `std::runtime_error` when no engine library opens or
  the engine refuses the config.

`MetatomicPot` compares `uncertainty_threshold` only with zero; the value itself
is not used as a threshold.
Each system carries `charge` as `rgpot::charge` and `spin` as
`rgpot::spin_multiplicity` and `rgpot::spin`, each name only when the model declares it in `requested_inputs`.
`attach_system_extras` attaches all three, for a model that reads them without
declaring them; it needs `check_consistency` off, because metatomic then rejects
data the model does not declare.
`engine_path` is read only by `MetatomicDlopen`, which tries it first, then `RGPOT_METATOMIC_ENGINE`, `METATOMIC_ENGINE`,
the platform name
(`libmetatomic_engine.so` on Linux) and the directories of `EON_POTENTIALS_PATH` and `RGPOT_ENGINE_PATH`.
`MetatomicDlopen` does not pass
`task_name`, `charge`, `spin` or `attach_system_extras` to the engine.

#### `rgpot::MetatomicPot`

```cpp
explicit MetatomicPot(const MetatomicConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `rgpot::MetatomicConfig`; the default constructor,
  where there is one, uses its defaults.
- Units :: positions are passed unchanged and declared to the model in
  `length_unit`; the energy is requested in eV.
  With the default `length_unit` that is Angstrom in, eV and eV/Angstrom out.
  The `variance` is a variance, so one square root gives a scale in the units of
  the quantity it describes.
  It is the square of the mean model `energy_uncertainty` in eV^2 when that
  output is used.
  Otherwise it is the mean square of the force deviation over the rotations, in
  eV^2 per Angstrom squared: the mean over every atom, Cartesian component and
  rotation of the squared difference from the force the potential returns.
  It is 0 when neither applies.
- Outputs :: a potential that evaluates the model in process with libtorch.
- Errors :: the constructor throws what metatomic raises when the model cannot
  be loaded, and `std::runtime_error` for a model dtype other than `float32` or
  `float64` or a model without an energy output.
  Forces propagate torch and metatomic exceptions.

The device is chosen by `metatomic_torch::pick_device` from the model's
supported devices and `device`.
`TorchDeterminismPolicy::Strict` changes process-global libtorch flags.
The build option is
`-Dwith_metatomic=true`; the class is not linked into `librgpot` when `-Dwith_python=true`.

#### `rgpot::MetatomicPot::setChargeSpin`

```cpp
void setChargeSpin(int charge, int spin);
```

- Inputs :: `charge` in elementary charges and `spin` as the multiplicity.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; later forces attach these values under the names the model
  reads (see `readsCharge` and `readsSpin`).
  The result-cache key from `paramsKey` is recomputed, so a result cached under
  the previous pair is not served for the new one.
- Errors :: none; a value the model does not read has no effect, and
  `libmetatomic_engine` refuses such a value without calling this.

#### `rgpot::MetatomicPot::paramsKey`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] uint64_t paramsKey() const noexcept override;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a 64-bit FNV-1a hash of every setting the model sees.
  These are the model path, device, length unit, extensions directory,
  uncertainty threshold, dtype override, rotation averaging, determinism policy,
  task name, extras flag, charge and spin, together with a kernel version.
  Instances that differ in these values get different result-cache keys, and
  `setChargeSpin` changes the key.
  The consistency check and the engine path are not part of the hash.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::MetatomicPot::readsCharge`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] bool readsCharge() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true when the model declares `rgpot::charge` in
  `requested_inputs` or `attach_system_extras` is true, so later forces attach
  the charge.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::MetatomicPot::readsSpin`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] bool readsSpin() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true when the model declares
  `rgpot::spin_multiplicity` or `rgpot::spin` in `requested_inputs`, or
  `attach_system_extras` is true, so later forces attach the multiplicity.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::MetatomicDlopen`

```cpp
explicit MetatomicDlopen(const MetatomicConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `rgpot::MetatomicConfig`;
  `engine_path` is read here, and `task_name`, `charge`, `spin` and
  `attach_system_extras` are not passed on.
- Units :: as `MetatomicPot`; `libmetatomic_engine` wraps a `MetatomicPot`.
- Outputs :: a frontend that loads
  `libmetatomic_engine` and drives it through the Metatomic C ABI in [[file:engine_abi.org][Engine
  C ABI]].
  An empty `device` runs on `cpu`.
- Errors ::
  `std::runtime_error` when no candidate library opens, when the library lacks `rgpot_mta_abi_version`,
  `rgpot_mta_create`, `rgpot_mta_destroy` or `rgpot_mta_force`, when the version
  is not
  `RGPOT_MTA_ABI_VERSION`, and with the engine's message when `rgpot_mta_create`
  fails.

The library is opened with `RTLD_GLOBAL`.
The destructor destroys the engine object and leaves the library mapped, because
the static teardown of torch and metatomic after `dlclose` crashes at process
exit.

#### `rgpot::MetatomicDlopen::available`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] bool available() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true while the engine object exists, which is the whole life of a
  constructed `MetatomicDlopen`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::MetatomicDlopen::forceImpl`

```cpp
void forceImpl(const ForceInput &in, ForceOut *out) const;
```

- Inputs :: `in`, the positions, atomic numbers and cell; `out`, where the
  energy, forces and variance go.
- Units :: as `MetatomicPot`.
- Outputs :: `out->energy`, `out->F` and `out->variance` from `rgpot_mta_force`.
  `out->has_stress` and `out->stress` are not written.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` with the return code when `rgpot_mta_force`
  returns nonzero; the engine prints the reason on stderr.

### UMA

The model family is Wood and coauthors, Advances in Neural Information
Processing Systems 38, pages 143528-143564 (2025), doi:10.52202/085713-4310.
UmaPotTest pins the ASE FAIRChemCalculator energy of HCN, uma-s-1p1 task omol,
at -2542.4200323230975 eV within 1e-4.
That figure is the test's parity pin, not a value from the paper.

#### `rgpot::UmaConfig`

- Inputs ::
  `model_path` (default empty; an AOTInductor `.pt2` package from `scripts/export_uma_aoti.py`), `task_name`
  (default `omol`), `device` (default `cpu`), `charge` (default 0), `spin`
  (integer from 0 to 100, default 1), `cutoff` (default 6.0),
  `max_neighbors` (default 300), `cache_dir` (default empty; the root of the
  persistent cache the package is unpacked into).
- Units :: `cutoff` in Angstrom; `charge` in elementary charges; the other
  fields have no unit.
- Outputs :: a plain struct read by `UmaPot`.
- Errors :: `UmaPot` throws `std::runtime_error` when `model_path` is empty or
  does not end in `.pt2`, and
  `std::invalid_argument` (via `rgpot::validate_uma_spin_for_task`) when `spin`
  is outside `[0, 100]`.
  The first force throws `std::runtime_error` when the cache root cannot be
  created or the package cannot be unpacked into it.
  An empty
  `cache_dir` means `$RGPOT_CACHE_DIR`, then `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/rgpot`, then `.rgpot-cache` in the working directory; the UMA unpack cache in [[file:engine_abi.org][Engine
  C ABI]] gives the layout.
  A `device` that is neither `cpu` nor starts with `cuda` runs on the CPU.
  A `cutoff` that is not positive and finite becomes 6.0, and a `max_neighbors`
  of zero or less keeps every neighbour.
  The package's `cutoff` and `max_neighbors` metadata replace the config values
  when present.
  A `task_name`, `charge` or `spin` that disagrees with the package metadata
  makes each force throw `rgpot::UmaContractError`.

#### `rgpot::validate_uma_spin_for_task`

```cpp
void validate_uma_spin_for_task(std::string_view task_name, int spin,
                                std::string_view where = "UmaPot");
```

- Inputs :: `task_name`, the UMA head name; `spin`, the integer spin; `where`,
  the caller prefix for error messages (default `UmaPot`).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; accepted values are not modified.
- Errors :: throws `std::invalid_argument` when `spin` is outside `[0, 100]`.

#### `rgpot::UmaPot`

```cpp
explicit UmaPot(const UmaConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `rgpot::UmaConfig`; the default constructor, where
  there is one, uses its defaults.
- Units :: positions in Angstrom are passed to the package unchanged, and its
  energy and forces are copied unchanged; packages from that script return eV
  and eV/Angstrom.
  The package's `cutoff` metadata replaces the config value when present.
- Outputs :: a potential that builds a neighbour list and runs the compiled
  graph.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` from the constructor when `model_path` is empty
  or does not end in `.pt2`, and
  `std::invalid_argument` when `spin` violates `rgpot::validate_uma_spin_for_task`.
  The package loads on the first force; loader errors and `std::runtime_error`
  for bad dtype metadata surface there.
  A force throws `rgpot::UmaContractError` when charge, spin, task or
  composition disagree with the package metadata, `rgpot::UmaShapeError` when
  the input does not fit the package shapes (both are
  `std::runtime_error`), and `std::runtime_error` for zero atoms, an empty edge
  list, mixed compositions in one batch, or output of the wrong shape.

The build option is
`-Dwith_metatomic=true`; the class is not linked into `librgpot` when `-Dwith_python=true`.

#### `rgpot::UmaPot::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const UmaConfig &config() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: `cutoff` in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the stored `UmaConfig`, including charge and spin set later.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::UmaPot::setChargeSpin`

```cpp
void setChargeSpin(int charge, int spin);
```

- Inputs :: `charge` in elementary charges and `spin` (integer in `[0, 100]`).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the config is updated and `paramsKey` is recomputed.
- Errors :: throws
  `std::invalid_argument` without mutating the config when `spin` violates `rgpot::validate_uma_spin_for_task`;
  the next force throws `rgpot::UmaContractError` when the package was exported
  for other values.

#### `rgpot::UmaPot::posDtypeName`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const char *posDtypeName() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `float32`, `float64` or `unset`: the `pos_dtype` recorded in the
  package.
  The pointer stays valid while the potential lives.
- Errors :: loads the package first, so it throws what loading throws.

#### `rgpot::UmaPot::modelDtypeName`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const char *modelDtypeName() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `float32`, `float64` or `unset`: the `model_dtype` recorded in the
  package.
- Errors :: as `posDtypeName`.

#### `rgpot::UmaPot::checkpointProvenance`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const UmaCheckpointProvenance &checkpointProvenance() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the checkpoint the package was exported from and the SHA-256 of its
  weights, read from the package metadata.
  Every field is unset for a package exported before the keys existed.
  The reference stays valid while the potential lives.
- Errors :: loads the package first, so it throws what loading throws, including
  the `std::runtime_error` of `UmaCheckpointProvenance::fromMetadata` for
  malformed keys.

#### `rgpot::UmaCheckpointProvenance`

- Inputs :: none; `fromMetadata` fills the six `std::optional<std::string>`
  fields `source`, `path`, `hf_repo`, `hf_filename`,
  `hf_revision` and `sha256` from the package keys `checkpoint_source`,
  `checkpoint_path`, `checkpoint_hf_repo`, `checkpoint_hf_filename`, `checkpoint_hf_revision` and `checkpoint_sha256`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `source` is `cli`, `env` or `hf`; `sha256` is 64 and `hf_revision`
  40 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
  `scripts/export_uma_aoti.py` writes `path` for `cli` and `env` and the three
  `hf_` fields for `hf`.
- Errors :: none; `fromMetadata` checks the values.

`CppCore/rgpot/UmaPot/UmaProvenance.hpp` declares it, and the UMA checkpoint
provenance in [Engine C ABI](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/engine_abi.html) lists the keys.
`sha256` is the digest of the checkpoint the exporter loaded, not of the `.pt2`;
`rgpot_engine_model_digest` hashes the package file.

#### `rgpot::UmaCheckpointProvenance::present`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] bool present() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true when any of the six fields is set.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::UmaCheckpointProvenance::fromMetadata`

```cpp
static UmaCheckpointProvenance
fromMetadata(const std::unordered_map<std::string, std::string> &meta);
```

- Inputs :: `meta`, the package metadata as key and value strings.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the provenance; a key that is missing or empty leaves its field
  unset.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when `checkpoint_source` is not `cli`, `env` or
  `hf`, when
  `checkpoint_sha256` is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, or when `checkpoint_hf_revision`
  is not 40.

### i-PI socket

The socket is the i-PI force-engine protocol of Ceriotti, More and Manolopoulos,
Computer Physics Communications 185, 1019-1026 (2014),
doi:10.1016/j.cpc.2013.10.027. i-PI 2.0 is Kapil and coauthors, Computer Physics Communications 236, 214-223 (2019), doi:10.1016/j.cpc.2018.09.020.
IPIPotTest's mock returns 0.25 Hartree.
The host energy must lie within 1e-12 of 0.25 times `HARTREE_TO_EV`, which is
6.802846561497 eV.
That is a unit conversion, not a path-integral energy.

#### `rgpot::IPIConfig`

- Inputs :: `address` (default empty), `timeout_s` (default 30.0).
  `address` is `unix:/absolute/path`, `unix:<name>` (the i-PI default path with
  prefix `ipi_`), `tcp:<host>:<port>` or `tcp:<port>` (host 127.0.0.1); port 0
  lets the kernel choose.
- Units :: `timeout_s` in seconds; it covers one whole force call, including the
  wait for the driver to connect.
- Outputs :: a plain struct read by `IPIPot`.
- Errors :: `IPIPot` throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for an address without a `unix:` or `tcp:` prefix, an empty UNIX address, a UNIX name containing `/=, a UNIX path too long for the socket address, a missing or out-of-range port, or a =timeout_s`
  that is negative or not finite.
  It throws `std::runtime_error` when the host does not resolve or the socket
  cannot be bound or listened on.

#### `rgpot::IPIPot`

```cpp
explicit IPIPot(const IPIConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `rgpot::IPIConfig`; the default constructor, where
  there is one, uses its defaults.
- Units :: positions and cell in Angstrom, energy in eV, forces in
  eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
  On the wire the class sends bohr (the cell with lattice vectors in columns,
  and its inverse) and converts the driver's Hartree energy,
  Hartree/bohr forces and Hartree virial; the stress is -W/V.
  `timeout_s` is in seconds and covers one whole force call, including the wait
  for the driver to connect.
- Outputs :: a potential that binds the socket at construction and evaluates
  through one i-PI driver.
- Errors ::
  `std::invalid_argument` from the constructor for a bad address, port or timeout or a UNIX path that is too long; `std::runtime_error`
  when the socket cannot be bound or listened on.
  A force throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for missing buffers, zero atoms, more atoms than the protocol limit, non-finite positions or cell, or a singular cell, and `std::runtime_error`
  on a timeout, a disconnect, an unexpected header, a driver that does not
  become READY, or a mismatched atom count.
  After a failed exchange the connection is closed and the next force waits for
  a new driver.

Atomic numbers are not sent; the driver keeps its own species list.
The destructor sends EXIT.
The force call does not write `ForceOut::stress`; read it with `copyStress`.
The build option is `-Dwith_ipi`; its default, `auto`, builds the class
everywhere except Windows.

#### `rgpot::IPIPot::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const IPIConfig &config() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: `timeout_s` in seconds.
- Outputs :: the `IPIConfig` given to the constructor.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::IPIPot::endpoint`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const std::string &endpoint() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the bound address, `unix:<path>` or `tcp:<host>:<port>` with the
  port the kernel chose for port 0.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::IPIPot::hasStress`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] bool hasStress() const;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true after a force call whose cell had a positive volume.
  Each force call clears it first.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::IPIPot::copyStress`

```cpp
bool copyStress(double out[9]) const;
```

- Inputs :: `out`, room for 9 doubles.
- Units :: eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: the last Cauchy stress, row-major, in `out`; returns false (and
  writes nothing) when there is none or `out` is null.
- Errors :: none.

This example compiles here; running it needs an i-PI driver that connects to the
socket.

```cpp
#include "rgpot/IPIPot/IPIPot.hpp"

#include <array>
#include <cstdio>
#include <vector>

int main() {
  rgpot::IPIPot pot({.address = "tcp:127.0.0.1:0", .timeout_s = 60.0});
  std::printf("driver should connect to %s\n", pot.endpoint().c_str());

  rgpot::types::AtomMatrix positions(2, 3);
  positions(0, 0) = 0.0;
  positions(0, 1) = 0.0;
  positions(0, 2) = 0.0;
  positions(1, 0) = 0.74;
  positions(1, 1) = 0.0;
  positions(1, 2) = 0.0;
  std::vector<int> numbers{1, 1};
  std::array<std::array<double, 3>, 3> box{{{10, 0, 0}, {0, 10, 0}, {0, 0, 10}}};
  auto [energy, forces, variance] = pot(positions, numbers, box);
  double stress[9];
  if (pot.copyStress(stress))
    std::printf("E = %g eV, sigma_xx = %g eV/A^3\n", energy, stress[0]);
  return 0;
}
```

### LAMMPS, GROMACS and OpenMM

These three classes evaluate the shifted 12-6 Lennard-Jones potential described
by `ExternalLjConfig`.
The C entry points with the same names as the three factory functions are in
`CppCore/rgpot/ExternalPot/external_potentials.h`.
The engines are Thompson and coauthors, Computer Physics Communications 271,
108171 (2022),
doi:10.1016/j.cpc.2021.108171, Abraham and coauthors, SoftwareX 1-2, 19-25 (2015), doi:10.1016/j.softx.2015.06.001,
and Eastman and coauthors, PLOS Computational Biology 13, e1005659 (2017),
doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005659. The pair form is Lennard-Jones, Proceedings of the Royal Society A 106, 463 (1924), doi:10.1098/rspa.1924.0082.
No test in this tree pins an energy for these three classes.

#### `rgpot::ExternalLjConfig`

- Inputs :: `u0` (well depth, default 1.0), `cutoff` (truncation distance,
  default 8.0), `psi` (zero crossing, default 1.0), `engine_path` (default
  empty).
- Units :: `u0` in eV; `cutoff` and `psi` in Angstrom; `engine_path` none.
- Outputs :: a plain struct read by the constructors of `LammpsPot`,
  `GromacsPot` and `OpenMMPot`.
- Errors :: those constructors throw `std::invalid_argument` when `u0`, `cutoff`
  or `psi` is not positive and finite.
  An
  `engine_path` that does not open, or lacks the required symbols, makes them throw `std::runtime_error`.

For `LammpsPot` an empty
`engine_path` searches `RGPOT_LAMMPS_ENGINE`, `LAMMPS_ENGINE`,
`liblammps_engine` and `liblj_engine`.
For `GromacsPot` and `OpenMMPot` an empty `engine_path` evaluates the potential
in process.

#### `rgpot::rgpot_lammps_potential`

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<LammpsPot>
rgpot_lammps_potential(const ExternalLjConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `ExternalLjConfig`.
- Units :: `u0` in eV, `cutoff` and `psi` in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a new `LammpsPot` built from `config`, owned by the returned
  `std::unique_ptr`.
- Errors :: what the `LammpsPot` constructor throws:
  `std::invalid_argument` for a non-positive parameter, `std::runtime_error`
  when no plugin loads or `rgpot_engine_create` fails.

#### `rgpot::rgpot_lammpc_potential`

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<LammpsPot>
rgpot_lammpc_potential(const void *config_capnp, size_t config_capnp_size,
                       const std::string &engine_path = "");
```

- Inputs ::
  `config_capnp` and `config_capnp_size`, a flat `PotentialConfig` whose `lammps` arm is `LammpsParams`, and `engine_path`.
  A non-empty `engine_path` is the only library tried.
  An empty `engine_path` tries `LAMMPC_LIBRARY` and `RGPOT_LAMMPC_ENGINE` when
  either is set and not empty, and nothing after them; with neither set it
  searches `liblammpc.so`, `./liblammpc.so` and the macOS and Windows names.
- Units :: those of `LammpsParams.unitsStyle`; `metal` is eV and Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a new `LammpsPot` that keeps one lammpc session, owned by the
  returned `std::unique_ptr`.
  Destroying it destroys the session.
  The last `LammpsPot` on a lammpc backend to go, or to have its session
  refused, calls `lammpc_finalize`.
- Errors :: `std::invalid_argument` when the bytes are missing, not a multiple
  of a Cap'n Proto word, truncated, or not a `PotentialConfig` with the `lammps`
  arm.
  `std::runtime_error` when the build has no Cap'n Proto headers, no `liblammpc` loads, its `Capabilities` fail the handshake of `rgpot::abi::checked_load`,
  the backend reports unavailable, or `lammpc_session_create_from_config`
  returns null.
  A non-empty `engine_path` that does not open, or whose backend the handshake
  refuses, throws a message that names it.

#### `rgpot::rgpot_gromacs_potential`

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<GromacsPot>
rgpot_gromacs_potential(const ExternalLjConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `ExternalLjConfig`.
- Units :: `u0` in eV, `cutoff` and `psi` in Angstrom; the potential stores them
  in kJ/mol and nm.
- Outputs :: a new `GromacsPot` built from `config`, owned by the returned
  `std::unique_ptr`.
- Errors :: what the `GromacsPot` constructor throws:
  `std::invalid_argument` for a non-positive parameter, `std::runtime_error`
  when
  `engine_path` is set and the library does not load or `rgpot_engine_create`
  fails.

#### `rgpot::rgpot_openmm_potential`

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<OpenMMPot>
rgpot_openmm_potential(const ExternalLjConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `ExternalLjConfig`.
- Units :: as `rgpot::rgpot_gromacs_potential`.
- Outputs :: a new `OpenMMPot` built from `config`, owned by the returned
  `std::unique_ptr`.
- Errors :: as `rgpot::rgpot_gromacs_potential`, for the `OpenMMPot`
  constructor.

#### `rgpot::LammpsPot`

```cpp
explicit LammpsPot(const ExternalLjConfig &config);
LammpsPot(const void *config_capnp, size_t config_capnp_size,
          const std::string &engine_path = "");
```

- Inputs :: `ExternalLjConfig`, or a flat `PotentialConfig`
  (`config_capnp`, `config_capnp_size`) with the `lammps` arm and `engine_path`.
- Units :: `u0` in eV, `cutoff` and `psi` in Angstrom; positions in Angstrom,
  energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom.
  The plugin receives these values as three doubles and nothing is converted.
  The lammpc constructor uses the units of `LammpsParams.unitsStyle`.
- Outputs :: a potential whose forces come from `rgpot_engine_force` of the
  loaded plugin, or from `lammpc_session_calculate_result` when the config bytes
  are given.
  The plugin or the lammpc session stays the backend.
  `caps().stress` is true only for a lammpc backend whose `Capabilities` list
  the `stress` operation; its forces then set `has_stress` and the stress.
- Errors ::
  `std::invalid_argument` when `u0`, `cutoff` or `psi` is not positive and finite; `std::runtime_error`
  when no library opens with `rgpot_engine_create`, `rgpot_engine_destroy` and
  `rgpot_engine_force`, or `rgpot_engine_create` fails.
  The lammpc constructor throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for missing or misaligned config bytes, and `std::runtime_error`
  when `liblammpc` does not load, fails the `Capabilities` handshake, reports
  unavailable, or refuses the session.
  A force throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for missing buffers and `std::runtime_error` when
  `rgpot_engine_force` returns nonzero, the lammpc result is refused, a stress
  is not 9 values, or a backend that declares `stress` returns none.

#### `rgpot::GromacsPot`

```cpp
explicit GromacsPot(const ExternalLjConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `ExternalLjConfig`.
- Units :: `u0` in eV, `cutoff` and `psi` in Angstrom; positions in Angstrom,
  energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom. The constructor stores `u0` in kJ/mol and
  the lengths in nm.
  With an `engine_path`, positions and cell go to `rgpot_md_native_force` in nm,
  and the kJ/mol energy, the (kJ/mol)/nm forces and the variance (kJ/mol
  squared) come back converted.
  The factors are in `CppCore/rgpot/ExternalPot/md_units.hpp`.
- Outputs :: a potential that evaluates in process with `rgpot::LJPot` when
  `engine_path` is empty, or through the native library otherwise.
  `caps().stress` is true only for the in-process path.
- Errors ::
  `std::invalid_argument` when `u0`, `cutoff` or `psi` is not positive and finite; `std::runtime_error`
  when the library does not open, lacks `rgpot_engine_create`,
  `rgpot_engine_destroy` or `rgpot_md_native_force`, or `rgpot_engine_create`
  fails.
  A force throws
  `std::invalid_argument` for missing buffers and `std::runtime_error` when
  `rgpot_md_native_force` returns nonzero.

The three classes are built in every configuration except
`-Dwith_rpc_client_only=true`.

#### `rgpot::OpenMMPot`

```cpp
explicit OpenMMPot(const ExternalLjConfig &config);
```

- Inputs :: `ExternalLjConfig`.
- Units :: as `rgpot::GromacsPot`.
- Outputs :: as `rgpot::GromacsPot`; the two classes share one implementation.
- Errors :: as `rgpot::GromacsPot`.

This example runs here because an empty `engine_path` evaluates in process.

```cpp
#include "rgpot/ExternalPot/ExternalPot.hpp"

#include <array>
#include <cstdio>
#include <vector>

int main() {
  rgpot::ExternalLjConfig cfg;
  cfg.u0 = 1.0;
  cfg.cutoff = 8.0;
  cfg.psi = 1.0;
  auto pot = rgpot::rgpot_gromacs_potential(cfg);

  rgpot::types::AtomMatrix positions(2, 3);
  for (int i = 0; i < 2; ++i)
    for (int k = 0; k < 3; ++k)
      positions(i, k) = 0.0;
  positions(1, 0) = 1.5;
  std::vector<int> numbers{1, 1};
  std::array<std::array<double, 3>, 3> box{{{20, 0, 0}, {0, 20, 0}, {0, 0, 20}}};
  auto [energy, forces, variance] = (*pot)(positions, numbers, box);
  std::printf("u0 = %g kJ/mol, E = %.10f eV, Fx0 = %.10f eV/A\n",
              pot->nativeU0(), energy, forces(0, 0));
  return 0;
}
```

#### `rgpot::OpenMMSessionConfig`

- Inputs :: `platform` (default `"Reference"`),
  `time_step` (default `0.001`), `friction` (default `1.0`), `temperature` (default `0.02585 * md::kKjPerEv`), `random_seed`
  (default `1`).
- Units :: `time_step` in ps, `friction` in ps^-1, `temperature` (kT) in kJ/mol.
- Outputs :: configuration struct read by `rgpot::OpenMMSession`, which manages
  an owned `OpenMM::System` and exposes `numParticles`, `masses`,
  `setPositions`, `setVelocities`, `stepLangevin` (3N projected BAOAB with
  specular planar walls and deterministic 64-bit PRNG), `stepNVE`, `state`
  (returning `OpenMMState` in nm, nm/ps, kJ/(mol nm), and kJ/mol), and
  `openmm_md_session_init` for the rgpot-unit C ABI.
- Errors :: `OpenMMSession` throws
  `std::invalid_argument` if `platform` is empty, `time_step` or `temperature`
  is not positive and finite, or `friction` is negative or non-finite.

#### `rgpot::CP2KPot::selectOrbitals`

```cpp
void selectOrbitals(int64_t key);
```

- Inputs :: `key`, an identifier of the calculation the following forces belong
  to (a band image, a ring-polymer bead).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; every later force names this key to the engine first, so each
  key restarts from its own converged orbitals.
  Every rank of a calculator names the same key before the same force.
  An engine without `cp2kc_session_select_orbitals` ignores the key.
- Errors :: none here; a force throws `std::runtime_error` when the engine
  refuses the key.

#### `rgpot::CPMDPot::selectOrbitals`

```cpp
void selectOrbitals(int64_t key);
```

- Inputs :: `key`, an identifier of the calculation the following forces belong
  to (a band image, a ring-polymer bead).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the key is applied to the live engine session when this call
  runs and is re-applied after a session recreation.
  Every rank of a calculator names the same key before the same force.
  An engine without `cpmdc_session_select_orbitals` ignores the key.
- Errors :: throws `std::runtime_error` immediately when the live engine session
  refuses the key, leaving the previous orbital key in place.

  orbital key.

- Outputs :: true when the loaded engine supports and accepts
  `cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals`.
  False when that primitive is unavailable or no session is active.
- Errors :: none; an engine rejection returns false.

#### `rgpot::CP2KPot::bindCalculators`

```cpp
static int bindCalculators(int ranks_per_calc);
```

- Inputs :: `ranks_per_calc`, the number of MPI ranks in one calculator.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: this rank's calculator index from `rgpot::bindCalculators`, which
  splits `MPI_COMM_WORLD` and hands the engine the calculator communicator. -1,
  before any split, when the default search finds no compatible library or the
  library lacks `cp2kc_adopt_calculator_comm`; -1 also when the world cannot be
  divided.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when the library's communicator callback
  changes between two loads; otherwise none.

Collective on `MPI_COMM_WORLD`: every rank calls it before the first force.
The adopting library stays loaded until the process exits.

# C++ support types

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/cpp_support.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/cpp_support.html

`meson.build` installs every header under `CppCore/rgpot`, so each type declared
there at namespace scope is part of the C++ surface.
This page covers the value types, handles, enums and helper classes that the
potential classes of [C++ potentials](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/cpp_potentials.html) and
[C++ engine-backed potentials](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/cpp_backends.html) take or return.
Nested types are described with the type that holds them.
The UMA loader keeps its archive and executable-stack helpers in
`aoti_unpack.hpp` and `aoti_execstack.hpp`; they implement `UmaPot` and are not
a supported interface.

Lengths are in Angstrom, energies in eV and forces in eV/Angstrom unless an
entry says otherwise.

### Batches and handles

#### `rgpot::types::AtomMatrix`

- Inputs :: `AtomMatrix(rows, cols)`, `AtomMatrix()`, or a nested initializer
  list; `AtomMatrix::Zero(rows, cols)` builds a zero matrix.
- Units :: none; the units are those of the data stored.
- Outputs :: a row-major matrix of doubles.
  `operator()(row, col)` reads or writes an element, `rows()`, `cols()` and
  `size()` give the extents, and the raw data pointer is available for mutation
  and for reading.
  Positions and forces cross the `PotentialBase::operator()` interface as
  `n x 3` matrices.
- Errors :: none declared; an index outside the matrix is the caller's error.

#### `rgpot::BatchInput`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: Angstrom for `positions` and `box`.
- Outputs :: one configuration: `positions` (an `AtomMatrix`), `atomic_numbers`
  and `box`, a 3 by 3 array with one cell vector per row.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::BatchResult`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: eV, eV/Angstrom and eV^2.
- Outputs :: `energy`, `forces` (an `AtomMatrix`) and `variance` of one
  configuration.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::BatchEvaluator`

- Inputs :: a `PotentialFactory` (a `std::function` that returns a
  `std::unique_ptr<PotentialBase>`) and `n_threads`, where 0 selects the
  hardware concurrency, at least 1.
  `evaluate(inputs)` takes a vector of `BatchInput`.
- Units :: those of the potential.
- Outputs :: an evaluator that owns one potential per worker, built by calling
  the factory once per worker.
  `evaluate` splits the inputs into contiguous ranges, one per worker, and
  returns a vector of `BatchResult` in which element `i= answers input =i`.
  The potentials share nothing, so no potential has to be reentrant across
  threads.
  `n_threads()` reports the worker count.
- Errors :: an empty factory or a factory that returns a null potential throws
  `std::invalid_argument` from the constructor.
  A worker that throws stops its range, and `evaluate` rethrows the exception of
  the lowest-numbered failing worker after every worker has joined.

#### `rgpot::DynLib`

- Inputs :: an optional library path.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a move-only handle on a shared library.
  `open(path)`, `close()` and `valid()` manage it, and `sym<T>(name)` and
  `sym_optional<T>(name)` resolve a symbol.
  The `MOPACPot` and `NWChemPot` directories each carry one; the class is the
  same on both.
- Errors :: `open` and `sym` throw
  `std::runtime_error` when the library or a required symbol is missing; `sym_optional`
  returns a null pointer.

#### `rgpot::MEAMLattice`

- Inputs :: one of the reference-structure enumerators from `FCC` through `SC`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the lattice used to build a MEAM element or mixed pair.
  `meam_lattice_from_name` parses the library spelling, and `meam_coordination`
  returns its first-neighbour count.
- Errors :: the parser returns false for an unknown or disallowed lattice.

#### `rgpot::MEAMElement`

- Inputs :: one MEAM library record: its name, reference lattice, atomic number,
  mass, decay lengths, lattice constant, cohesive energy, embedding constant,
  angular weights, density scale and `ibar` selector.
- Units :: Angstrom for lengths, eV for energy and g/mol for mass.
- Outputs :: the immutable element record consumed by `rgpot::MEAMParameters`.
- Errors :: validation occurs when the parameter or model object is built.

#### `rgpot::MEAMParameters`

- Inputs :: a nonempty vector of `rgpot::MEAMElement` records.
  `set` applies a parameter-file key to zero, one, two or three zero-based
  element indices, according to the key.
- Units :: eV and Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the element table and all scalar, pair and triple parameters used
  to build a model.
- Errors :: the constructor and `set` throw `std::invalid_argument` for an
  invalid lattice, density, index count, index or key value.

#### `rgpot::MEAMModel`

- Inputs :: a completed `rgpot::MEAMParameters` value.
- Units :: eV and Angstrom.
- Outputs :: immutable mixed parameters, reference densities and cubic pair
  tables.
  Its accessors expose the radial cutoff, screening radius, element records,
  pair values and angular-density functions.
- Errors :: construction throws `std::invalid_argument` when a table cannot be
  built, including an unsupported `ibar`, a second-neighbour C11 pair or a
  nonpositive cutoff width.

#### `rgpot::Fnv1a`

- Inputs :: bytes, doubles, integers, booleans or strings fed through `bytes`,
  `f64`, `i64`, `u64`, `b8` and `str`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a 64-bit FNV-1a state in `h`, starting at 0xcbf29ce484222325 with
  prime 0x100000001b3.
  A double is hashed by its bit pattern and a string by its length and then its
  bytes.
  Potentials fingerprint their configuration field by field into
  `PotentialBase::paramsKey()` with it, so cached results never cross parameter
  sets; a struct is never hashed by its bytes because of padding.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::cache::EvalCounts`

- Inputs :: none; a struct returned by `PotentialCache::counts`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `computed`, the results the kernel produced while the cache was
  attached, and `served`, the results answered from the cache without running
  the kernel.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::cache::KeyHash`

- Inputs :: a `size_t` hash.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the numeric key of a configuration, with `slice()`, which returns
  the raw bytes of the hash as a `rocksdb::Slice`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::cache::PotentialCache`

- Inputs ::
  `PotentialCache(db_path, create_if_missing = true)` opens a RocksDB database; the default constructor holds none, and `set_db`
  adopts an open one.
- Units :: none; the stored energy, forces, variance and stress are in the units
  of the potential that produced them.
- Outputs :: a result cache.
  `add_serialized` stores a configuration, `deserialize_hit` reads one back, and
  `counts()` and `reset_counts()` read and zero the computed and served
  counters, which are atomic.
  Records keep the energy and force prefix and append versioned variance and
  stress metadata; energy-and-force-only records stay readable.
  The database mutex covers the database handle only.
- Errors :: see `rgpot.PotentialCache` for a database that cannot be opened.
  Available only when the library is built with RocksDB (`rgpot.has_cache`).

### Hessian-vector products

#### `rgpot::HvpScheme`

- Inputs :: none; an enum whose values match `rgpot_hvp_scheme_t`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `Auto` (0; analytic when the potential has it, otherwise
  `Forward`), `Forward` (1; one displaced force call against the cached centre),
  `Central` (2; two displaced force calls, one on each side) and `Analytic` (3;
  the potential's `hessianVectorImpl`).
- Errors :: `Analytic` is refused for a potential without `hessianVectorImpl`.

#### `rgpot::HvpCentre`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: eV, eV^2 and eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: `energy`, `variance` and `forces`, 3 * `nAtoms` doubles in
  row-major order, at a centre geometry.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::HvpCounts`

- Inputs :: none; a struct whose fields match `rgpot_hvp_counts_t`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `products` (products answered), `forceCalls` (force evaluations
  made), `centreReused` (requests served from the cached centre) and `analytic`
  (products taken from `hessianVectorImpl`).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::HessianVectorCache`

- Inputs :: none to construct; a non-copyable object.
  `centre(pot, in)` takes a potential and a `ForceInput`.
  `apply(pot, in, v, hv, step = 0.0, scheme = HvpScheme::Auto)` takes a
  direction `v= and an output =hv`, each 3 * `in.nAtoms` doubles that must not
  overlap.
- Units :: Angstrom for `step`, which is the displacement along the direction; 0
  selects `kHvpDefaultStep` (1.0e-3).
  The product has units eV/Angstrom^2 times the direction.
- Outputs :: `centre` returns the energy and forces at `in`, served from the
  cached centre when positions, species and cell carry the same bits, and
  otherwise from one force call that becomes the centre.
  `apply` writes the product H v to `hv`; a zero direction gives a zero product
  without a call.
  `counts()` returns an `HvpCounts`, `resetCounts()` zeroes it while the centre
  stays, and `invalidate()` drops the centre, which a caller must do when the
  potential changes while the geometry does not.
  The cache may be shared between threads; the lock covers the cached centre,
  not the force calls.
- Errors ::
  `std::invalid_argument` for a malformed request and `std::domain_error` when
  the kernel returns a non-finite value.

### Fused engine calls and kept potentials

#### `rgpot::FusedSource`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `Computed` when an answer came from the engine and `Stored` when it
  came from the stored entry.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::FusedSettingsSpec`

- Inputs :: none; a struct whose fields match `rgpot_fused_settings_t`.
- Units :: as the field names say.
- Outputs :: the engine settings that change the answer at a fixed geometry:
  `periodic` (bit i set means periodic along cell vector i), `spin` (the number
  of unpaired electrons), `sccMaxIterations`, `charge` (elementary charges),
  `accuracy`, `electronicTemperature` (Kelvin), `warmMove` (Angstrom, the
  wavefunction-reuse displacement), `warmMinGap` (eV, the reuse gap threshold),
  `sccMixer` and `engineBuild`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::FusedFingerprint`

- Inputs :: none; a struct that compares equal field by field.
- Units :: floating-point fields are stored by bit pattern as 64-bit integers.
- Outputs :: everything but the positions that decides the answer of an engine
  call: the optional `atomicNumbers` and `cell` (nine bit patterns), `periodic`,
  `charge`, `spin`, `accuracy`, `electronicTemperature`, `warmMove`,
  `warmMinGap`, `sccMaxIterations`, `sccMixer`, `engineBuild` and `epoch`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::FusedKey`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the positions by bit pattern plus the `FusedFingerprint`.
  Equality is exact.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::SccNotConverged`

- Inputs :: the message string.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: an exception derived from `std::runtime_error` that reports a
  self-consistent field which did not converge.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::KeptKey`

- Inputs :: `f64(v)`, `i64(v)` and `ptr(v)` append an eight-byte field;
  `atoms(n, species)` sets the atom count and the species pointer, which may be
  null for a call without species and is read, not copied, until the key is
  kept.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: what a kept potential was built for.
  The key holds up to 16 eight-byte fields (`kBytes` is 128).
  A key that outgrows it never matches, so every call builds.
  The key compares bits: 0.0 and -0.0 differ and a NaN matches itself.
- Errors :: none; the methods are `noexcept`.

#### `rgpot::KeptCounts`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `builds` and `reuses` of the potential type on one thread.
- Errors :: none.

### Locality, staging and parallel slices

#### `rgpot::Locality`

- Inputs :: none; a struct returned by a potential's `locality()` member.
- Units :: `cutoff` is in the length unit of the potential.
- Outputs :: `cutoff` (the range of a site energy; 0 declares no finite range),
  `pairwise` (every energy term is a function of one pair distance) and
  `densities` (values per atom that the density stage sums; 0 without
  densities).
  `finite()` is true for a positive cutoff, and `forceRange()` is `cutoff` for a
  pairwise potential and twice that otherwise: the distance within which the
  atoms set the force on one atom.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::PerAtomOut`

- Inputs :: none; a struct of two pointers.
- Units :: eV for energy; the virial is in energy units.
- Outputs :: `energy`, `nAtoms` entries that sum to `ForceOut::energy`, and
  `virial`, 6 * `nAtoms` entries (xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy per atom).
  A null pointer skips that quantity.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::HalfList`

- Inputs :: none; a struct that a host fills.
- Units :: `pos` is in the host's length unit.
- Outputs :: a host's half neighbour list over its own atoms and their copies.
  Atoms `[0, nOwned)` are owned and `[nOwned, nAtoms)` are copies.
  `pos` holds 3 * `nAtoms` coordinates and `atmnrs` one atomic number per atom.
  Row `k= belongs to owned atom =rows[k]`, whose neighbours are
  `neighbours[i][0 .. count[i])`, the layout of a LAMMPS `NeighList`.
  `indexMask` clears bits a host sets in an entry besides the index, and
  `newton` selects the case in which only one of two hosts that hold an owned
  and copy pair lists it, and the stages write the copy's share for the host to
  add to its owner.
  Entries beyond the cutoff are skipped, so a list built with a skin works.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::StageTally`

- Inputs :: none; a struct that `forceStage` fills.
- Units :: eV for energy; the virial is in energy units.
- Outputs :: the host's share of the energy and of the virial W = -V sigma in
  Voigt order (xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy), plus a `PerAtomOut`.
  The share is all of a pair that only this host lists, half of a pair both
  hosts list, and the site energy of each owned atom.
  A copy's per-atom entries are written only with `HalfList::newton`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::Range`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the items `[begin, end)` as two `std::int64_t` values.
  `partition(n, slice, nslices)` returns the contiguous run for a slice; the
  runs cover `n` without overlap, in slice order, and an out-of-range slice is
  empty.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::TeamCap`

- Inputs :: `TeamCap(threads)`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a scope guard.
  While it is alive, OpenMP regions this thread opens through `Slices.hpp` start
  at most `threads` threads; zero or less lifts the cap.
  Slices and results do not change.
  The previous cap returns on destruction, and the guard is not copyable.
- Errors :: none; the constructor is `noexcept`.

#### `rgpot::TeamFrom`

- Inputs :: none; a struct of three atom counts, `two`, `three` and `more`, each
  0 by default.
- Units :: atoms.
- Outputs :: the atom counts from which a team of two threads, of three, and of
  four or more opens.
  `of(threads)` returns `two` for two threads or fewer, `three` for three and
  `more` above that, and `least()` the smallest of the three.
  `teamSize(n, from, team)` and `forEachBatchSystem` take one; the default opens
  every team at `from`.
  A potential keeps its own as `kTeamFrom` in its class, and on any thread count
  sums atom by atom in index order from `least()`, its `kTeamMinAtoms`, so its
  bits do not depend on the thread count.
- Errors :: none; the members are `constexpr` and `noexcept`.

#### `rgpot::TeamThreshold`

- Inputs :: `TeamThreshold(atoms)`.
- Units :: atoms.
- Outputs :: a scope guard.
  While it is alive, a potential called on this thread takes `atoms` as its
  threshold in place of its own and opens a team on any thread count above one,
  so a benchmark can time every team on either side of its own threshold.
  `teamThreshold(own)` returns the threshold of the innermost guard alive on
  this thread, else `own`, and `teamThresholdActive()` reports whether one is
  alive.
  The bits still do not depend on the thread count, but a call between the two
  thresholds sums in the other order and its energy can differ in the last bits.
  The previous threshold returns on destruction, and the guard is not copyable.
- Errors :: none; the constructor is `noexcept`.

#### `rgpot::QuinticSwitch`

- Inputs :: `QuinticSwitch::endingAt(cutoff, width)` builds the switch over the
  last `width` Angstrom below `cutoff`; the fields are `r_on` and `inv_width`.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the C^2 switch S(t) = 1 - 10 t^3 + 15 t^4 - 6 t^5 with t = (r -
  r_on) / (cutoff - r_on) clamped to [0, 1].
  `operator()(r)` returns `Value{s, dsdr}`, and `d2sdr2(r)` returns -60 t (1 -
  t) (1 - 2t) / w^2, where w is the width.
  Below `r_on` the switch is exactly 1, and at the cutoff it and its first two
  derivatives vanish.
- Errors :: `endingAt` throws `std::invalid_argument` unless 0 < width <=
  cutoff.

#### `rgpot::CentreDirect`

- Inputs :: `CentreDirect(i, force, energy, strain)`, with `strain` null when no
  strain is wanted.
- Units :: those of the potential.
- Outputs :: the terms of centre `i`, added to the totals as they come:
  `energy(e)`, `pair(a, j, sx, sy, sz)`, `triplet(a, j, b, k, scale, g1x, ...)`,
  `pairStrain` and `bondStrain`.
  `strained()` reports whether a strain accumulator exists.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CentreTerms`

- Inputs :: `CentreTerms(strained)`; `reset(i, bonds)` starts centre `i` with
  one row per bond in the order of `bonds`, whose entries carry the partner in
  `.j`.
- Units :: those of the potential.
- Outputs :: the same calls as `CentreDirect`, summed per atom, so the
  contribution of one centre can be added to the totals in a fixed order with
  `addTo(force, energy, strain)`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CentreLedger`

- Inputs :: `keep(terms)` takes a finished `CentreTerms`.
- Units :: those of the potential.
- Outputs :: the finished centres of one slice, in the order they finished.
  `addTo(force, energy, strain)` adds each centre into the totals as
  `CentreTerms::addTo` would, and `clear()` empties the ledger.
- Errors :: none.

### Potential parameter types

#### `rgpot::D3Damping`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `BJ`, rational Becke-Johnson damping, and `Zero`, zero damping.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::EAMTableFormat`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `Funcfl` (LAMMPS `eam`, one element), `Setfl`
  (`eam/alloy`) and `FinnisSinclair` (`eam/fs`), the three file layouts of
  [Tabulated EAM](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/eam_table.html).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::EAMTable`

- Inputs :: none; a struct of tabulated functions after the LAMMPS file2array
  step.
- Units :: `drho` is in the density unit of the file, `dr`, `cutoff` in
  Angstrom, and energies in eV.
- Outputs :: `nrho`, `drho`, `nr`, `dr`, `cutoff`, `rhomax`, the atomic numbers
  `z= and the arrays =frho` (F_a, one per element), `rhor` (rho_ab at index
  `b * n + a`, the density element b puts at an a site) and `z2r` (r phi_ab at
  index `a (a + 1) / 2 + b` for a >= b).
  Entry `m= of an array sits at =m * dr` or `m * drho`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::eam::Spline1D`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: `origin` and `h` are in the argument unit of the table.
- Outputs :: a uniform cubic Hermite table: `origin`, `h=, =inv_h`, `nseg` and
  the coefficient vector `c=; =eval(r)` evaluates it.
  The nodes sit close enough to keep a pair within 1e-12 relative of the
  analytic exponential it replaces.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::eam::ElementSpline`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: Angstrom for distances, eV for energies.
- Outputs :: one element's splines: `rho` (density), `fscale` (density force),
  `phi` (pair energy) and `fcomp` (pair force), with `Z=, =cutoff2`, a pointer
  `embed` to the embedding table, the grid constants `kOrigin` (0.05) and
  `kStep` (5e-5), and the methods `density`, `densityForce`, `pairEnergy` and
  `pairForce`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::SuttonChenScales`

- Inputs :: none; a struct returned by `sutton_chen_scales(cfg)`.
- Units :: `nearest_neighbor` in Angstrom and `well_depth` in eV.
- Outputs :: the bulk nearest-neighbour distance and the positive cohesive well
  depth of the fcc crystal for a `SuttonChenConfig`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::ZblPairCoeffs`

- Inputs :: none; a struct for one ordered pair of species.
- Units :: `zze` in eV Angstrom; the others are dimensionless coefficients.
- Outputs :: the screening exponents `d1` to `d4` scaled by the pair radius,
  `zze` (Z_i Z_j e^2), the quadratic and cubic switching coefficients of the
  force (`sw1`, `sw2`), the cubic and quartic coefficients of the energy (`sw3`,
  `sw4`) and the constant energy offset at the cutoff (`sw5`).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::ZblTables`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: see `ZblPairCoeffs`.
- Outputs :: the sorted unique atomic numbers `z= and the coefficients =pairs`,
  a `z.size()` by `z.size()` row-major table of `ZblPairCoeffs`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::GFNMethod`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `GFNFF`, `GFN0xTB`, `GFN1xTB` and `GFN2xTB`, the methods of
  `XTBPot`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::TBLiteMethod`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `GFN1`, `GFN2` and `IPEA1`, the methods of `TBLitePot`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::TorchDeterminismPolicy`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `Fast` (0; leave process-global LibTorch state alone) and `Strict`
  (1; apply deterministic algorithms, the math attention backend, no TF32 and
  deterministic cuDNN).
  The flags are process-global.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::CP2KScfError`

- Inputs :: the message string.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: an exception derived from `std::runtime_error`, thrown when the SCF
  did not converge.
  The shim agrees on the outcome over the calculator's communicator, so every
  rank of the calculator throws it for the same call and no rank aborts the
  world.
  A caller may reject the geometry and continue.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::UmaContract`

- Inputs :: none; a struct built from the metadata JSON embedded in a `.pt2`
  package.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: optional fields `task_name`, `charge`, `spin`, `z_set`, `counts`
  (atomic number to atom count), `natoms`, `natoms_min`, `natoms_max`,
  `nedges_min`, `nedges_max` and `z_max`, plus the declared shapes `pos_decl`
  and `edge_decl` (each with `known`, a list of `Axis` values and the original
  `text`).
  Every field is optional: a key the exporter did not write is not checked.
  A dynamic package declares `pos_shape` `natoms,3` and `edge_index_shape`
  `2,nedges`.
  The static function `fixedEdgesFromShapes` returns the second extent of
  `edge_index` from the exporter's `shapes` dictionary, or nothing for a missing
  or non-fixed entry.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::UmaContractError`

- Inputs :: `field`, `package`, `actual` and a location string.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a `std::runtime_error` for a charge, spin, task or composition that
  disagrees with what the package was exported for.
  `field()` is the metadata key (`charge`, `spin`, `task_name`, `z_set`,
  `counts` or `natoms`), `package()` the embedded value and `actual()` the value
  the config or the input carries.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::UmaShapeError`

- Inputs :: `field`, `actual` and `package`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a `std::runtime_error` for positions or an edge list that are not
  the shape the package was compiled for.
  The message names both shapes and contains `shape is`.
  `field()`, `actual()` and `package()` return the parts.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::XcGrid`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none; the arrays carry the units of the host.
- Outputs :: `npts` and `nbf`, and row-major arrays `chi` (nbf * npts), `dchi`
  (3 * nbf * npts), `lapl_chi` (nbf * npts, or null) and `hess_chi` (6 * nbf *
  npts, or null).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::XcMo`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: `e_ia` is in the energy unit of the host.
- Outputs :: occupied and virtual MO blocks for TDA and RPA: `nao`, `nocc`,
  `nvir`, `Co` (`nao` by `nocc`), `Cv` (`nao` by `nvir`) and
  `e_ia` (`nocc` by `nvir`, with `e_ia[i, a] = e_vir[a] - e_occ[i]`), all
  row-major.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::XcFields`

- Inputs :: none; a struct returned by `XcKernel::fieldsFromDensity`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the vectors `rho`, `sigma`, `tau` and `lapl`, each `npts` long, and
  `grad_rho`, 3 * `npts` with xyz packed.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::XcKernel`

- Inputs :: `XcKernel(name)`, a contraction name from `XcKernel::catalog()`, for
  example `xck_gga_r_o2`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: an in-process exchange-correlation contraction kernel over the
  `libxckernel` C ABI.
  It is not a geometry potential and has no `PotentialConfig` arm: the operands
  are collocation values, named Libxc derivative arrays and fields, and the
  results are AO matrices.
  `contract(grid, scal, out)` assembles the scalar operands in the order of
  `scalNames()` and accumulates into `out` (`nbf * nbf`, added to).
  The static members `fieldsFromDensity`, `transitionDm`, `rpaTransitionDm`,
  `projectOv`, `tdaSigma` and `rpaSigma` build fields and sigma vectors from the
  MO blocks, and `applyFxc`, `tdaSigma` and `rpaSigma` take a ground-state
  operand map and a host Coulomb matrix.
  The C kernels are reentrant on distinct output buffers, and distinct instances
  may run concurrently.
- Errors :: `contract` returns 2 for an incomplete grid and otherwise the C ABI
  code, 0 on success.
  Laplacian kernels need `lapl_chi`.
  `catalog()` is empty without `-Dwith_xckernel`.

#### `rgpot::fortranpots::FortranWorkspace`

- Inputs :: none to construct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the owner of one Fortran workspace handle, available through
  `get()`.
  A copy gets a workspace of its own, so a cloned potential never shares a
  neighbour table.
  The object is not movable.
- Errors :: none.

### Long-range summands

#### `rgpot::lr::Pair`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: one neighbour pair with atom indices `i= and =j`, the vector
  `(x, y, z)` equal to r_j + S H - r_i for the lattice shift S and cell H, and
  its length `r`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::DualList`

- Inputs :: `DualList(short_cut, long_cut, skin)`;
  `update(pos, n, box, periodic)` takes a row-major box of nine values.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: two pair lists at two cutoffs, `short_pairs()` and `long_pairs()`,
  each rebuilt only when an atom has moved past the skin.
  `short_rebuilt()` and `long_rebuilt()` report whether the last update rebuilt
  them.
  A null `box` or `periodic = false` builds a vacuum cell large enough that no
  periodic image lies inside the long cutoff.
  The object is not copyable.
- Errors :: none declared.

#### `rgpot::lr::CellGeom`

- Inputs :: none; a struct with a `fractional(r, s)` method.
- Units :: Angstrom and Angstrom^-1.
- Outputs :: the cell matrix `H=, its inverse =inv`, the reciprocal vectors
  `recip` (rows b_i with b_i . a_j = delta_ij and no factor 2 pi) and the
  `volume`.
  `fractional` computes s = r H^-1, and the physical wave vector is k = 2 pi
  sum_i m_i recip[i].
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::Neumaier`

- Inputs :: values added with `add(x)` or another accumulator.
- Units :: those of the summands.
- Outputs :: a compensated sum, `total()` being `sum + c`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::CoulombMethod`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `Ewald` (tinfoil boundary; orthorhombic and triclinic cells),
  `SPME` (smooth particle-mesh Ewald with the same split and a B-spline order
  from 3 to 16) and `DSF` (Fennell-Gezelter damped shifted force, gas phase).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::ChargeSource`

- Inputs :: `load(in, q, total)` takes a `ForceInput`.
- Units :: elementary charges.
- Outputs :: an abstract provider of one charge per atom in `q` and the net
  charge in `total`, which is the G=0 background charge and must match the sum
  of the per-atom charges.
- Errors :: set by the implementation.

#### `rgpot::lr::FixedCharges`

- Inputs :: `FixedCharges(q, total)`.
- Units :: elementary charges.
- Outputs :: a `ChargeSource` that returns the charges it was given.
- Errors :: none declared.

#### `rgpot::lr::FnCharges`

- Inputs :: `FnCharges(fn, user)`, where `fn` has the signature
  `void (const ForceInput &, double *, double *, void *)`.
- Units :: elementary charges.
- Outputs :: a `ChargeSource` that calls `fn` with the user pointer.
- Errors :: set by the function.

#### `rgpot::lr::ChargeResponse`

- Inputs :: `accumulate(in, dE_dq, force)`.
- Units :: `dE_dq` is the derivative of the energy with respect to each charge.
- Outputs :: an abstract hook for the chain rule of charges that depend on
  coordinates: `dE_dq[i]` is the partial of the electrostatic energy at fixed
  positions, and `accumulate` adds the resulting force.
- Errors :: set by the implementation.

#### `rgpot::lr::ElecOut`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: eV; `strain` is the derivative of the energy with respect to the
  strain, in Voigt order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy.
- Outputs :: `energy`, `strain` and `has_stress`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::PmeTrace`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: microseconds for the `_us` fields; the `_team` fields are thread
  counts.
- Outputs :: the time spent in the spread, FFT, kernel, gather and real-space
  stages of a particle-mesh Ewald call and the team size each used.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::CudaCoulombIn`

- Inputs :: none; a struct for the CUDA Coulomb path.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: `method` (0 Ewald, 1 PME), the positions `pos`, charges `q`, the
  count `n=, the net charge =total`, the `box`, the pair arrays
  (`pair_i`, `pair_j`, `pair_x`, `pair_y`, `pair_z`, `pair_r`) with `npair`, and
  the parameters `alpha` (0.3), `cutoff` (9.0), `kmax` (4), `grid` (16) and
  `order` (4).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::DispersionKind`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `D3BJ`, `D4`, `MBD` and `QDO`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::D3BjParam`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none are stated; the values are the defaults of the damping.
- Outputs :: the Becke-Johnson damping parameters `s6` (1.0), `s8` (0.7875),
  `s9` (1.0), `a1` (0.4289), `a2` (4.4407) and `alp` (14.0).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::D4BjParam`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none are stated; the values are the defaults of the damping.
- Outputs :: `s6` (1.0), `s8` (0.95948085), `s9` (1.0), `a1` (0.38574991), `a2`
  (4.80688534) and `alp` (16.0).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::RatioSource`

- Inputs :: `load(in, h, c6)`.
- Units :: dimensionless ratios.
- Outputs :: an abstract provider of per-atom ratios `h` and, optionally,
  dispersion coefficients `c6`.
- Errors :: set by the implementation.

#### `rgpot::lr::UnitRatios`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a `RatioSource` whose ratios are all 1.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::lr::FixedRatios`

- Inputs :: `FixedRatios(h, c6)`.
- Units :: dimensionless.
- Outputs :: a `RatioSource` that returns the vectors it was given.
- Errors :: none declared.

#### `rgpot::lr::RatioResponse`

- Inputs :: `jacobians(in, dh, dc6)`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: an abstract hook that returns the Jacobians of the ratios with
  respect to the geometry.
- Errors :: set by the implementation.

#### `rgpot::lr::DispersionModel`

- Inputs :: `evaluate(in, pairs, h, c6, cfg, energy, F, strain, has_stress)`.
- Units :: eV, eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: an abstract dispersion summand with `name()` and `kind()`.
  `evaluate` adds the energy and forces for a pair list and writes the strain
  derivative.
- Errors :: set by the implementation.

### Neighbour lists

The C ABI of these types is in [Neighbour-list C ABI](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/nlist_abi.html).

#### `rgpot::nlist::Code`

- Inputs :: none; an enum shared with the C ABI.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `Ok` (0, never thrown), `Abi` (1), `Null` (2), `Cutoff` (3), `Box`
  (4), `Shape` (5), `Short` (6), `Nomem` (7) and `Skin` (8), matching the
  `RGPOT_NLIST_*` values.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Error`

- Inputs :: a `Code` and a message.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a `std::runtime_error` for a rejected query; `code()` is the C ABI
  value and `what()` a sentence the caller can show.
  Builders throw it and leave a previous table in place.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Shell`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `Half` keeps one direction of each pair, with the same image rule
  vesin uses for a self image; `Full` keeps both directions.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Pairs`

- Inputs :: none; a struct with a `shell` field (default `Half`).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the shape of one pair per interaction.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Cluster4`

- Inputs :: none; an empty struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the shape of four consecutive central atoms, one partner and a
  4-bit mask.
  The interactions are the full set; there is no half cluster, so the type has
  no shell.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Cut`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `Strict` keeps pairs with distance strictly below the cutoff;
  `Loose` keeps pairs out to cutoff + skin, which a Verlet rebuild needs.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Fields`

- Inputs :: none; a struct of three booleans, all true by default.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `shifts`, `vectors` and `distances`, the arrays a table or chunk
  carries; an unset field is left empty rather than filled with zeros.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Query`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: `cutoff` and `skin` in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: `cutoff`, `skin`, `shape` (a `Pairs` or `Cluster4`, default
  `Pairs{}`), `cut` (default `Strict`), `periodic` (all true) and `fields`.
  `build` and `Builder` store the pairs and `Walk` streams them; there is no
  setting that stores nothing.
- Errors :: `Error` with code `Cutoff`, `Shape`, `Skin` or `Box` when the query
  is rejected.

#### `rgpot::nlist::View`

- Inputs :: none; a struct of spans.
- Units :: `vector` and `distance` in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a non-owning view of a structure-of-arrays table: `first`,
  `second`, `shift` (empty or three per pair), `vector` (empty or three per
  pair), `distance` and `mask` (one byte per pair; 0xff for a pair list, bits 0
  to 3 for a cluster of four).
  The spans are invalidated by the next rebuild of the table that owns them.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Table`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: as `View`.
- Outputs :: the owning arrays `first`, `second`, `shift`, `vector`, `distance`
  and `mask`, the `device` (0 for host memory) and `stored`.
  `size()` is the pair count, `view()` returns a `View` and
  `column_major_vectors()` the vectors as a Fortran `(3, npairs)` array over the
  same memory.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Systems`

- Inputs :: none; a struct of pointers.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: several systems that do not interact: `positions`, the
  concatenation of every system; `count`, the atoms of each; `systems`, their
  number; and `box9`, nine lattice values per system.
  A count of 0 is an empty system.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Batch`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: as `Table`.
- Outputs :: the pairs of a `Systems` build: `pairs`, a `Table` whose `first`
  and `second` index the concatenated positions, and `system`, which names the
  system that owns each pair.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Builder`

- Inputs :: `update(positions, n, box9, query)`.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a stored list with a skin rebuild.
  A later update keeps the table while every atom has moved by at most half the
  skin and the cell and the query are unchanged; skin 0 rebuilds unless the
  coordinates match.
  `table()`, `builds()` and `reused()` report the table, the rebuild count and
  whether the last update kept the table.
  One thread uses a builder; two builders may update at the same time.
- Errors :: `Error` when the geometry is rejected; the previous table stays.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Buffers`

- Inputs :: none; a struct of spans.
- Units :: as `View`.
- Outputs :: caller-owned buffers for one chunk.
  `first` and `second` have the same length, the most pairs this pull writes;
  `shift` and `vector` are empty or three times that length; `distance` and
  `mask` follow the request.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Walk`

- Inputs :: `Walk(positions, n, box9, query)`, which borrows `positions` and
  `box9` until it is destroyed; `pull(dest, done)` takes a `Buffers`.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a stream of pairs for one central atom, or one cluster of four, at
  a time into caller storage, without a list of the whole system.
  `pull` returns the number of pairs written and sets `done` when the geometry
  is exhausted.
  One thread uses a walk.
- Errors :: a requested field whose span is too short throws `Error` and does
  not advance.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Image`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: how the minimum image is formed: `Round` is the orthorhombic
  truncation used by the pair kernels, `Half` is one correction about the
  half-box after coordinates have been wrapped, and `General` uses
  `MinimumImage` for a non-orthogonal cell or a periodic side shorter than the
  search.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Mode`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `Stored` keeps a Verlet list of candidate pairs; `Stream` walks the
  cells and stores nothing beyond the atoms and the bins; `Auto` stores when the
  candidate index fits in the memory the operating system reports as available
  and streams otherwise.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Spec`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: `cutoff` and `skin` in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: `cutoff`, `skin`, `periodic` (all true), `image` (default `Round`)
  and `mode` (default `Auto`).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::MinimumImage`

- Inputs :: `MinimumImage(cell, periodic)`, a row-major cell of nine values and
  three periodic flags.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the nearest periodic image d - n H. `fold(dx, dy, dz)` folds a
  displacement in place, and `foldWithin(dx, dy, dz, within2)` returns false
  when every image is longer than the squared length `within2`.
  A cell whose condition estimate would spend more than half the double
  significand is Minkowski-reduced, and a basis that is still ill-conditioned
  searches the 27 images with coefficients in -1, 0 and 1.
  The static `searches()` counts the folds on the calling thread that searched
  over images.
- Errors :: a singular or non-finite cell, or an index that does not fit in an
  `int64`, throws.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Neighbours`

- Inputs :: `update(xyz, n, box9, spec)`.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: candidate pairs around one configuration.
  A stored list is reused while every atom has moved by at most half the skin
  and the cell, the count and the spec are unchanged; skin 0 reuses it only when
  the coordinates and the cell match.
  An infinite cutoff or skin makes every pair a candidate, bins nothing and
  stores nothing.
  `forDirected`, `forHalf`, `forCellTeam` and the per-atom walks visit the
  pairs, `mode()`, `streaming()`, `allPairs()`, `reused()`, `builds()` and
  `slots()` report the state, and `offsets()` and `neighbours()` expose the
  stored index.
  Candidates lie inside the cutoff plus the skin; the caller drops the rest.
- Errors :: see `MinimumImage` for a rejected cell.

#### `rgpot::nlist::NeighborList`

- Inputs :: `skin`, the extra search distance in Angstrom.
- Units :: Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a reusable pair list for `orderedPairs`.
  A null list passed to `orderedPairs` rebuilds every call.
  The stored pairs (`lo`, `hi` and the folded `dx`, `dy`, `dz`) are reused while
  every atom has moved by at most skin/2 and the cell is unchanged; skin 0
  reuses the list only when the coordinates match.
  `use_stored` is true when `dx`, `dy` and `dz` match the current coordinates,
  and `clear()` drops the list.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::nlist::Overlap`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: what a pair of atoms on one point does: `Skip` ignores it and
  `Poison` makes the energy NaN.
- Errors :: none.

### Engine table, handshake and plugins

#### `rgpot::engine::Unsupported`

- Inputs :: the message string.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a `std::runtime_error` that a setting hook throws for a value the
  backend cannot take.
  The adapter returns 3 with the reason in `last_error`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::engine::Backend`

- Inputs :: none; a struct a backend hands the adapter at create.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the potential `pot`, the
  `model_path` whose SHA-256 identifies the loaded model (empty without a model file), and the optional hooks `set_charge_spin(charge, spin)`, `set_num_threads(intra_op, inter_op)`, `select_orbitals(key)`
  and `copy_orbitals(from_key, to_key)`.
  An empty hook means the backend does not support that setting.
- Errors :: `set_charge_spin` throws `Unsupported`, before changing anything,
  for a value it cannot take.

#### `rgpot::engine::Created`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `backend`, a pointer, and `error`, the reason when `backend` is
  null.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::engine::Builtin`

- Inputs :: none; a struct read from the `BuiltinParams` arm of the engine
  configuration.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `name`, lowercased, and `library`, an optional explicit engine
  library path.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::engine::Sha256`

- Inputs :: data fed through `update(data, size)`; `reset()` restarts.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a SHA-256 digest.
  `hex_digest()` returns the lowercase hexadecimal digest and resets the object, and the static `of_file(path)`
  digests a whole file.
- Errors :: `of_file` returns an empty string when the file cannot be read.

#### `rgpot::abi::CxxSoversionEntry`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: one recorded no-cache layout hash: `tag`, a platform tag of the
  form `os-arch-stdlib-datamodel`, and `hash`.
  `kCxxSoversionTable` lists one entry for each platform that CI builds.
  How to update it is in the developer guide
  [ABI bump rules](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/contributing/developer/abi-bump.html).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::abi::Expectation`

- Inputs :: none; a struct with defaults.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: what the host requires of a backend: the protocol `family` (default
  `rgpot.potentials`) and
  `protocol_major` (1) with `protocol_minor_min`, the `schema_id`, the bridge
  `bridge_abi_major`, `bridge_abi_minor_max`, `bridge_layout`, the DLPack
  `dlpack_major` and `dlpack_minor_max`, `bridge_features` (0x3, gradient and
  batch) and `required_operations` (default energy and forces).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::abi::ProfileResult`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: `energy_h` is in Hartree.
- Outputs :: `ok`, `energy_h` and `message`, 512 bytes.
  The layout equals that of every backend result (`NWChemCResult`, `CPMDCResult`
  and the others), which makes the prefix-generic function pointers of
  `ProfileLoader` well defined.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::abi::ProfileLoader`

- Inputs ::
  `load(prefix, explicit_path = "")`; the static `candidates(prefix, explicit_path)`
  lists the library paths tried.
- Units :: those of the profile functions.
- Outputs :: a loader that opens the first loadable candidate and resolves the
  full minimum profile into the public function pointers
  `abi_version`, `version`, `last_error`, `available`, `finalize`, `configure`,
  `session_create_from_config`, `session_configure`,
  `session_destroy`, `session_calculate_result`, `calculate_result_from_config`,
  `potential_result_size_for_force_input` and `capabilities_result`.
  `loaded()`, `prefix()` and `capabilities()` (the flat `Capabilities` message
  bytes) report the state.
- Errors :: `load` throws `std::runtime_error` naming every missing symbol, so a
  non-conforming build fails at load time instead of at dispatch.

#### `rgpot::plugin::LoadedPlugin`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `handle`, the descriptor pointer `desc`, the library `path` and a
  `library` reference that keeps the mapping alive.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::plugin::PluginRegistry`

- Inputs :: `PluginRegistry::instance()` returns the process-wide registry; the
  object is not copyable.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `discover()` loads descriptors from the directories named by
  `RGPOT_PLUGIN_PATH`,
  `load_plugin(path)` loads one library, `register_builtin(desc)` adds a
  descriptor of static lifetime,
  `list_plugins()` returns the names, `find(name)` returns the entry (valid across later registrations) and `retain_library(desc)`
  keeps a registered library mapped for a live instance.
- Errors :: `load_plugin` returns false for an invalid library or an existing
  plugin name.

#### `rgpot::DerivativeCaps`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: derivative capability flags reported by Hessian-vector helpers.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::DerivativeCounts`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: counters of derivative evaluations and cache reuse.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::HessianScheme`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the Hessian construction strategy (finite-difference or analytic
  paths).
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::SumComponent`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: eV and eV^2.
- Outputs :: one term record from `SumPot`: name, enabled flag, weight, energy
  contribution and variance contribution.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::SumTerm`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none on metadata; child potentials use standard rgpot units.
- Outputs :: one configured child term in `SumPot`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::abi::BytesView`

- Inputs :: a pointer and size.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a non-owning byte span for ABI helpers.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::abi::CandidateOptions`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: loader options that rank or filter engine candidates.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::abi::PinnedEngine`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: one engine candidate pinned by the loader policy.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::ad::Derivatives2`

- Inputs :: none; a dual-number carrier.
- Units :: value and derivative units follow the expression it carries.
- Outputs :: value, gradient and Hessian entries for analytic model derivatives.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot::pair_hessian::Block`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: eV/Angstrom^2 on Hessian entries.
- Outputs :: one dense block in the pair Hessian assembly.
- Errors :: none.
