# i-PI driver client

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/ipi_driver.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/ipi_driver.html

`IPIDriver` is the client side of the i-PI socket protocol.
Its header is `CppCore/rgpot/IPIPot/IPIDriver.hpp`.
It connects to a server and answers each geometry with an rgpot evaluation.
`IPIPot` is the server side.
[The i-PI how-to](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/howto/ipi.html) shows both directions.
The protocol is Ceriotti, More and Manolopoulos, CPC 185, 1019 (2014).
The i-PI 3.0 paper is J Chem Phys 161, 062504 (2024).
The class is built with `-Dwith_ipi` (CMake `RGPOT_WITH_IPI`).
The default, `auto`, builds it everywhere except Windows.

On the wire, lengths are bohr, energies hartree and forces hartree/bohr.
The cell arrives with its lattice vectors in the columns.
The driver transposes it to rgpot rows.
The virial is the extensive tensor `W = -sigma V` in hartree, row-major.
That is the tensor `IPIPot` reads.

### `rgpot::IPIDriverConfig`

- Inputs :: `address` (default empty) and `species` (default empty).
  `unix_prefix` (default `/tmp/ipi_`).
  `connect_timeout_s` (default 30.0) and `timeout_s` (default 0.0).
  `cutoff` (default 0.0) and `stress_step` (default 0.0).
  `preserve_open_cell` (default false).
  `extras_json` (default true).
  `address` is `unix:/absolute/path`, `unix:<name>`, `tcp:<host>:<port>` or
  `tcp:<port>`.
  `unix:<name>` connects to `unix_prefix` followed by the name.
  `tcp:<port>` uses the host 127.0.0.1.
  `species` holds one atomic number per atom, in the server's atom order.
- Units :: `connect_timeout_s` and `timeout_s` are seconds.
  `timeout_s` bounds each message, and 0 waits forever.
  `cutoff` is in Angstrom.
  It is the range used to tile a thin periodic cell and to pad an open box.
  `stress_step` is a dimensionless strain.
  Above 0 it turns on the central-difference virial for a stress-free kernel.
- Outputs :: a plain struct read by `IPIDriver`.
- Errors :: `IPIDriver` throws `std::invalid_argument` for these values.
  An empty species list or an atomic number outside 1 to 118.
  More atoms than the protocol limit of 10^7.
  An address without a `unix:` or `tcp:` prefix, or an empty UNIX address.
  A UNIX name containing `/`, or a path too long for the socket address.
  A missing, out-of-range or zero port.
  A timeout or cutoff that is negative or not finite.
  A `stress_step` outside [0, 0.1).

### `rgpot::IPIDriver`

```cpp
IPIDriver(const IPIDriverConfig &config, IPIEvaluator evaluate);
```

- Inputs :: `config`, an `rgpot::IPIDriverConfig`.
  `evaluate`, an `rgpot::IPIEvaluator`.
  `IPIEvaluator` is `std::function<void(const ForceInput &, ForceOut *)>`.
  It gets the positions, the atomic numbers and the cell.
  Its `ForceOut` arrives with zeroed forces.
  The `eval` member of `rgpot::spec::Built` fits it.
  That struct is what `engines/pot_spec.hpp` returns.
  A lambda around any potential's `forceImpl` fits it too.
- Units :: the evaluation sees Angstrom, with the cell vectors as rows.
  It returns eV, eV/Angstrom and any Cauchy stress in eV/Angstrom^3.
  The driver sends hartree, hartree/bohr and the virial `-sigma V` in hartree.
- Outputs :: a driver that has checked its configuration and not connected.
- Errors :: `std::invalid_argument` for an empty `evaluate`.
  The configuration errors are those of `rgpot::IPIDriverConfig`.

The driver follows the reference `driver.py`.
`STATUS` gets `NEEDINIT` before the first `INIT`.
It gets `HAVEDATA` while a result waits for `GETFORCE`, and `READY` otherwise.
`INIT` carries a bead index and an init string, and both are kept.
An init string that requests `batch_size` above 1 is rejected: one driver
connection evaluates one structure per request.
`POSDATA` carries the cell, its inverse and the positions.
Its atom count must equal the length of `species` on every message.
`GETFORCE` gets `FORCEREADY`, the energy, the atom count and the forces.
The virial and the extra string follow.
`EXIT` closes the connection and ends `run()`.
A server that closes between two messages ends it the same way.
ASE's `SocketIOCalculator` closes like that, and ASE's own client agrees.

ASE sends a singular cell (zero volume) for a cluster.
The driver evaluates such a geometry in a cube at least 100 Angstrom wide.
The cube is also wider than twice the cluster extent plus `cutoff`.
This is the open box of the PLUMED and GROMACS hosts.
A periodic cell can be no wider than twice `cutoff` along an axis.
The driver tiles such a cell along that axis.
The energy is divided by the number of copies.
The forces of the first copy are sent.
With `preserve_open_cell=true` a singular cell and the original positions reach
the evaluator unchanged.

An evaluation may report no stress while `stress_step` is above 0.
The virial is then a central difference of the energy under strain.
Positions and cell are deformed together by `stress_step`.
That costs twelve extra evaluations per geometry.
Otherwise a missing stress is sent as a zero virial.

`extras_json` sends `{"virial": "<source>", "virial_units": "hartree"}`.
The source is `kernel`, `finite_difference` or `none`.
Without it the extra string is empty.

### `rgpot::IPIDriver::connect`

```cpp
void connect();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: the retry window `connect_timeout_s` is in seconds.
- Outputs :: an open connection; a call while connected does nothing.
  A refused, reset or missing socket is retried every 50 ms.
  The retries stop when `connect_timeout_s` ends.
  So the driver may start before the server listens.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when the window ends without a connection.
  The same when the error cannot be retried or a TCP host does not resolve.

### `rgpot::IPIDriver::step`

```cpp
bool step();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: `timeout_s` in seconds bounds the message.
- Outputs :: true after a `STATUS`, `INIT`, `POSDATA` or `GETFORCE` message.
  False after `EXIT`, or when the server closes between messages.
  Both close the connection.
- Errors :: `std::runtime_error` when the driver is not connected.
  The same on a timeout.
  The same on a disconnect inside a message (`i-PI server disconnected`).
  The same on an unexpected header.
  The same on an `INIT` string length outside 0 to 2^20.
  The same when an `INIT` string requests `batch_size` above 1.
  The same on a `POSDATA` atom count that differs from `species`.
  The same on non-finite positions or cell values.
  The same on `GETFORCE` before `POSDATA`.
  An exception from the evaluation propagates unchanged.
  Every error closes the connection.

### `rgpot::IPIDriver::run`

```cpp
void run();
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: those of `connect` and `step`.
- Outputs :: returns after `EXIT`.
- Errors :: those of `connect` and `step`.

### `rgpot::IPIDriver::close`

```cpp
void close() noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the connection is closed without a message.
  The next connection starts at `NEEDINIT`.
  The destructor calls it.
- Errors :: none.

### `rgpot::IPIDriver::config`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const IPIDriverConfig &config() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: those of `rgpot::IPIDriverConfig`.
- Outputs :: the configuration given to the constructor.
- Errors :: none.

### `rgpot::IPIDriver::endpoint`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const std::string &endpoint() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `unix:<path>` with the prefix applied, or `tcp:<host>:<port>`.
- Errors :: none.

### `rgpot::IPIDriver::connected`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] bool connected() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: true from a successful `connect` until `EXIT`, `close` or an error.
- Errors :: none.

### `rgpot::IPIDriver::bead`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] int32_t bead() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the bead index of the last `INIT`, or -1 before one.
- Errors :: none.

### `rgpot::IPIDriver::initString`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] const std::string &initString() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the init string of the last `INIT`, empty before one.
- Errors :: none.

### `rgpot::IPIDriver::evaluations`

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] uint64_t evaluations() const noexcept;
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the number of `POSDATA` messages evaluated.
  The finite-difference virial does not add to it.
- Errors :: none.

This example compiles here.
Running it needs a server listening on `/tmp/ipi_rgpot`.
`IPIPot` with `unix:rgpot` is one; ASE's `SocketIOCalculator` is another.

```cpp
#include "rgpot/IPIPot/IPIDriver.hpp"
#include "rgpot/LennardJones/LJPot.hpp"

#include <cstdio>

int main() {
  rgpot::LJPot pot({.u0 = 0.0104, .cutoff = 8.5, .psi = 3.40});
  rgpot::IPIDriverConfig cfg;
  cfg.address = "unix:rgpot";
  cfg.species.assign(108, 18);
  cfg.cutoff = 8.5;
  rgpot::IPIDriver driver(cfg, [&pot](const rgpot::ForceInput &in,
                                      rgpot::ForceOut *out) {
    pot.forceImpl(in, out);
  });
  driver.run();
  std::printf("served %llu geometries\n",
              static_cast<unsigned long long>(driver.evaluations()));
  return 0;
}
```

### The rgpot-ipi-driver program

`engines/rgpot_ipi_driver.cpp` builds the `rgpot-ipi-driver` program.
It is built with `-Dwith_ipi` and installed with the other engine programs.
It wraps `IPIDriver` around any potential that `engines/pot_spec.hpp` builds.
[Potential names and options](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/potential_names.html) lists the names.
`--list` prints the names this build accepts.

```bash
rgpot-ipi-driver --pot "LJ u0 0.0104 psi 3.40 cutoff 8.5" --species 'Ar*108' -u -a rgpot
rgpot-ipi-driver -m EAMCell --species-from start.xyz -a localhost -p 31415
```

| Flag                     | Meaning                                                |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `--pot SPEC`             | name and `key value` options in one string             |
| `-m`, `--mode NAME`      | name only, as `i-pi-py_driver -m`                      |
| `-o`, `--param LIST`     | `key=value` pairs separated by commas, for `-m`        |
| `--list`                 | print the accepted names and exit                      |
| `--species LIST`         | symbols or atomic numbers; `Sym*N` repeats             |
| `--species-from FILE`    | symbols from an `.xyz`, `.extxyz` or eOn `.con` file   |
| `-u`, `--unix`           | UNIX socket; `-a` is a name or an absolute path        |
| `-a`, `--address`        | TCP host or UNIX name, default `localhost`             |
| `-p`, `--port`           | TCP port, default 12345                                |
| `-S`, `--sockets-prefix` | prefix of a UNIX name, default `/tmp/ipi_`             |
| `--cutoff A`             | cutoff for a spec without one; tiling and box range    |
| `--preserve-open-cell`   | pass a singular cell through instead of padding it     |
| `--stress-step H`        | finite-difference virial for a stress-free potential   |
| `--timeout S`            | seconds per message; 0, the default, waits forever     |
| `--connect-timeout S`    | seconds to retry connecting, default 30                |
| `--no-extras`            | empty extra string instead of JSON                     |
| `-v`, `--verbose`        | connection, `INIT` and call count on stderr            |

The species list is needed because the protocol carries no species.
It has one entry per atom, in the server's atom order.
The tiling and open-box range is the potential's own cutoff when it has one.
`LJ`, `Morse` and `SuttonChen` have one.
For a kernel with a fixed range, `--cutoff` sets it.
The exit code is 0 after `EXIT` or a close between messages.
It is 2 for a usage error, an unknown potential or a bad species list.
It is 1 when the connection or an evaluation fails.
`SIGPIPE` is ignored, so a peer that closes cannot kill the program.

---

# Command-line programs

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/cli.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/cli.html

The build installs five programs for users, and the repository carries one
project tool, `potctl`.
Each entry lists the arguments, the units on the wire or on the pipe, and how
the program fails.

### Potential programs

`potserv`, `potserv_mpi`, `rgpot-lj` and `rgpot-ipi-driver` are installed unless
rgpot is built as a Meson subproject.
`rgpot-eval` is built for the tests and the how-to pages and is not installed.

#### `potserv`

```bash
potserv <port> <PotentialType>
```

- Inputs :: `port`, the TCP port to listen on, and `PotentialType`, the backend
  name.
  `LJ`, `LJCluster`, `Morse`, `ZBL`, `Eckart`, `MullerBrown`,
  `ModifiedMullerBrown`, `LEPS-HH2`, `LEPS-HCl2`, `LEPS-FH2`, `DoubleWell`,
  `CoupledProtonWell`, `NWChem[:basis[:theory[:xc]]]` and `CPMD` are always
  offered.
  The rest depend on the build: `CuH2`, `CBE`, `IPI:unix:<path>`,
  `IPI:tcp:<host>:<port>`, `XTB`, `GFNFF`, `GFN0xTB`, `GFN1xTB`, `TBLite`,
  `TBLiteGFN2`, `TBLiteGFN1`, `TBLiteIPEA1`, `D3`, `D4`,
  `Metatomic:<model_path>[:<device>]`, `Uma:<model_path>[:<task>]`,
  `Skala[:<basis>]` and `CP2K`.
  The program is built only with the RPC stack and not with
  `with_rpc_client_only`.
- Units :: those of the `ForceInput` of [the schema](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/capnp_schema.html),
  which default to Angstrom and eV.
- Outputs :: a server on `localhost` that prints "Server running on port N with
  TYPE potential." and serves the `Potential` interface until it is stopped.
- Errors :: fewer than two arguments print the usage with the names of this
  build and exit with 1.
  A port that is not an integer prints a notice and falls back to 12345.
  An unknown type, a type this build lacks, or an `IPI` type without an address
  exits with 1.
  `CP2K` in a build without it exits with 1 and names the build option.

#### `potserv_mpi`

```bash
mpirun -n N potserv_mpi <port> <PotentialType>
```

- Inputs :: the arguments of `potserv`.
- Units :: as `potserv`.
- Outputs :: the same source as `potserv`, built with `RGPOT_POTSERV_MPI` and
  linked to MPI.
  Rank 0 serves the RPC and the other ranks work for it.
  It is built only when MPI is found; see [the MPI page](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/mpi.html).
- Errors :: as `potserv`; more than one rank with a type other than `NWChem`,
  `CPMD` or `CP2K` is refused, because only those backends are collective.

#### `rgpot-eval`

```bash
rgpot-eval Name [key value ...] < geometry
```

- Inputs :: `Name` and key value options, built the way a LAMMPS
  `pair_coeff * * Name ...` line builds them (see [[file:potential_names.org][Potential
  names]]), and a geometry on standard input: the atom count, nine cell values
  (one vector per row) and one `z x y z` line per atom.
  The argument count must be even and at least two.
- Units :: positions in Angstrom; the stress is in eV/Angstrom^3.
- Outputs :: `energy E`, one `force i fx fy fz` line per atom and, when the
  kernel reports a stress, a `stress` line with nine row-major values.
  Numbers carry 17 significant digits.
- Errors :: exit status 2 for a usage error or a malformed geometry, with the
  missing item named on standard error; 1 when the potential cannot be built or
  throws, with its message on standard error.

#### `rgpot-lj`

```bash
rgpot-lj < input
rgpot-lj --kJ-per-eV
```

- Inputs :: standard input holds `u0 cutoff psi`, the atom count, nine cell
  values and one `z x y z` line per atom.
  `--kJ-per-eV` prints a factor and exits without reading input.
- Units :: as `LJPot`; the factor is the library's kJ/mol per eV.
- Outputs :: `energy E` and one `force i fx fy fz` line per atom, in `%.16e`
  form.
  No stress is printed.
- Errors :: exit status 2 for a malformed input, and 1 with the text "evaluation
  rejected the geometry" when the kernel returns a non-zero status.

#### `rgpot-ipi-driver`

```bash
rgpot-ipi-driver --pot "Name [key value ...]" (--species LIST | --species-from FILE) [options]
```

- Inputs :: exactly one of `--pot SPEC` (a name and key value options in one
  string) and `-m, --mode NAME` with `-o, --param LIST` (`key=value` pairs
  separated by commas); exactly one of `--species LIST` (symbols or atomic
  numbers separated by commas, with `Sym*N` repeating a symbol) and
  `--species-from FILE` (an `.xyz`, `.extxyz` or eOn `.con` file).
  The i-PI protocol carries no species, so the list has one entry per atom in
  server order.
  Socket options follow
  `i-pi-py_driver`: `-u, --unix`, `-a, --address` (default `localhost`), `-p, --port` (default 12345, ignored with `-u`) and `-S, --sockets-prefix` (default `/tmp/ipi_`).
  Other options are `--cutoff A`, `--stress-step H`, `--timeout S` (0 waits
  forever), `--connect-timeout S` (default 30), `--no-extras` (send an empty
  extra string instead of JSON), `-v, --verbose`, `--list` (print the names of
  this build and exit) and `-h, --help`.
- Units :: `--cutoff` is in Angstrom: the cutoff of a potential whose spec names
  none, and the range used to tile thin periodic cells and pad open boxes.
  `--stress-step` is the strain step of a central-difference virial for a
  potential that reports no stress; 0 sends a zero virial.
- Outputs :: a client that connects to an i-PI server and answers it with an
  rgpot potential.
  It is built only with i-PI support.
  See [the i-PI driver page](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/ipi_driver.html).
- Errors :: a usage error prints the synopsis and exits with 2: a flag without a
  value, both or neither of `--pot` and `-m`, `-o` without `-m`, both or neither
  of the species options, a negative `--cutoff`, a value that is not a number,
  or an unknown argument.

### Project tool

`potctl` is the repository's project control plane.
It lives beside `rgpot-core` in the Cargo workspace, is not published, and is
run as `cargo run -q -p potctl -- <command>` from inside the checkout, which it
locates by `meson.build`, `pixi.toml` and `rgpot-core/`.
A failure prints `error: potctl: <message>` and exits with a non-zero status.

#### `potctl release sync`

```bash
potctl release sync VERSION
```

- Inputs :: `VERSION`, a semantic version with an optional leading `v`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: writes the version into `[workspace.package]` of the root
  `Cargo.toml`, the one hand-written copy.
  `cog` then regenerates the other copies from it.
- Errors :: a string that is not a semantic version is refused, as is a
  `Cargo.toml` with no version under `[workspace.package]`.

#### `potctl release assert`

```bash
potctl release assert [VERSION] [--require-changelog]
```

- Inputs :: an optional `VERSION`, usually the tag without the `v`, and
  `--require-changelog` (or the environment variable `REQUIRE_CHANGELOG`), which
  also demands a `## [version]` section in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: nothing on success.
  Every version copy, among them `meson.build`, `CMakeLists.txt`,
  `towncrier.toml`, `pixi.toml` and the C header, agrees with `Cargo.toml`.
- Errors :: a copy that differs, a release version that is not semver, a version
  that differs from `VERSION`, or a missing changelog section when one is
  required.

#### `potctl release notes`

```bash
potctl release notes VERSION [-o PATH]
```

- Inputs :: `VERSION` and `-o, --out PATH`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the `CHANGELOG.md` section of the version, on standard output or in
  the file, for the body of a release.
- Errors :: a version that has no section.

#### `potctl ci preflight`

```bash
potctl ci preflight [--no-lockstep]
```

- Inputs :: `--no-lockstep`, which skips the version agreement check.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: "preflight ok" when `meson.build`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `pixi.toml`,
  the `Cargo.toml` of `rgpot-core` and of `potctl`, `towncrier.toml`,
  `pyproject.toml` and `cog.toml` exist and, by default, the versions agree.
  With `--no-lockstep` it prints the release version instead.
- Errors :: a list of the missing files, or the lockstep error.

#### `potctl ci darwin-env`

```bash
eval "$(potctl ci darwin-env [--force] [--conda-prefix DIR] [--sdkroot DIR])"
```

- Inputs :: `--force`, which emits the macOS plan even when the runner is not
  macOS; `--conda-prefix`, which overrides `CONDA_PREFIX`; `--sdkroot`, which
  overrides `SDKROOT`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `export` and `unset` lines that use the host Apple clang and SDK
  while keeping the conda search paths on macOS under pixi, and a no-op on
  Linux.
  Meson then takes `$POTCTL_MESON_EXTRA`.
  The build commands below apply the same plan themselves.
- Errors :: none beyond a failure to read the environment.

#### `potctl ci meson-test`

```bash
potctl ci meson-test --rpc true|false --cache true|false [--build-dir DIR] [--no-darwin]
```

- Inputs :: `--rpc` and `--cache`, the feature switches of a matrix leg, each
  `true`, `false`, `1=, =0`, `yes`, `no`, `on` or `off`; `--build-dir` (default
  `bbdir`); `--no-darwin`, which skips the macOS plan.
  The environment variables `POTCTL_MESON_EXTRA` (extra setup arguments) and
  `POTCTL_WITH_MPI=enabled` (turns MPI on) are read.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `meson setup`, `meson compile` and `meson test --print-errorlogs`.
- Errors :: a switch that is not a boolean, and the failure of the first step
  that fails.

#### `potctl ci cmake-test`

```bash
potctl ci cmake-test --rpc true|false --cache true|false [--build-dir DIR] [--no-darwin]
```

- Inputs :: the arguments of `meson-test`, with `--build-dir` defaulting to
  `build`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: CMake configure, build and `ctest --output-on-failure`.
- Errors :: as `meson-test`.

#### `potctl ci build-test`

```bash
potctl ci build-test --sys meson|cmake --rpc true|false --cache true|false [--build-dir DIR] [--no-darwin]
```

- Inputs :: `--sys`, which selects `meson` or `cmake`, and the arguments of the
  two commands above; the build directory defaults to `bbdir` for Meson and
  `build` for CMake.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the run of `meson-test` or `cmake-test`.
- Errors :: "unknown build sys" for another `--sys` value, and the errors of the
  chosen command.

#### `potctl ci release-assert`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the lockstep check of `release assert`, a read of `cog.toml`, and
  `cog --version`.
- Errors :: a failed assertion, an empty or invalid `cog.toml`, or a missing or
  failing `cog`.

#### `potctl ci towncrier-draft`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `towncrier build --draft` when `docs/newsfragments` holds a `.md`
  file; otherwise a note that the draft is skipped.
- Errors :: no usable `towncrier`, or its failure.

#### `potctl ci cog-bump-dry-run`

```bash
potctl ci cog-bump-dry-run [--bump auto|patch|minor|major]
```

- Inputs :: `--bump`; without it the workspace version is used.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a `cog bump --dry-run`.
  Without `--bump` a non-zero `cog` status is reported as a note and does not
  fail the command.
- Errors :: a `--bump` value other than the four listed, and, with `--bump`, the
  failure of `cog`.

#### `potctl ci cog-check`

```bash
potctl ci cog-check [--from BASE]
```

- Inputs :: `--from`, the base commit of a pull request.
  Without it the check covers the whole repository and is advisory.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `cog check` over `BASE..HEAD`, followed by a check that every
  commit subject in the range is a conventional subject.
- Errors :: "cog check failed" when `cog` rejects the range, and the first
  commit subject that is not conventional.

#### `potctl ci towncrier-check`

```bash
potctl ci towncrier-check --compare-with BASE
```

- Inputs :: `--compare-with`, the base commit.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `towncrier check --compare-with BASE`.
- Errors :: an empty base, no usable `towncrier`, or its failure.

#### `potctl ci ensure-torch-metatomic`

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: CPU Torch and the metatensor, metatomic and vesin layout under the
  `purelib` of the active Python for the metatomic leg.
  A missing or CUDA Torch is replaced by a CPU one.
  The Torch and CMake paths are appended to `GITHUB_ENV`.
- Errors :: a missing Python or a failed install step.

#### `potctl ci metatomic-test`

```bash
potctl ci metatomic-test [--build-dir DIR] [--rpc]
```

- Inputs :: `--build-dir` (default `bbdir-mta`) and `--rpc`, which builds with
  the RPC stack and so turns on the `libuma_engine` plugin.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the Meson metatomic and vesin build and test.
- Errors :: the failure of the first step that fails.

#### `potctl ci plugin-test`

```bash
potctl ci plugin-test [--build-dir DIR] [--no-darwin]
```

- Inputs :: `--build-dir` (default `bbdir-plugin`) and `--no-darwin`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a Meson build with the plugin host, then `PluginTest`,
  `PluginContractTest`, `ExternalPluginTest` and the rest of the plugin suite.
- Errors :: the failure of the first step that fails.

#### `potctl ci xtb-tblite-test`

```bash
potctl ci xtb-tblite-test [--build-dir DIR]
```

- Inputs :: `--build-dir` (default `bbdir-tb`).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the xtb and tblite potentials leg.
- Errors :: the failure of the first step that fails.

#### `potctl ci xckernel-test`

```bash
potctl ci xckernel-test [--build-dir DIR]
```

- Inputs :: `--build-dir` (default `bbdir-xck`).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a Meson build with `-Dwith_xckernel=true` and the `xckernel` test
  suite.
  The default matrix leaves `with_xckernel` off.
- Errors :: the failure of the first step that fails, or a build whose tests
  lack `XcKernelGoldens`.

#### `potctl ci rpc-integ`

```bash
potctl ci rpc-integ [--server-bin PATH]
```

- Inputs :: `--server-bin` (default `bbdir/CppCore/potserv`).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `tests/rpc_integ.py` run against that server with `python`, or
  `python3` when `python` is missing.
- Errors :: a missing script, or the failure of the test.

#### `potctl ci bridge-server-build`

```bash
potctl ci bridge-server-build [--build-dir DIR]
```

- Inputs :: `--build-dir` (default `bbdir_server`).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the Meson RPC server build of the client bridge stress leg.
- Errors :: the failure of the build.

#### `potctl ci bridge-client-build`

```bash
potctl ci bridge-client-build [--build-dir DIR]
```

- Inputs :: `--build-dir` (default `build_client`).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the CMake RPC client-only build of the same leg.
- Errors :: the failure of the build.

#### `potctl ci bridge-stress`

```bash
potctl ci bridge-stress [--server-build-dir DIR] [--client-build-dir DIR] [--port N] [--potential NAME]
```

- Inputs :: the two build directories (defaults
  `bbdir_server` and `build_client`), `--port` (default 12345) and `--potential`
  (default `LJ`).
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: starts `potserv` from the server build, waits two seconds, runs
  `ctest` in the client build against it, then stops the server.
- Errors :: "missing potserv" when the server build has not run, and the failure
  of `ctest`.

#### `potctl ci bridge-stress-full`

- Inputs :: the options of `bridge-stress`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the whole leg in one call: the server build, the client build, then
  the stress run.
- Errors :: the failure of the first step that fails.

#### `potctl cosmo build`

- Inputs :: none; the environment variables `COSMO`, `POTCTL_COSMO_OUT`,
  `POTCTL_COSMO_ARCHS`, `COSMO_CC` and `COSMOCC_ARCHES` configure the build.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: builds `potctl` as a Cosmopolitan APE binary with a nightly `rustc`
  and a `cosmocc` linker shim, and builds the host `potctl-cosmo-ld` when it is
  missing.
  The command exists only in a build with the `cosmo-host` feature and is not
  compiled into the APE binary itself.
- Errors :: a missing toolchain or an unset `COSMO`.

# Build options

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/build_options.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/build_options.html

Meson is the primary build.
CMake declares fewer options than Meson.
Both tables list every option the build files declare.
`docs/doccheck.py facts` fails when a row disagrees with `meson_options.txt` or
`CMakeLists.txt`.

### Meson

Pass an option to `meson setup` as `-D<option>`<value>=.
A `feature` option takes `enabled`, `disabled` or `auto`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| `with_tests` | boolean | `false` | Build and register the C++ tests (`meson test`). |
| `with_examples` | boolean | `false` | Build the examples. Unless `with_rpc_client_only` is set, this requires fmt and uses Eigen3 when it is found. |
| `with_xtensor` | boolean | `false` | Link xtensor and xtensor-blas and define `WITH_XTENSOR`. |
| `with_eigen` | boolean | `false` | Link Eigen3. A missing Eigen3 is an error only when this option is true. |
| `with_rpc` | boolean | `false` | Build the Cap'n Proto RPC stack and the `potserv` server. |
| `with_rpc_client_only` | boolean | `false` | Build only the RPC client and the dlopen frontends. Implies the RPC stack; disables the server and the cache. |
| `with_mdi` | boolean | `false` | Build the optional `rgpot-mdi` compatibility frontend over `rgpot_potential_t`. Needs `with_rust_core=true` and the official MDI Library at runtime. |
| `with_cache` | boolean | `false` | Link RocksDB and xxhash and build `PotentialCache`. |
| `pure_lib` | boolean | `true` | When false, link fmt and define `NOT_PURE_LIB`. |
| `use_openmp` | boolean | `true` | Compile the OpenMP regions of the cell walk and the potentials. Off builds every target serially, with no OpenMP flag or runtime on `librgpot` or its consumers. |
| `with_rust_core` | boolean | `false` | Build `rgpot-core` with cargo and link `librgpot_core.a`, or `librgpot_bundle.a` when the fast pair list is on too. The cargo features `rpc`, `mdi` and `cache` follow `with_rpc`, `with_mdi` and `with_cache`. The C header is the checked-in `rgpot-core/include/rgpot.h`; cbindgen does not run. |
| `team_min_atoms` | integer | `8192` | Minimum atom count for opening an OpenMP team in a call without a threshold of its own, such as a neighbour-list build or `EMTPot`. Each classical potential keeps its own counts as `kTeamFrom`. |
| `with_fast_nlist` | feature | `auto` | linkcell/minimage pair list. Auto when cargo and rustc 1.89 or newer are found; otherwise the C++ pair scan is used. |
| `with_cp2k` | feature | `disabled` | CP2KPot, the potserv CP2K backend and libcp2kc_rgpot.so against libcp2k (pkg-config libcp2k); needs with_rpc |
| `with_potlibc` | feature | `disabled` | Build `libpotlibc_engine.so` against the potlibc C API. |
| `with_mpi` | feature | `disabled` | Build `librgpot_mpi`, which `librgpot` loads with `dlopen` so calculator groups can split and share across ranks. `librgpot` itself never links MPI. |
| `with_xtb` | boolean | `false` | Link xtb (`dependency('xtb')`) and build `XTBPot`. |
| `with_xckernel` | boolean | `false` | Build the in-process libxckernel XC kernel (`XcKernel`, generated C ABI; not a Potential). |
| `with_dftd3` | boolean | `false` | Link s-dftd3 (installed, or the s-dftd3 wrap built static) and build `D3Pot`. Needs a Fortran compiler. |
| `with_dftd4` | boolean | `false` | Link dftd4 (installed, or the dftd4 wrap built static) and build `D4Pot`. Needs a Fortran compiler. |
| `lapack` | combo | `auto` | LAPACK vendor for the dftd4 wrap and the nested multicharge wrap. Choices: `auto`, `mkl`, `mkl-rt`, `openblas`, `netlib`, `custom`. |
| `with_expr` | boolean | `false` | Compile the vendored OpenMM Lepton (`third_party/lepton`) and build `ExprPot`. |
| `with_tblite` | boolean | `false` | Link tblite and build `TBLitePot`. |
| `with_metatomic` | boolean | `false` | Build the Metatomic potential and engine against torch and metatomic. |
| `with_uma` | boolean | `false` | Build the UMA potential (`UmaPot`) and engine plugin against torch alone, without the metatensor and metatomic packages. Torch is a Python package or a libtorch tree named by `RGPOT_TORCH_ROOT` (`lib`, `include` and a `build-version` file), and without `with_metatomic` the plugin records that library directory as its run path. `with_metatomic` builds the plugin too. The plugin needs `with_rpc`. Neither `UmaPot` nor the plugin is built when `with_python` is true. |
| `with_skala` | boolean | `false` | Build `SkalaPot`, Skala XC through NWChemPot and `libnwchemc`. Needs `with_rpc` or `with_rpc_client_only`. |
| `with_python` | boolean | `false` | Build the pip-installable Python package (`rgpot._core`). |
| `with_fortran_pots` | feature | `auto` | Fortran 2018 kernels in `CppCore/rgpot/fortran` (CuH2, EDIP, LenoskySi, EAMAl, FeHe, WaterH, SWSi and the Tersoff silicon gather). `auto` builds them when a Fortran compiler is found. Independent of the RPC options. |
| `with_highway` | feature | `auto` | Google Highway runtime ISA dispatch for the `rgpot::simd` LJ, Morse, EAM and orthorhombic-fold kernels; the shipped potentials do not call them (see [SIMD](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/explanation/simd.html)). `auto` uses libhwy >= 1.2, or the `highway` wrap when its source tree is already unpacked under `subprojects/`; `enabled` also downloads it. `disabled` keeps the scalar kernels. |
| `with_ipi` | feature | `auto` | i-PI socket server Potential (IPIPot), driver client (IPIDriver) and rgpot-ipi-driver (POSIX sockets). auto is on except on Windows. |
| `with_water` | boolean | `false` | Flexible TIP4P, SPC/E and TIP4P-Pt kernels. Defaults false, matching the eOn with_water option. |
| `with_eam_table` | boolean | `false` | EAM and Finnis-Sinclair potentials read from LAMMPS funcfl, setfl and eam/fs tables. |
| `with_orca` | boolean | `false` | ORCAPot: ORCA energy and gradient through the orca executable run as a child process (POSIX). The executable is found at run time. |
| `with_cbe` | feature | `disabled` | Link `potlibc` and build the CBE (CH5 2008) H + CH4 frontend. potlibc must provide `potlibc_gradient_jet`. |
| `with_lammps` | feature | `auto` | LAMMPS pair_style rgpot and the lj/cut comparison. Needs the lammps Python module. pair_style rgpot also needs lammps_src. |
| `lammps_src` | string | `(empty)` | LAMMPS src directory that contains pair.h, matching the liblammps that will load the plugin. |
| `lammps_exe` | string | `(empty)` | lmp built from lammps_src. When set, the LAMMPS test also runs pair_style rgpot. |
| `with_gromacs` | feature | `auto` | GROMACS mdrun -plumed using the RGPOT collective variable. |
| `with_gromacs_dropin` | feature | `disabled` | librgpot_gromacs, the libcp2k API that GROMACS built with `-DGMX_CP2K=ON` links, so mdrun takes QM/MM energies and forces from any rgpot potential. |
| `gromacs_dropin_gmx` | string | `(empty)` | gmx of a double-precision GROMACS linked against librgpot_gromacs. Empty looks for gmx_d on PATH and skips the mdrun tests without it. |
| `with_openmm` | feature | `auto` | OpenMM shifted Lennard-Jones comparison. |
| `with_plumed` | feature | `auto` | PLUMED RGPOT collective variable. |
| `with_long_range` | boolean | `false` | Build the Ewald, PME, dispersion and NLH summands (`CppCore/rgpot/LongRange`). |
| `with_cuda` | boolean | `false` | Compile the long-range CUDA path with nvcc and link cudart. Used only with `with_long_range`. |

|-|-|-|-|

The test `mdi_concrete_potentials` runs when python can import `mdi`. |
| `RGPOT_BUILD_TESTS` | BOOL | ON when rgpot is the top-level project, else OFF | Build the tests. |
| `RGPOT_WITH_CP2K` | BOOL | OFF | `CP2KPot`, the `potserv` CP2K backend and `libcp2kc_rgpot` against libcp2k. |

# PotentialConfig arms

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/potential_config.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/potential_config.html

This page lists the arms of the Cap'n Proto `PotentialConfig` union and what
`potserv` does with each.

### rgpot user parameters (`PotentialConfig`) over RPC

Backend options for a live `Potential` go in `PotentialConfig`
(`CppCore/rgpot/rpc/Potentials.capnp`, a copy of the pinned potentials-schema).
It is a union whose arms and ordinals are `none` @0, `nwchem` @1, `cpmd` @2,
`metatomic` @4, `lammps` @5, `xtb` @6, `tblite` @7, `uma` @8, `lj` @9, `morse`
@10, `zbl` @11, `d3` @12, `d4` @13, `mopac` @14, `skala` @15, `expr` @16, `cp2k`
@17, `composite` @18, `d2` @19, `d2cpmd` @20 and `mullerBrown` @21.
`composite`, `d2`, `d2cpmd` and `mullerBrown` are local additions
(`CppCore/rgpot/rpc/local/composite.diff`, `d2.diff`, `d2cpmd.diff` and
`muller-brown.diff`) to the pinned schema, as are `D4Params.periodic`
(`d4-periodic.diff`) and `D2CpmdParams.symmetry` (`d2cpmd-symmetry.diff`).
Outside the union, `common` @3 is a `CommonMethodSpec` overlay.
Geometry stays on `ForceInput`; `configure(config)` applies method and backend
setup only.
`potserv` applies `nwchem`, `cpmd`, `morse`, `composite`, `d2`, `d2cpmd` and
`mullerBrown` on the matching backend.
It applies `cp2k` on a build with CP2K and `d4` on a build with dftd4.
`none` is a no-op on every backend.
Every other arm gets `ok=false` with a message that names the arm.
An arm from a newer schema is named by its discriminant.
`D3Pot` stays an in-process `Potential` summand; `potserv` refuses the `d3` arm.

### NWChem arm (`PotentialConfig.nwchem` / `NWChemParams`)

With `potserv <port> NWChem`, pass `configure` with the `nwchem` arm set.
The payload fields (`basis`, `theory`, `scfType`, `charge`, `multiplicity`,
`enginePath`, `nwchemRoot`, `task`, `title`, `memoryMb`, `scratchDir`,
`permanentDir`, `inputBlocks`, `inputStanzas`) are NWChem-specific.

Python: `tests/nwchem_params.py` builds `PotentialConfig` with the `nwchem` arm.
The helper uses `RGPOT_NWCHEM_ENGINE` for `enginePath` and `NWCHEM_TOP` for
`nwchemRoot` when explicit values are not supplied.
For BLYP, set `theory="dft"` and `scfType="blyp"`.
`calculate` still needs a loadable `libnwchemc` engine.

### Morse arm (`PotentialConfig.morse` / `MorseParams`)

With `potserv <port> Morse`, pass `configure` with the `morse` arm set.
`MorseParams` carries `de`, `a=, =re` and `cutoff`, with the platinum defaults
of `MorseConfig` (0.7102 eV, 1.6047 1/Angstrom, 2.897 Angstrom, 9.5 Angstrom).
The server rebuilds its `MorsePot` from those values and keeps its switch width,
so the next `calculate` uses them.
A non-finite value, a cutoff that is not positive, or a cutoff below the switch
width gets `ok=false` and leaves the pot as it was.
`tests/rpc_integ.py` doubles `de` and checks that the energy at `re` doubles.

### Muller-Brown arm (`PotentialConfig.mullerBrown` / `MullerBrownParams`)

With `potserv <port> MullerBrown`, the `mullerBrown` arm rebuilds the surface.
The six list fields are `amplitude`, `a=, =b`, `c=, =x0` and `y0`.
Their schema names are `MullerBrownParams.amplitude`, `MullerBrownParams.a`,
`MullerBrownParams.b`, `MullerBrownParams.c`, `MullerBrownParams.x0` and
`MullerBrownParams.y0`.

The parameter rule is the same wherever these lists are set.
Each call describes the whole surface.
Nothing carries over from an earlier call or from the pot it replaces.
A list that is empty, or not set, takes its published default.
A list of four finite values replaces that default.
Any other length, or a non-finite value, is an error.
An unset list reads as an empty one, so the wire cannot tell them apart.
That leaves no way to keep a value from an earlier call.

The rule applies to these entry points.
- `configure` on a `MullerBrown` server.
  An error, or any arm other than `mullerBrown`, gets `ok=false` and leaves the
  pot as it was.
- The classical engine reads `BuiltinParams.config` when `name` is
  `muller_brown`.
  An arm that does not belong on a builtin is refused with an error that names
  it.
- The `rgpot.MullerBrownPot` constructor.
  An error raises `ValueError`.
- `rgpot::MullerBrownConfig`, whose members start at the published defaults.
  A field that is not assigned stays at its default.
- `rgpot_builtin_muller_brown_new`, where a NULL config is the defaults.
  Its arrays are fixed at four values, so it has no empty form.

### Composite arm (`PotentialConfig.composite` / `CompositeParams`)

With `potserv <port> Composite`, pass `configure` with the `composite` arm set.
The server starts with an empty sum, whose energy is 0.
`CompositeParams.terms` is a list of `CompositeTerm`, summed in order:

| field | type | default | meaning |
|-------|------|---------|---------|
| `CompositeTerm.name` | Text | empty | label in the component record and the log; empty becomes `term<i>` |
| `CompositeTerm.enabled` | Bool | true | a disabled term is recorded and never built or evaluated |
| `CompositeTerm.weight` | Float64 | 1.0 | multiplies the term's energy, forces and stress; the sign is allowed |
| `CompositeTerm.pot` | `PotentialSpec` | unset | the child backend |

The `builtin` arm of `PotentialSpec` builds `lj`, `morse`, `zbl`, `d2`, `d2cpmd`
and, on a build with dftd4, `d4` with the parameters of its `config` arm (`lj`,
`morse`, `zbl`, `d2`, `d2cpmd`, `d4`, or `none` for the defaults) and
`composite` (or `sum`) for a nested sum.
The `cpmd` arm builds a `CPMDPot` from its `CPMDParams`, which loads `libcpmdc`.
Other `PotentialSpec` arms, an unknown builtin name, a builtin config arm that
belongs to another backend, an enabled term without a `pot` and a weight that is
not finite get `ok=false` with a message that names the term, and leave the
previous sum in place.
`CppCore/rgpot/rpc/CompositeConfigure.hpp` holds the mapping, which
`libcomposite_engine` also uses.
`tests/rpc_integ.py` checks that a weight of -1 cancels a term, that a weight
scales one, that a disabled term with an unknown name is not built, that an LJ
plus D2 sum is the sum of the two and loses the D2 again under a second D2 term
at weight -1, and that every other arm is refused.

### D2 arm (`PotentialConfig.d2` / `D2Params`)

With `potserv <port> D2`, pass `configure` with the `d2` arm set; the same
struct is the `config` of a `d2` builtin in a composite term.
The server starts with the BLYP defaults and rebuilds its `D2Pot` from the arm.

| field | type | default | meaning |
|-------|------|---------|---------|
| `D2Params.s6` | Float64 | 1.2 | global scaling (BLYP) |
| `D2Params.d` | Float64 | 20.0 | steepness of the damping |
| `D2Params.sr` | Float64 | 1.1 | scale on the tabulated R0 |
| `D2Params.cutoff` | Float64 | 150.0 | pair cutoff over all images, Angstrom |
| `D2Params.functional` | Text | empty | a dftd3 `-func` name; when set, its `s6` and `d` replace the two fields |

An unknown functional, a cutoff that is not positive and finite, or an `sr` that
is not positive gets `ok=false` and leaves the pot as it was.
`tests/rpc_integ.py` switches the functional to PBE and checks that the energy
scales by the ratio of the two `s6`.

### CPMD D2 arm (`PotentialConfig.d2cpmd` / `D2CpmdParams`)

With `potserv <port> D2Cpmd`, pass `configure` with the `d2cpmd` arm set; the
same struct is the `config` of a `d2cpmd` builtin in a composite term, where a
weight of -1 takes CPMD's built-in D2 back out of a `cpmd` term.

| field | type | default | meaning |
|-------|------|---------|---------|
| `D2CpmdParams.s6` | Float64 | 1.2 | CPMD's `S6GRIMME` (BLYP) |
| `D2CpmdParams.alpha` | Float64 | 20.0 | damping exponent |
| `D2CpmdParams.vdweps` | Float64 | 0.01 | pairs with \(\lvert\alpha (r/R_r - 1)\rvert \ge 1/\mathrm{vdweps}\) drop |
| `D2CpmdParams.functional` | Text | empty | a CPMD functional name; when set, its `set_s6` value replaces `s6` |
| `D2CpmdParams.symmetry` | Int32 | -1 | the `SYMMETRY` code of the run, which picks the branch of CPMD's `pbc3`; -1 reads it from the box, which cannot name 12 |

An unknown functional, a `vdweps` that is not positive or a `symmetry` that is
not -1, 1 to 8, 12 or 14 gets `ok=false` and leaves the pot as it was.
`tests/rpc_integ.py` checks the PBE switch as for `d2` and that a composite of
`d2cpmd` at weight -1 and `d2` is the difference of the two.

### D4 arm (`PotentialConfig.d4` / `D4Params`)

With `potserv <port> D4` on a build with dftd4, pass `configure` with the `d4`
arm set; the same struct is the `config` of a `d4` builtin in a composite term.
The server starts with the defaults below and rebuilds its `D4Pot` from the arm.

| field | type | default | meaning |
|-------|------|---------|---------|
| `D4Params.functional` | Text | `"pbe"` | dftd4 method key; dftd4 supplies its rational damping parameters (`"blyp"` for BLYP) |
| `D4Params.charge` | Float64 | 0.0 | total charge, elementary charges |
| `D4Params.atm` | Bool | true | the three-body (ATM) term |
| `D4Params.periodic` | Bool | false | pass the box as a 3D lattice and return the stress; off, the box is ignored |

A functional dftd4 has no parameters for gets `ok=false` with dftd4's message
and leaves the pot as it was.
`tests/rpc_integ.py` switches to periodic BLYP and checks the refusals when
`potserv` lists `D4`.

### CPMD arm (`PotentialConfig.cpmd` / `CPMDParams`)

With `potserv <port> CPMD`, pass `configure` with the `cpmd` arm set.
`CPMDParams` is method and backend setup only; each `calculate()` call still
carries geometry in `ForceInput`.

The rgpot frontend loads `libcpmdc` at run time and forwards serialized
`CPMDParams` to that C ABI.
Engine lookup tries `CPMDParams.enginePath`, then
`CPMDC_LIBRARY`, `RGPOT_CPMDC_ENGINE`, `RGPOT_CPMD_ENGINE`, and the default
shared-library names.
A non-empty `CPMDParams.cpmdRoot` is exported as `CPMD_ROOT` before the engine
loads (not on Windows).

The payload fields are method-level defaults (`functional`, `cutOffRy`,
`charge`, `multiplicity`, `task`, `title`, `memoryMb`), frontend hints
(`enginePath`, `cpmdRoot`), file placement (`scratchDir`, `permanentDir`), raw
`inputBlocks`, and structured `inputSections`.
`CPMDInputSection` has typed arms for `system`, `cpmd`, `dft`, `atoms` and
`set`, a `generic` arm, a `raw` arm, directive-only arms for the other CPMD
sections, and typed arms for `&VDW`, `&PROP`, `&LINRES`, `&PIMD`, `&PATH`,
`&TDDFT`, `&RESP`, `&EXTE` and `&VECTORS`.
The typed `cpmd` section includes wavefunction and geometry optimization,
molecular dynamics, orbital and geometry convergence thresholds, iteration
limits, timestep, electron mass, CP/BO/EH/PT/classical MD variants, MD file,
Nose/Berendsen/Langevin/annealing/quench thermostat controls,
RATTLE/SHAKE, constraints, Trotter factor, restart, print/store, center
molecule,
DIIS/ODIIS/PCG/diagonalization, free-energy, interface, QMMM, bicanonical, CDFT, properties, and trajectory controls. The typed `dft` section includes functional, LSD, GC cutoff, XC driver, LIBXC, LR kernel, refunct, MTS high/low
functionals, HFX, HFX screening, Hubbard, alpha, beta, old/new code selection,
correlation, exchange, and Becke88 controls.

Python: `tests/cpmd_params.py` builds `PotentialConfig` with the `cpmd` arm.
The helper uses `CPMD_ROOT` for `cpmdRoot` and `CPMDC_LIBRARY`,
`RGPOT_CPMDC_ENGINE` or `RGPOT_CPMD_ENGINE` for `enginePath` when explicit
values are not supplied.
Its `input_sections` argument builds the `generic`, `system`, `cpmd`, `dft`,
`atoms`, `set` and `raw` arms without raw Cap'n Proto builder code in clients.

Typed `atoms` sections carry pseudopotential entries and structured `directives`
for ATOMS keywords that are not pseudopotential entries.
Per `CppCore/rgpot/CPMDPot/README.md`, the engine groups `ForceInput`
coordinates into `&ATOMS`, requires entries for every atomic number present in a
step, and without an `atoms` section has built-in BLYP defaults for H and O
only.

The `cpmd` configure result is `ok=false` when no usable `libcpmdc` engine can
be loaded or when the engine rejects the params.
The integration script exercises RPC `configure()` with the `cpmd` arm:

```bash
pixi run -e rpctest python tests/rpc_integ.py \
  --server-bin build/CppCore/potserv \
  --cpmd-smoke
```

# Stillinger-Weber silicon (1985)

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/sw_si.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/sw_si.html

`StillingerWeberSi` (`PotType::SWSi1985`) evaluates the silicon potential of F.
H. Stillinger and T. A. Weber, Phys.
Rev. B 31, 5262 (1985), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.31.5262.

The two-body and three-body parameters are equation (2.7).
Sigma is 0.20951 nm.
Epsilon is the value equation (2.9) prints, 3.4723e-12 erg per atom pair.
With 1 erg = 1e-7 J and the CODATA electron-volt (1.602176634e-19 J) that is
2.16723920 eV.
`PotType::SWSi`, the Fortran `SWPot` kernel, is not this potential.
It uses eOn's rescaled epsilon, 2.16826 × 1.06767385 = 2.3149945 eV.
The ratio of that epsilon to the published value is 1.068176741337.

The product is copied from
`client/potentials/SW/SWFortran.f90` in TheochemUI/eOn.
The file header says "Last change: AA 3 Apr 2002", and the same lines are
present at tags `svn-Dec16_2020` and `v2.8.0`:

```
  EPSILON = 2.16826D0 * 1.06767385d0, &  !* 1.07d0
  LAMBDA  = 21.0d0,                   &  !* 1.07d0
```

Lambda stays 21 and is not multiplied.
Neither that file nor the rgpot port (commit 7a3b5016, per `rgpot_sw.f90`)
derives 1.06767385.
The factor is untraced.

### Calls

Lengths are Angstrom and the energy is eV.
The cell is periodic in each direction.
`forceImpl` writes the force, which is minus the gradient.
`energyAndGradient` writes the energy and dE/dx for one configuration.
`energyAndGradientBatch` writes both for several configurations that share one
cell and one species list, so a caller enters the library once per batch.
A configuration is spread across the threads `OMP_NUM_THREADS` requests when
`StillingerWeberSi` would not open a team for that atom count.
`teamSize` decides, from `StillingerWeberSi::kTeamMinAtoms` and
`StillingerWeberSi::kTeamFrom`, and a call already inside a team or with one
thread requested does not spread.
Each configuration is evaluated whole.
A configuration that would open a team, or a batch that contains one, stays on
the calling thread.
The bits match a one-thread batch and a fresh `energyAndGradient` of the same
configuration.
The Python method `energy_gradient` accepts positions of shape `(n_atoms, 3)` or
`(n_config, n_atoms, 3)` and uses that entry.

`forceImpl` and `energyAndGradient` take their pairs from the instance neighbour
layer (`nlist::updateCells`).
The skin is that of a `nlist::NeighborList` passed to `energyAndGradient` when
it is positive.
Otherwise it is one fifth of the cutoff, or 0 under
`setNeighbourMode(nlist::Mode::Stream)`.
The pairs are reused while every atom has moved by at most half the skin and the
cell and the atom count are unchanged.
With skin 0 they are reused only for identical coordinates.
`energyAndGradientBatch` builds a new layer for each configuration, on the
thread that evaluates it, and passes no `nlist::NeighborList`.
That layer starts empty, so it is not reused across configurations.
Its skin is the same default.

### Stress

`forceImpl` writes the Cauchy stress, sets `has_stress`, and `caps().stress` is
true.
The convention is the one of `LJPot`, `MorsePot` and `ZBLPot`, set in
`stress.hpp`.
The stress is sigma = dE/dε / V for the strain that sends every position and
every cell row r to r (I + ε).
It is row-major and symmetric, in eV/Angstrom^3.
A compressed cell has negative diagonal entries, the sign ASE uses.
For the LAMMPS virial W, sigma = -W / V.

The virial adds d ⊗ g for the folded bond vector d of each pair term and for
both bonds of each three-body term, where g is the energy gradient with respect
to d.
That sum is the many-body virial of Thompson, Plimpton and Mattson, J. Chem.
Phys. 131, 154107 (2009), doi:10.1063/1.3245303.
`energyAndGradient` and the batch call skip the virial.

`SWSiTest` checks all nine entries against a fourth-order central difference of
the energy in the strain, step 2e-4.
The cells are compressed cubic diamond, a sheared diamond cell and a rattled
cubic cell.
The tolerance is 5e-10 eV/Angstrom^3.

The Fortran `SWPot` writes the same stress from the folded vectors of its own
neighbour table, and its `caps().stress` is true.
Both kernels are linear in epsilon, so the `SWPot` stress is the
`StillingerWeberSi` stress times 1.068176741337.
`FortranPotsTest` checks that ratio to 1e-14 eV/Angstrom^3, and the strain
difference to 5e-10, on a compressed cubic cell and a sheared, rattled cell.
`SWPot::forceBatch`, the call eOn's engine makes, skips the virial, and its
outputs have `has_stress` 0 and a zero tensor.
`FortranPotsTest` checks that its energies and forces equal those of
`forceImpl`.

In Python, `evaluate` on `StillingerWeberSi` or `SWPot` returns the stress as a
3 × 3 array, and `caps()` reports it.
`RgpotCalculator` then gives the ASE stress for either potential.

### Domain decomposition

`locality` returns the cutoff `kCut * kSigma` with a full neighbour list and a
reach of 2, so the copies a host must hold go out to twice the cutoff.
`densityStage` writes nothing.
`forceStage` evaluates owned centres on that full list.
A two-body term is counted from the atom whose partner sits strictly above it in
z, then y, then x.
A three-body term is counted at each owned centre.
With newton on, the host adds the forces written on copies back to their owners
and sums the owned energies.
`Staged3BodyTest` checks that split against `forceImpl` to a relative tolerance
of 1e-10, including a triclinic cell and a slab thinner than two cutoffs.
The whole-cell call is unchanged.

### Diamond energy

At the tetrahedral angle the three-body term is zero, and the diamond minimum
puts every nearest neighbour at the minimum of the pair term, where that term
equals -1.
Each atom then has two bonds, so the energy per atom is -2 epsilon.
Equation (2.8) prints -1.999993 epsilon for the lattice sum at the density
quoted there.
`SWSiTest` checks both figures, and checks the analytic gradient against a
finite difference.

---

# Tersoff silicon-carbon (1989)

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/tersoff_sic.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/tersoff_sic.html

`TersoffSiC` is the 1989 silicon, carbon, and silicon-carbide kernel of J.
Tersoff, Phys.
Rev. B 39, 5566 (1989),
doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.39.5566. The erratum, Phys. Rev. B 41, 3248 (1990), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.41.3248.2,
sets carbon B to 346.74 eV and d to 4.3484.
Carbon beta is 1.5724e-7 and is dimensionless.
It is the Table I value in the NIST and LAMMPS transcriptions.
The erratum does not print it.

`TersoffSiC` and the Fortran `TersoffPot` both report `PotType::TersoffSi`.
There is no `PotType::TersoffSiC`.
The engine name `tersoff` builds `TersoffPot`.
In `TersoffPot`, an all-silicon configuration and a null species pointer use the
Fortran gather, and a call with any atomic number other than 14 uses this
kernel.
The `pot_spec` name `TersoffSi` builds `TersoffSiC` itself.
Calling `TersoffSiC` directly always evaluates the 1989 form, including an
all-silicon cell, whose silicon column matches that gather.

Atomic number 14 is silicon and 6 is carbon.
Any other species throws `std::invalid_argument`. lambda3 is zero for both
elements, so the factor exp(lambda3^m (rij - rik)^m) is identically one and is
not evaluated.
The cross term uses chi = 0.9776.
The lambdas are arithmetic means and the repulsive amplitude is a geometric
mean.
The attractive amplitude is chi times the geometric mean.
The inner cutoffs and the outer cutoffs are each mixed as geometric means.

### Calls

Lengths are Angstrom and the energy is eV.
The cell is periodic in each direction.
`forceImpl` writes the force, which is minus the gradient.
`energyAndGradient` writes the energy and dE/dx for one configuration.
`energyAndGradientBatch` writes both for several configurations that share one
cell and one species list, so a caller enters the library once per batch.
A configuration is spread across the threads `OMP_NUM_THREADS` requests when
`TersoffSiC` would not open a team for that atom count.
`teamSize` decides, from `TersoffSiC::kTeamMinAtoms` and
`TersoffSiC::kTeamFrom`, and a call already inside a team or with one thread
requested does not spread.
Each configuration is evaluated whole.
A configuration that would open a team, or a batch that contains one, stays on
the calling thread.
The bits match a one-thread batch and a fresh `energyAndGradient` of the same
configuration.
The Python method `energy_gradient` accepts positions of shape `(n_atoms, 3)` or
`(n_config, n_atoms, 3)` and uses that entry.

`forceImpl` and `energyAndGradient` take their pairs from the instance neighbour
layer (`nlist::updateCells`), searched to the silicon outer cutoff, 3.0
Angstrom, the longest in this set.
The skin is that of a `nlist::NeighborList` passed to `energyAndGradient` when
it is positive.
Otherwise it is one fifth of that cutoff, 0.6 Angstrom, or 0 under
`setNeighbourMode(nlist::Mode::Stream)`.
The pairs are reused while each atom has moved by at most half the skin and the
cell and the atom count are unchanged.
With skin 0 they are reused only for identical coordinates.
`energyAndGradientBatch` builds a new layer for each configuration, on the
thread that evaluates it, and passes no `nlist::NeighborList`.
That layer starts empty, so it is not reused across configurations.
Its skin is the same default.
Species and kind scratch stay `thread_local`.

### Held list on the force path

By default (held skin 0) `forceImpl` keeps no `nlist::NeighborList` and uses the
skin of the section above.
`setHeldSkin(skin)` with a positive skin in Angstrom makes the instance keep one
`nlist::NeighborList` across `forceImpl` calls, and that skin replaces the
default.
The list is rebuilt when any atom has moved by more than half the skin since the
last build, or when the cell or the atom count changes.
`setHeldSkin(0)` drops the list and goes back to the default.
A negative or non-finite skin throws `std::invalid_argument`.
`heldList()` returns the list, so a caller can see when it was last built.

The instance always reports `Reentrancy::PerInstance`.
With a positive held skin it also reports `perImageInstances`, since a call
writes the list.
`TersoffPot::setHeldSkin` passes the skin to its own 1989 kernel.
All-silicon calls through `TersoffPot` stay on the Fortran gather, which keeps
its own neighbour table (`rgpot_neighbors`) with a skin of 0.3 Angstrom, a tenth
of its 3.0 Angstrom cutoff.

On the call that builds the list, and on a call with the coordinates of that
build, a held list returns the same bits as an instance without one given the
same calls.
After a move inside the skin the bits also match while every atom stays in its
cell of the cutoff-edged grid that orders the pairs.
An atom that crosses a cell face keeps the pair order of the last build, so the
bonds of a centre can be summed in another order.
`TersoffSiCTest` bounds that difference by 1e-12 on 512 and 4096 atoms.
`tersoff_held_bench` reports the largest difference it sees and the time per
atom of a rebuild, a held list, and the Fortran gather.

### Stress

`TersoffSiC::forceImpl` writes the Cauchy stress, sets `has_stress`, and
`caps().stress` is true, with or without a held list.
The convention is the one of `LJPot`, `MorsePot` and `ZBLPot`, set in
`stress.hpp`.
The stress is sigma = dE/dε / V for the strain that sends every position and
every cell row r to r (I + ε).
It is row-major and symmetric, in eV/Angstrom^3.
A compressed cell has negative diagonal entries, the sign ASE uses.
For the LAMMPS virial W, sigma = -W / V.

The virial adds d ⊗ g for each folded bond vector d, where g is the energy
gradient with respect to d.
Each bond i-j adds its radial term, and each bond i-k in the bond order of i-j
adds the angular and cutoff terms of both bonds.
That sum is the many-body virial of Thompson, Plimpton and Mattson, J. Chem.
Phys. 131, 154107 (2009), doi:10.1063/1.3245303.
`energyAndGradient` and the batch call skip the virial, and the energy and the
forces keep their bits.

`TersoffSiCTest` checks all nine entries against a fourth-order central
difference of the energy in the strain, step 2e-4.
The cells are compressed cubic silicon, a sheared silicon cell, and a sheared,
rattled silicon carbide cell whose Si-Si pairs sit inside the cutoff taper.
The tolerance is 5e-10 eV/Angstrom^3.

`TersoffPot` keeps `caps().stress` true.
All-silicon calls run the Fortran gather and publish its Cauchy stress; mixed
silicon-carbon calls dispatch to `TersoffSiC` and publish the same stress and
forces as that kernel.
A zero-atom call with a null box succeeds without stress.
`has_stress` stays 0 and the nine entries are zero.
A call with no atoms does the same for any box.
An all-silicon call with atoms and a null box throws
`std::runtime_error` `Tersoff potential failed (status 2): rgpot_neighbors: a required neighbour pointer is null`.
An all-silicon call with atoms and a zero-volume or non-finite box throws
`std::runtime_error` `Tersoff potential failed (status 4): rgpot_neighbors: box must be finite, and a periodic box must have positive volume`.
A mixed-species call with atoms and a null box throws `std::invalid_argument`
`TersoffSiC: null cell`.
A mixed-species call with atoms and a zero-volume orthorhombic cell leaves
`has_stress` at 0 and the nine entries at zero.
A mixed-species call with atoms and a singular skewed cell throws
`std::invalid_argument` `periodic cell must be nonsingular`.
A mixed-species call with a non-finite cell throws `std::invalid_argument`
`periodic cell must be finite`.

### Domain decomposition

`locality` returns the silicon outer cutoff, 3 Angstrom, with a full neighbour
list and a reach of 2, so the copies a host must hold go out to twice that
cutoff.
`densityStage` writes nothing.
`forceStage` evaluates owned centres on that full list.
Every directed bond is kept, because the 1989 sum already carries the one half,
and the partner's owner counts the bond that leaves the partner.
Pairs beyond a pair's own outer cutoff are skipped.
With newton on, the host adds the forces written on copies back to their owners
and sums the owned energies.
`Staged3BodyTest` checks a periodic silicon carbide cell, split into 2, 4 and 8
slabs, against `forceImpl` to a relative tolerance of 1e-10, including a
triclinic cell and a slab thinner than two cutoffs.
The whole-cell call is unchanged.

### Diamond energies

At a0 = 5.432 Angstrom the silicon diamond energy is -4.629595
eV/atom. At a0 = 3.5656 Angstrom the carbon diamond energy is -7.370514 eV/atom.
Those are the closed forms of this parameter set at the lattice constants that
reproduce the fitted cohesive energies, 4.63 eV and 7.37 eV.
`TersoffSiCTest` pins both and checks the analytic gradient against a finite
difference.

---

# MPI

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/mpi.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/mpi.html

`with_mpi` is a Meson feature option in `meson_options.txt`.
The default is `disabled`.
The accepted values are `auto`, `enabled`, and `disabled`.

```bash
meson setup bbdir -Dwith_tests=true -Dwith_rpc=true -Dwith_mpi=enabled
```

`auto` builds `librgpot_mpi` when Meson finds MPI.
`enabled` stops configuration when MPI is absent.
`disabled` does not build `librgpot_mpi`.

`librgpot` never links MPI.
`librgpot_mpi` (meson dependency and pkg-config name `rgpot-mpi`) holds every
MPI call of the calculator groups.
`bindCalculators` and `calculatorsUseMpi` load it with `dlopen` on first use, so
a host that never asks for calculator groups never maps `libmpi` or its
transport layers.
The loader, `loadCalculatorMpi`, tries the file the host names, else the
`RGPOT_MPI_LIBRARY` environment variable, then
`RGPOT_MPI_LIBRARY_NAME` in the directory of `librgpot` (or of the executable, when rgpot is linked statically), then `RGPOT_MPI_LIBRARY_NAME`
through the dynamic linker's search path.
It opens the library with `RTLD_NOW | RTLD_GLOBAL`.
`RGPOT_MPI_LIBRARY_NAME` is `librgpot_mpi.so.3` (`librgpot_mpi.3.dylib` on
macOS), the library's own SONAME with soversion 3.
It is not `librgpot`'s SONAME.
The two libraries meet at one C symbol,
`rgpot_mpi_api_v1` (`RGPOT_MPI_API_SYMBOL`), which returns the function table of
`CppCore/rgpot/calculator_mpi_abi.h`.
`RGPOT_MPI_ABI_VERSION` is 1.
Windows has no loader; there the load fails with "calculator groups need
dlopen".
Until the library is loaded every calculator call behaves as in a build without
MPI.
When `bindCalculators` cannot load it, one rank per calculator or a value <= 0
gives group 0 of one rank, and any other value gives index -1.

A process with
`librgpot_mpi` loaded can call `bindCalculators` to split `MPI_COMM_WORLD` into
calculator groups.
`shareFromCalculator` broadcasts one group's bytes to every rank.
When more than one rank is bound, a rank that cannot enter that broadcast makes
every rank print the error and call `MPI_Abort` on `MPI_COMM_WORLD`.
The same abort runs when one rank leaves `CPMDPot::forceImpl` or
`CP2KPot::forceImpl` by an exception, with one exception for CP2K: an
unconverged SCF is agreed over the calculator's communicator, and every rank of
that calculator throws `rgpot::CP2KScfError` without aborting.
`finalizeMpiAtExit` registers an exit handler, and `CPMDPot` and `CP2KPot` call
it from their force calls.
That handler calls `MPI_Finalize` when `bindCalculators` called `MPI_Init`.
A host that called `MPI_Init` finalizes itself.
After `abortMpiAtExit` the handler calls
`MPI_Abort` instead, whoever called `MPI_Init`.

How `CPMDPot` and `CP2KPot` run a force call across the ranks of a calculator,
how the result cache agrees on hits, and how CP2K takes its communicator are
explained in [Calculator groups over MPI](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/explanation/mpi.html).

### C ABI of librgpot_mpi

`CppCore/rgpot/CalculatorGroupMpi.cc` implements the table.
The library keeps one calculator split per process.

#### `rgpot_mpi_group_t`

- Inputs :: none; `bind` fills it.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `index` is the calculator of this rank, or -1 when the world cannot
  be split as asked.
  `ranks` is the number of ranks per calculator, `rank_in_group` this rank's
  rank in its calculator, and `world_size` the size of `MPI_COMM_WORLD`.
  World rank `r= is in calculator =r / ranks` with rank `r % ranks`.
- Errors :: none.

It mirrors `rgpot::CalculatorGroup`.

#### `rgpot_mpi_api_t`

- Inputs :: none; `rgpot_mpi_api_v1` returns a static table.
  The members take the arguments described under Outputs.
- Units :: none; `share` and `agree` move bytes and the other members take
  counts, ranks and handles.
- Outputs :: `abi_version` is `RGPOT_MPI_ABI_VERSION` and
  `struct_size` is `sizeof(rgpot_mpi_api_t)` of the library.
  `bind(ranks_per_calculator, out)` is collective on `MPI_COMM_WORLD`, calls
  `MPI_Init` when MPI is not up, splits the world into calculators of `ranks_per_calculator`
  ranks (<= 0 means one calculator) and writes the group into `*out` when `out`
  is not null.
  `comm(comm_out, comm_bytes)` copies the calculator's
  `MPI_Comm` into `comm_out` and returns 1 when
  `comm_bytes` is `sizeof(MPI_Comm)` and a split exists, else 0.
  `initialized()` returns 1 when `MPI_Initialized` reports MPI up, else 0.
  `share(owner, data, bytes)` broadcasts `bytes` bytes from the first rank of
  calculator `owner` to `MPI_COMM_WORLD` and returns 1.
  `finalize_at_exit(abort_requested)` registers the exit handler once and stores the latest callback; at exit, while MPI is up and not finalized, the handler calls `MPI_Abort`
  when `abort_requested` returns nonzero, else `MPI_Finalize` when `bind` called
  `MPI_Init`.
  With
  `RGPOT_MPI_FINALIZE_TRACE` set to `1= the handler prints =rgpot MPI_Finalize`
  to standard error before it finalizes.
  `agree(flags, n)` replaces `flags[0..n)` with their logical AND over the
  calculator's communicator and returns 1; it returns 0 and leaves `flags`
  unchanged when MPI is not up or finalized, before a split, or on a calculator
  of one rank.
  `publish_error(message, len)` is entered by every rank of the calculator with its message (`len` 0 for none); when any rank has one, every message, cut to 512 bytes, prints on every rank of the calculator and `MPI_COMM_WORLD`
  aborts, otherwise it returns.
  `adopt(callback)` calls `callback` with the address and byte size of the
  calculator's `MPI_Comm` and the ranks per calculator, and returns its result;
  the handle is borrowed.
- Errors :: `share` returns 0 in a single-rank or unbound world for a missing
  split, a null `data` with `bytes > 0`, or an owner out of range.
  In a bound world of more than one rank those cases, or ranks that disagree on
  `owner` or `bytes`, make every rank print the reasons and call
  `MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1)`.
  With no split, or on a calculator of one rank, `publish_error` aborts at once
  when its own message is not empty.
  A rank with a message also aborts with it when the exchange does not complete
  within 10 s.
  Without MPI up, `publish_error` returns.
  `adopt` returns -1 for a null callback, before a split, or when the split was
  refused.

The loader accepts a table whose `abi_version` equals `RGPOT_MPI_ABI_VERSION`
and whose `struct_size` is at least the size it was compiled against.
A later version may append members.

#### `rgpot_mpi_api_fn`

```c
typedef const rgpot_mpi_api_t *(*rgpot_mpi_api_fn)(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the type of `rgpot_mpi_api_v1`, which a loader casts the `dlsym`
  result to.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot_mpi_api_v1`

```c
const rgpot_mpi_api_t *rgpot_mpi_api_v1(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a pointer to the library's static table, valid while the library is
  loaded.
- Errors :: none; the call cannot fail.
  `loadCalculatorMpi` rejects a library without the symbol ("lacks
  rgpot_mpi_api_v1") or a table with another `abi_version` or a smaller
  `struct_size` ("has an incompatible rgpot MPI ABI"), and
  `calculatorMpiLoadError` returns that reason.

### C ABI of librgpot calculator helpers

`CppCore/rgpot/CalculatorGroup.cc` also exports C entry points from
`calculator_mpi_abi.h` so hosts no longer dlopen Itanium-mangled C++ names.

#### `rgpot_mpi_host_abi_version`

```c
uint32_t rgpot_mpi_host_abi_version(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `RGPOT_MPI_ABI_VERSION`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot_mpi_bind_calculators`

```c
int rgpot_mpi_bind_calculators(int ranks_per_calculator, rgpot_mpi_group_t *out);
```

- Inputs :: `ranks_per_calculator`, as for `bindCalculators`.
  `out`, optional storage for the resulting `rgpot_mpi_group_t`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: this rank's calculator index, and when `out` is not null the same
  group fields `bindCalculators` stores.
- Errors :: none; refusals are reported as index -1.

#### `rgpot_mpi_share_bytes`

```c
int rgpot_mpi_share_bytes(int owner, void *data, size_t bytes);
```

- Inputs :: `owner`, `data` and `bytes`, as for `shareFromCalculator`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the return code of `shareFromCalculator` (1 on a successful
  collective share, 0 otherwise).
- Errors :: none; in collective error cases it aborts the world as described for
  `shareFromCalculator`.

### Example

A host that opens `librgpot_mpi` itself and checks the table.
This build has no `librgpot_mpi`, so the block is only compiled.

```c
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include "rgpot/calculator_mpi_abi.h"

int main(void) {
  void *handle = dlopen(RGPOT_MPI_LIBRARY_NAME, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_GLOBAL);
  if (handle == NULL) {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", dlerror());
    return 1;
  }
  rgpot_mpi_api_fn get = (rgpot_mpi_api_fn)dlsym(handle, RGPOT_MPI_API_SYMBOL);
  const rgpot_mpi_api_t *api = get ? get() : NULL;
  if (api == NULL || api->abi_version != RGPOT_MPI_ABI_VERSION ||
      api->struct_size < sizeof(rgpot_mpi_api_t)) {
    fprintf(stderr, "incompatible %s\n", RGPOT_MPI_LIBRARY_NAME);
    return 1;
  }
  rgpot_mpi_group_t group;
  api->bind(0, &group);
  printf("calculator %d of %d ranks, world %d\n", group.index, group.ranks, group.world_size);
  return 0;
}
```

# C ABI of rgpot-core

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/c_abi.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/c_abi.html

`rgpot-core/include/rgpot.h` declares the C ABI of the Rust crate `rgpot-core`.
The header is generated by cbindgen from `rgpot-core/src`.
It includes `dlpack/dlpack.h` and uses `eindir_objective_t` and
`eindir_abi_stamp_t` without declaring them.
A C caller includes
`rgpot/eindir_abi.hpp` first, which declares both; a C++ caller includes `rgpot/c_api.hpp`.
The RPC names are declared only when `RGPOT_HAS_RPC` is defined before the
header.
The neighbour-list, fast-list and plugin symbols of `librgpot` have their own
pages: [Neighbour-list C ABI](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/nlist_abi.html),
[Fast neighbour list](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/fast_nlist.html) and
[Plugin ABI](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/plugin_abi.html).
Why the ABI stamp exists is in
[ABI stamps](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/explanation/abi-stamps.html), and how to bump it is in
[Bump the ABI numbers](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/contributing/developer/abi-bump.html).
The reasons for the Hessian-vector design are in
[Hessian-vector products](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/explanation/hessian-vector.html).

The C ABI converts no units.
Positions and cell are in the length unit of the potential behind the callback,
energy in its energy unit, and forces in energy per length.
The C++ potentials of `librgpot` use Angstrom and eV.

The examples on this page are compiled against the header and not run: a Meson
build exports these functions only when it is configured with `with_rust_core`.

### Version

`RGPOT_VERSION`, `RGPOT_VERSION_MAJOR`, `RGPOT_VERSION_MINOR` and `RGPOT_VERSION_PATCH`
are the package version of the header.
The functions below report the version of the library that is loaded.

#### `rgpot_version`

```c
const char *rgpot_version(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the crate version as `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, a NUL-terminated string
  in static storage.
  Do not free it.
- Errors :: none; the call cannot fail.

#### `rgpot_source_revision`

```c
const char *rgpot_source_revision(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the source revision recorded when the crate was built, in static
  storage.
  `rgpot-core/build.rs` takes the environment variable `RGPOT_SOURCE_REVISION`,
  else `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD` of the checkout, else the empty string.
- Errors :: none; the call cannot fail.

#### `rgpot_version_major`

```c
uint32_t rgpot_version_major(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the major version of the loaded library.
- Errors :: none; the call cannot fail.

#### `rgpot_version_minor`

```c
uint32_t rgpot_version_minor(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the minor version of the loaded library.
- Errors :: none; the call cannot fail.

#### `rgpot_version_patch`

```c
uint32_t rgpot_version_patch(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the patch version of the loaded library.
- Errors :: none; the call cannot fail.

### Errors

#### `rgpot_status_t`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs ::
  `RGPOT_SUCCESS` (0), `RGPOT_INVALID_PARAMETER` (1), `RGPOT_INTERNAL_ERROR` (2), `RGPOT_RPC_ERROR` (3), `RGPOT_BUFFER_SIZE_ERROR`
  (4),
  `RGPOT_SCC_NOT_CONVERGED` (5), `RGPOT_NO_JET` (6), `RGPOT_JET_BRANCH` (7), `RGPOT_JET_DOMAIN`
  (8).
- Errors :: none.
  The only functions of `rgpot-core` that return
  `RGPOT_BUFFER_SIZE_ERROR` themselves are `rgpot_potential_taylor_jet` and
  `rgpot_ch5_2008_taylor_jet`, for an `order` whose `order + 1` doubles overflow
  in bytes; a callback may return it and it is passed through.
  `RGPOT_SCC_NOT_CONVERGED` is the status of a callback whose engine ran its self-consistent field out of iterations; `rgpot_potential_calculate` and the Hessian-vector entry points return it unchanged, and `rgpot_potential_fused_error_kind`
  reports the same distinction for the eindir path, whose own status type has no
  such value.

A function wrapped in the crate's panic guard returns `RGPOT_INTERNAL_ERROR` for
a caught Rust panic and stores the panic message.
The guarded functions are `rgpot_potential_calculate`, `rgpot_potential_hvp`,
`rgpot_potential_hvp_resolved`, `rgpot_potential_hvp_centre`,
`rgpot_potential_hessian`, `rgpot_potential_set_taylor_jet`,
`rgpot_potential_taylor_jet`, `rgpot_ch5_2008_taylor_jet`, `rgpot_rpc_calculate`, `rgpot_rpc_server_start`
and `rgpot_mdi_server_start`.

#### `rgpot_set_last_error`

```c
void rgpot_set_last_error(const char *msg);
```

- Inputs :: `msg` a NUL-terminated string, or NULL.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the calling thread's `rgpot_last_error()` message is `msg`; NULL
  clears it.
  A callback calls this before it returns an error status, so that the text
  reaches the caller of `rgpot_potential_calculate`, or of the eindir functions,
  which do not store a message for a failed callback.
- Errors :: none; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are replaced.

#### `rgpot_last_error`

```c
const char *rgpot_last_error(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the message of the last failure recorded on the calling thread,
  NUL-terminated, or the empty string when none was recorded.
  Do not free it.
- Errors :: none; the call cannot fail.

The message is thread-local.
A failing call replaces it; a successful call leaves the previous message in
place, so read it only after a call returned an error.
The header states that the pointer is valid until the next `rgpot_*` call on the
same thread.
A message that contains a NUL byte is stored as
`(error message contained interior NUL)`.
When the force callback of `rgpot_potential_calculate` returns an error status,
`rgpot-core` stores no message of its own: the text is whatever the callback
stored, or an older message.
The Hessian-vector and Hessian entry points clear the message before they call a
callback, so a failing callback that stored none is named with its status.

```c
#include <stdio.h>

#include "rgpot/eindir_abi.hpp"
#include "rgpot.h"

int report(const rgpot_potential_t *pot, const rgpot_force_input_t *input,
           rgpot_force_out_t *output) {
  rgpot_status_t s = rgpot_potential_calculate(pot, input, output);
  if (s != RGPOT_SUCCESS) {
    fprintf(stderr, "rgpot error %d: %s\n", (int)s, rgpot_last_error());
    return 1;
  }
  return 0;
}
```

### Tensors

The tensor functions take and return DLPack `DLManagedTensorVersioned` pointers.
Every tensor they create is on the CPU with device id 0, row-major strides and
DLPack version 1.0.
The borrowing constructors do not check their arguments;
`rgpot_tensor_owned_cpu_f64_2d` and the accessors handle NULL as their entries
say.

#### `rgpot_tensor_cpu_f64_2d`

```c
DLManagedTensorVersioned *rgpot_tensor_cpu_f64_2d(double *data, int64_t rows, int64_t cols);
```

- Inputs :: `data` points to `rows * cols` doubles that stay alive while the
  tensor lives; `rows` and `cols` are the shape.
- Units :: those of `data`.
- Outputs :: a new tensor of shape `[rows, cols]`, dtype float64, that borrows
  `data`.
  Free it with `rgpot_tensor_free`, which frees the metadata and not `data`.
- Errors :: none checked; the pointer and the shape are stored as given.

#### `rgpot_tensor_cpu_i32_1d`

```c
DLManagedTensorVersioned *rgpot_tensor_cpu_i32_1d(int *data, int64_t len);
```

- Inputs :: `data` points to `len` `int` values that stay alive while the tensor
  lives.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a new tensor of shape `[len]`, dtype int32, that borrows `data`.
  Free it with `rgpot_tensor_free`.
- Errors :: none checked.

#### `rgpot_tensor_cpu_f64_matrix3`

```c
DLManagedTensorVersioned *rgpot_tensor_cpu_f64_matrix3(double *data);
```

- Inputs :: `data` points to 9 doubles that stay alive while the tensor lives.
- Units :: those of `data`.
- Outputs :: a new tensor of shape `[3, 3]`, dtype float64, that borrows `data`;
  the same as `rgpot_tensor_cpu_f64_2d(data, 3, 3)`.
