
- Inputs :: `pot`, a handle or NULL.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 1 when `XTBPot::reusedWavefunction` is true, else 0; 0 for NULL.
- Errors :: none.

### Metatomic table

`CppCore/rgpot/MetatomicPot/metatomic_c_abi.h` declares the table that
`libmetatomic_engine` exports next to the engine table and that
`MetatomicDlopen` loads.
`CppCore/rgpot/MetatomicPot/MetatomicEngineAbi.cc` implements it over a
`MetatomicPot`.
Positions and cells are in Angstrom, energies in eV and forces in eV/Angstrom,
unless the config names another `length_unit`.
`RGPOT_MTA_ABI_VERSION` is 1.
The return codes of `rgpot_mta_force` are not those of the engine table.

#### `RgpotMtaPot`

- Inputs :: none; an opaque handle.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: returned by `rgpot_mta_create` and released by `rgpot_mta_destroy`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `RgpotMtaConfig`

- Inputs :: `model_path`, `device`, `length_unit`,
  `extensions_directory`, `check_consistency`,
  `uncertainty_threshold`, `dtype_override`,
  `random_rotation`, `n_symmetry_rotations` and `so3_probe_scatter`, the `MetatomicConfig` fields with those names, and `torch_determinism_strict`
  (0 for `TorchDeterminismPolicy::Fast`, 1 for `Strict`).
  A null string counts as empty.
- Units :: as `MetatomicConfig`.
- Outputs :: read by `rgpot_mta_create`.
- Errors :: none here; `rgpot_mta_create` reports a missing model.

An empty `device` becomes `cpu`, not metatomic's choice, and an empty
`length_unit` becomes `angstrom`.
The struct has no `engine_path`, `task_name`, `charge`, `spin` or
`attach_system_extras`.

#### `rgpot_mta_abi_version`

```c
int rgpot_mta_abi_version(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `RGPOT_MTA_ABI_VERSION` (1).
- Errors :: none.

`MetatomicDlopen` refuses a library that returns another value.

#### `rgpot_mta_available`

```c
int rgpot_mta_available(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 1.
- Errors :: none.

`MetatomicDlopen` does not call it.

#### `rgpot_mta_create`

```c
RgpotMtaPot *rgpot_mta_create(const RgpotMtaConfig *cfg,
                              char *errbuf, size_t errlen);
```

- Inputs :: `cfg`, the settings; `errbuf` and `errlen`, a buffer for the failure
  reason (may be null or 0).
- Units :: as `RgpotMtaConfig`.
- Outputs :: a new handle, or NULL on failure.
- Errors :: returns NULL and writes
  `rgpot_mta_create: model_path required` for a null `cfg` or an empty `model_path`.
  Returns NULL with the message of the `MetatomicPot` constructor when the model
  does not load, has no energy output, or has a dtype other than `float32` or
  `float64`.

#### `rgpot_mta_destroy`

```c
void rgpot_mta_destroy(RgpotMtaPot *pot);
```

- Inputs :: `pot`, a handle from `rgpot_mta_create` or NULL.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the handle and its `MetatomicPot` are freed.
- Errors :: none; NULL is accepted.

#### `rgpot_mta_force`

```c
int rgpot_mta_force(RgpotMtaPot *pot, long nAtoms,
                    const double *positions, const int *atomicNrs,
                    double *forces, double *energy,
                    double *variance, const double *box);
```

- Inputs :: as `rgpot_xtb_force`, with an `RgpotMtaPot` handle.
- Units :: as `MetatomicPot`: Angstrom in, eV and eV/Angstrom out with the
  default `length_unit`.
  The `*variance` is eV^2, or eV^2 per Angstrom squared without model
  uncertainty.
- Outputs :: 0, with `*energy`, `forces` and `*variance`, the `MetatomicPot`
  variance, written.
- Errors :: 1 for a null handle, a null pointer other than `variance`, or
  `nAtoms` of zero or less. 2 when the potential threw, after printing
  `rgpot_mta_force: <message>` on stderr.
  Nothing is written on an error.

A thread that holds the Python GIL releases it for the evaluation, so torch
autograd can run.
The engine looks the CPython calls up at run time and does not link libpython.

### Rust loader (`rgpot-core` `engine` feature)

Enable the `engine` feature on `rgpot-core` to expose
`rgpot_core::engine`, a thin Rust wrapper over the symbols declared in `CppCore/rgpot/engine_c_abi.h`.
No second engine abstraction is added: `EnginePotential::into_potential` wraps
the handle as a `PotentialImpl`.

#### Plugin lifetime

Engine plugins stay resident.
The loader keeps one process-wide registry entry per plugin file, keyed by the
device and inode of the canonical path.
An entry holds the `dlopen` handle and the resolved `EngineSymbols`.
A later load of the same file through any path, symlink or hard link reuses the
entry and does not call `dlopen` again.
The library is opened with `RTLD_NODELETE`, and the loader never calls `dlclose`
on it.
Dropping an `EnginePotential`, or the `PotentialImpl` built from it, calls
`rgpot_engine_destroy` and leaves the library mapped.

A backend may keep OpenMP or CUDA runtimes, Torch thread pools, MPI state,
GROMACS, LAMMPS or OpenMM state, TLS destructors or `atexit` handlers that call
into the library after its last instance is gone.
Unmapping such a library crashes the process later, or at exit.
A load that fails its required-symbol check, its ABI check or
`rgpot_engine_create` does not stay resident.
The loader destroys any engine the attempt created, closes the handle, and keeps
no registry entry for the file.
A later load of the same file opens it again, runs its static constructors
again, and returns the same error.
A library linked with `-z nodelete` stays mapped after that close, as it does
after any `dlclose`.

Two loads are refused with `EngineError::Load`:

- A path whose file was replaced after it was loaded :: The path names a new
  inode, but the dynamic linker would return the mapping of the old one.
  A file replaced while its first load runs is refused the same way, and the
  handle of that attempt is closed.
  Load the new file from another path, or restart the process.
- A bare library name such as `libuma_engine.so` :: The dynamic loader resolves
  it through its search path rather than the filesystem, so the file cannot be
  identified before it is opened.
  Pass a path that names the file.

A plugin can opt out of residency.
When it exports
`rgpot_engine_unload_policy` returning `RGPOT_ENGINE_UNLOAD_SAFE` and its stamp
reports minor 7 or later, the loader opens it without `RTLD_NODELETE`.
It still stays loaded until the `unsafe` `EnginePotential::unload(path)` removes
its registry entry and calls `dlclose`.
`unload` returns `EngineError::Unsupported` for `rgpot_engine_unload_policy`
when the plugin has not opted in, and `EngineError::Invalid` while an
`EnginePotential` or a `PotentialImpl` built from it is alive or when the file
was never loaded.
`unload` releases the registry lock before it calls `dlclose`, so a destructor
of the plugin may load another engine.
A later `load` opens the file again.

`libuma_engine`, `libmetatomic_engine`, `libxtb_engine`, `libopenmm_engine`,
`libnwchem_engine` and `libskala_engine` are also linked with `-z nodelete`, so
a host that does call `dlclose` on them leaves them mapped.

- `ENGINE_ERR_LOCK` :: Rust constant for `RGPOT_ENGINE_ERR_LOCK` (-2).
- `ENGINE_ABI_VERSION`, `ENGINE_ABI_MINOR`,
  `ENGINE_ABI_LAYOUT_REVISION` :: Host ABI identity (`1=, =11`, `1=) matching =RGPOT_ENGINE_ABI_VERSION`,
  `RGPOT_ENGINE_ABI_MINOR` and `RGPOT_ENGINE_ABI_LAYOUT_REVISION`.
- `ENGINE_UNLOAD_RESIDENT`, `ENGINE_UNLOAD_SAFE`,
  `ENGINE_UNLOAD_POLICY_MINOR` :: `RGPOT_ENGINE_UNLOAD_RESIDENT` (`0`),
  `RGPOT_ENGINE_UNLOAD_SAFE` (`1=), and the first minor (=7`) that defines `rgpot_engine_unload_policy`.
- `RgpotEngineAbiStamp` :: Compatibility stamp (`abi_major`, `abi_minor`,
  `layout_revision`) with `RgpotEngineAbiStamp::HOST` and `serves(host)` accepting any plugin of the same major and layout revision whose minor is at most `host.abi_minor`
  (rejecting plugins with a newer minor than the host's).
- `RgpotEnginePot` :: Opaque handle type matching `struct RgpotEnginePot`.
- `RgpotEngineComponent` :: Per-term composite record matching
  `RgpotEngineComponent` of the header.
- `CoupledWellConfig`, `PotlibcConfig` :: Typed version-2 create messages for
  `libcoupled_well_engine` and
  `libpotlibc_engine`, laid out as `RgpotCoupledWellConfigV2` (`COUPLED_WELL_CONFIG_MAGIC`,
  `COUPLED_WELL_CONFIG_VERSION` 2, `COUPLED_WELL_CONFIG_VERSION_V1` 1, `COUPLED_WELL_CONFIG_V1_SIZE` 48, `COUPLED_WELL_CONFIG_MIN_SIZE` 56, with `size` at byte offset 4) and `RgpotPotlibcConfigV2` (`POTLIBC_CONFIG_MAGIC`, `POTLIBC_CONFIG_VERSION` 2, `POTLIBC_CONFIG_VERSION_V1`
  1, `POTLIBC_CONFIG_V1_SIZE` 144, `POTLIBC_CONFIG_MIN_SIZE` 152,
  `POTLIBC_SURFACE_ID_CAPACITY` 128, with `size` at byte offset 4).
  Both are `#[non_exhaustive]`, implement `Default` and have `with_*` builders,
  `validate` (the create-time checks of the message itself) and `as_bytes` (the
  bytes for `EnginePotential::load`).
  `PotlibcConfig::with_surface_id` refuses an empty, over-long or NUL-containing
  identifier.
  The engines also accept the version-1 layouts of 48 and 144 bytes when their
  `version` field is set to the `_V1` constant.
- `CoordTransformFn`, `AbiVersionFn`, `AvailableFn`, `AbiStampFn`, `CreateFn`,
  `DestroyFn`, `ForceFn`, `ForceBatchFn`, `HvpFn`, `TaylorJetFn`, `CapsFn`,
  `LastErrorFn`, `LastComponentsFn`, `ComponentNameFn`, `ModelStateFn`,
  `SetCallbacksFn`, `HintFn`, `UnloadPolicyFn` :: `extern "C"` function-pointer
  types matching the C declarations above.
- `EngineSymbols` :: Resolved symbol table holding required
  (`abi_version`, `create`, `destroy`, `force`) and optional (`available`, `abi_stamp`,
  `force_batch`, `hvp`, `taylor_jet`, `caps`, `last_error`, `last_components`,
  `component_name`, `model_state`, `set_callbacks`, `hint`) function pointers.
  The struct is
  `#[non_exhaustive]`: build it with `EngineSymbols::new` for the four required symbols and one `with_*`
  method per optional symbol, such as `with_available` or `with_hint`.
- `EngineError` :: Typed error enum covering `Load`, `Missing`, `Abi`
  (`expected`, `found`), `AbiStamp` (`expected`, `found`), `Unavailable`,
  `Create`, `Invalid`, `Unsupported`, `Recoverable` (`code`, `message`), `Fatal`
  (`code`, `message`), and `Lock` (`operation`, `message`).
- `EngineRequest` :: Single-geometry input with `positions` (Angstrom, row-major
  `[n_atoms, 3]`), `atomic_numbers`, and `box_matrix` (row-major 3x3 lattice in
  Angstrom).
- `EngineEvaluation` :: Output containing `energy` (eV) and `forces`
  (eV/Angstrom, row-major `[n_atoms, 3]`).
- `EnginePotential::load(path, config)` /
  `EnginePotential::from_symbols(symbols, config)` :: `load` takes the resident
  registry entry for `path`, opening the file on first use.
  Both verify
  `rgpot_engine_abi_version() == ENGINE_ABI_VERSION`, resolve the optional `rgpot_engine_abi_stamp`
  (treating an engine without it as minor 0, layout 1) and require
  `stamp.serves(RgpotEngineAbiStamp::HOST)`, copy `config` into an
  8-byte-aligned `Vec<u64>` buffer (so engines that cast `config` to
  `capnp::word` never receive an unaligned pointer), check
  `rgpot_engine_available() !` 0= when the engine exports it, and call
  `rgpot_engine_create`.
  `EnginePotential::abi_stamp()` returns the resolved stamp.
  When the engine exports `rgpot_engine_caps`, one call at creation reads
  `reentrancy`.
  A negative code (`EngineError::Lock` for `RGPOT_ENGINE_ERR_LOCK`,
  `EngineError::Fatal` otherwise) rejects the engine: the loader destroys the
  new handle once and returns the error.
  A positive code or a truncated answer is not trusted, so the engine is
  serialized process wide like `reentrancy` 2.
  Only a successful answer of 0 or 1 skips that lock.
- `EnginePotential::force(&request)` and
  `EnginePotential::force_batch(&atomic_numbers, &positions, &boxes)` ::
  Validates input lengths and output finiteness, dispatches to
  `rgpot_engine_force` or
  `rgpot_engine_force_batch`, and maps positive codes to `EngineError::Recoverable` and negative codes to `EngineError::Fatal` using `rgpot_engine_last_error`
  when present.
  A negative status, including
  `RGPOT_ENGINE_ERR_LOCK` (`EngineError::Lock`), poisons the handle: every later call on that `EnginePotential` (or the `PotentialImpl` built from it) returns the same error without calling into native code, while dropping the handle still calls `rgpot_engine_destroy`
  once to release the `RgpotEnginePot` allocation.
  The process-wide lock of a `reentrancy` 2 engine is poisoned when a thread
  panics inside native code that holds it.
  The first call that finds it poisoned returns `EngineError::Lock` and poisons
  its handle the same way, without calling into native code.
- `EngineSession` :: Owns the callbacks of one `EnginePotential`.
  It borrows a `CoordinateTransform` only for the duration of each `force` or
  `force_batch` call and never keeps it.
  A callback or transform failure during a call is considered before the code
  the engine returns.
  A fatal failure from either side wins over a recoverable one.
  The first fatal failure poisons the handle, and every later call returns that
  `EngineError::Fatal` with the same code and message.
  A failure reported without a message carries one that names its code.
- `EngineSession::set_callbacks(callbacks)` :: Registers owned callbacks, or clears them with `None`, which passes a NULL table to `rgpot_engine_set_callbacks`.
  On success the session installs the new callbacks first and then drops the old
  ones, so the engine never holds a context the session has freed.
  A panic in the old callbacks' destructor is caught and reported as a fatal
  failure, which poisons the session; it never unwinds out of the call.
  On a nonzero return the previous callbacks stay registered and the refused
  ones are kept alive until the engine is destroyed, because an engine built
  before the header forbade it may have retained them.
  Dropping the session destroys the engine before it frees any callbacks.
- `EngineSession::attach_cache(path)`, `EngineSession::cache_counts()` and
  `EngineSession::clear_cache()` :: Attach a result cache, read its counts, and detach it through `rgpot_engine_set_cache`
  and `rgpot_engine_cache_counts`.
  `cache_counts()` returns `(computed, served)` and reports
  `EngineError::Unsupported` when no cache is attached or the plugin lacks the
  symbols.
  `clear_cache()` detaches the cache and leaves its entries on disk.
  Each call goes through the same fatal-failure handling as a force call.
- `EngineSession::model_state()` and `EngineSession::hint(message)` :: Read `rgpot_engine_model_state`
  (zero when the engine lacks it) and send a typed hint through
  `rgpot_engine_hint`.
  The message of a failed hint is the one the engine wrote to the error buffer,
  or one naming the code when it wrote none.
- `EnginePotential::caps()` / `EnginePotential::hvp(&request, direction)` ::
  Reads the size-prefixed engine capability structure and dispatches the exact
  product.
  A missing symbol, a false
  `analytic_hvp` bit, or `RGPOT_ENGINE_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` returns
  `EngineError::Unsupported` (retaining the engine's last-error message) without
  a finite-difference fallback.
- `EnginePotential::taylor_jet(&JetBatchRequest, order)` :: Dispatches `rgpot_engine_taylor_jet`
  for a uniform batch in one engine call and returns a `GradientJet`: `order()`,
  `n_systems()`, `derivative(k)` (every system, `k= in =1..=order`; block 0 is the Hessian-vector product), `system_derivative(k, s)`
  and `report()`, a `DerivativeReport` (`operations` summed, `scale` the
  largest) or `None` when the engine does not count operations.
  `JetBatchRequest` holds `atomic_numbers`, `positions`, `directions` and
  `boxes`.
  A missing symbol, a
  `jet_order` below `order`, or `RGPOT_ENGINE_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` returns
  `EngineError::Unsupported` naming `rgpot_engine_taylor_jet` (retaining the
  engine's last-error message) without a finite-difference fallback.
  `order` 0, a length mismatch and a non-finite position, direction or box are
  `EngineError::Invalid` before the engine is called.
  A non-finite or negative report scale is `EngineError::Invalid`, and the
  loader substitutes no other scale.
  `EngineSession::taylor_jet(&JetBatchRequest, order)` is the same call on a
  session: a failure a registered callback reports during the call is settled
  with the engine's return code as for `EngineSession::force`, so a fatal one
  poisons the session.
  `EnginePotential::caps()` asks the engine once and caches the answer;
  `EngineCaps::jet_order` carries the capability and is 0 for an engine whose
  caps struct ends before the field.
- `EnginePotential::into_potential(self)` :: Converts the instance into a `PotentialImpl` callback handle, serializes calls to its engine instance, and registers an analytic callback on the underlying `rgpot_potential_t` only when both `rgpot_engine_caps` and `rgpot_engine_hvp` are exported and `analytic_hvp`
  is true.
- `unsafe EnginePotential::unload(path)` :: Removes the registry entry of a
  plugin that declared itself unload-safe and calls `dlclose`, as described
  under the plugin lifetime above.
  The caller vouches for the declaration: no thread, TLS destructor, `atexit`
  handler or callback of the library may run afterwards, and no function pointer
  taken from it may be called.

---

# Quantum engine C ABIs

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/quantum_abi.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/quantum_abi.html

NWChem, CPMD, MOPAC and CP2K run outside `librgpot`.
Each frontend (`NWChemPot`, `CPMDPot`, `MOPACPot`, `CP2KPot`) opens an engine
library with `dlopen` and calls the symbols declared in the headers below.
The four ABIs keep their own prefixes: `nwchemc_`, `cpmdc_`,
`mopacc_` and `cp2kc_`.
The generic engine table of [Engine plugin ABI](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/engine_abi.html) is a
separate interface with its own units.

Every engine library ships with a stub that the repository builds: the stub
exports the same symbols, reports `*_available` as 0, fails every evaluation and
returns the version string `nwchemc-stub/1.0.0`, `cpmdc-stub/0.1.0` or
`mopacc-stub/1.0.0`.
A frontend that finds only the stub reports that the embed is not available.
The behaviour of a real engine beyond what the headers state is documented by
its own project; this page states what the headers promise and what the stubs
do.

Units at these ABIs are not the units of `librgpot`.
Geometry is in Angstrom (Bohr for CP2K), energy in Hartree and gradients in
Hartree/Bohr; the frontends convert to Angstrom, eV and eV/Angstrom.
Options cross the ABI as an unpacked flat Cap'n Proto message for NWChem and
CPMD (root `NWChemParams` or `CPMDParams`, see
[the schema](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/capnp_schema.html)), as the packed struct `MopacCParams` for
MOPAC, and as input-deck text for CP2K.

### NWChem: `nwchem_c_abi.h`

The header is `CppCore/rgpot/NWChemPot/nwchem_c_abi.h`.
`RGPOT_NWCHEMC_API` expands to
`__declspec(dllexport)` when `RGPOT_NWCHEMC_BUILD` is defined on Windows and to
nothing elsewhere.

#### `NWChemCResult`

- Inputs :: none; a struct returned by value.
- Units :: `energy_h` is in Hartree.
- Outputs :: `ok` (1 on success, 0 on failure), `energy_h` (total energy), and
  `message`, a NUL-terminated status or error text of at most 512 bytes.
- Errors :: none; a failure is `ok` equal to 0 with the reason in `message`.

#### `nwchemc_set_params`

```c
int nwchemc_set_params(const void *params_capnp, size_t params_capnp_size_bytes);
```

- Inputs :: `params_capnp`, an unpacked flat `NWChemParams` message, and its
  size in bytes.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 0 on success.
  The method options are kept for later calls.
- Errors :: non-zero when the embed is unavailable or the parameters are
  invalid; the stub always returns -1.

#### `nwchemc_energy_gradient`

```c
NWChemCResult nwchemc_energy_gradient(int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, const void *params_capnp, size_t params_capnp_size_bytes, double *grad_h_bohr);
```

- Inputs :: `n_atoms`; `positions_ang`,
  3*n doubles, row-major xyz; `atomic_numbers`, n atomic numbers; `params_capnp` and its size, as for `nwchemc_set_params`; `grad_h_bohr`, room for 3*n
  doubles.
- Units :: positions in Angstrom, energy in Hartree, gradient in Hartree/Bohr.
- Outputs :: an `NWChemCResult` with the energy, and the gradient written to
  `grad_h_bohr` row-major.
- Errors :: `ok` equal to 0 with the reason in `message`.
  The stub returns that with the text "NWChem embed not available (stub)" and
  the hint to provide `libnwchemc.so` on the dlopen path.

#### `nwchemc_version`

```c
const char *nwchemc_version(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the engine version string, in static storage.
  Do not free it.
- Errors :: none.

#### `nwchemc_available`

```c
int nwchemc_available(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 1 when the library embeds NWChem (`RGPOT_HAS_NWCHEM` in the engine
  build), 0 for the stub.
- Errors :: none.

### CPMD: `cpmd_c_abi.h`

The header is `CppCore/rgpot/CPMDPot/cpmd_c_abi.h`.
The engine is `libcpmdc`, documented at
[cpmdc.rgoswami.me](https://cpmdc.rgoswami.me).
Two call styles exist.
The one-shot calls take the parameter message on every call.
A session holds the parameters once, and each step then passes a serialized
`ForceInput` and receives an unpacked flat `PotentialResult`.
Positions are in Angstrom and energies in Hartree.
A gradient is in Hartree/Bohr; a force is the negative of a gradient.
The result-message calls convert to `ForceInput.energyUnit` and
`energyUnit / lengthUnit`.

#### `CPMDCResult`

- Inputs :: none; a struct returned by value.
- Units :: `energy_h` is in Hartree (the CPMD native energy).
- Outputs :: `ok` (non-zero on success), `energy_h`, and `message`, a
  NUL-terminated status or error text of at most 512 bytes.
- Errors :: none; a failure is `ok` equal to 0 with the reason in `message`.

#### `CPMDCSession`

- Inputs :: none; an opaque type, created by `cpmdc_session_create`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a handle for repeated evaluations with one parameter set.
  It owns a copy of the serialized parameters, so the caller may free its buffer
  after creation.
- Errors :: none.
  Destroy it with `cpmdc_session_destroy`.

#### `CPMDCFeatureKind`

- Inputs :: none; an enum.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `CPMDC_FEATURE_SECTION` (1), `CPMDC_FEATURE_PARAMS` (2),
  `CPMDC_FEATURE_ABI` (3) and `CPMDC_FEATURE_KEYWORD` (4).
- Errors :: none.

#### `CPMDCFeatureEntry`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs ::
  `feature_id`, a string such as `section.dft` or `catalog.section.DFT`; `kind`, a `CPMDCFeatureKind`; `stub_applicable`
  and `embed_applicable`, non-zero when the feature applies to the stub and to
  the real embed.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cpmdc_set_params`

```c
int cpmdc_set_params(const void *params_capnp, size_t params_capnp_size_bytes);
```

- Inputs :: `params_capnp`, an unpacked flat `CPMDParams` message, and its size
  in bytes.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 0 on success.
- Errors :: -1 on a parse or configuration failure; the stub always returns -1.

#### `cpmdc_energy_gradient`

```c
CPMDCResult cpmdc_energy_gradient(int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, const void *params_capnp, size_t params_capnp_size_bytes, double *grad_h_bohr);
```

- Inputs :: `n_atoms`; `positions_ang`,
  3*n doubles; `atomic_numbers`, n values; the parameter message and its size; `grad_h_bohr`, room for 3*n
  doubles.
- Units :: Angstrom in, Hartree and Hartree/Bohr out.
  CPMD's ionic forces are negated into a nuclear gradient, as `nwchemc` does.
- Outputs :: a `CPMDCResult` with the energy; the gradient is written to
  `grad_h_bohr`.
- Errors :: `ok` equal to 0 with the reason in `message`.
  The stub returns "CPMD embed not available in cpmdc stub".

#### `cpmdc_energy`

```c
CPMDCResult cpmdc_energy(int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, const void *params_capnp, size_t params_capnp_size_bytes);
```

- Inputs :: as `cpmdc_energy_gradient`, without the gradient buffer.
- Units :: Angstrom in, Hartree out.
- Outputs :: a `CPMDCResult` with the total energy; no gradient is allocated.
- Errors :: as `cpmdc_energy_gradient`.

#### `cpmdc_energy_forces`

```c
CPMDCResult cpmdc_energy_forces(int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, const void *params_capnp, size_t params_capnp_size_bytes, double *forces_h_bohr);
```

- Inputs :: as `cpmdc_energy_gradient`, with `forces_h_bohr` for the forces.
- Units :: Angstrom in, Hartree and Hartree/Bohr out.
- Outputs :: a `CPMDCResult` with the energy, and the negative gradient written
  to `forces_h_bohr`.
- Errors :: as `cpmdc_energy_gradient`.

#### `cpmdc_session_create`

```c
CPMDCSession *cpmdc_session_create(const void *params_capnp, size_t params_capnp_size_bytes);
```

- Inputs :: the unpacked flat `CPMDParams` message and its size.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a new session that holds a copy of the message.
- Errors :: the stub returns NULL.

#### `cpmdc_session_set_params`

```c
int cpmdc_session_set_params(CPMDCSession *session, const void *params_capnp, size_t params_capnp_size_bytes);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, a parameter message and its size.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 0 on success.
  Call it before the session accepts a topology.
- Errors :: non-zero on failure; the stub returns -1.

#### `cpmdc_session_destroy`

```c
void cpmdc_session_destroy(CPMDCSession *session);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, a handle from `cpmdc_session_create`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: nothing; the session is released.
- Errors :: none; the call cannot fail.
  The stub ignores its argument.

#### `cpmdc_session_select_orbitals`

```c
int cpmdc_session_select_orbitals(CPMDCSession *session, long long key);
```

- Inputs :: `session` and `key`, the name of the calculation the next
  evaluations belong to.
  The engine keeps the converged orbitals per key, so a calculator that
  evaluates several images or beads in turn starts each SCF from that image's or
  bead's own previous orbitals.
  The symbol is optional: an engine without it keeps one stored copy.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 0 when `session` is non-null and the runtime accepts `key`.
  A new key is seeded from the session's current orbitals, and a key with a
  stored copy gets those orbitals back.
- Errors :: -1 when `session` is NULL, `key` is refused, or the library is the
  stub; the session's active key and orbitals are then unchanged.

#### `cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals`

```c
int cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals(CPMDCSession *session, long long from_key, long long to_key);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, and the two keys.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 0 after the orbitals stored under
  `from_key` are copied to `to_key`.
- Errors :: -1 when either key is invalid or unsupported; the stub returns -1.

#### `cpmdc_session_energy_gradient`

```c
CPMDCResult cpmdc_session_energy_gradient(CPMDCSession *session, int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, double *grad_h_bohr);
```

- Inputs :: `session`; the geometry as for `cpmdc_energy_gradient`; the gradient
  buffer.
- Units :: Angstrom in, Hartree and Hartree/Bohr out.
- Outputs :: a `CPMDCResult` with the energy; the gradient in `grad_h_bohr`.
- Errors :: `ok` equal to 0 with the reason in `message`; the stub returns the
  not-available text.

#### `cpmdc_session_energy`

```c
CPMDCResult cpmdc_session_energy(CPMDCSession *session, int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers);
```

- Inputs :: `session` and the geometry.
- Units :: Angstrom in, Hartree out.
- Outputs :: a `CPMDCResult` with the total energy.
- Errors :: as `cpmdc_session_energy_gradient`.

#### `cpmdc_session_energy_forces`

```c
CPMDCResult cpmdc_session_energy_forces(CPMDCSession *session, int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, double *forces_h_bohr);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, the geometry and a force buffer.
- Units :: Angstrom in, Hartree and Hartree/Bohr out.
- Outputs :: a `CPMDCResult` with the energy; the forces in `forces_h_bohr`.
- Errors :: as `cpmdc_session_energy_gradient`.

#### `cpmdc_session_calculate_forces`

```c
CPMDCResult cpmdc_session_calculate_forces(CPMDCSession *session, const void *force_input_capnp, size_t force_input_capnp_size_bytes, double *forces_h_bohr, size_t forces_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`; `force_input_capnp`, a serialized `ForceInput` for one
  step, and its size; `forces_h_bohr` with room for `forces_len` doubles.
- Units :: the session keeps the `CPMDParams`; the call returns CPMD native
  units, Hartree and Hartree/Bohr.
- Outputs :: a `CPMDCResult` with the energy; the forces in `forces_h_bohr`.
- Errors :: `ok` equal to 0 with the reason in `message`; the stub returns the
  not-available text.

#### `cpmdc_session_calculate_result`

```c
CPMDCResult cpmdc_session_calculate_result(CPMDCSession *session, const void *force_input_capnp, size_t force_input_capnp_size_bytes, void *potential_result_capnp, size_t potential_result_capnp_capacity_bytes, size_t *potential_result_capnp_size_bytes);
```

- Inputs :: `session`; a serialized `ForceInput` and its size; an output buffer
  with its capacity in bytes; a pointer for the number of bytes written.
- Units :: the energy and forces leave in `ForceInput.energyUnit` and
  `energyUnit / lengthUnit`.
- Outputs :: a `CPMDCResult`, and an unpacked flat `PotentialResult` written to
  the buffer.
- Errors :: when the capacity is too small the call returns `ok` equal to 0,
  writes the required size to `potential_result_capnp_size_bytes` and does not
  evaluate CPMD; `cpmdc_potential_result_size_for_force_input` gives the size
  beforehand.
  The stub returns the not-available text.

#### `cpmdc_calculate_result`

```c
CPMDCResult cpmdc_calculate_result(const void *params_capnp, size_t params_capnp_size_bytes, const void *force_input_capnp, size_t force_input_capnp_size_bytes, void *potential_result_capnp, size_t potential_result_capnp_capacity_bytes, size_t *potential_result_capnp_size_bytes);
```

- Inputs :: the parameter message and its size, then the arguments of
  `cpmdc_session_calculate_result` without the session.
  A caller that takes many steps creates one session instead.
- Units :: as `cpmdc_session_calculate_result`.
- Outputs :: a `CPMDCResult` and the `PotentialResult` bytes.
- Errors :: as `cpmdc_session_calculate_result`.

#### `cpmdc_potential_result_size_for_force_input`

```c
size_t cpmdc_potential_result_size_for_force_input(const void *force_input_capnp, size_t force_input_capnp_size_bytes);
```

- Inputs :: a serialized `ForceInput` and its size.
- Units :: the result is a byte count.
- Outputs :: the number of bytes a `PotentialResult` for this input needs.
  The call parses the geometry only; it neither initializes nor evaluates CPMD.
- Errors :: returns 0 when the message is invalid or too large for the ABI; the
  stub always returns 0.

#### `cpmdc_version`

```c
const char *cpmdc_version(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the compiled library version string.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cpmdc_available`

```c
int cpmdc_available(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 1 when the embedded OpenCPMD runtime is available, 0 for the stub.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cpmdc_finalize`

```c
void cpmdc_finalize(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.

- Errors :: none; the stub does nothing.

#### `cpmdc_feature_count`

### MOPAC: `mopac_c_abi.h`

The header is `CppCore/rgpot/MOPACPot/mopac_c_abi.h`; it must stay in lockstep
with `mopacc.h` of the `mopacc` project.
Options are the packed struct `MopacCParams`, not Cap'n Proto.
The version macro `RGPOT_MOPACC_C_ABI_VERSION` is 1.
The model codes are `MOPACC_MODEL_PM7` (0),
`MOPACC_MODEL_PM6_D3H4` (1), `MOPACC_MODEL_PM6_ORG` (2), `MOPACC_MODEL_PM6` (3),
`MOPACC_MODEL_AM1` (4) and `MOPACC_MODEL_RM1` (5).

#### `MopacCParams`

- Inputs :: none; a struct.
- Units :: none stated by the header; the fields are those of
  `MOPACPot::Config`.
- Outputs :: `charge` (an int), `spin` (an int), `model` (a `MOPACC_MODEL_*`
  code), `tolerance` (a double) and `max_time` (an int).
  `MOPACPot` defaults are 0, 0, 4 (AM1), 1.0 and 3600.
- Errors :: none.

#### `MopacCResult`

- Inputs :: none; a struct returned by value.
- Units :: `energy_h` is in Hartree.
- Outputs :: `ok`, `energy_h` and `message`, a NUL-terminated text of at most
  512 bytes.
- Errors :: none; a failure is `ok` equal to 0 with the reason in `message`.

#### `mopacc_set_params`

```c
int mopacc_set_params(const void *params, size_t params_size_bytes);
```

- Inputs :: `params`, a `MopacCParams`, and its size in bytes.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 0 on success.
  `MOPACPot` calls it once when the symbol exists and ignores the status.
- Errors :: the stub returns -1.

#### `mopacc_energy_gradient`

```c
MopacCResult mopacc_energy_gradient(int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, const void *params, size_t params_size_bytes, double *grad_h_bohr);
```

- Inputs :: `n_atoms`; positions in Angstrom, 3*n doubles; `atomic_numbers`;
  `params` and its size; `grad_h_bohr`, room for 3*n doubles.
- Units :: Angstrom in, Hartree and Hartree/Bohr out.
- Outputs :: a `MopacCResult` with the energy; the gradient in `grad_h_bohr`.
- Errors :: `ok` equal to 0 with the reason in `message`.
  The stub returns "mopacc embed not available (stub)" and the hint to provide
  `libmopacc.so` on the dlopen path.

#### `mopacc_c_abi_version`

```c
int mopacc_c_abi_version(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the ABI version the library was built against.
  `MOPACPot` refuses a library whose value differs from
  `RGPOT_MOPACC_C_ABI_VERSION`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `mopacc_available`

```c
int mopacc_available(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: non-zero when the library can run OpenMOPAC, 0 for the stub.
- Errors :: none.

#### `mopacc_version`

```c
const char *mopacc_version(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the library version string, in static storage.
- Errors :: none.

### CP2K: `cp2kc_abi.h`

The header is `CppCore/rgpot/CP2KPot/cp2kc_abi.h`.
The shim `libcp2kc_rgpot` owns the libcp2k state: initialisation, the MPI
communicator, one force environment per orbital key, and the SCF convergence
check.
It speaks CP2K's atomic units and takes no Cap'n Proto.
Positions and cell vectors arrive in Bohr, the energy leaves in Hartree and the
forces in Hartree/Bohr.
Every rank of a calculator calls the session functions together, in the same
order and with the same arguments.
The macro `CP2KC_ABI_VERSION` is 1.
The return codes of `cp2kc_session_calculate` are
`CP2KC_OK` (0), `CP2KC_BAD_ARGUMENT` (1), `CP2KC_SCF_NOT_CONVERGED` (2) and
`CP2KC_FATAL` (-1, and any other negative value).

#### `CP2KCSession`

- Inputs :: none; an opaque type, created by `cp2kc_session_create`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a handle that owns every force environment of the session.
- Errors :: none.
  Destroy it with `cp2kc_session_destroy`.

#### `cp2kc_abi_version`

```c
int cp2kc_abi_version(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the `CP2KC_ABI_VERSION` the shim was built with.
  `CP2KPot` refuses a shim that reports another.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cp2kc_version`

```c
const char *cp2kc_version(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the shim and CP2K version text.
  The pointer stays valid.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cp2kc_available`

```c
int cp2kc_available(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: non-zero when the shim can run CP2K.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cp2kc_adopt_calculator_comm`

```c
int cp2kc_adopt_calculator_comm(const void *comm, size_t comm_bytes, int ranks_per_calc);
```

- Inputs :: `comm`, a pointer to an `MPI_Comm` of `comm_bytes` bytes, and
  `ranks_per_calc`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the calculator index.
  The shim keeps the handle, converts it to the Fortran handle libcp2k takes,
  and never frees it.
  Without this call the shim runs every force environment on `MPI_COMM_WORLD`.
- Errors :: -1 when the shim refuses the communicator.

#### `cp2kc_session_create`

```c
CP2KCSession *cp2kc_session_create(const char *deck, const char *dir, char *err, size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `deck`, the complete CP2K input text; `dir`, an existing directory;
  `err`, a buffer of `err_len` bytes for a message.
  The shim writes the deck to
  `dir/input.inp`; CP2K writes its output to `dir/cp2k.out` for the first force
  environment and `dir/cp2k-<n>.out` for later ones.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a new session.
  The first session initialises libcp2k, with
  `cp2k_init_without_mpi` when MPI is already initialised and `cp2k_init`
  otherwise; in that second case the shim finalises CP2K and MPI at exit.
- Errors :: NULL, with the reason in `err`.

#### `cp2kc_session_select_orbitals`

```c
int cp2kc_session_select_orbitals(CP2KCSession *session, long long key);
```

- Inputs :: `session` and `key`, the name of the calculation the following
  evaluations belong to.
  The shim creates one force environment per key on the key's first evaluation,
  so each band image or ring-polymer bead keeps its own wavefunction and
  extrapolation history.
  Before the first call the key is 0.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: 0.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cp2kc_session_calculate`

```c
int cp2kc_session_calculate(CP2KCSession *session, int n_atoms, const double *pos_bohr, const double *cell_bohr9, double *e_ha, double *f_ha_bohr, char *err, size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`; `n_atoms`, which must match the deck; `pos_bohr`, 3*n
  Cartesian positions;
  `cell_bohr9`, the cell vectors a, b and c as the rows of a row-major 3x3 matrix (the shim calls `cp2k_set_cell` only when the cell differs from the one the key's force environment last saw); `e_ha`
  and `f_ha_bohr`, the outputs; `err` and `err_len`, a message buffer.
- Units :: positions and cell in Bohr, energy in Hartree, forces (not gradients)
  in Hartree/Bohr.
- Outputs :: 0 with the potential energy in
  `e_ha` and 3*n forces in `f_ha_bohr`.
- Errors :: `CP2KC_BAD_ARGUMENT` for a null argument or an atom count that
  differs from the deck; `CP2KC_SCF_NOT_CONVERGED` when the SCF failed, returned
  on every rank for the same call with the energy and forces not valid; a
  negative value when the failure is fatal.

#### `cp2kc_session_destroy`

```c
void cp2kc_session_destroy(CP2KCSession *session);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, a handle from `cp2kc_session_create`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: nothing; every force environment of the session is destroyed and
  the session is freed.
- Errors :: none.

# Cap'n Proto schema

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/capnp_schema.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/capnp_schema.html

This page is generated by `docs/gen_capnp_reference.py` from the schema the
build compiles, which is `CppCore/rgpot/rpc/Potentials.capnp` with the
diffs of `CppCore/rgpot/rpc/local/series` applied.
Change a comment in the schema, then run the script again; do not edit this
page.

Cap'n Proto names a field, union arm, enumerant or method on the wire by its
ordinal, so a row keeps its ordinal for good.
The type column is as written in the schema, and the default column is empty
when the schema gives none (zero, empty or false by the Cap'n Proto rule).
A union arm is written `name @N :Type`; exactly one arm is set.
A row that reads "No comment in the schema" has none upstream, so the
comment has to be added to the pinned schema before this page can say more.
The meaning of each `PotentialConfig` arm and the ordering of the overlay are
in `potential_config`.

### Wire messages and the service

#### struct ForceInput

Input configuration for a potential energy evaluation.
Unit strings are parsed by rgpot::units::unit_conversion_factor().
Examples: "angstrom", "bohr", "eV", "hartree", "kJ/mol", "kcal/mol".

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `ForceInput.pos` | 0 | `List(Float64)` |  | Flat array of atomic coordinates [natoms * 3]. |
| `ForceInput.atmnrs` | 1 | `List(Int32)` |  | Array of atomic numbers [natoms]. |
| `ForceInput.box` | 2 | `List(Float64)` |  | Simulation cell vectors [9] (row-major 3x3). |
| `ForceInput.lengthUnit` | 3 | `Text` | `"angstrom"` | Unit for positions and box vectors. |
| `ForceInput.energyUnit` | 4 | `Text` | `"eV"` | Unit for energy and forces output. |
| `ForceInput.hasCharge` | 5 | `Bool` | `false` | Override NWChemParams.charge for this step. |
| `ForceInput.charge` | 6 | `Int32` | `0` | Per-step charge when hasCharge is true. |
| `ForceInput.hasMultiplicity` | 7 | `Bool` | `false` | Override NWChemParams.multiplicity for this step. |
| `ForceInput.multiplicity` | 8 | `Int32` | `1` | Per-step spin multiplicity when hasMultiplicity is true. |
| `ForceInput.neighbors` | 9 | `NeighborRequest` |  | Optional. Old clients leave it unset and no neighbour list is returned. |
| `ForceInput.hasOrbitalKey` | 10 | `Bool` | `false` | Select keyed orbitals for this image or bead. |
| `ForceInput.orbitalKey` | 11 | `Int64` | `0` | Per-step orbital key when hasOrbitalKey is true. |

#### struct PotentialResult

Results returned from a potential energy evaluation.

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `PotentialResult.energy` | 0 | `Float64` |  | Calculated potential energy. |
| `PotentialResult.forces` | 1 | `List(Float64)` |  | Flat array of atomic forces [natoms * 3]. |
| `PotentialResult.hessian` | 2 | `List(Float64)` |  | Dense Cartesian Hessian [natoms * 3]^2. |
| `PotentialResult.dipole` | 3 | `List(Float64)` |  | Total dipole vector [3] in atomic units. |
| `PotentialResult.quadrupole` | 4 | `List(Float64)` |  | Traceless quadrupole [6] in atomic units. |
| `PotentialResult.optimizedPos` | 5 | `List(Float64)` |  | Optimized Cartesian coordinates [natoms * 3]. |
| `PotentialResult.frequencies` | 6 | `List(Float64)` |  | Harmonic vibrational frequencies [natoms * 3] in cm^-1. |
| `PotentialResult.intensities` | 7 | `List(Float64)` |  | Harmonic IR intensities [natoms * 3] in atomic units. |
| `PotentialResult.stress` | 8 | `List(Float64)` |  | Stress tensor [9] in energy/length^3 units. |
| `PotentialResult.polarizability` | 9 | `List(Float64)` |  | Polarizability / aoresponse vector (backend-defined length). |
| `PotentialResult.gradient` | 10 | `List(Float64)` |  | Flat nuclear gradient [natoms * 3] in energy/length units. |
| `PotentialResult.normalModes` | 11 | `List(Float64)` |  | Dense Cartesian normal-mode matrix [natoms * 3]^2. |
| `PotentialResult.zeroPointEnergy` | 12 | `Float64` |  | Vibrational zero-point correction in energy units. |
| `PotentialResult.thermalEnergy` | 13 | `Float64` |  | Vibrational thermal energy correction in energy units. |
| `PotentialResult.thermalEnthalpy` | 14 | `Float64` |  | Vibrational thermal enthalpy correction in energy units. |
| `PotentialResult.entropy` | 15 | `Float64` |  | Vibrational total entropy (backend units). |
| `PotentialResult.heatCapacityCv` | 16 | `Float64` |  | Constant-volume heat capacity (backend units). |
| `PotentialResult.projectedFrequencies` | 17 | `List(Float64)` |  | Frequencies with translations/rotations projected out. |
| `PotentialResult.projectedIntensities` | 18 | `List(Float64)` |  | IR intensities for projected modes. |
| `PotentialResult.energyComponents` | 19 | `List(Float64)` |  | ener_com scalars etot..eefield (24) when componentsValid. |
| `PotentialResult.componentsValid` | 20 | `Bool` | `false` | True when energyComponents holds a harvested vector. |
| `PotentialResult.chargeIntegrals` | 21 | `List(Float64)` |  | chrg: csumg,csumr,csums,csumsabs |
| `PotentialResult.chargeValid` | 22 | `Bool` | `false` | True when chargeIntegrals holds a harvested vector. |
| `PotentialResult.multiStateEnergies` | 23 | `List(Float64)` |  | ener_c + ener_d catalog |
| `PotentialResult.multiStateValid` | 24 | `Bool` | `false` | True when multiStateEnergies holds a harvested vector. |
| `PotentialResult.mdTrajectoryRow` | 25 | `List(Float64)` |  | MD ENERGY row incl. EKINC when MD ran |
| `PotentialResult.mdTrajectoryValid` | 26 | `Bool` | `false` | True when mdTrajectoryRow holds a harvested row. |
| `PotentialResult.embedMdPropsSkipped` | 27 | `Bool` | `true` | true when MD/PROP not harvested this eval (honest skip) |
| `PotentialResult.neighborList` | 28 | `NeighborList` |  | Present only when ForceInput.neighbors was set. A stream is one chunk; more is true when the client should ask again with the same query. |

#### struct Capabilities

Backend self-description returned by `<p>_capabilities_result()`.
Loaders (rgpot) negotiate against this message before dispatching work: which calculate operations the backend implements, which CommonMethodSpec fields its overlay lowers, and which PotentialConfig arms it accepts.
Backends fill it from their compiled feature inventory, so a stub build reports available = false with the same operation surface as the embed.

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `Capabilities.backendName` | 0 | `Text` |  | ABI prefix, e.g. "nwchemc" or "cpmdc". |
| `Capabilities.backendVersion` | 1 | `Text` |  | `<p>_version()` string. |
| `Capabilities.abiVersion` | 2 | `Int32` |  | `<p>_abi_version()` value. |
| `Capabilities.available` | 3 | `Bool` |  | `<p>_available()`: embed shell linked in. |
| `Capabilities.operations` | 4 | `List(Operation)` |  | Calculate operations the ABI serves. |
| `Capabilities.loweredCommonFields` | 5 | `List(Text)` |  | CommonMethodSpec field names the overlay lowers. |
| `Capabilities.configKinds` | 6 | `List(Text)` |  | PotentialConfig arms accepted, e.g. "nwchem". |
| `Capabilities.schemaVersion` | 7 | `Text` |  | Potentials.capnp release the backend compiled against. |
| `Capabilities.protocolFamily` | 8 | `Text` |  | Stable RPC family, e.g. "rgpot.potentials". |
| `Capabilities.protocolMajor` | 9 | `UInt16` |  | Wire-incompatible changes increment this value. |
| `Capabilities.protocolMinor` | 10 | `UInt16` |  | Additive wire-compatible changes increment this value. |
| `Capabilities.schemaId` | 11 | `Text` |  | Stable Cap'n Proto schema identity. |
| `Capabilities.bridgeAbiMajor` | 12 | `UInt16` |  | eindir objective ABI major revision. |
| `Capabilities.bridgeAbiMinor` | 13 | `UInt16` |  | eindir objective ABI minor revision. |
| `Capabilities.bridgeLayout` | 14 | `UInt32` |  | eindir objective layout revision. |
| `Capabilities.dlpackMajor` | 15 | `UInt16` |  | DLPack callback major revision. |
| `Capabilities.dlpackMinor` | 16 | `UInt16` |  | DLPack callback minor revision. |
| `Capabilities.bridgeFeatures` | 17 | `UInt64` |  | eindir bridge feature bitset. |
| `Capabilities.buildVersion` | 18 | `Text` |  | Version of the build that produced this message; empty when unknown. |
| `Capabilities.buildRevision` | 19 | `Text` |  | Source revision of that build (e.g. a git commit); empty when unknown. |

#### enum Capabilities.Operation

| Enumerant | Ordinal | Description |

| `Capabilities.Operation.energy` | 0 | The operation that `Potential.calculateEnergy` serves. |
| `Capabilities.Operation.forces` | 1 | The operation that `Potential.calculateForces` serves. |
| `Capabilities.Operation.gradient` | 2 | The operation that `Potential.calculateGradient` serves. |
| `Capabilities.Operation.hessian` | 3 | The operation that `Potential.calculateHessian` serves. |
| `Capabilities.Operation.dipole` | 4 | The operation that `Potential.calculateDipole` serves. |
| `Capabilities.Operation.polarizability` | 5 | The operation that `Potential.calculatePolarizability` serves. |
| `Capabilities.Operation.quadrupole` | 6 | The operation that `Potential.calculateQuadrupole` serves. |
| `Capabilities.Operation.stress` | 7 | The operation that `Potential.calculateStress` serves. |
| `Capabilities.Operation.optimize` | 8 | The operation that `Potential.calculateOptimize` serves. |
| `Capabilities.Operation.frequencies` | 9 | The operation that `Potential.calculateFrequencies` serves. |
| `Capabilities.Operation.hessianVector` | 10 | The operation that `Potential.calculateHvp` serves. |

#### interface Potential

The RPC interface for remote calculations.

| Method | Ordinal | Signature | Description |
|-
| `Potential.calculate` | 0 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Executes the potential and force calculation. The input atomic configuration. The resulting energy and force vector. |
| `Potential.configure` | 1 | `(config:PotentialConfig)->(ok:Bool,message:Text)` | Apply rgpot user parameters (PotentialConfig) before calculate(). Backend-tagged options (nwchem, future metatomic/xtb/...). ok=false if the arm does not match the server backend or apply failed. |
| `Potential.calculateEnergy` | 2 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Compute only the scalar potential energy for this geometry. PotentialResult.energy in ForceInput.energyUnit. |
| `Potential.calculateForces` | 3 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Compute potential energy and force vector for this geometry. PotentialResult.energy and PotentialResult.forces. |
| `Potential.calculateHessian` | 4 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Compute a dense Cartesian Hessian for this geometry. PotentialResult.hessian in energyUnit / lengthUnit^2. |
| `Potential.calculateDipole` | 5 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Compute the total electric dipole vector for this geometry. PotentialResult.dipole in atomic units. |
| `Potential.calculateQuadrupole` | 6 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Compute the total traceless electric quadrupole tensor. PotentialResult.quadrupole in atomic units as xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz. |
| `Potential.calculateStress` | 7 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Compute the periodic stress tensor for this geometry. PotentialResult.stress in energyUnit / lengthUnit^3. |
| `Potential.calculateHvp` | 14 | `(fip:ForceInput,direction:List(Float64))->(product:List(Float64))` | Exact Cartesian energy-Hessian product for one direction. |
| `Potential.calculateOptimize` | 8 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Optimize this geometry and return final coordinates. PotentialResult.optimizedPos in ForceInput.lengthUnit. |
| `Potential.calculateFrequencies` | 9 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Compute harmonic vibrational frequencies and IR intensities. PotentialResult.frequencies in cm^-1 and intensities in atomic units. |
| `Potential.calculatePolarizability` | 10 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Compute the electric polarizability response vector. PotentialResult.polarizability stores NWChem aoresponse:alpha. |
| `Potential.calculateGradient` | 11 | `(fip:ForceInput)->(result:PotentialResult)` | Compute potential energy and nuclear gradient for this geometry. PotentialResult.energy and PotentialResult.gradient. |
| `Potential.getCapabilities` | 12 | `()->(capabilities:Capabilities)` | Capabilities of this server, read before any calculate call. The protocol, schema, eindir bridge, DLPack and build identity. buildVersion and buildRevision are empty when the build does not know them. |
| `Potential.neighbours` | 13 | `(fip:ForceInput,request:NeighborRequest)->(neighbors:NeighborList)` | One chunk of a neighbour query. The whole list is not required on the wire. The client sends NeighborRequest.cursor and repeats the call while NeighborList.more is true, passing NeighborList.next back as the next cursor. |

### Configuration carrier

#### struct CommonMethodSpec

NOMAD-metainfo-aligned normalized method overlay (the thin Esperanto).
Field names follow NOMAD's normalized method quantities (xc functional as libxc identifiers, Monkhorst-Pack k mesh, smearing kind/width, SCF thresholds).
This struct lowers ONE-WAY into the native backend arm before it is applied; any knob the native arm also sets wins.
It never replaces the arms -- the long tail of code-specific options stays code-native.

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `CommonMethodSpec.xcFunctionals` | 0 | `List(Text)` |  | libxc names ("GGA_X_PBE", "GGA_C_PBE") or composites ("PBE", "B3LYP"). |
| `CommonMethodSpec.basisSet` | 1 | `Text` | `""` | Gaussian basis name, or "planewave". |
| `CommonMethodSpec.planewaveCutoffEv` | 2 | `Float64` | `0.0` | >0 configures the plane-wave cutoff (eV). |
| `CommonMethodSpec.charge` | 3 | `Int32` | `0` | Net charge of the system, in units of the elementary charge. |
| `CommonMethodSpec.spinMultiplicity` | 4 | `Int32` | `0` | 2S+1; 0 = unset (backend default). |
| `CommonMethodSpec.scfEnergyToleranceEv` | 5 | `Float64` | `0.0` | SCF energy-change convergence (eV); 0 = unset. |
| `CommonMethodSpec.scfMaxIterations` | 6 | `Int32` | `0` | 0 = unset. |
| `CommonMethodSpec.kMesh` | 7 | `List(Int32)` |  | Monkhorst-Pack divisions [3]; empty = molecular/Gamma. |
| `CommonMethodSpec.smearing` | 8 | `Smearing` |  | Occupation smearing; the kind and the width are in Smearing. |
| `CommonMethodSpec.vanDerWaalsMethod` | 9 | `Text` | `""` | e.g. "DFT-D3", "DFT-D3(BJ)". |
| `CommonMethodSpec.relativityMethod` | 10 | `Text` | `""` | e.g. "ZORA", "DKH". |
| `CommonMethodSpec.vanDerWaalsS6` | 11 | `Float64` | `0.0` | Global dispersion scaling s6; 0 = engine default. |

#### struct CommonMethodSpec.Smearing

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `CommonMethodSpec.Smearing.kind` | 0 | `Kind` | `none` | The smearing function; none switches smearing off. |
| `CommonMethodSpec.Smearing.widthEv` | 1 | `Float64` | `0.0` | The smearing width in eV. |

#### enum CommonMethodSpec.Smearing.Kind

| Enumerant | Ordinal | Description |
|-
| `CommonMethodSpec.Smearing.Kind.none` | 0 | The `none` value of `enum Kind`. |
| `CommonMethodSpec.Smearing.Kind.fermi` | 1 | The `fermi` value of `enum Kind`. |
| `CommonMethodSpec.Smearing.Kind.gaussian` | 2 | The `gaussian` value of `enum Kind`. |
| `CommonMethodSpec.Smearing.Kind.methfesselPaxton` | 3 | The `methfesselPaxton` value of `enum Kind`. |

#### struct PotentialSpec

One backend, named and configured, as a value that can be carried inside another backend's configuration.
Backend selection is otherwise a property of which engine library a host dlopens, which works while a potential is a leaf.
A learning surrogate is not a leaf: it wraps an oracle and has to say which one and how it is configured, so the choice has to travel on the wire rather than in the host's loader.
This is that value, one arm per params struct already in this file.
Purely additive: no existing field is renumbered, so a reader that does not know this struct is unaffected.

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `PotentialSpec.nwchem` | 0 | `arm NWChemParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `NWChemParams`. |
| `PotentialSpec.cpmd` | 1 | `arm CPMDParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `CPMDParams`. |
| `PotentialSpec.metatomic` | 2 | `arm MetatomicParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `MetatomicParams`. |
| `PotentialSpec.uma` | 3 | `arm UmaParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `UmaParams`. |
| `PotentialSpec.lammps` | 4 | `arm LammpsParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `LammpsParams`. |
| `PotentialSpec.builtin` | 5 | `arm BuiltinParams` |  | Backends whose configuration is entirely a library path plus the geometry on ForceInput carry no params struct of their own. |
| `PotentialSpec.cp2k` | 6 | `arm CP2KParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `CP2KParams`. |

A named term may contain another expression or a configured leaf.

| `ExprTerm.pot` | 1 | `PotSpec` |  | The potential that evaluates the term. |

#### struct PotSpec

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `PotSpec.expr` | 0 | `arm ExprParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `ExprParams`. |
| `PotSpec.none` | 1 | `arm Void` |  | Selects this arm, which carries no data. |
| `PotSpec.potential` | 2 | `arm PotentialSpec` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `PotentialSpec`. |

#### struct PotentialConfig

rgpot user parameters (extensible, in/out via Cap'n Proto only).
This is the single user-facing options carrier for rgpot: pass in to configure a live Potential (RPC `configure` or in-process apply), and/or round-trip out when a backend supports get.
One schema for wire + embed - no parallel TOML/JSON/YAML option files for backends.
Tagged union: exactly one backend's options (or none).
Add new arms as new potentials gain runtime knobs (e.g. metatomic @2 :MetatomicParams).
`calculate` geometry stays on ForceInput; this struct is method/backend setup only.

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `PotentialConfig.none` | 0 | `arm Void` |  | No backend-specific options (or no-op configure). |
| `PotentialConfig.nwchem` | 1 | `arm NWChemParams` |  | NWChemPot / potserv ... NWChem |
| `PotentialConfig.cpmd` | 2 | `arm CPMDParams` |  | CPMDPot / potserv ... OpenCPMD |
| `PotentialConfig.metatomic` | 4 | `arm MetatomicParams` |  | MetatomicPot (torch ML models) |
| `PotentialConfig.lammps` | 5 | `arm LammpsParams` |  | lammpc dynlib shim (LAMMPS library API) |
| `PotentialConfig.xtb` | 6 | `arm XTBParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `XTBParams`. |
| `PotentialConfig.tblite` | 7 | `arm TBLiteParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `TBLiteParams`. |
| `PotentialConfig.uma` | 8 | `arm UmaParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `UmaParams`. |
| `PotentialConfig.lj` | 9 | `arm LennardJonesParams` |  | LJPot or LJClusterPot, selected by name. |
| `PotentialConfig.morse` | 10 | `arm MorseParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `MorseParams`. |
| `PotentialConfig.zbl` | 11 | `arm ZBLParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `ZBLParams`. |
| `PotentialConfig.d3` | 12 | `arm D3Params` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `D3Params`. |
| `PotentialConfig.d4` | 13 | `arm D4Params` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `D4Params`. |
| `PotentialConfig.mopac` | 14 | `arm MOPACParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `MOPACParams`. |
| `PotentialConfig.skala` | 15 | `arm SkalaParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `SkalaParams`. |
| `PotentialConfig.expr` | 16 | `arm ExprParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `ExprParams`. |
| `PotentialConfig.cp2k` | 17 | `arm CP2KParams` |  | CP2KPot / libcp2k shim |
| `PotentialConfig.composite` | 18 | `arm CompositeParams` |  | rgpot::SumPot over PotentialSpec terms |
| `PotentialConfig.d2` | 19 | `arm D2Params` |  | rgpot::D2Pot, Grimme 2006 lattice sum |
| `PotentialConfig.d2cpmd` | 20 | `arm D2CpmdParams` |  | rgpot::D2CpmdPot, CPMD's minimum-image D2 |
| `PotentialConfig.mullerBrown` | 21 | `arm MullerBrownParams` |  | Selects this arm of the union, which carries a `MullerBrownParams`. |
| `PotentialConfig.common` | 3 | `CommonMethodSpec` |  | Normalized overlay applied BEFORE the native arm; native settings win. |

#### struct NWChemScfConvergence

Logical SCF convergence card (was directive-only "convergence tight/loose/...").

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `NWChemScfConvergence.mode` | 0 | `Mode` | `unspecified` | No comment in the schema. |

#### enum NWChemScfConvergence.Mode

| Enumerant | Ordinal | Description |
|-
| `NWChemScfConvergence.Mode.unspecified` | 0 | Do not emit convergence line from this struct. |
| `NWChemScfConvergence.Mode.tight` | 1 | Emit "convergence tight". |
| `NWChemScfConvergence.Mode.loose` | 2 | Emit "convergence loose". |
| `NWChemScfConvergence.Mode.default` | 3 | Emit "convergence default" (NWChem spelling). |
| `NWChemScfConvergence.Mode.energy` | 4 | Emit "convergence energy" (energy-only criterion). |
| `NWChemScfConvergence.Mode.density` | 5 | Emit "convergence density". |
| `NWChemScfConvergence.Mode.gradient` | 6 | Emit "convergence gradient". |

#### struct NWChemScfSemidirect

Logical SCF semidirect integral storage (was directive-only semidirect card). filesize/memsize in megawords when >0; promote int2e:* on embed when set. enabled alone (no sizes) emits "semidirect" on full and embed (no RTDB for the keyword). disabled is a no-op (leave NWChem default; no explicit off keyword).

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `NWChemScfSemidirect.enabled` | 0 | `NWChemToggle` | `unspecified` | enabled => emit semidirect; disabled => no-op. |
| `NWChemScfSemidirect.filesize` | 1 | `Int32` | `0` | Promote int2e:filesize when >0 (omit size tokens on embed). |
| `NWChemScfSemidirect.memsize` | 2 | `Int32` | `0` | Promote int2e:memsize when >0 (omit size tokens on embed). |

#### struct CPMDParams

CPMD-specific knobs (backend arm inside PotentialConfig / rgpot params).
Not a standalone config language — only used when the active potential is CPMD.
Same fields in/out via Cap'n Proto.
Geometry for each evaluation is ForceInput.

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `CPMDParams.functional` | 0 | `Text` | `"BLYP"` | Default DFT functional (also in dft section). |
| `CPMDParams.cutOffRy` | 1 | `Float64` | `70.0` | Plane-wave cutoff in Rydberg. |
| `CPMDParams.charge` | 2 | `Int32` | `0` | No comment in the schema. |
| `CPMDParams.multiplicity` | 3 | `Int32` | `1` | 2S+1; >1 enables LSD when rendering defaults. |
| `CPMDParams.task` | 4 | `Text` | `"gradient"` | energy / gradient / md / optimize (frontend hint). |
| `CPMDParams.title` | 5 | `Text` | `""` | Optional comment header in rendered deck. |
| `CPMDParams.memoryMb` | 6 | `UInt32` | `0` | Frontend memory hint; 0 => environment defaults. |
| `CPMDParams.scratchDir` | 7 | `Text` | `""` | Fallback &CPMD FILEPATH directory. |
| `CPMDParams.permanentDir` | 8 | `Text` | `""` | Preferred &CPMD FILEPATH restart directory. |
| `CPMDParams.cpmdRoot` | 9 | `Text` | `""` | OpenCPMD source/build tree; empty => env CPMD_ROOT. |
| `CPMDParams.enginePath` | 10 | `Text` | `""` | Frontend engine selection hint. |
| `CPMDParams.inputBlocks` | 11 | `List(Text)` |  | Raw &SECTION blocks applied before generated ones. |
| `CPMDParams.inputSections` | 12 | `List(CPMDInputSection)` |  | Structured CPMD input sections. |

#### struct GprParams

Learning-surrogate arm: a Gaussian process that answers where its posterior is resolved and calls an oracle where it is not.
The oracle is a nested PotentialSpec rather than a callback, so a host that selects this backend does not also have to supply ground truth through a side channel.
That is the difference between an engine eOn can load and one eOn can use: its GenericEngineLoader resolves create/destroy/force and never calls set_callbacks, so an engine that expects its oracle by callback gets none.
The gate is two-sided and stated in multiples of the model's own likelihood noise rather than in absolute energy, so it transfers across systems.

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `GprParams.oracle` | 0 | `PotentialSpec` |  | Ground truth. Required. |
| `GprParams.sigmaLoFactor` | 1 | `Float64` | `1.0` | Answer from the model below this * sigma. |
| `GprParams.sigmaHiFactor` | 2 | `Float64` | `20.0` | Above this * sigma, do not learn the row. |
| `GprParams.certifyBelowForce` | 3 | `Float64` | `0.0` | A predicted force magnitude under this (eV/Angstrom) forces a ground-truth call, so a driver's convergence claim is checked rather than trusted. Non-positive disables the certificate, which leaves a driver free to converge on the surrogate's own minimum. |
| `GprParams.refitTrainingRevisions` | 4 | `UInt64` | `5` | Refit cadence in appends. |

#### struct LammpsParams

LAMMPS backend arm driving the lammpc dynlib shim. lammpc calls the actual liblammps functions directly, in process: instance creation, pair setup and pair compute, position/force array access.
No command-string parsing, no input scripts, no file traffic anywhere in the force loop.
Geometry arrives per step via ForceInput; these fields fix the interaction model once per session.

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |

| `LammpsParams.atomStyle` | 1 | `Text` | `"atomic"` | No comment in the schema. |
| `LammpsParams.pairStyle` | 2 | `Text` | `""` | pair_style args, e.g. "eam/alloy" or "lj/cut 10.0". |
| `LammpsParams.pairCoeffs` | 3 | `List(Text)` |  | pair_coeff argument lines, one entry per line. |
| `LammpsParams.typeToAtomicNumber` | 4 | `List(Int32)` |  | LAMMPS type i+1 -> Z; maps ForceInput.atmnrs. |

#### struct NeighborRequest

Neighbour query.
The same columns as rgpot::nlist::Query and rgpot_nlist_soa. format: 0 half pairs, 1 full pairs, 2 cluster of four.
A cluster is the full interaction set.
There is no half cluster, because format is one field. cut: 0 strict (distance < cutoff), 1 loose (distance < cutoff + skin, or distance <= cutoff when skin is 0). mode: 1 one stored chunk, 2 a stream that honours cursor and limit. 0 is not a mode. cursor is the pair index this chunk starts at. limit is the maximum pairs in the reply. 0 means 4096 on a stream. periodic empty means every axis is periodic.
Box rows are the lattice vectors.

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `NeighborRequest.cutoff` | 0 | `Float64` |  | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.skin` | 1 | `Float64` | `0` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.format` | 2 | `UInt8` | `0` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.cut` | 3 | `UInt8` | `0` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.periodic` | 4 | `List(Bool)` |  | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.shifts` | 5 | `Bool` | `true` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.vectors` | 6 | `Bool` | `true` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.distances` | 7 | `Bool` | `true` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.mode` | 8 | `UInt8` | `1` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.cursor` | 9 | `UInt64` | `0` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.limit` | 10 | `UInt32` | `0` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborRequest.systems` | 11 | `List(NeighborSystem)` |  | Empty for one system. Each entry is a system that does not interact with the others. Positions are concatenated in the same order, and NeighborList.first indexes that concatenation. NeighborList.system is the system of each pair. |

#### struct NeighborSystem

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `NeighborSystem.count` | 0 | `UInt32` |  | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborSystem.box` | 1 | `List(Float64)` |  | No comment in the schema. |

#### struct NeighborList

One chunk. first and second have the same length. shift has 3 times that length when shifts were requested, vector has 3 times that length, distance has that length. mask is one byte per pair, 0xff for a pair list and the low four bits for a cluster. more is true when a later chunk exists. next is the cursor to send for that chunk. status 0 is success. message is a sentence when status is not 0.
The lists are empty in that case.

| Member | Ordinal | Type | Default | Description |
|-
| `NeighborList.first` | 0 | `List(Int32)` |  | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborList.second` | 1 | `List(Int32)` |  | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborList.shift` | 2 | `List(Int32)` |  | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborList.vector` | 3 | `List(Float64)` |  | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborList.distance` | 4 | `List(Float64)` |  | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborList.mask` | 5 | `List(UInt8)` |  | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborList.more` | 6 | `Bool` | `false` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborList.next` | 7 | `UInt64` | `0` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborList.status` | 8 | `Int32` | `0` | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborList.message` | 9 | `Text` |  | No comment in the schema. |
| `NeighborList.system` | 10 | `List(Int32)` |  | System id of each pair. Empty when the request named one system. |
