# GROMACS QM/MM drop-in reference

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/gromacs_dropin.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/gromacs_dropin.html

`librgpot_gromacs` implements the C API of the CP2K library, which GROMACS calls for its QM group when built with `-DGMX_CP2K=ON`.
The steps are in
[GROMACS QM/MM drop-in](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/howto/engine-gromacs-qmmm.html), and why it
implements the CP2K interface is in
[GROMACS QM/MM through the CP2K interface](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/explanation/gromacs-qmmm.html).

### The `&RGPOT` section

The run uses `qmmm-cp2k-qmmethod = INPUT` and a `-qmi` file with an `&RGPOT`
section.
The keys `grompp` checks stay as CP2K has them.
The `&RGPOT` keys are:

| Key                     | Value                                                |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `POTENTIAL` Name        | a name from `potential_names`                   |
| `OPTIONS` key value ... | its options in Angstrom and eV; may repeat           |
| `ENGINE` path           | an `rgpot_engine_*` library, instead of `POTENTIAL`  |
| `CONFIG` path           | the engine's Cap'n Proto parameters message          |
| `CELL` PERIODIC or NONE | the GROMACS box as the cell, or an isolated region   |
| `EMBEDDING` NONE        | accept charged MM atoms that do not act on QM atoms  |

Exactly one of `POTENTIAL` and `ENGINE` is required.
`OPTIONS` go with `POTENTIAL` and `CONFIG` with `ENGINE`.
An engine's configuration is the flat message the engine ABI takes.

### Atoms, charge and multiplicity

`mdrun` writes the PDB file itself and passes its name in place of
`COORD_FILE_NAME`.
The PDB file gives each atom its element and marks it QM or MM.
Only QM atoms are passed to the potential; MM atoms get zero force from it and
keep whatever the GROMACS force field gives them.
`grompp` already removes the QM-QM nonbonded pairs and bonded terms, so the QM
region interacts only through rgpot.
A `POTENTIAL` needs `CHARGE 0` and `MULTIPLICITY 1`.
An `ENGINE` keeps a spin its `CONFIG` set explicitly when the qmi `MULTIPLICITY`
is 1, the value `grompp` writes unless it is changed.
That covers `CHARGE -1` with `MULTIPLICITY 1` as well as the default pair
`CHARGE 0` and `MULTIPLICITY 1`.
`rgpot_engine_set_charge_spin` takes the charge and the spin together and the
ABI has no getter, so the drop-in reads that spin back out of the `CONFIG`
message it already loaded.
A `CHARGE` other than 0 is applied with the configured spin.
The default pair is left on the `CONFIG`, so the call is skipped and the
configured spin stays.
Only a `MULTIPLICITY` other than 1 replaces the spin, and it is sent with the
qmi charge.
When the `CONFIG` leaves the spin at its schema default, the qmi charge and
multiplicity are both applied.
A spin the `CONFIG` sets below the least its engine accepts is refused at
start-up and never rewritten: 0 is valid for `uma`, and `metatomic`, `skala` and
`nwchem` need 1 or more.
When the engine lacks `rgpot_engine_set_charge_spin` or the call returns 3, a
charge other than 0 or a multiplicity other than 1 is refused and the file needs
`CHARGE 0` and `MULTIPLICITY 1`.

### Errors

Nothing can be returned through the libcp2k API, so every error stops `mdrun`
with status 1.
The message starts with `rgpot-gromacs:` on standard error and is repeated in
the `md_cp2k.out` file GROMACS names.
Examples are an unknown potential or option, a missing `&RGPOT` section (as with
a generated method such as `PBE`), a QM atom without an element, a `&LINK`
section, a charged MM atom without `EMBEDDING NONE`, and a failed or non-finite
evaluation at any step.

### Units and cell

GROMACS sends positions in Bohr and takes energies and forces in atomic units.
It converts them with the constants of its `units.h`, which `qmmm_units.hpp`
copies expression for expression.
So GROMACS reports the rgpot energy times 96.48533212331002
kJ/mol per eV and the forces times 964.8533212331002 kJ/(mol nm) per
eV/Angstrom, up to rounding.

With a periodic potential and `pbc = xyz`, the default is `CELL PERIODIC`: each
step the QM atoms are wrapped into the GROMACS box, which goes to the potential
as the cell, triclinic or not.
GROMACS 2024 and 2025 send the box transposed and 2026 does not; a GROMACS box
is lower triangular, so the library tells the two apart from the zeros.
`CELL NONE`, the default for a potential with free boundaries, keeps each QM
atom at the image nearest its previous position, so a molecule split by the box
stays whole, and centres the region in a cube with sides of at least 100
Angstrom and of twice the region's extent plus the cutoff plus 10 Angstrom.

### Limits

- No virial: pressure, NPT and `gmx energy` pressure terms exclude rgpot.
- No electrostatic embedding: MM charges do not act on the QM region, and no
  link atoms, so the QM group must be whole molecules or a whole crystal.
- One thread-MPI rank (`-ntmpi 1`); OpenMP threads are fine.
  `cp2k_create_force_env_comm` stops with an error.
- Tested with double-precision GROMACS only.
- The shim wraps atoms every step, as the LAMMPS pair style does.
  A kernel whose neighbour list has a Verlet skin rebuilds it whenever an atom
  crosses a cell face, so the cost per MD step exceeds that of repeated calls on
  one geometry; the benchmark in
  [GROMACS QM/MM drop-in](https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/howto/engine-gromacs-qmmm.html) measures
  both.

### C API

`engines/gromacs/libcp2k.h` declares the functions with CP2K's signatures
(`cp2k/src/start/libcp2k.h`), leaving out those GROMACS does not call.
`engines/gromacs/rgpot_gromacs.cpp` implements them.
Positions and cells are in Bohr, energies in Hartree and forces in Hartree/Bohr,
as in CP2K.
Every `n_el` is three values per atom of the PDB file, QM and MM, in its order.
A call that fails stops `mdrun` as described under Errors.

#### `force_env_t`

- Inputs :: none; an `int` handle.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `cp2k_create_force_env` returns handles 1 to 16, one per live force
  environment of the process.
- Errors :: a handle that names no live force environment stops `mdrun` with
  `<function>: no force environment <handle>`.

#### `cp2k_get_version`

```c
void cp2k_get_version(char *version_str, int str_length);
```

- Inputs :: `version_str`, a buffer of `str_length` bytes.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `rgpot <version>`, cut to fit and NUL-terminated, where `<version>`
  is the Meson project version `librgpot_gromacs` was built from.
- Errors :: none; a null buffer or a length of zero or less writes nothing.

#### `cp2k_init`

```c
void cp2k_init(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the call does nothing.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cp2k_init_without_mpi`

```c
void cp2k_init_without_mpi(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the call does nothing.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cp2k_finalize`

```c
void cp2k_finalize(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the call does nothing.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cp2k_finalize_without_mpi`

```c
void cp2k_finalize_without_mpi(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the call does nothing.
- Errors :: none.

#### `cp2k_create_force_env`

```c
void cp2k_create_force_env(force_env_t *new_force_env, const char *input_file_path,
                           const char *output_file_path);
```

- Inputs :: `input_file_path`, the CP2K input `mdrun` writes from the `-qmi`
  file; `output_file_path`, the log file, or NULL or empty for none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `*new_force_env`, a new handle.
  The `&RGPOT` section selects the potential or engine, which is opened here,
  and the PDB file the input names gives the atoms.
  The log file gets the library version, the backend, the atom counts, the
  energy of the first step in eV and, when the force environment is destroyed,
  the number of evaluations.
- Errors :: more than 16 live force environments, a null or empty
  `input_file_path`, an input or PDB file that does not parse, a backend that
  does not open, a charge or multiplicity the backend does not take,
  `CELL PERIODIC` with a backend that has free boundaries, and charged MM atoms
  without `EMBEDDING NONE`.

#### `cp2k_create_force_env_comm`

```c
void cp2k_create_force_env_comm(force_env_t *new_force_env, const char *input_file_path,
                                const char *output_file_path, int mpi_comm);
```

- Inputs :: as `cp2k_create_force_env`, and `mpi_comm`, a Fortran MPI
  communicator.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none.
- Errors :: always stops `mdrun`, with a message asking for a thread-MPI GROMACS
  with one rank (`-ntmpi 1`).

#### `cp2k_destroy_force_env`

```c
void cp2k_destroy_force_env(force_env_t force_env);
```

- Inputs :: `force_env`, a handle.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none; the engine object is destroyed, the log file closed and the
  handle freed.
  An engine library stays loaded, because a tensor runtime keeps process-wide
  state.
- Errors :: an unknown handle, as under `force_env_t`.

#### `cp2k_set_positions`

```c
void cp2k_set_positions(force_env_t force_env, const double *new_pos, int n_el);
```

- Inputs :: `force_env`; `new_pos`, `n_el` coordinates of every QM and MM atom.
- Units :: Bohr.
- Outputs :: none; the positions are kept for the next evaluation.
- Errors :: an unknown handle, or an `n_el` other than three times the atoms of
  the PDB file.

#### `cp2k_set_cell`

```c
void cp2k_set_cell(force_env_t force_env, const double *new_cell);
```

- Inputs :: `force_env`; `new_cell`, nine values, the GROMACS box row by row
  from GROMACS 2026 and transposed from 2024 and 2025.
- Units :: Bohr.
- Outputs :: none; the box rows are kept for the next evaluation.
  A cell of zeros counts as no box.
- Errors :: an unknown handle, or a cell that is neither lower nor upper
  triangular.

#### `cp2k_get_natom`

```c
void cp2k_get_natom(force_env_t force_env, int *natom);
```

- Inputs :: `force_env`; `natom`, where the count goes.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `*natom`, the number of atoms in the PDB file, QM and MM.
- Errors :: an unknown handle.

#### `cp2k_get_positions`

```c
void cp2k_get_positions(force_env_t force_env, double *pos, int n_el);
```

- Inputs :: `force_env`; `pos`, a buffer of `n_el` doubles.
- Units :: Bohr.
- Outputs :: the positions of the last `cp2k_set_positions`, unchanged, because
  the library moves no atom.
- Errors :: an unknown handle, or a wrong `n_el`.

#### `cp2k_get_forces`

```c
void cp2k_get_forces(force_env_t force_env, double *force, int n_el);
```

- Inputs :: `force_env`; `force`, a buffer of `n_el` doubles.
- Units :: Hartree/Bohr.
- Outputs :: the forces of the last evaluation on every atom; MM atoms get zero.
- Errors :: an unknown handle, a wrong `n_el`, or a call before the first
  evaluation.

#### `cp2k_get_potential_energy`

```c
void cp2k_get_potential_energy(force_env_t force_env, double *e_pot);
```

- Inputs :: `force_env`; `e_pot`, where the energy goes.
- Units :: Hartree.
- Outputs :: `*e_pot`, the energy of the last evaluation.
- Errors :: an unknown handle, or a call before the first evaluation.

#### `cp2k_calc_energy_force`

```c
void cp2k_calc_energy_force(force_env_t force_env);
```

- Inputs :: `force_env`.
- Units :: positions and cell in Bohr in, the stored energy in Hartree and
  forces in Hartree/Bohr; the potential itself sees Angstrom and returns eV.
- Outputs :: none; one rgpot evaluation of the QM atoms, with the cell chosen as
  under Units and cell.
- Errors :: an unknown handle, a call before `cp2k_set_positions`, a singular
  box, `CELL PERIODIC` without a box, a failed evaluation, or a non-finite
  energy.

#### `cp2k_calc_energy`

```c
void cp2k_calc_energy(force_env_t force_env);
```

- Inputs :: `force_env`.
- Units :: as `cp2k_calc_energy_force`.
- Outputs :: as `cp2k_calc_energy_force`, forces included.
- Errors :: as `cp2k_calc_energy_force`.

# Plugin C ABI

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/plugin_abi.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/plugin_abi.html

`include/rgpot/plugin.h` declares the descriptor a potential plugin exports.
The header needs only `<stddef.h>` and `<stdint.h>`.
A plugin shared library exports one function, `rgpot_plugin_init`, of type
`rgpot_plugin_init_fn`.
`RGPOT_PLUGIN_API_VERSION` is 1.
`RGPOT_PLUGIN_EXPORT` marks a symbol for export: `__declspec(dllexport)` on
Windows, default visibility elsewhere.

The host side is in `CppCore/rgpot/plugin/`.
`rgpot::plugin::PluginRegistry::discover` reads `RGPOT_PLUGIN_PATH`, a list of
directories separated by `:= (`;= on Windows).
It opens every regular file with the platform's library suffix (`.so`, `.dylib`
or `.dll`) in sorted order, with `RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL` on POSIX, and calls
`rgpot_plugin_init`.
A library without that symbol is skipped.
A descriptor that fails validation is skipped with a line
`[rgpot] invalid plugin PATH: REASON` on standard error.
A plugin whose name is already registered is refused.
The existing registration, including a built-in, keeps the name.
The host prints `[rgpot] plugin name collision PATH: NAME is already registered`
on standard error and `load_plugin` returns false.
The registry always holds the built-in plugins `lennard-jones`,
`classical-morse` and `sutton-chen`.
When tabulated EAM is built it also holds `eam-funcfl` and `eam-setfl`.
`lennard-jones` ignores its configuration string.
`classical-morse` reads a flat JSON object whose keys are `De`, `a=, =re`,
`cutoff` and `switch_width`; a null string, an empty string or `"{}"` selects
the potential's defaults.
`sutton-chen` reads `epsilon`, `c=, =a`, `n=, =m`, `cutoff`, `periodic` and
`stress`.
Its default is periodic, unlike the C++ struct, because the plugin advertises
`RGPOT_CAP_PERIODIC`; `"periodic": false` clears that capability and allows a
null cell.
`eam-funcfl` and `eam-setfl` read `path`, `format` (`funcfl`, `setfl` or `fs`),
`periodic`, `stress` and `skin`.
A string that is not a JSON object is the table path.
A missing path is rejected.
An unknown or duplicate key is rejected.
A built-in `calculate` returns `RGPOT_PLUGIN_INVALID_PARAM` when `n_atoms` is
zero or when `positions`, `atomic_numbers`, `forces` or, because that potential
is periodic, `cell` is null.
A zero-atom call is reported as `nAtoms must be positive`, including when
`forces` is also null.
`last_error` is the message of the last failure.
A later successful `calculate` does not clear it.
Nothing in `librgpot` calls `discover` on its own; the C++ host calls it.
`rgpot::plugin::create_from_plugin` turns a descriptor and a configuration
string, `"{}"` by default, into a potential.

### Types

#### `rgpot_plugin_status_t`

- Inputs :: none; the return type of `create` and `calculate`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `RGPOT_PLUGIN_OK` (0),
  `RGPOT_PLUGIN_INVALID_PARAM` (1), `RGPOT_PLUGIN_ERROR` (2), `RGPOT_PLUGIN_NOT_SUPPORTED`
  (3).
- Errors :: the host treats every value other than `RGPOT_PLUGIN_OK` as a
  failure and does not distinguish the others.

#### `rgpot_plugin_caps_t`

- Inputs :: none; the bits a `capabilities` callback returns.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `RGPOT_CAP_ENERGY` (1), `RGPOT_CAP_FORCES` (2),
  `RGPOT_CAP_VARIANCE` (4), `RGPOT_CAP_STRESS` (8, reserved),
  `RGPOT_CAP_INSTANCE_SAFE` (16), `RGPOT_CAP_PERIODIC` (32).
- Errors :: the host throws
  `std::invalid_argument` ("plugin must provide both energy and forces") when `RGPOT_CAP_ENERGY` or `RGPOT_CAP_FORCES`
  is missing.

The host reads
`RGPOT_CAP_INSTANCE_SAFE` and `RGPOT_CAP_PERIODIC` and ignores `RGPOT_CAP_VARIANCE` and `RGPOT_CAP_STRESS`.
With `RGPOT_CAP_INSTANCE_SAFE` the potential reports per-instance reentrancy and
calls are not locked.
Without it, every `calculate` takes one process-wide lock that all plugins
without the flag share.
`create` and `destroy` always take that lock.
`RGPOT_CAP_PERIODIC` sets the potential's `periodic` capability.

#### `rgpot_plugin_input_t`

- Inputs :: `n_atoms`, `positions` (`3 * n_atoms` doubles, row-major `x y z` per
  atom), `atomic_numbers` (`n_atoms` ints) and `cell` (9 doubles, lattice
  vectors as rows).
- Units :: `positions` and `cell` are in the plugin's `length_unit`; the host
  multiplies Angstrom values by the conversion factor before the call.
  `n_atoms` and `atomic_numbers` have none.
- Outputs :: none; the host fills it and the plugin reads it during `calculate`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot_plugin_output_t`

- Inputs :: `forces` points at `3 * n_atoms` doubles that the host allocates.
- Units :: `energy` is in the plugin's
  `energy_unit`, `variance` in that unit squared, and `forces` in `energy_unit`
  per `length_unit`.
  The host converts them to eV, eV^2 and eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: the plugin writes `energy`, `variance` and every element of
  `forces`, row-major like `positions`.
  The host presets `energy` and every force to NaN and `variance` to 0.
- Errors :: the host throws `std::runtime_error` ("plugin returned invalid
  energy or variance") for a non-finite energy or variance or a negative
  variance, and ("plugin returned invalid forces") for a non-finite force, so a
  field left unset fails.

#### `rgpot_plugin_instance`

- Inputs :: none; an opaque type the plugin defines.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot_plugin_create_fn`

```c
typedef rgpot_plugin_status_t (*rgpot_plugin_create_fn)(
    const char *config_json, rgpot_plugin_instance **out);
```

- Inputs :: `config_json`, the configuration string the host was given, and
  `out`, where the instance goes.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: `RGPOT_PLUGIN_OK` and a non-null `*out`.
- Errors :: a status other than `RGPOT_PLUGIN_OK`, or a null
  `*out`, makes the host throw `std::runtime_error` with the `last_error` text of `*out`,
  or "plugin create failed" when `*out` is null or has no message.
  The host calls `destroy` on a non-null `*out` even when the status is a
  failure.

#### `rgpot_plugin_calculate_fn`

```c
typedef rgpot_plugin_status_t (*rgpot_plugin_calculate_fn)(
    rgpot_plugin_instance *instance, const rgpot_plugin_input_t *input,
    rgpot_plugin_output_t *output);
```

- Inputs :: `instance` from `create`, `input` and `output`.
- Units :: as `rgpot_plugin_input_t` and `rgpot_plugin_output_t`.
- Outputs :: `RGPOT_PLUGIN_OK`, with `output` filled.
- Errors :: any other status makes the host throw
  `std::runtime_error` with the `last_error` text, or "plugin calculate failed"
  when there is none.

#### `rgpot_plugin_destroy_fn`

```c
typedef void (*rgpot_plugin_destroy_fn)(rgpot_plugin_instance *instance);
```

- Inputs :: `instance`, a non-null instance from `create`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: frees the instance; the host calls it once per instance.
- Errors :: none; the function has no way to report one.

#### `rgpot_plugin_capabilities_fn`

```c
typedef uint32_t (*rgpot_plugin_capabilities_fn)(
    const rgpot_plugin_instance *instance);
```

- Inputs :: `instance` from `create`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a bitmask of `rgpot_plugin_caps_t` values; the host calls it once,
  after `create`.
  A null `capabilities` in the descriptor means
  `RGPOT_CAP_ENERGY | RGPOT_CAP_FORCES`.
- Errors :: the host rejects a mask without both energy and forces, as listed
  under `rgpot_plugin_caps_t`.

#### `rgpot_plugin_last_error_fn`

```c
typedef const char *(*rgpot_plugin_last_error_fn)(
    const rgpot_plugin_instance *instance);
```

- Inputs :: `instance`, a non-null instance; the host does not call it without
  one.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the message of the last failure of that instance, owned by the
  plugin.
  The host copies it at once.
- Errors :: none; a null or empty string makes the host use its own fallback
  text.

#### `rgpot_plugin_descriptor_t`

- Inputs :: `descriptor_size` is `sizeof(rgpot_plugin_descriptor_t)` as the
  plugin compiled it, and `api_version` is `RGPOT_PLUGIN_API_VERSION`.
  `name` is a non-empty identifier and `version` a free-form string that may be
  null.
  `length_unit` and `energy_unit` name the plugin's units in the syntax of the
  unit parser, for example `"bohr"`, `"hartree"` or `"kJ/mol"`; null or empty
  means Angstrom and eV.
  `create`, `destroy` and `calculate` are required; `capabilities` and
  `last_error` may be null.
- Units :: `length_unit` and `energy_unit` set the units of every number the
  plugin sees and returns.
- Outputs :: none; the plugin owns the descriptor.
- Errors :: the host throws `std::invalid_argument` when `descriptor_size` does
  not reach `capabilities` ("plugin descriptor is missing required fields"),
  when `api_version` differs ("plugin API version mismatch"), or when `name` is
  null or empty or a required function is null ("plugin descriptor has invalid
  required fields").
  An unknown unit, a dimension mismatch or a non-positive factor throws
  `std::invalid_argument`.

The host reads `capabilities` and `last_error` only when `descriptor_size`
covers them, so a later version can append fields.
The name, version, configuration string and unit names enter the potential's
parameter key.

#### `rgpot_plugin_init_fn`

```c
typedef const rgpot_plugin_descriptor_t *(*rgpot_plugin_init_fn)(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a pointer to the plugin's descriptor, which stays valid until the
  library is closed.
- Errors :: a null pointer, or a descriptor that fails validation, makes the
  registry skip the library.

### Example

A plugin with a harmonic bond to the origin, called the way the host calls it.

```c
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "rgpot/plugin.h"

typedef struct rgpot_plugin_instance {
  double k;
} instance_t;

static rgpot_plugin_status_t create(const char *config_json, rgpot_plugin_instance **out) {
  (void)config_json;
  if (!out)
    return RGPOT_PLUGIN_INVALID_PARAM;
  *out = malloc(sizeof **out);
  if (!*out)
    return RGPOT_PLUGIN_ERROR;
  (*out)->k = 2.0;
  return RGPOT_PLUGIN_OK;
}

static void destroy(rgpot_plugin_instance *instance) { free(instance); }

static rgpot_plugin_status_t calculate(rgpot_plugin_instance *instance,
                                       const rgpot_plugin_input_t *input,
                                       rgpot_plugin_output_t *output) {
  if (!instance || !input || !output)
    return RGPOT_PLUGIN_INVALID_PARAM;
  output->energy = 0.0;
  output->variance = 0.0;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < 3 * input->n_atoms; ++i) {
    const double x = input->positions[i];
    output->energy += 0.5 * instance->k * x * x;
    output->forces[i] = -instance->k * x;
  }
  return RGPOT_PLUGIN_OK;
}

static uint32_t capabilities(const rgpot_plugin_instance *instance) {
  (void)instance;
  return RGPOT_CAP_ENERGY | RGPOT_CAP_FORCES | RGPOT_CAP_INSTANCE_SAFE;
}

RGPOT_PLUGIN_EXPORT const rgpot_plugin_descriptor_t *rgpot_plugin_init(void) {
  static const rgpot_plugin_descriptor_t desc = {
      sizeof(rgpot_plugin_descriptor_t), RGPOT_PLUGIN_API_VERSION,
      "harmonic", "1.0", NULL, NULL,
      create, destroy, calculate, capabilities, NULL};
  return &desc;
}

int main(void) {
  rgpot_plugin_init_fn init = rgpot_plugin_init;
  const rgpot_plugin_descriptor_t *desc = init();
  rgpot_plugin_instance *instance = NULL;
  if (desc->create("{}", &instance) != RGPOT_PLUGIN_OK)
    return 1;
  const double positions[3] = {1.0, 0.0, 0.0};
  const int numbers[1] = {1};
  const double cell[9] = {10.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 10.0};
  double forces[3];
  rgpot_plugin_input_t input = {1, positions, numbers, cell};
  rgpot_plugin_output_t output = {NAN, 0.0, forces};
  const rgpot_plugin_status_t status = desc->calculate(instance, &input, &output);
  desc->destroy(instance);
  if (status != RGPOT_PLUGIN_OK || output.energy != 1.0 || forces[0] != -2.0)
    return 1;
  printf("%s %.1f %.1f\n", desc->name, output.energy, forces[0]);
  return 0;
}
```

---

# External engine C ABI

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/external_abi.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/external_abi.html

`CppCore/rgpot/ExternalPot/external_potentials.h` declares the C constructors of
the LAMMPS, GROMACS and OpenMM shifted Lennard-Jones potentials.
`CppCore/rgpot/ExternalPot/ExternalPot.cc` implements them in `librgpot`.
Positions and cells are Angstrom, energies eV and forces eV/Angstrom at this
interface.
A box is nine doubles, the lattice vectors as rows.
Every call that can fail takes `err` and `err_len`.
On failure it writes a message of at most
`err_len - 1` characters and a terminating null into `err`; a null `err` or an `err_len`
of 0 writes nothing.

### Types

#### `rgpot_external_potential`

- Inputs :: none; an opaque handle from one of the constructors.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none.
- Errors :: none.

One handle holds one potential.
Each potential serialises the force calls of its own instance with a mutex.

An engine library stays resident once a constructor opens it.
The first successful open is kept and marked `RTLD_NODELETE`, so the mapping
stays resident after `dlclose` and a later constructor of the same file reuses
that open instead of taking another reference.
An open that does not become the resident engine is closed after the constructor
releases its table lock.
`rgpot_external_potential_free` destroys the engine instance and leaves the
library mapped.
A backend may keep OpenMP, CUDA, MPI, GROMACS, LAMMPS or OpenMM state that does
not survive an unload.
A later constructor that opens the same file gets the dynamic linker's existing
handle.

### Unit factors

#### `rgpot_md_kj_per_ev`

```c
double rgpot_md_kj_per_ev(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: kJ/mol per eV.
- Outputs :: the elementary charge times the Avogadro number divided by 1000,
  from the exact 2019 SI values in `CppCore/rgpot/ExternalPot/md_units.hpp`.
- Errors :: none; the call cannot fail.

#### `rgpot_md_nm_per_angstrom`

```c
double rgpot_md_nm_per_angstrom(void);
```

- Inputs :: none.
- Units :: nm per Angstrom.
- Outputs :: 0.1.
- Errors :: none; the call cannot fail.

### Constructors

#### `rgpot_lammps_potential`

```c
rgpot_external_potential *rgpot_lammps_potential(const char *engine_path,
                                                double u0, double cutoff,
                                                double psi, char *err,
                                                size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `engine_path`, the engine library, or null or empty to search.
  `u0` is the well depth, `cutoff` the cutoff and `psi` the zero crossing of the
  12-6 potential.
  `err` and `err_len` receive a failure message.
- Units :: `u0` is eV; `cutoff` and `psi` are Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a new handle, freed with `rgpot_external_potential_free`.
  The constructor opens the engine library, resolves `rgpot_engine_create`,
  `rgpot_engine_destroy` and `rgpot_engine_force`, and calls
  `rgpot_engine_create` with the three doubles `u0`, `cutoff`, `psi` in eV and
  Angstrom.
  Every force call goes to `rgpot_engine_force`.
  A non-empty `engine_path` is the only library tried.
  Otherwise the constructor tries `RGPOT_LAMMPS_ENGINE`, then
  `LAMMPS_ENGINE` when they are set and not empty, then `liblammps_engine.so`
  and `liblj_engine.so` through the dynamic linker's search path (`.dylib` on
  macOS, `.dll` on Windows).
- Errors :: returns null and writes `err` when `u0`, `cutoff` or `psi` is not
  positive and finite ("u0, cutoff and psi must be positive and finite (eV and
  Angstrom)").
  Returns null and writes `err` when no candidate opens with all three symbols
  ("engine library was not opened: " and the reason for each candidate) or when
  `rgpot_engine_create` returns null (its message, or "rgpot_engine_create
  failed").
  Returns null and writes `err`, without trying the next candidate, when the
  opened file cannot be identified through `dladdr` and `realpath`, or when its
  canonical path was loaded before and now names another inode ("was replaced
  after it was loaded").

#### `rgpot_lammpc_potential`

```c
rgpot_external_potential *rgpot_lammpc_potential(const char *engine_path,
                                                const void *config_capnp,
                                                size_t config_capnp_size,
                                                char *err, size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `engine_path`, the lammpc library, or null or empty to search.
  `config_capnp` and `config_capnp_size` are a flat `PotentialConfig` with the
  `lammps` arm.
  `err` and `err_len` receive a failure message.
- Units :: those of `LammpsParams.unitsStyle`; `metal` is eV and Angstrom.
- Outputs :: a new handle, freed with `rgpot_external_potential_free`.
  Freeing the last handle on a lammpc backend calls `lammpc_finalize`.
  The constructor loads `liblammpc`, resolves the lammpc profile, checks its
  `Capabilities` with the profile handshake, and calls
  `lammpc_session_create_from_config`.
  A non-empty `engine_path` is the only library tried.
  Otherwise the constructor tries `LAMMPC_LIBRARY`, then `RGPOT_LAMMPC_ENGINE`,
  when either is set and not empty, and nothing after them.
  With neither set it tries `liblammpc.so`.
- Errors :: returns null and writes `err` when the config bytes are missing, not
  word-aligned, truncated, or not a `PotentialConfig` with the `lammps` arm,
  when no library opens, when its `Capabilities` fail the handshake (an
  incompatible protocol, schema, bridge ABI or DLPack revision), when the
  backend reports unavailable, or when `lammpc_session_create_from_config`
  returns null.
  A non-empty `engine_path` that does not open writes a message that names it.

#### `rgpot_gromacs_potential`

```c
rgpot_external_potential *rgpot_gromacs_potential(const char *engine_path,
                                                 double u0, double cutoff,
                                                 double psi, char *err,
                                                 size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs ::
  `engine_path`, a library, or null or empty to evaluate in process; `u0`, `cutoff`, `psi`, `err` and `err_len`
  as in `rgpot_lammps_potential`.
- Units :: `u0` is eV; `cutoff` and `psi` are Angstrom.
  The constructor stores them once as kJ/mol and nm.
- Outputs :: a new handle, freed with `rgpot_external_potential_free`.
  Without a library the force is the in-process `LJPot` with `u0`, `cutoff` and
  `psi`.
  With a library the constructor resolves `rgpot_engine_create`,
  `rgpot_engine_destroy` and
  `rgpot_md_native_force`, and calls `rgpot_engine_create` with the three doubles in kJ/mol and nm. Each force call then passes positions and box in nm to `rgpot_md_native_force`
  and converts the
  kJ/mol energy and the (kJ/mol)/nm forces back to eV and eV/Angstrom.
- Errors :: returns null and writes `err` for a `u0`, `cutoff` or `psi` that is
  not positive and finite, a library that does not open or lacks one of the
  three symbols, a library that cannot be identified or was replaced, or a
  failed `rgpot_engine_create`, with the messages of `rgpot_lammps_potential`.

#### `rgpot_openmm_potential`

```c
rgpot_external_potential *rgpot_openmm_potential(const char *engine_path,
                                                double u0, double cutoff,
                                                double psi, char *err,
                                                size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: as `rgpot_gromacs_potential`.
- Units :: `u0` is eV; `cutoff` and `psi` are Angstrom, stored once as kJ/mol
  and nm.
- Outputs :: a new handle that behaves as the one from
  `rgpot_gromacs_potential`, with the OpenMM potential type.
- Errors :: as `rgpot_gromacs_potential`.

### Evaluation

#### `rgpot_external_potential_free`

```c
void rgpot_external_potential_free(rgpot_external_potential *pot);
```

- Inputs :: `pot`, a handle from a constructor, or null.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: destroys the potential, calls the engine's `rgpot_engine_destroy`
  when there is one, and leaves its library mapped.
- Errors :: none; a null `pot` is ignored.

#### `rgpot_external_potential_energy_forces`

```c
int rgpot_external_potential_energy_forces(
    rgpot_external_potential *pot, const double *xyz, const int *atomic_numbers,
    size_t n, const double *box9, double *forces, double *energy, char *err,
    size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `pot`, `xyz` (`3 * n` doubles, row-major `x y z` per atom),
  `atomic_numbers` (`n= ints), =box9` (nine doubles, lattice vectors as rows), `forces` (room for `3 * n` doubles), `energy`, `err` and `err_len`.
  `box9` must not be null, also when `n` is 0.
- Units :: `xyz` and `box9` are Angstrom, `*energy` is eV and `forces`
  eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: returns 0 and writes `*energy` and the `3 * n` forces, row-major
  like `xyz`.
  The variance the engine reports is not returned.
- Errors :: returns 1 and writes
  "energy_forces needs a potential and a geometry" for a null `pot`, `energy` or `box9`, or, when `n > 0`, a null `xyz`, `atomic_numbers`
  or `forces`. Returns 1 and writes the message when the evaluation throws, for
  example "rgpot_engine_force failed" or "rgpot_md_native_force failed" when the
  engine returns nonzero.

### Example

The GROMACS potential evaluated in process, a dimer 1.5 Angstrom apart.

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include "rgpot/ExternalPot/external_potentials.h"

int main(void) {
  char err[256] = "";
  rgpot_external_potential *pot = rgpot_gromacs_potential(NULL, 1.0, 8.0, 1.0, err, sizeof err);
  if (pot == NULL) {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", err);
    return 1;
  }
  const double xyz[6] = {0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.5, 0.0, 0.0};
  const int z[2] = {1, 1};
  const double box9[9] = {20.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 20.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 20.0};
  double forces[6];
  double energy = 0.0;
  const int rc = rgpot_external_potential_energy_forces(pot, xyz, z, 2, box9, forces, &energy,
                                                        err, sizeof err);
  rgpot_external_potential_free(pot);
  if (rc != 0) {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", err);
    return 1;
  }
  if (!(energy < 0.0) || forces[0] != -forces[3]) {
    return 1;
  }
  printf("%.10f eV, %.6f eV/Angstrom\n", energy, forces[0]);
  printf("%.6f kJ/mol per eV, %.1f nm per Angstrom\n", rgpot_md_kj_per_ev(),
         rgpot_md_nm_per_angstrom());
  return 0;
}
```

### Generic MD sessions

The
`rgpot_md_session_*` interface lets any dynamics backend (OpenMM, GROMACS nblib, LAMMPS) implement one vtable in rgpot units: positions and plane/wall coordinates in Angstrom, velocities in Angstrom/ps, forces in eV/Angstrom, energies and `kT` in eV, `time_step`
in ps, `friction` in ps^-1, masses in amu, and the periodic box in Angstrom
(nine doubles, the lattice vectors as rows).

A sampler such as a hyperplane, PAFI, OH-TST, Bennett-Chandler or forward-flux
driver needs only these calls, and none of them is special to one engine:
positions, velocities and the box are set and read;
`rgpot_md_session_run_langevin` steps Langevin dynamics with a time step, a
friction and a seed, on a hyperplane with a holonomic constraint force reported
per step, between planar walls that reflect or reject the drift;
`rgpot_md_session_reseed_velocities` draws Maxwell-Boltzmann velocities; and the
energies and forces are read back.
The random stream is the same on every engine: the draws are made by rgpot, not
by the backend.

#### Random streams

`seed` names a stream.
A call with the seed of the previous call continues the stream, with its
Box-Muller spare, so a run split in chunks equals one long run.
A different seed starts a new stream.
Setting positions or velocities ends the stream, so the same seed after a new
state replays the same noise.
Two sessions given the same states and seeds draw the same numbers.

#### Constraint force

With a plane `n . (x - p) = 0`, run_langevin reports for each step the Lagrange
multiplier `lambda = -(n . M^-1 F) / (n . M^-1 n)` for the unit normal `n` over
the `3N` coordinates and the mass matrix `M`, in eV/Angstrom: the mean of the
two force kicks of the step.
The constraint force on the system is `lambda n`.
For a plane of fixed normal the mean of `lambda` over the constrained ensemble
is `dF/dc` for the plane offset `c = n . p`, which PAFI integrates and the
Bennett-Chandler transmission coefficient needs.
A backend with distance constraints of its own topology holds them along with
the plane, and the multiplier of the plane accounts for them.

#### `rgpot_md_session`

- Inputs :: none; an opaque handle from `rgpot_md_session_from_ops` or
  `rgpot_md_session_create`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: none.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot_md_session_ops`

- Inputs :: `struct_size` (`sizeof(rgpot_md_session_ops)`) and backend callbacks
  `set_positions`, `set_velocities`, `step_langevin`, `step_nve`,
  `get_state`, `get_masses`, and `destroy`, followed by the optional
  `set_periodic_box`, `get_periodic_box`, `initialize`,
  `run_langevin`, `get_neighbors`, and `set_neighbors`.
  The macro `RGPOT_MD_OPS_HAS(ops, member)` tests that a vtable carries an
  optional member.
- Units :: rgpot host units (Angstrom, eV, ps, amu).
- Outputs :: vtable consumed by `rgpot_md_session_from_ops` and exported by
  engine plugins implementing `rgpot_md_session_engine_create_fn`.
- Errors :: `rgpot_md_session_from_ops` rejects null required callbacks or a
  `struct_size` that ends before `destroy`.
  A vtable that ends earlier than an optional member, or leaves it null, makes
  that call fail with a message naming the missing callback.

#### `rgpot_md_langevin_request`

- Inputs :: `struct_size`, `kT`, `friction`, `time_step`, `steps`, `seed`, `n3`,
  `plane_point` and `plane_normal` (both null for no plane),
  `n_walls` with `wall_points` and `wall_normals` of `n_walls * n3` doubles, and
  `wall_mode` (`RGPOT_MD_WALL_REFLECT` or `RGPOT_MD_WALL_REJECT`).
- Units :: `kT` in eV, `friction` in ps^-1, `time_step` in ps, points in
  Angstrom.
- Outputs :: none; the argument of `rgpot_md_session_run_langevin`.
- Errors :: a `struct_size` below `sizeof(rgpot_md_langevin_request)` is
  rejected.

#### `rgpot_md_langevin_result`

- Inputs :: `struct_size`, and `constraint_force` with its length
  `constraint_force_len`, or null.
- Units :: `constraint_force` in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: `wall_hits`, and one multiplier per step in `constraint_force` when
  a plane is set; nothing is written without a plane.
- Errors :: a `constraint_force_len` below the number of steps is rejected.

#### `rgpot_md_session_engine_create_fn`

```c
typedef int (*rgpot_md_session_engine_create_fn)(
    const void *spec, size_t spec_len, const char *options,
    rgpot_md_session_ops *ops, void **ctx, size_t *n_atoms, char *err,
    size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: opaque backend specification `spec` of length `spec_len` and backend
  `options` string.
- Units :: the returned callbacks speak rgpot units.
- Outputs :: returns 0 and populates `*ops`, `*ctx`, and `*n_atoms`.
- Errors :: returns 1 and writes `err` on failure.

#### `rgpot_md_session_from_ops`

```c
rgpot_md_session *rgpot_md_session_from_ops(void *ctx,
                                            const rgpot_md_session_ops *ops,
                                            size_t n_atoms, char *err,
                                            size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: backend context `ctx`, vtable `ops`, atom count
  `n_atoms`, and error buffer `err` of length `err_len`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: a new `rgpot_md_session *` handle freed by
  `rgpot_md_session_destroy`.
- Errors :: returns null and writes `err` when `ctx` is null, `ops` is invalid,
  or `n_atoms` is 0.

#### `rgpot_md_session_create`

```c
rgpot_md_session *rgpot_md_session_create(const char *engine,
                                          const char *engine_path,
                                          const void *spec, size_t spec_len,
                                          const char *options, char *err,
                                          size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `engine` name (such as `"openmm"`), optional explicit
  `engine_path`, opaque `spec` buffer of length `spec_len`, optional `options`,
  and `err`/`err_len`.
- Units :: the returned session speaks rgpot units (Angstrom, eV, ps, amu).
- Outputs :: opens the engine plugin
  (`engine_path`, else `RGPOT_<ENGINE>_ENGINE`, else `<ENGINE>_ENGINE`, else
  `lib<engine>_engine`), resolves `rgpot_md_session_engine_create`, and returns a new `rgpot_md_session *`.
- Errors :: returns null and writes `err` if no library opens or engine
  initialization fails.

#### `rgpot_md_session_n_atoms`

```c
size_t rgpot_md_session_n_atoms(const rgpot_md_session *session);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, or null.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: the atom count of `session`, or 0 if null.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot_md_session_get_masses`

```c
int rgpot_md_session_get_masses(rgpot_md_session *session, double *masses,
                                size_t n_atoms, char *err, size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, output buffer `masses` of length

- Outputs :: returns 0 and writes `n_atoms` particle masses.
- Errors :: returns 1 and writes `err` on null pointers or size mismatch.

#### `rgpot_md_session_step_langevin`

```c
int rgpot_md_session_step_langevin(
    rgpot_md_session *session, double kT, double friction, double time_step,
    const double *plane_point, const double *plane_normal,
    const double *wall_points, const double *wall_normals, size_t n_walls,
    size_t n3, size_t steps, uint64_t seed, uint64_t *wall_hits, char *err,
    size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, `kT`, `friction`,
  `time_step`, hyperplane vectors `plane_point` and
  `plane_normal` of length `n3`, `n_walls` flat wall pairs
  `wall_points` and `wall_normals` each of length
  `n_walls * n3`, step count `steps`, 64-bit `seed` naming the random stream, optional `wall_hits`
  output, and `err`/`err_len`.
  It reflects at walls and reports no constraint force;
  `rgpot_md_session_run_langevin` does both.
- Units :: `kT` in eV, `friction` in ps^-1, `time_step` in ps, positions and
  wall points in Angstrom.
- Outputs :: returns 0 and writes the total specular wall reflection count to
  `*wall_hits` when non-null.
- Errors :: returns 1 and writes `err` on invalid controls, buffer mismatch,
  non-finite inputs, or backend failure.

#### `rgpot_md_session_step_nve`

```c
int rgpot_md_session_step_nve(rgpot_md_session *session, double time_step,
                              size_t steps, char *err, size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, `time_step`, `steps`, and `err`/`err_len`.
- Units :: `time_step` in ps.
- Outputs :: returns 0 after advancing unconstrained velocity-Verlet dynamics.
- Errors :: returns 1 and writes `err` on null session, invalid `time_step`, or
  backend failure.

```c
int rgpot_md_session_get_state(rgpot_md_session *session, double *positions,

                               double *potential_energy, double *kinetic_energy,
                               char *err, size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, optional flat xyz output arrays `positions`,
  `velocities`, and `forces` of length `n3`, optional scalar pointers

- Units :: `positions` in Angstrom, `velocities` in
  Angstrom/ps, `forces` in eV/Angstrom, energies in eV.
- Outputs :: returns 0 and fills any non-null output buffers.
- Errors :: returns 1 and writes `err` on null session, length mismatch, or
  backend failure.

```c
                                size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session` and `err`/`err_len`.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: returns 0 once the backend has evaluated its first forces at the

  A backend without the callback has nothing to prepare and also returns 0.

#### `rgpot_md_session_run_langevin`

```c
int rgpot_md_session_run_langevin(rgpot_md_session *session,
                                  const rgpot_md_langevin_request *request,
                                  rgpot_md_langevin_result *result, char *err,
                                  size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, a `request` and a `result` (see above), and
  `err`/`err_len`.
- Units :: `kT` in eV, `friction` in ps^-1,
  `time_step` in ps, positions and wall points in Angstrom, `constraint_force`
  in eV/Angstrom.
- Outputs :: returns 0 after advancing BAOAB Langevin dynamics, writes
  `result->wall_hits`, and with a plane and a buffer writes the constraint force
  of every step.
- Errors :: returns 1 and writes `err` on a null argument, a short struct,
  invalid controls, a buffer mismatch, non-finite inputs, a start outside a
  wall, a backend without the callback, or backend failure.

#### `rgpot_md_session_reseed_velocities`

```c
int rgpot_md_session_reseed_velocities(rgpot_md_session *session, double kT,
                                       uint64_t seed,
                                       const double *plane_normal, size_t n3,
                                       char *err, size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, `kT`, `seed`, an optional
  `plane_normal` of length `n3`, and `err`/`err_len`.
- Units :: `kT` in eV; the velocities set are in Angstrom/ps.
- Outputs :: returns 0 after setting Maxwell-Boltzmann velocities of variance
  `kT/m` per coordinate, conditioned on `n . v = 0` when a normal is given.
  The draw is made from the session masses, so it is the same on every engine.
- Errors :: returns 1 and writes `err` on a null session, a wrong `n3`, a
  negative or non-finite `kT`, a normal that acts on no massive atom, or backend
  failure.

```c
                                size_t n3, double *potential_energy,
                                char *err, size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, an output array `forces` of length `n3`, an optional
  `potential_energy` pointer, and `err`/`err_len`.
- Units :: eV/Angstrom and eV.
- Outputs :: returns 0 and fills the forces at the current positions and, if
  given, the potential energy.
- Errors :: returns 1 and writes `err` on a null buffer, length mismatch, or
  backend failure.

#### `rgpot_md_session_get_energy`

```c
int rgpot_md_session_get_energy(rgpot_md_session *session,
                                double *potential_energy,
                                double *kinetic_energy, char *err,
                                size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, optional `potential_energy` and `kinetic_energy`
  pointers, and `err`/`err_len`.
- Units :: eV.
- Outputs :: returns 0 and writes the non-null energies.
- Errors :: returns 1 and writes `err` on a null session or backend failure.

#### `rgpot_md_session_get_neighbors`

```c
int rgpot_md_session_get_neighbors(rgpot_md_session *session,
                                   const rgpot_nlist_request *request,
                                   rgpot_nlist_soa *out, size_t *count,
                                   size_t *needed, char *err, size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, neighbour `request` in the shared `rgpot_nlist_request`
  shape, optional output `out` (`rgpot_nlist_soa`), optional `count` and
  `needed`, and `err`/`err_len`.
- Units :: position and cell units follow the session ABI (Angstrom).
- Outputs :: returns `RGPOT_MD_NLIST_OK` and forwards the engine's pair list
  using the shared neighbour columns and semantics.
- Errors :: returns
  `RGPOT_MD_NLIST_UNSUPPORTED` when the engine has no neighbour query slot, or `RGPOT_MD_NLIST_ERROR`
  with `err` on invalid input or backend failure.

#### `rgpot_md_session_set_neighbors`

```c
int rgpot_md_session_set_neighbors(rgpot_md_session *session,
                                   const rgpot_nlist_request *request,
                                   const rgpot_nlist_soa *pairs, size_t count,
                                   char *err, size_t err_len);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, neighbour `request`, shared neighbour columns `pairs`
  containing `count` rows, and `err`/`err_len`.
- Units :: pair geometry is Angstrom in the same shared neighbour convention.
- Outputs :: returns `RGPOT_MD_NLIST_OK` when the engine accepted the supplied
  pair list.
- Errors :: returns
  `RGPOT_MD_NLIST_UNSUPPORTED` when the engine has no setter slot, or `RGPOT_MD_NLIST_ERROR`
  with `err` on invalid input or backend failure.

#### `rgpot_md_session_destroy`

```c
void rgpot_md_session_destroy(rgpot_md_session *session);
```

- Inputs :: `session`, or null.
- Units :: none.
- Outputs :: destroys the backend session and closes any loaded plugin library.
- Errors :: none; null is ignored.

# FMA dispatch and exp

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/simd_exp.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/simd_exp.html

The classical pair kernels return the same bits on every x86-64 instruction set,
on AArch64, and with any C library.
This page lists what that rests on.

### Fused multiply-add

The pair-list force updates and the minimum-image fold use a fused multiply-add.
A build for the x86-64 baseline picks the path once per process:

- the hardware instruction, in functions compiled with `target("fma")`, when
  `simd::detail::fma_hw_active()` is true;
- otherwise `simd::exact_fma`, a Dekker product and a round-to-odd sum (Boldo
  and Melquiond, IEEE Trans. Comput. 57(4), 2008); inputs outside the normal
  range and subnormal results go to `std::fma`.

`fma_hw_active()` reads CPUID leaf 1 (FMA, OSXSAVE and AVX) and XCR0 itself, so
it needs no support from the C library.
On glibc 2.33 and newer it also asks glibc, so
`GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.cpu.hwcaps`-FMA= selects the software path.
`RGPOT_FMA=software` selects it on any C library.

Both paths compute `a*b+c` with one rounding, so they return the same bits.
`exact_fma` hands inputs with a very large or small exponent, and zero or
subnormal results, to the C library's `fma`. mingw-w64's `fma` is not fused: it
returns the rounded `a*b+c` when that is infinite or NaN, and otherwise sums
separately rounded partial products.
A MinGW build uses `simd::detail::fma_soft` there, a correctly rounded fma in
integer arithmetic.
The hardware bodies call `simd::detail::fma_insn`.
Inlined into a `target("fma")` function it is the instruction; a copy left out
of line calls the C library's `fma`, and at `-O0` every copy is out of line, so
an unoptimized MinGW build calls `fma_soft` there too.
`ExactFmaEq` checks this against the hardware instruction on 1.5 million cases:
edge values, ties, near cancellation, the whole exponent range, and a million
uniform bit patterns.
`FmaPathEq` hashes LJ and Morse energies and forces on both paths, the software
one through `RGPOT_FMA=software`.

### exp

`simd::exp_fixed` replaces the C library's `exp` in the Morse kernel.
The C library's `exp` has variants for each instruction set, and its last bit
can change between them and between library versions.
`exp_fixed` uses only IEEE additions, multiplications and bit operations, with
no table and no fused multiply-add:

1. Clamp `x` to [-746, 710], keeping overflow and underflow.
2. Reduce `x = k ln2 + r` by the Cody-Waite split of fdlibm.
   `k ln2_hi` is exact and the subtraction is exact by Sterbenz's lemma, so
   `|r| <` 0.3466=.
3. Evaluate `1 + r + r^2 q(r)`, with `q` a degree 9 Horner polynomial.
4. Scale by 2^k as two powers of two, so only the last product rounds.

The scalar function and the vector loops run this body, and their bits match.
On x86-64 Linux, `exp_fixed_n` is compiled as `target_clones` for the baseline,
AVX2 and AVX-512F; a ThreadSanitizer build keeps only the baseline copy.
The loader picks one clone from libgcc's or compiler-rt's own CPU check.
Contraction is off in these files, and `-fno-trapping-math -fno-math-errno` let
GCC vectorise them without changing a value.

Error bounds:

| quantity                                  | bound                   | source                            |
|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| polynomial against exp on the interval    | 3.8e-18 relative        | Sollya `supnorm`                  |
| reduction, ln2 split                      | 1.2e-26 absolute        | `exp_constants.py` (sympy)        |
| normal results, a priori, first order     | 1.24 ulp                | `exp_bound.py`                    |
| measured against `expl`, 2^20 inputs      | 0.944 ulp               | `ExpFixedEq` on x86-64            |

The scripts are in `scripts/exp_fixed/`.
`fit.sollya` reproduces the coefficients and the approximation bound.
`exp_constants.py` checks the constants, the clamp limits and the exponent
construction with exact rationals.
`exp_bound.py` propagates a running rounding-error bound over the reduced
argument.
`ExpFixedEq` pins a digest of 2^20 results, so a change in any bit fails the
test on every platform.

The Morse kernel version moved to 2 with this function, so cached results
computed with the C library's `exp` are not reused.

---

# Sutton-Chen potential

Source: docs/orgmode/reference/sutton_chen.org
URL: https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/sutton_chen.html

`SuttonChenPot` evaluates

```
E = epsilon * [ 1/2 sum_i sum_{j != i} (a / r_ij)^n
                - c * sum_i sqrt(rho_i) ]
rho_i = sum_{j != i} (a / r_ij)^m
```

The form is Sutton and Chen, Philosophical Magazine Letters 61, 139 (1990),
doi:10.1080/09500839008206493.
The default parameters are the reduced gold and platinum set: `n = 10`, `m = 8`,
`c = 34.408`, `epsilon = 1`, `a = 1`.
Doye and Wales use that set for the 10-8 cluster tables and write it on the
first line of each deposited point file.
The deposited Pt38 Oh geometry gives -10117.2454 and the Pt75 D5h geometry gives
-20431.3452, in units of epsilon, to the four digits printed in the 10-8 table.

Cagin, Dereli, Uludogan, and Tomak, arXiv:cond-mat/9709114, Table I, reprint the
Sutton-Chen rows and cite Sutton and Chen 1990 as their reference 1.
Platinum is epsilon = 1.98330e-2 eV, a = 3.92 Angstrom, c = 34.408, m = 8, n = 10.
Gold on the same row is epsilon = 1.27930e-2 eV, a = 4.08 Angstrom, with the
same c, m, and n.
Those two rows are `sutton_chen_platinum` and `sutton_chen_gold`.
The bulk nearest-neighbor distance and the cohesive well depth are
`sutton_chen_scales`.
The length is the static fcc minimum.
The depth is minus the energy per atom there. c is fitted to zero pressure at
the lattice parameter, so the minimum is a / sqrt(2) for every row of the Cagin
table.
The reduced 10-8 well is 295.4645 epsilon, which is 5.860 eV for platinum and
3.780 eV for gold.

The default cutoff is 40 in the coordinate unit, with no energy shift.
`cutoff = 0` keeps every pair.
Cluster evaluation does not fold the cell.
Periodic evaluation uses the minimum image and needs a positive cutoff and a
cell; otherwise it throws `std::invalid_argument`.
Pairs come from the shared neighbour layer (`nlist::updateCells`), with a skin
of one fifth of the cutoff, or none in `nlist::Mode::Stream`.
With `cutoff = 0` the layer searches without a bound: it bins nothing, stores no
list, and each pass takes the pairs straight from the coordinates, in the order
of the one bin that a search wider than the cluster gives.
A call on fewer than `SuttonChenPot::kTeamMinAtoms` atoms runs on the calling
thread whatever `OMP_NUM_THREADS` asks for, since starting a team costs more
than such a call.
From there up each atom keeps the energy and strain of its pairs with
higher-index partners, and the atoms are added in index order.
When the call has at least the atoms `SuttonChenPot::kTeamFrom` asks of the
`OMP_NUM_THREADS` threads, a team splits the atoms into as many runs.
One thread walks each pair once, in the order of those rows.
On a stored neighbour list, that team runs one three-phase OpenMP region over an
upper-pair index when the candidate upper pairs are at least 4096
(`kMinParallelHalfPairs`), `total_up <` term_limit= and
`pairScratchFits(total_up, atoms, scratch_avail)` holds: phase 0 evaluates each
upper pair once across work-balanced atom slices rounded to 8-atom boundaries,
phase 1 accumulates per-atom densities and embedding weights in pair-index
order, and phase 2 sums forces, stress, and per-atom virials from the stored
pair terms.
`pairScratchFits` checks that the per-slot vectors fit within half of
`nlist::availableBytes()` (or allows the path when `availableBytes()` returns
0): 69 bytes per candidate upper pair (`active` 1 byte +
`pair_phi` 8 + `pair_force` 48 + `up_j` 4 + `lo_refs` 8), or 77 bytes when
`atoms.energy` is non-null (`pair_he` adds 8).
Per-atom vectors (`up_off`, `lo_off`, `rho`, `weight`, `row_e`, `row_emb`, and
`row_s` with stress) are `O(nAtoms)`, already bounded by `Neighbours::buildCells` and present as `rho_`
and `weight_` on the two-pass walk, so they are not counted against the
pair-slot budget; the per-call scratch vectors in the thread-local workspace are
released when the three-phase call finishes while the half-pair index and slice
splits stay cached for Verlet reuse.
When
`est_half_pairs > term_limit` the three-phase path is skipped before `buildStoredHalfIndex`, and when `total_up > term_limit`
or `pairScratchFits` refuses the call falls back to the threaded two-pass row
walk.
Sparser stored lists stay on one thread, and streaming or unbounded walks still
evaluate each atom's row on its owning slice when the team opens.
The energy, the forces, the stress and the per-atom terms therefore keep the
bits of one thread on any thread count, also when the runtime starts fewer
threads.
On the two-pass walks, one pass builds the densities and a second pass writes
the forces.
The density pass keeps the powers and `1/r^2` that the force of each pair takes
in `PairTerms<3>` (24 bytes per pair), and the force pass reads them back
instead of raising the distance to `n= and =m` in the second pass.
With `a = 1` those are the density's own powers; otherwise the force's powers of
`a^2 (1/r^2)` are kept, since they can differ from those of `a^2 / r^2` in the
last bit.
`SuttonChenPot::setPairTermLimit` takes a pair count `pairs`, defaulting to
`PairTerms<3>::kDefaultLimit` (1398101 pairs, which is 32 MiB of two-pass
`PairTerms<3>` storage at 24 bytes per pair): it requires `total_up <` pairs= on
the three-phase stored path and caps the two-pass `PairTerms<3>` buffer at
`pairs / lanes` per lane, while the two-pass force pass computes the terms of
any pairs past the kept room from the coordinates, with the same bits.

`rgpot_sutton_chen_energy_forces` is the C entry point.
It takes an `rgpot_sc_config` and writes one energy and one force array.
Each thread keeps the potential of its last call in `rgpot::Kept`
(`rgpot/KeptPotential.hpp`), so a call with the same parameters and atom count
reuses its neighbour update and the room for the pair terms.
Any other call drops that potential and builds a new one, and so does a call
that throws.

### Cost of a call

`sc_call_bench` (`meson test --benchmark sc_call_bench`) times the C entry on
free clusters with no cutoff, one thread pinned to one core, against a plain
loop over the half pairs that keeps each pair's powers for its force.
Both give the same bits.
The medians of five runs, in microseconds per call:

| Atoms | 12-6 entry | 12-6 plain loop | 9-6 entry | 9-6 plain loop |
|-------|------------|-----------------|-----------|----------------|
|    13 |      0.749 |           0.580 |     0.848 |          0.634 |
|    38 |      6.434 |           4.939 |     6.686 |          5.223 |
|    55 |     13.690 |          10.267 |    13.739 |         10.914 |
|   147 |     91.082 |          72.088 |    94.165 |         75.244 |
|   561 |   1302.449 |        1063.068 |  1374.253 |       1122.602 |

## Reduced cluster pairs

`rgpot_lj_gradient` and `rgpot_morse_gradient` return the energy gradient of an
unshifted cluster.
`rgpot_lj_curvature_pairs` fills energy, slope, and curvature for a list of
squared distances in one call.
The `rgpot-pair` crate exposes the same trees as `lj_unit` and `morse_unit`,
which a Rust caller can inline.
The unit Lennard-Jones branch is the direct inverse-power tree, with contraction
off, so a search sees the same rounding as that expression.

## Stress

`SuttonChenConfig::stress` is off by default.
When it is set, `forceImpl` writes the Cauchy stress `sigma = (1/V) dE/dstrain`
into `ForceOut::stress` in row-major order.
It also sets `has_stress` to 1, and `caps().stress` is true.
The units are energy over length cubed, eV/Angstrom^3 for the
`sutton_chen_platinum` and `sutton_chen_gold` rows.
The sign is that of `stress.hpp`: a compressed crystal has negative diagonal
entries, and the pressure is minus a third of the trace.
A cell with no positive volume, such as a cluster with a null box, leaves
`has_stress` at 0.

The force pass writes the stress as well, because the energy depends on
positions only through pair distances.
With `d = r_i - r_j` and a force `fscale * d` on atom i, each pair adds
`-fscale * d d^T` to dE/dstrain.
That fscale already includes the embedding term, so the stress needs no third
loop.
Thompson, Plimpton and Mattson give the many-body virial under periodic
boundaries.
Their paper is in the Journal of Chemical Physics 131, 154107 (2009).

With the flag clear, `forceImpl` leaves the stress slots and `has_stress` as the
caller set them.
`caps()`, `paramsKey()`, the energy and the forces are then the same bits as
before the flag existed.
Setting the flag changes `paramsKey()`, so a cached result without stress is not
served to a caller that asked for one.
The C entry point `rgpot_sutton_chen_energy_forces` and `rgpot_sc_config` do not
carry the flag.

Periodic evaluation keeps one image of each partner.
The stress, like the energy, is the whole sum only while the cutoff is under
half the smallest face spacing of the cell.

### Checks

`rgpot-pair` independently checks the bulk scale against a conventional
four-site fcc cell summed inside a spherical cutoff.
Its Cu, Ag, Au and Ni rows recover the published conventional lattice constants
3.61, 4.09, 4.08 and 3.52 Angstrom within 1e-5 Angstrom and the cohesive
energies 3.50, 2.96, 3.78 and 4.44 eV within 2e-4 eV.
The production sum instead walks half-cell integer triples with `i + j + k`
even, which is fcc; restricting the triples to all even or all odd would be bcc.
Thus the reported fcc-neighbour bug does not apply to the current solver.

`SuttonChenPotTest` compares the platinum row with the Large-scale
Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS), version 22 Jul 2025.
LAMMPS runs the potential as `pair_style eam/fs`, the embedded atom method (EAM)
style for Finnis-Sinclair tables.
`CppCore/tests/data/sutton_chen/make_lammps_ref.py` writes the table and the two
108-atom references, with a cutoff of 5.5 Angstrom.

| Cell    | energy gap (eV) | largest force gap (eV/Angstrom) | largest stress gap (eV/Angstrom^3) |
|---------|-----------------|---------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| cubic   |         3.4e-13 |                         2.0e-11 |                            8.3e-14 |
| sheared |         2.2e-12 |                         2.8e-11 |                            2.0e-13 |

Tables of 12501, 25001 and 50001 points move the LAMMPS stress by at most
5.8e-13 eV/Angstrom^3, so the gaps above are not set by the table.
The test also takes each Voigt component as a central difference of the energy
under a symmetric strain of 1e-6.

The last test takes the pressure of the perfect face-centered cubic (fcc)
platinum crystal at the lattice parameter `a = 3.92` Angstrom.
Sutton and Chen fit c to zero pressure of the infinite crystal at a.
Their `c = 34.408` is that zero-pressure value rounded to three decimals.
The fcc lattice sum with `n = 10` and `m = 8` gives `c = 34.408374`.
The published c therefore leaves about 0.0015 GPa in the infinite crystal at a.
With the cutoff at 0.49 of the cell edge, rgpot gives

| Atoms | Cutoff (Angstrom) | Pressure at a (GPa) | Pressure at 0.99 a (GPa) |
|-------|-------------------|---------------------|--------------------------|
|   256 |            7.6832 |              0.0864 |                   9.3308 |
|   864 |           11.5248 |              0.0155 |                   9.2560 |
|  2048 |           15.3664 |              0.0053 |                   9.2446 |
|  4000 |           19.2080 |              0.0027 |                   9.2423 |

The pressure at a falls toward that 0.0015 GPa as the cutoff grows, not toward
zero.
The test asks it to shrink from 256 to 2048 atoms and to stay under 1e-3 of the
stress at 0.99 a, about 0.009 GPa.

### Cost

Pinned to one core, the flag adds 5.9 to 8.5 percent to a call.
A jittered 864-atom cell at a cutoff of 7 Angstrom takes about 880 ns per atom
without the stress and 930 with it.
A 4000-atom cell with a cutoff of 19 Angstrom takes about 25800 and 27500.
With the flag clear, six cases from 108 to 4000 atoms take the same time as
before the flag existed, to within 4 percent.

### C entry points

`rgpot_sutton_chen_energy_forces` does not carry the stress flag.
`box` may be null when `periodic` is 0.
Each thread keeps the potential of its last call when the parameters and the
atom count match.

#### `rgpot_sc_config`

- Inputs :: `epsilon`, `c=, =a`, `n=, =m`, `cutoff` and `periodic`.
  Field order is part of the ABI.
- Units :: `epsilon` sets the energy unit and `a` the length unit.
  `cutoff` is in the coordinate unit.
  `c=, =n`, `m= and =periodic` are dimensionless.
- Outputs :: the parameter block of `rgpot_sutton_chen_energy_forces` and
  `rgpot_sutton_chen_scales`.
- Errors :: none.
  The call that reads the block reports a bad value.

#### `rgpot_sutton_chen_energy_forces`

```c
int rgpot_sutton_chen_energy_forces(const rgpot_sc_config *cfg,
                                    int32_t natoms, const double *positions,
                                    const double *box, double *energy,
                                    double *forces);
```

- Inputs :: `cfg`, `natoms`, positions (3 `natoms` doubles), `box` (nine
  doubles, one cell vector per row) and the energy and force pointers.
- Units :: positions, `box` and `cutoff` in the coordinate unit.
  Energy in the unit of `epsilon`, forces in energy per length.
- Outputs :: one energy and 3 `natoms` forces, which are minus the gradient.
  Returns 0 on success.
- Errors :: returns 1 when `cfg` or `energy` is null, `natoms` is negative,
  `natoms` is positive and `positions` or `forces` is null, or the config is
  rejected.
  A periodic call also returns 1 when the cutoff is not positive or the cell is
  not usable.

#### `rgpot_sc_scales`

- Inputs :: `nearest_neighbor` and `well_depth`.
- Units :: `nearest_neighbor` in the coordinate unit.
  `well_depth` in the energy unit, and it is positive.
- Outputs :: the bulk scales written by `rgpot_sutton_chen_scales`.
- Errors :: none.

#### `rgpot_sutton_chen_scales`

```c
int rgpot_sutton_chen_scales(const rgpot_sc_config *cfg,
                             rgpot_sc_scales *out);
```

- Inputs :: `cfg` and `out`.
- Units :: as `rgpot_sc_config` and `rgpot_sc_scales`.
  The length is the static fcc minimum and the depth is minus the energy per
  atom there.
- Outputs :: the two scales.
  Returns 0 on success.
- Errors :: returns 1 when `cfg` or `out` is null, or when the config is
  rejected.
